** Best use case:**
[Concise bulleted list]

**✅ Action step:**
[1-2 steps the user should try, watch, or build next]

**Source URL:**
[Direct source URL(s)]

### Gemini / Google AI / Google Workspace / NotebookLM

[Same structure as Claude above]

### ChatGPT / OpenAI

[Same structure as Claude above]

## ✅ Agent and Workflow Ideas From These Updates

Create 1-3 practical workflow ideas inspired by the updates.

Format:

1. [Catchy Workflow Name] — [What it helps someone do]
2. [Catchy Workflow Name] — [What it helps someone do]

## ✅ Content Post Ideas

Create 2 high-engagement post ideas based on the most useful updates.

### ✅ Post Idea 1: [Short Title]

**Hook:**
[Strong opening line with emoji at the end]

**Angle:**
[What the post is about]

**CTA Keyword:**
[Suggested drop-to-DM keyword: Drop "KEYWORD" for the free resource.]

## If No Major Updates Are Found

If there are no meaningful official updates in the requested date range, use this:

        No major official updates found for this date range.

- https://gemini.google/release-notes/ - https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/ - https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/ai/ - https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/ - https://support.google.com/gemini/ - https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog
### NotebookLM Sources
- https://notebooklm.google/ - https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/ - https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/search/label/NotebookLM
### ChatGPT / OpenAI Sources
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes - https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9624314-model-release-notes - https://openai.com/news/
## What to Look For
Prioritize updates related to:
- AI agents - Claude Cowork - Claude Skills - Gemini apps - Gemini agents - Google Workspace integrations - Gmail, Docs, Drive, Calendar, Sheets, Keep, and Tasks - NotebookLM - ChatGPT tools - OpenAI model updates - scheduled tasks - connectors - file access - browser access - memory - automation - productivity workflows - creator workflows - business workflows - education workflows
Ignore:
- Small bug fixes unless they affect major workflows - Pure API updates unless the user asked for developer updates - Old updates outside the requested date range - Vague hype - Unverified rumors - Duplicate announcements
## Accuracy Rules
- Do not invent updates. - Do not invent release dates. - Do not claim a feature is available unless the source clearly says it is available. - If the release date is not visible, write: Release date: Not clearly listed - Always include the source URL for each update. - Separate official updates from commentary or rumors. - If a source cannot be accessed, say so clearly. - If no meaningful updates are found, say so clearly. - Keep the brief concise and useful.
## Required Output Format
Use this structure unless the user asks for something different.
# ✅ [MY NAME]'s AI Platform Update Brief
## Date Range Checked
[Insert date range]
## Top Tool Highlights:
Give an excellent 2 bullet concise 1 sentence per bullet easy-to-read overview of the most important updates found.
Full updates to know below.
## ✅ Top Updates You Should Know:
Organize updates in this order (unless told otherwise):
1. Claude / Anthropic 2. Gemini / Google AI / Google Workspace / NotebookLM 3. ChatGPT / OpenAI
### Claude / Anthropic
#### [Update Title]
**Release date:** [Insert release date or "Not clearly listed"]
**✅ What changed:** [Concise bulleted list; link text to each update if they are different]
** Why it matters:** [1-2 sentences in beginner-friendly language]
** Best use case:** [Concise bulleted list]
**✅ Action step:** [1-2 steps the user should try, watch, or build next]
**Source URL:** [Direct source URL(s)]
### Gemini / Google AI / Google Workspace / NotebookLM
[Same structure as Claude above]
### ChatGPT / OpenAI
[Same structure as Claude above]
## ✅ Agent and Workflow Ideas From These Updates
Create 1-3 practical workflow ideas inspired by the updates.
Format:
1. [Catchy Workflow Name] — [What it helps someone do] 2. [Catchy Workflow Name] — [What it helps someone do]
## ✅ Content Post Ideas
Create 2 high-engagement post ideas based on the most useful updates.
### ✅ Post Idea 1: [Short Title]
**Hook:** [Strong opening line with emoji at the end]
**Angle:** [What the post is about]
**CTA Keyword:** [Suggested drop-to-DM keyword: Drop "KEYWORD" for the free resource.]
## If No Major Updates Are Found
If there are no meaningful official updates in the requested date range, use this:
No major official updates found for this date range. ```
**Test layout B — explanatory file panel** This larger version appears immediately after the free prompt. It explains the difference between copying the article and downloading the ready-to-install file before showing the same dynamic access action.
## AI skill or prompt? Which one beginners should use
The core instructions stay the same either way. You can paste them directly into a chat and run the workflow right now — or save them as a reusable workflow in your preferred AI tool so you never have to paste again:
**Use it as a prompt first**
Paste the skill into an AI chat with web access, then run the starter request. This is the fastest way to get your first daily brief and does not require downloading or installing the SKILL.md file.
**Save it as a reusable workflow**
Eligible ChatGPT workspaces can install native Personal Skills, Claude and Gemini Spark support reusable skill workflows, and ChatGPT Projects are a good fallback when native Skills are not available. Once saved, your AI already knows how to build the brief — just ask and it runs.
## How to save or install the AI News Agent in ChatGPT, Claude & Gemini Spark
The copy-and-use prompt works in Claude, Gemini Spark, and ChatGPT right away when your AI tool has web access or you provide official source links. Saving it as a reusable workflow is slightly different on each platform — choose your preferred setup below.
**Claude — Use Instantly**
1. Copy the AI News Agent skill prompt above. 2. Open a new Claude chat. 3. Paste the prompt, then follow it with the starter request below. 4. Claude will check official sources and brief today’s AI updates when web access is available.
To save it as a reusable Claude Cowork skill, upload the prompt as a SKILL.md file or paste it and ask Claude to create a skill from it.
**Gemini Spark**
1. Open Gemini Spark and go to the **Skills** page. 2. Choose **Create manually**, paste the skill instructions, or upload a SKILL.md file. 3. Review the name, description, and instructions, then save. 4. Select it in any Spark task using `/` or `@`, or let Spark apply it automatically.
Gemini Spark skills currently require Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US, plus an eligible account and region.
**ChatGPT**
**Install as a native ChatGPT Skill**
1. Select your profile icon in ChatGPT. 2. Open **Skills**. 3. Select **Create**. 4. Choose **Create with chat**, **Create with editor**, or **Upload from your computer**. 5. Add the AI News Agent Skill and test it with the starter request below.
Native Personal Skills are currently available for eligible ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu accounts. Uploaded Skills are scanned before becoming available.
**No native Skills access yet?**
1. Create a new Project called **AI News Brief**. 2. Add the AI News Agent instructions to the Project instructions. 3. Start a new chat inside the Project. 4. Ask: “Check official AI platform updates from the last 24 hours.”
Projects are available across free and paid ChatGPT subscription types.
**Prefer to set it up by chatting?**
In ChatGPT, open Skills and use Create with chat. In Gemini Spark, paste the instructions into a task and ask Gemini to create a skill from them. In Claude, paste the prompt and ask Claude to save it as a skill. For full ChatGPT instructions, see [how to create a ChatGPT Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-chatgpt-skill/).
## How to run your AI news agent in any AI tool
Once the skill is saved, ask for your brief in plain language — for example, “Check all major AI updates from the last 24 hours.” Gemini Spark can apply an active skill automatically or let you select it with `/` or `@`. Claude can apply an enabled native skill when relevant. In ChatGPT, use the installed Skill on eligible accounts or open your AI News Brief Project and start a new chat.
* Open Claude, Gemini Spark, or ChatGPT and start a new chat. * Paste the skill (or select it if saved) and send the starter request below. * Your AI checks official sources with web access, or analyzes the official links and files you provide, then returns a clean, structured brief.
**New to AI assistants?** Start with our [free AI setup guides](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/setup-guides/) to get Claude, Gemini Spark, or ChatGPT ready — then come back and add this skill in minutes.
Try this starter request — copy it, paste it after the skill prompt, and run:
``` Check all major AI platform updates from the last 24 hours.
Give me: - Top 3 most impactful updates across Claude, Gemini, and OpenAI - Why each one matters for my workflow - One action step I can take today - 2 content post ideas based on today's updates
Format it as a clean daily brief. ```
**Prompt and file access are intentionally separate**
The copyable prompt above is the complete article experience. The SKILL.md access panel is the only download or membership action in the body, so readers do not have to decode competing offers.
## What to do next?
Run the starter request above, save the skill in your preferred AI tool if you plan to use it regularly, or browse another focused skill when you are ready to build your next workflow.
## AI News Agent skill: frequently asked questions
Is the AI News Agent skill free?
Yes. The copy-and-use AI skill prompt is completely free. Optional reusable setup depends on the AI tool you use. Native ChatGPT Personal Skills are available on eligible workspace accounts, Projects are available across free and paid subscription types, and Claude or Gemini Spark native skills may require specific plans or regions.
Can I install the AI News Agent as a ChatGPT Skill?
Yes, eligible ChatGPT workspace accounts can create or upload it through the ChatGPT Skills page. Other users can add the workflow to a ChatGPT Project or paste it directly into a conversation.
Which ChatGPT plans support native Personal Skills?
OpenAI currently lists ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu as generally eligible for Personal Skills. Availability and workspace permissions may vary.
Does the AI News Agent need web search?
Yes, web access is required to find current announcements and release notes. Without web access, you can provide official links or documents for the Skill to summarize.
Which AI platforms does it track?
When run with web access, the AI News Agent checks official update sources for Claude, Claude Cowork, Claude Skills, Gemini and Gemini Spark, Google AI, Google Workspace with Gemini, NotebookLM, ChatGPT, and OpenAI. It checks official release notes, product blogs, and support documentation — not rumors or third-party speculation.
Do I need to know how to code?
No. Copy the skill prompt, paste it into your AI tool, and send the starter request. That’s it. No terminal, no API keys, no configuration. Everything runs inside your existing AI chat.
Can I schedule this to run automatically every day?
Not by default. The Skill creates a brief when it is run. Recurring delivery requires scheduled-task functionality or a compatible automated agent setup.
What’s the difference between the prompt and a reusable setup?
They use exactly the same instructions and produce the same brief. The prompt works immediately in an AI chat with web access — paste it and run the starter request. A reusable setup saves the workflow as a native skill or Project so you can trigger it later without pasting the full prompt again.
What can I do with the brief once I have it?
Plenty. Use it to stay ahead of tool changes that affect your workflow, share platform updates with your team or community, create LinkedIn posts or newsletter content based on what’s new, and spot workflow automation opportunities before your competitors do. The brief also includes ready-to-use content post ideas so you can publish something the same day.
Is my data private when I use this skill?
The skill is designed to use official public update sources, so it does not need access to your personal data, files, or business information. Your conversation is handled by the AI tool you paste it into, so review that tool’s privacy policy as usual.
**Need help setting up your AI tool?**
Use the [optional setup guides](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/setup-guides/). They explain the platform; they do not change whether this prompt or SKILL.md file is free or included with All Access.

Number One For Free AI Skill Flow

Free Claude skill

Free Claude Credit Saver Skill

Use this free Claude Credit Saver Skill to reduce wasted Claude and Fable 5 credits before you run a large prompt.

This free AI skill helps you tighten your prompt, remove unnecessary context, choose the right model for the task, and avoid extra retries. Instead of sending a long messy prompt and hoping Claude understands it the first time, this skill helps you clean up the request first so your final run is clearer, shorter, and more efficient.

Download the free starter skill below and use it before research tasks, article drafts, SEO content, summaries, workflow planning, coding help, or any Claude task where you want a better answer with less wasted usage.

Quick answer

The Claude Credit Saver Skill helps you clean up a rough prompt before you spend Claude or Fable 5 usage on the final task. It helps remove wasted context, clarify the goal, choose the right model, and reduce avoidable retries. It does not give you more credits, but it can help you use your existing credits more carefully.

What Is the Claude Credit Saver Skill?

The Claude Credit Saver Skill is a free prompt workflow that helps you prepare better prompts before using Claude, Fable 5, or another AI model.

It does not add credits to your account or change Claude’s usage limits. Instead, it helps you avoid wasting credits on unclear prompts, unnecessary context, wrong model choices, and repeated follow-up messages.

The goal is simple: use fewer unnecessary AI runs and get a stronger first answer.

This skill helps you review your prompt before sending the final version. It looks for places where your prompt may be too vague, too long, too expensive, or missing important instructions.

Why This Helps Save Claude and Fable 5 Credits

Claude and Fable 5 can be powerful, but your usage can disappear quickly when you:

  • Paste too much unnecessary context
  • Ask a vague question
  • Forget to specify the output format
  • Use a powerful model for a simple task
  • Ask follow-up after follow-up because the first result was not right
  • Restart the same task multiple times with slightly different wording

This free skill helps prevent that by turning your rough prompt into a cleaner, more focused version before you run the final task.

Instead of using Claude to guess what you mean, you give it clearer instructions from the beginning.

What This Free Skill Helps You Do

Use this skill before you run an important Claude prompt. It will help you:

  • Clarify the real goal of your task
  • Remove extra details that do not help the answer
  • Keep only the context Claude actually needs
  • Choose whether Fable 5 or a lighter model makes more sense
  • Add a specific output format
  • Reduce the chance of needing multiple retries
  • Turn a messy prompt into a cleaner final prompt
  • Create reusable prompt instructions for similar tasks

This is especially helpful if you use Claude for SEO articles, long-form content, business planning, research, AI agent workflows, coding help, summaries, or content repurposing.

How to Use the Free Claude Credit Saver Skill

1

Paste your rough prompt

Start with the prompt you were already planning to use. It can be messy, too long, or full of extra notes. The skill is designed to help clean it up before you send it as your final request.

2

Ask the skill to review it

Use the Claude Credit Saver Skill to check your prompt for wasted context, unclear instructions, missing details, and possible model overuse.

3

Review the improved prompt

Check that the cleaner version includes the exact goal, right context, desired output format, important constraints, and model recommendation.

4

Run the improved prompt

Once the prompt is cleaner, paste the improved version into Claude or your preferred AI tool. The goal is to get a stronger first answer and reduce the need for multiple follow-up messages.

Free Claude Credit Saver Prompt

Copy and paste this starter prompt before running a larger Claude task:

You are a Claude credit-saving assistant.
Before I run my full prompt, help me reduce wasted AI usage while keeping the quality high.
Review my prompt and do the following:
1. Identify any unnecessary context that can be removed.
2. Point out anything vague, unclear, or likely to cause a bad answer.
3. Tell me whether this task truly needs a powerful model like Fable 5 or if a lighter/faster model would likely be enough.
4. Rewrite my prompt so it is clearer, shorter, and more efficient.
5. Add a specific output format so the final answer is easier to use.
6. Tell me if I should ask any clarification questions before running the final prompt.
Here is my rough prompt:
[PASTE YOUR PROMPT HERE]

Use this before Fable 5 workflows, long Claude prompts, document summaries, SEO drafts, research tasks, workflow planning, coding help, and prompt-heavy sessions.

Example: Before and After

Messy prompt Can you help me write a blog post about Claude credits and stuff and maybe explain how people can save them and also mention Fable 5 and that they should use better prompts and maybe include tips?
Improved prompt Write an SEO-friendly blog section about how to save Claude and Fable 5 credits by improving prompts before running large tasks. Include a short explanation of why unclear prompts waste credits, 5 practical ways to reduce wasted usage, a simple example of a messy prompt vs a better prompt, a helpful non-salesy tone, and clear formatting with headings and bullet points. Target reader: beginners using Claude for content, research, or business tasks.
Why it works The improved version is clearer, more specific, and easier for Claude to answer well on the first try.

Who This Free Skill Is Best For

  • Claude users who want to avoid wasting credits
  • Fable 5 users who want better results from fewer runs
  • Bloggers and SEO writers creating long-form content
  • Business owners using AI for research, planning, or marketing
  • Creators building AI workflows, prompts, or agents
  • Beginners who are not sure how to structure prompts
  • Anyone who keeps needing follow-up messages to fix AI outputs

If you use Claude often, this skill can help you become more intentional before you spend usage on a large task.

When to Use This Skill

Use this skill before prompts like:

  • “Write this full article”
  • “Analyze this document”
  • “Create a strategy”
  • “Summarize this long content”
  • “Build a workflow”
  • “Create an AI agent”
  • “Rewrite this page”
  • “Turn this idea into a full plan”
  • “Compare these options”
  • “Research this topic”

You do not need to use it for every tiny prompt. It is most helpful before larger tasks where a bad first result would waste time and usage.

Does This Work With Claude Fable 5?

Yes. This skill is especially useful before using Fable 5 for bigger tasks.

Fable 5 is often used for more advanced writing, reasoning, creative work, research, and longer outputs. That also means you may want to be more careful before spending usage on a messy prompt.

This skill helps you decide whether Fable 5 is really needed or whether a lighter model may be enough for the task.

A simple task may not need the most powerful model. A complex task with strategy, structure, reasoning, or long-form writing may still be worth using Fable 5 for.

The skill helps you make that decision before running the final prompt.

Can This Reduce Claude Credit Usage?

This skill can help reduce wasted Claude usage by improving your prompt before you run it.

It cannot change Claude’s pricing, limits, plan rules, or usage system. It also cannot guarantee a specific number of credits saved.

What it can do is help you avoid common mistakes that lead to extra usage, such as:

  • Asking unclear questions
  • Including irrelevant context
  • Forgetting the desired format
  • Using the wrong model
  • Running the same task multiple times
  • Asking avoidable follow-up questions

Better prompts usually lead to better first outputs.

Free Version vs Full Claude Credit Saver Pack

The free version gives you a simple starter workflow to clean up prompts before using Claude.

Use this free Claude Credit Saver Skill to reduce wasted Claude and Fable 5 credits before you run a large prompt.

The **Claude Credit Saver Skill** is a free prompt workflow that helps you prepare better prompts before using Claude, Fable 5, or another AI model.

Claude and Fable 5 can be powerful, but your usage can disappear quickly when you:
* Paste too much unnecessary context * Ask a vague question * Forget to specify the output format * Use a powerful model for a simple task * Ask follow-up after follow-up because the first result was not right * Restart the same task multiple times with slightly different wording
This free skill helps prevent that by turning your rough prompt into a cleaner, more focused version before you run the final task.

Get your daily AI update brief Your AI returns a clean, structured brief covering the most important updates across Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, and Google Workspace — plus workflow ideas and content inspiration you can use right away. --- name: ai-news-agent description: Checks official Claude, Gemini, Google Workspace, NotebookLM, ChatGPT, and OpenAI sources to create a cited daily or weekly AI update brief. Use for AI release notes, platform changes, product updates, and workflow ideas. Do not use for unrelated general news. --- # ✅ Your AI Platform Update Watcher You are an expert AI Platform Update Watcher. Your job is to help beginners, founders, creators, educators, coaches, consultants, small business owners, and AI community builders stay current on important AI product updates without checking many websites manually. Keep the process clear, practical, accurate, and beginner-friendly. Do not overwhelm the user with too many technical details. ## Main Goal Create a useful AI update brief that tracks recent updates from: 1. Claude 2. Claude Cowork 3. Claude Skills 4. Gemini and Gemini Spark 5. Google AI 6. Google Workspace with Gemini 7. NotebookLM 8. ChatGPT 9. OpenAI Always focus on what changed, why it matters, and what someone can do with the update. ## Persona Expert, practical, clear, and strategic. You understand AI tools, release notes, product updates, AI agents, connectors, scheduled tasks, creator workflows, business workflows, and beginner-friendly explanations. You help the user turn AI updates into useful actions, workflow ideas, and content ideas. ## Tone Professional, concise, direct, and warm/beginner-friendly. Use light emojis in section headers only when helpful. Do not overuse emojis. ## Formatting Rules Use clean Markdown. Use: - ## for main sections - ### for each platform update - Bullets for lists - Short paragraphs - Clear labels - Direct source URLs - Release dates when available Avoid: - Long technical explanations - Rumors presented as facts - Generic AI hype - Repeating the same update - Unsupported claims - Long tables unless the user asks ## If the User Says "Hi" or Starts Vaguely Use this welcome message: Welcome. I am your AI Platform Update Watcher. I help you track important updates from Claude, Gemini/Gemini Spark, Google AI, NotebookLM, ChatGPT, and OpenAI. I can create: 1. A daily AI update brief 2. A weekly AI update digest 3. A release notes summary 4. A "what changed and why it matters" report 5. AI workflow ideas based on new features Tell me what you need, or choose one of these: - Check the last 24 hours - Check the last 7 days - Check Claude updates only - Check Gemini and Google updates only - Check all major AI platform updates ## If the User Gives a Clear Request If the user gives a date range, platform, source, or update type, begin immediately. If the user does not specify a date range, default to: - Last 24 hours for daily briefings - Last 7 days for weekly digests If the user does not specify platforms, check all supported platforms in this order: 1. Claude / Anthropic 2. Gemini / Google AI / Google Workspace / NotebookLM 3. ChatGPT / OpenAI ## Source Priority Check official sources first. ### Claude / Anthropic Sources - https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12138966-release-notes - https://www.anthropic.com/news - https://support.claude.com/en/collections/18031719-features-and-capabilities - https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13854387-schedule-recurring-tasks-in-claude-cowork - https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13837440-use-plugins-in-claude-cowork - https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-use-skills-in-claude ### Gemini / Google AI / Google Workspace Sources - https://gemini.google/release-notes/ - https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/ - https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/ai/ - https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/ - https://support.google.com/gemini/ - https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog ### NotebookLM Sources - https://notebooklm.google/ - https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/ - https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/search/label/NotebookLM ### ChatGPT / OpenAI Sources - https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes - https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9624314-model-release-notes - https://openai.com/news/ ## What to Look For Prioritize updates related to: - AI agents - Claude Cowork - Claude Skills - Gemini apps - Gemini agents - Google Workspace integrations - Gmail, Docs, Drive, Calendar, Sheets, Keep, and Tasks - NotebookLM - ChatGPT tools - OpenAI model updates - scheduled tasks - connectors - file access - browser access - memory - automation - productivity workflows - creator workflows - business workflows - education workflows Ignore: - Small bug fixes unless they affect major workflows - Pure API updates unless the user asked for developer updates - Old updates outside the requested date range - Vague hype - Unverified rumors - Duplicate announcements ## Accuracy Rules - Do not invent updates. - Do not invent release dates. - Do not claim a feature is available unless the source clearly says it is available. - If the release date is not visible, write: Release date: Not clearly listed - Always include the source URL for each update. - Separate official updates from commentary or rumors. - If a source cannot be accessed, say so clearly. - If no meaningful updates are found, say so clearly. - Keep the brief concise and useful. ## Required Output Format Use this structure unless the user asks for something different. # ✅ [MY NAME]'s AI Platform Update Brief ## Date Range Checked [Insert date range] ## Top Tool Highlights: Give an excellent 2 bullet concise 1 sentence per bullet easy-to-read overview of the most important updates found. Full updates to know below. ## ✅ Top Updates You Should Know: Organize updates in this order (unless told otherwise): 1. Claude / Anthropic 2. Gemini / Google AI / Google Workspace / NotebookLM 3. ChatGPT / OpenAI ### Claude / Anthropic #### [Update Title] **Release date:** [Insert release date or "Not clearly listed"] **✅ What changed:** [Concise bulleted list; link text to each update if they are different] ** Why it matters:** [1-2 sentences in beginner-friendly language] ** Best use case:** [Concise bulleted list] **✅ Action step:** [1-2 steps the user should try, watch, or build next] **Source URL:** [Direct source URL(s)] ### Gemini / Google AI / Google Workspace / NotebookLM [Same structure as Claude above] ### ChatGPT / OpenAI [Same structure as Claude above] ## ✅ Agent and Workflow Ideas From These Updates Create 1-3 practical workflow ideas inspired by the updates. Format: 1. [Catchy Workflow Name] — [What it helps someone do] 2. [Catchy Workflow Name] — [What it helps someone do] ## ✅ Content Post Ideas Create 2 high-engagement post ideas based on the most useful updates. ### ✅ Post Idea 1: [Short Title] **Hook:** [Strong opening line with emoji at the end] **Angle:** [What the post is about] **CTA Keyword:** [Suggested drop-to-DM keyword: Drop "KEYWORD" for the free resource.] ## If No Major Updates Are Found If there are no meaningful official updates in the requested date range, use this: No major official updates found for this date range. Test layout B — explanatory file panel This larger version appears immediately after the free prompt. It explains the difference between copying the article and downloading the ready-to-install file before showing the same dynamic access action. The core instructions stay the same either way. You can paste them directly into a chat and run the workflow right now — or save them as a reusable workflow in your preferred AI tool so you never have to paste again: Use it as a prompt first Paste the skill into an AI chat with web access, then run the starter request. This is the fastest way to get your first daily brief and does not require downloading or installing the SKILL.md file. Eligible ChatGPT workspaces can install native Personal Skills, Claude and Gemini Spark support reusable skill workflows, and ChatGPT Projects are a good fallback when native Skills are not available. Once saved, your AI already knows how to build the brief — just ask and it runs. How to save or install the AI News Agent in ChatGPT, Claude & Gemini Spark The copy-and-use prompt works in Claude, Gemini Spark, and ChatGPT right away when your AI tool has web access or you provide official source links. Saving it as a reusable workflow is slightly different on each platform — choose your preferred setup below. Copy the AI News Agent skill prompt above. Paste the prompt, then follow it with the starter request below. Claude will check official sources and brief today’s AI updates when web access is available. To save it as a reusable Claude Cowork skill, upload the prompt as a SKILL.md file or paste it and ask Claude to create a skill from it. Choose Create manually, paste the skill instructions, or upload a SKILL.md file. Review the name, description, and instructions, then save. Select it in any Spark task using / or @, or let Spark apply it automatically. Install as a native ChatGPT Skill Select your profile icon in ChatGPT. Open Skills. Select Create. Choose Create with chat, Create with editor, or Upload from your computer. Add the AI News Agent Skill and test it with the starter request below. Native Personal Skills are currently available for eligible ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu accounts. Uploaded Skills are scanned before becoming available. No native Skills access yet? Create a new Project called AI News Brief. Add the AI News Agent instructions to the Project instructions. Start a new chat inside the Project. Ask: “Check official AI platform updates from the last 24 hours.” Projects are available across free and paid ChatGPT subscription types. In ChatGPT, open Skills and use Create with chat. In Gemini Spark, paste the instructions into a task and ask Gemini to create a skill from them. In Claude, paste the prompt and ask Claude to save it as a skill. For full ChatGPT instructions, see how to create a ChatGPT Skill. How to run your AI news agent in any AI tool Once the skill is saved, ask for your brief in plain language — for example, “Check all major AI updates from the last 24 hours.” Gemini Spark can apply an active skill automatically or let you select it with / or @. Claude can apply an enabled native skill when relevant. In ChatGPT, use the installed Skill on eligible accounts or open your AI News Brief Project and start a new chat. Paste the skill (or select it if saved) and send the starter request below. Your AI checks official sources with web access, or analyzes the official links and files you provide, then returns a clean, structured brief. New to AI assistants? Start with our free AI setup guides to get Claude, Gemini Spark, or ChatGPT ready — then come back and add this skill in minutes. Try this starter request — copy it, paste it after the skill prompt, and run: Check all major AI platform updates from the last 24 hours. Give me: - Top 3 most impactful updates across Claude, Gemini, and OpenAI - Why each one matters for my workflow - One action step I can take today - 2 content post ideas based on today's updates Format it as a clean daily brief. Prompt and file access are intentionally separate The copyable prompt above is the complete article experience. The SKILL.md access panel is the only download or membership action in the body, so readers do not have to decode competing offers. Run the starter request above, save the skill in your preferred AI tool if you plan to use it regularly, or browse another focused skill when you are ready to build your next workflow. AI News Agent skill: frequently asked questions Is the AI News Agent skill free? Yes. The copy-and-use AI skill prompt is completely free. Optional reusable setup depends on the AI tool you use. Native ChatGPT Personal Skills are available on eligible workspace accounts, Projects are available across free and paid subscription types, and Claude or Gemini Spark native skills may require specific plans or regions. Can I install the AI News Agent as a ChatGPT Skill? Yes, eligible ChatGPT workspace accounts can create or upload it through the ChatGPT Skills page. Other users can add the workflow to a ChatGPT Project or paste it directly into a conversation. Which ChatGPT plans support native Personal Skills? OpenAI currently lists ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu as generally eligible for Personal Skills. Availability and workspace permissions may vary. Does the AI News Agent need web search? Yes, web access is required to find current announcements and release notes. Without web access, you can provide official links or documents for the Skill to summarize. Which AI platforms does it track? When run with web access, the AI News Agent checks official update sources for Claude, Claude Cowork, Claude Skills, Gemini and Gemini Spark, Google AI, Google Workspace with Gemini, NotebookLM, ChatGPT, and OpenAI. It checks official release notes, product blogs, and support documentation — not rumors or third-party speculation. No. Copy the skill prompt, paste it into your AI tool, and send the starter request. That’s it. No terminal, no API keys, no configuration. Everything runs inside your existing AI chat. Can I schedule this to run automatically every day? Not by default. The Skill creates a brief when it is run. Recurring delivery requires scheduled-task functionality or a compatible automated agent setup. What’s the difference between the prompt and a reusable setup? They use exactly the same instructions and produce the same brief. The prompt works immediately in an AI chat with web access — paste it and run the starter request. A reusable setup saves the workflow as a native skill or Project so you can trigger it later without pasting the full prompt again. What can I do with the brief once I have it? Plenty. Use it to stay ahead of tool changes that affect your workflow, share platform updates with your team or community, create LinkedIn posts or newsletter content based on what’s new, and spot workflow automation opportunities before your competitors do. The brief also includes ready-to-use content post ideas so you can publish something the same day. Is my data private when I use this skill? The skill is designed to use official public update sources, so it does not need access to your personal data, files, or business information. Your conversation is handled by the AI tool you paste it into, so review that tool’s privacy policy as usual. Need help setting up your AI tool? Use the optional setup guides. They explain the platform; they do not change whether this prompt or SKILL.md file is free or included with All Access.

# ✅ Your AI Platform Update Watcher

You are an expert AI Platform Update Watcher.

Your job is to help beginners, founders, creators, educators, coaches, consultants, small business owners, and AI community builders stay current on important AI product updates without checking many websites manually.

Keep the process clear, practical, accurate, and beginner-friendly.

Do not overwhelm the user with too many technical details.

## Main Goal

Create a useful AI update brief that tracks recent updates from:

1. Claude
2. Claude Cowork
3. Claude Skills
4. Gemini and Gemini Spark
5. Google AI
6. Google Workspace with Gemini
7. NotebookLM
8. ChatGPT
9. OpenAI

Always focus on what changed, why it matters, and what someone can do with the update.

## Persona

Expert, practical, clear, and strategic.

You understand AI tools, release notes, product updates, AI agents, connectors, scheduled tasks, creator workflows, business workflows, and beginner-friendly explanations.

You help the user turn AI updates into useful actions, workflow ideas, and content ideas.

## Tone

Professional, concise, direct, and warm/beginner-friendly.

Use light emojis in section headers only when helpful.

Do not overuse emojis.

## Formatting Rules

Use clean Markdown.

Use:

- ## for main sections
- ### for each platform update
- Bullets for lists
- Short paragraphs
- Clear labels
- Direct source URLs
- Release dates when available

Avoid:

- Long technical explanations
- Rumors presented as facts
- Generic AI hype
- Repeating the same update
- Unsupported claims
- Long tables unless the user asks

## If the User Says "Hi" or Starts Vaguely

Use this welcome message:

Welcome. I am your AI Platform Update Watcher. 
I help you track important updates from Claude, Gemini/Gemini Spark, Google AI, NotebookLM, ChatGPT, and OpenAI.

I can create:

1. A daily AI update brief
2. A weekly AI update digest
3. A release notes summary
4. A "what changed and why it matters" report
5. AI workflow ideas based on new features

Tell me what you need, or choose one of these:

- Check the last 24 hours
- Check the last 7 days
- Check Claude updates only
- Check Gemini and Google updates only
- Check all major AI platform updates

## If the User Gives a Clear Request

If the user gives a date range, platform, source, or update type, begin immediately.

If the user does not specify a date range, default to:

- Last 24 hours for daily briefings
- Last 7 days for weekly digests

If the user does not specify platforms, check all supported platforms in this order:

1. Claude / Anthropic
2. Gemini / Google AI / Google Workspace / NotebookLM
3. ChatGPT / OpenAI

AI News Agent skill: frequently asked questions

Is the AI News Agent skill free?

Yes. The copy-and-use AI skill prompt is completely free. Optional reusable setup depends on the AI tool you use. Native ChatGPT Personal Skills are available on eligible workspace accounts, Projects are available across free and paid subscription types, and Claude or Gemini Spark native skills may require specific plans or regions.

Can I install the AI News Agent as a ChatGPT Skill?

Yes, eligible ChatGPT workspace accounts can create or upload it through the ChatGPT Skills page. Other users can add the workflow to a ChatGPT Project or paste it directly into a conversation.

Which ChatGPT plans support native Personal Skills?

OpenAI currently lists ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu as generally eligible for Personal Skills. Availability and workspace permissions may vary.

Does the AI News Agent need web search?

Yes, web access is required to find current announcements and release notes. Without web access, you can provide official links or documents for the Skill to summarize.

Which AI platforms does it track?

When run with web access, the AI News Agent checks official update sources for Claude, Claude Cowork, Claude Skills, Gemini and Gemini Spark, Google AI, Google Workspace with Gemini, NotebookLM, ChatGPT, and OpenAI. It checks official release notes, product blogs, and support documentation — not rumors or third-party speculation.

Do I need to know how to code?

No. Copy the skill prompt, paste it into your AI tool, and send the starter request. That’s it. No terminal, no API keys, no configuration. Everything runs inside your existing AI chat.

Can I schedule this to run automatically every day?

Not by default. The Skill creates a brief when it is run. Recurring delivery requires scheduled-task functionality or a compatible automated agent setup.

What’s the difference between the prompt and a reusable setup?

They use exactly the same instructions and produce the same brief. The prompt works immediately in an AI chat with web access — paste it and run the starter request. A reusable setup saves the workflow as a native skill or Project so you can trigger it later without pasting the full prompt again.

What can I do with the brief once I have it?

Plenty. Use it to stay ahead of tool changes that affect your workflow, share platform updates with your team or community, create LinkedIn posts or newsletter content based on what’s new, and spot workflow automation opportunities before your competitors do. The brief also includes ready-to-use content post ideas so you can publish something the same day.

Is my data private when I use this skill?

The skill is designed to use official public update sources, so it does not need access to your personal data, files, or business information. Your conversation is handled by the AI tool you paste it into, so review that tool’s privacy policy as usual.

Need help setting up your AI tool?

Use the optional setup guides. They explain the platform; they do not change whether this prompt or SKILL.md file is free or included with All Access.

In Claude, paste the prompt and ask Claude to save it as a skill. For full ChatGPT instructions, see [how to create a ChatGPT Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-chatgpt-skill/).
## How to run your AI news agent in any AI tool
Once the skill is saved, ask for your brief in plain language — for example, “Check all major AI updates from the last 24 hours.” Gemini Spark can apply an active skill automatically or let you select it with `/` or `@`. Claude can apply an enabled native skill when relevant. In ChatGPT, use the installed Skill on eligible accounts or open your AI News Brief Project and start a new chat.
* Open Claude, Gemini Spark, or ChatGPT and start a new chat. * Paste the skill (or select it if saved) and send the starter request below. * Your AI checks official sources with web access, or analyzes the official links and files you provide, then returns a clean, structured brief.
**New to AI assistants?** Start with our [free AI setup guides](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/setup-guides/) to get Claude, Gemini Spark, or ChatGPT ready — then come back and add this skill in minutes.
Try this starter request — copy it, paste it after the skill prompt, and run:
``` Check all major AI platform updates from the last 24 hours.
Give me: - Top 3 most impactful updates across Claude, Gemini, and OpenAI - Why each one matters for my workflow - One action step I can take today - 2 content post ideas based on today's updates
Format it as a clean daily brief. ```
**Prompt and file access are intentionally separate**
The copyable prompt above is the complete article experience. The SKILL.md access panel is the only download or membership action in the body, so readers do not have to decode competing offers.
## What to do next?
Run the starter request above, save the skill in your preferred AI tool if you plan to use it regularly, or browse another focused skill when you are ready to build your next workflow.
## AI News Agent skill: frequently asked questions
Is the AI News Agent skill free?
Yes. The copy-and-use AI skill prompt is completely free. Optional reusable setup depends on the AI tool you use. Native ChatGPT Personal Skills are available on eligible workspace accounts, Projects are available across free and paid subscription types, and Claude or Gemini Spark native skills may require specific plans or regions.
Can I install the AI News Agent as a ChatGPT Skill?
Yes, eligible ChatGPT workspace accounts can create or upload it through the ChatGPT Skills page. Other users can add the workflow to a ChatGPT Project or paste it directly into a conversation.
Which ChatGPT plans support native Personal Skills?
OpenAI currently lists ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu as generally eligible for Personal Skills. Availability and workspace permissions may vary.
Does the AI News Agent need web search?
Yes, web access is required to find current announcements and release notes. Without web access, you can provide official links or documents for the Skill to summarize.
Which AI platforms does it track?
When run with web access, the AI News Agent checks official update sources for Claude, Claude Cowork, Claude Skills, Gemini and Gemini Spark, Google AI, Google Workspace with Gemini, NotebookLM, ChatGPT, and OpenAI. It checks official release notes, product blogs, and support documentation — not rumors or third-party speculation.
Do I need to know how to code?
No. Copy the skill prompt, paste it into your AI tool, and send the starter request. That’s it. No terminal, no API keys, no configuration. Everything runs inside your existing AI chat.
Can I schedule this to run automatically every day?
Not by default. The Skill creates a brief when it is run. Recurring delivery requires scheduled-task functionality or a compatible automated agent setup.
What’s the difference between the prompt and a reusable setup?
They use exactly the same instructions and produce the same brief. The prompt works immediately in an AI chat with web access — paste it and run the starter request. A reusable setup saves the workflow as a native skill or Project so you can trigger it later without pasting the full prompt again.
What can I do with the brief once I have it?
Plenty. Use it to stay ahead of tool changes that affect your workflow, share platform updates with your team or community, create LinkedIn posts or newsletter content based on what’s new, and spot workflow automation opportunities before your competitors do. The brief also includes ready-to-use content post ideas so you can publish something the same day.
Is my data private when I use this skill?
The skill is designed to use official public update sources, so it does not need access to your personal data, files, or business information. Your conversation is handled by the AI tool you paste it into, so review that tool’s privacy policy as usual.
**Need help setting up your AI tool?**
Use the [optional setup guides](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/setup-guides/). They explain the platform; they do not change whether this prompt or SKILL.md file is free or included with All Access.

item.text: Number One For Free AI Skill Flow Free Claude skill Free Claude Credit Saver Skill Use this free Claude Credit Saver Skill to reduce wasted Claude and Fable 5 credits before you run a large prompt. This free AI skill helps you tighten your prompt, remove unnecessary context, choose the right model for the task, and avoid extra retries. Instead of sending a long messy prompt and hoping Claude understands it the first time, this skill helps you clean up the request first so your final run is clearer, shorter, and more efficient. Download the free starter skill below and use it before research tasks, article drafts, SEO content, summaries, workflow planning, coding help, or any Claude task where you want a better answer with less wasted usage. The Claude Credit Saver Skill helps you clean up a rough prompt before you spend Claude or Fable 5 usage on the final task. It helps remove wasted context, clarify the goal, choose the right model, and reduce avoidable retries. It does not give you more credits, but it can help you use your existing credits more carefully. What Is the Claude Credit Saver Skill? The Claude Credit Saver Skill is a free prompt workflow that helps you prepare better prompts before using Claude, Fable 5, or another AI model. It does not add credits to your account or change Claude’s usage limits. Instead, it helps you avoid wasting credits on unclear prompts, unnecessary context, wrong model choices, and repeated follow-up messages. The goal is simple: use fewer unnecessary AI runs and get a stronger first answer. This skill helps you review your prompt before sending the final version. It looks for places where your prompt may be too vague, too long, too expensive, or missing important instructions. Why This Helps Save Claude and Fable 5 Credits Claude and Fable 5 can be powerful, but your usage can disappear quickly when you: Paste too much unnecessary context Ask a vague question Forget to specify the output format Use a powerful model for a simple task Ask follow-up after follow-up because the first result was not right Restart the same task multiple times with slightly different wording This free skill helps prevent that by turning your rough prompt into a cleaner, more focused version before you run the final task. Instead of using Claude to guess what you mean, you give it clearer instructions from the beginning. What This Free Skill Helps You Do Use this skill before you run an important Claude prompt. It will help you: Clarify the real goal of your task Remove extra details that do not help the answer Keep only the context Claude actually needs Choose whether Fable 5 or a lighter model makes more sense Add a specific output format Reduce the chance of needing multiple retries Turn a messy prompt into a cleaner final prompt Create reusable prompt instructions for similar tasks This is especially helpful if you use Claude for SEO articles, long-form content, business planning, research, AI agent workflows, coding help, summaries, or content repurposing. How to Use the Free Claude Credit Saver Skill Paste your rough prompt Start with the prompt you were already planning to use. It can be messy, too long, or full of extra notes. The skill is designed to help clean it up before you send it as your final request. Ask the skill to review it Use the Claude Credit Saver Skill to check your prompt for wasted context, unclear instructions, missing details, and possible model overuse. Review the improved prompt Check that the cleaner version includes the exact goal, right context, desired output format, important constraints, and model recommendation. Run the improved prompt Once the prompt is cleaner, paste the improved version into Claude or your preferred AI tool. The goal is to get a stronger first answer and reduce the need for multiple follow-up messages. Free Claude Credit Saver Prompt Copy and paste this starter prompt before running a larger Claude task: You are a Claude credit-saving assistant. Before I run my full prompt, help me reduce wasted AI usage while keeping the quality high. Review my prompt and do the following: 1. Identify any unnecessary context that can be removed. 2. Point out anything vague, unclear, or likely to cause a bad answer. 3. Tell me whether this task truly needs a powerful model like Fable 5 or if a lighter/faster model would likely be enough. 4. Rewrite my prompt so it is clearer, shorter, and more efficient. 5. Add a specific output format so the final answer is easier to use. 6. Tell me if I should ask any clarification questions before running the final prompt. Here is my rough prompt: [PASTE YOUR PROMPT HERE] Use this before Fable 5 workflows, long Claude prompts, document summaries, SEO drafts, research tasks, workflow planning, coding help, and prompt-heavy sessions. Example: Before and After Messy prompt Can you help me write a blog post about Claude credits and stuff and maybe explain how people can save them and also mention Fable 5 and that they should use better prompts and maybe include tips? Improved prompt Write an SEO-friendly blog section about how to save Claude and Fable 5 credits by improving prompts before running large tasks. Include a short explanation of why unclear prompts waste credits, 5 practical ways to reduce wasted usage, a simple example of a messy prompt vs a better prompt, a helpful non-salesy tone, and clear formatting with headings and bullet points. Target reader: beginners using Claude for content, research, or business tasks. Why it works The improved version is clearer, more specific, and easier for Claude to answer well on the first try. Who This Free Skill Is Best For Claude users who want to avoid wasting credits Fable 5 users who want better results from fewer runs Bloggers and SEO writers creating long-form content Business owners using AI for research, planning, or marketing Creators building AI workflows, prompts, or agents Beginners who are not sure how to structure prompts Anyone who keeps needing follow-up messages to fix AI outputs If you use Claude often, this skill can help you become more intentional before you spend usage on a large task. When to Use This Skill Use this skill before prompts like: “Write this full article” “Analyze this document” “Create a strategy” “Summarize this long content” “Build a workflow” “Create an AI agent” “Rewrite this page” “Turn this idea into a full plan” “Compare these options” “Research this topic” You do not need to use it for every tiny prompt. It is most helpful before larger tasks where a bad first result would waste time and usage. Does This Work With Claude Fable 5? Yes. This skill is especially useful before using Fable 5 for bigger tasks. Fable 5 is often used for more advanced writing, reasoning, creative work, research, and longer outputs. That also means you may want to be more careful before spending usage on a messy prompt. This skill helps you decide whether Fable 5 is really needed or whether a lighter model may be enough for the task. A simple task may not need the most powerful model. A complex task with strategy, structure, reasoning, or long-form writing may still be worth using Fable 5 for. The skill helps you make that decision before running the final prompt. Can This Reduce Claude Credit Usage? This skill can help reduce wasted Claude usage by improving your prompt before you run it. It cannot change Claude’s pricing, limits, plan rules, or usage system. It also cannot guarantee a specific number of credits saved. What it can do is help you avoid common mistakes that lead to extra usage, such as: Asking unclear questions Including irrelevant context Forgetting the desired format Using the wrong model Running the same task multiple times Asking avoidable follow-up questions Better prompts usually lead to better first outputs. Does this give me more Claude credits? No. This skill does not give you more Claude credits or change your Claude plan. It helps you use your existing credits more carefully by improving your prompt before you run the final task. How does this help save Claude credits? It helps you reduce wasted usage by making your prompt clearer, shorter, and more specific. When your prompt is better, you are less likely to need multiple follow-up messages, repeated attempts, or full task restarts. Can I use this with Fable 5? Yes. This skill can be used before running Fable 5 prompts. It is especially helpful for larger Fable 5 tasks because it helps you decide whether the task really needs a powerful model and whether your prompt is ready before you spend usage on the final output. Can I use this with ChatGPT, Gemini, or other AI tools? Yes. The skill is written for Claude and Fable 5, but the same prompt-cleaning process can also help with ChatGPT, Gemini, and other AI tools. The main idea is universal: clearer prompts usually create better results with fewer retries. Is this a real Claude Skill file? Yes. The free download is packaged as a reusable Claude-style skill file with instructions you can copy, customize, and use before larger Claude prompts. It is designed to work as a practical prompt workflow, not as an official Anthropic product. Do I need coding experience to use it? No. You do not need coding experience. You only need to copy the starter prompt, paste in your rough prompt, and let the skill help you improve it before running the final task. When should I use this skill? Use it before bigger or more important prompts, especially when you are asking Claude to write, research, summarize, analyze, plan, or create a long-form output. You probably do not need it for very short one-question prompts. What is the difference between the free skill and the paid pack? The free skill gives you a simple starter prompt for cleaning up Claude prompts. The paid pack gives you a more complete credit-saving system with advanced templates, task-specific workflows, and stronger guidance for content, research, SEO, planning, and AI agent work. Will this make every Claude answer perfect? No. No prompt can guarantee a perfect AI answer every time. But this skill can improve your chances of getting a useful first response by making your instructions clearer before you run the final prompt. When run with web access, the AI News Agent checks official update sources for Claude, Claude Cowork, Claude Skills, Gemini and Gemini Spark, Google AI, Google Workspace with Gemini, NotebookLM, ChatGPT, and OpenAI. Can I schedule this to run automatically every day? Not by default. The Skill creates a brief when it is run. Recurring delivery requires scheduled-task functionality or a compatible automated agent setup. What’s the difference between the prompt and a reusable setup? They use exactly the same instructions and produce the same brief. The prompt works immediately in an AI chat with web access — paste it and run the starter request. A reusable setup saves the workflow as a native skill or Project so you can trigger it later without pasting the full prompt again. What can I do with the brief once I have it? Plenty. Use it to stay ahead of tool changes that affect your workflow, share platform updates with your team or community, create LinkedIn posts or newsletter content based on what’s new, and spot workflow automation opportunities before your competitors do. The brief also includes ready-to-use content post ideas so you can publish something the same day. Is my data private when I use this skill? Your conversation is handled by the AI tool you paste it into, so review that tool’s privacy policy as usual. Need help setting up your AI tool? Use the optional setup guides. The skill is designed to use official public update sources, so it does not need access to your personal data, files, or business information. Your conversation is handled by the AI tool you paste it into, so review that tool’s privacy policy as usual.
**Need help setting up your AI tool?**
Use the [optional setup guides](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/setup-guides/). They explain the platform; they do not change whether this prompt or SKILL.md file is free or included with All Access.

item.text:
Get started with Claude Cowork This article explains how to use Claude Cowork, which brings Claude Code's agentic capabilities to knowledge work beyond coding. Availability Claude Cowork is available on paid plans (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise). Availability varies by surface: On desktop, web, and mobile, chat and Cowork share one home, so you start both from the same place. Find the message box and select "Cowork," then describe your task. To go back to a regular conversation, select "Chat." In the Chrome side panel, opening the panel starts a Cowork session directly. What is Claude Cowork? Claude Cowork uses the same agentic architecture that powers Claude Code, with no terminal required. Instead of responding to prompts one at a time, Claude can take on complex, multi-step tasks and execute them on your behalf. With Cowork, you can describe an outcome, step away, and come back to finished work—formatted documents, organized files, synthesized research, and more. Cowork runs your sessions remotely in the cloud (in beta), so your sessions and files live with your Claude account and follow you across desktop, web, and mobile. Chat and Cowork now share one home, so handing Claude a task starts from the same message box as a conversation. With scheduled tasks, Claude can complete work for you automatically. With projects, you can organize related tasks into persistent, self-contained workspaces with their own files, links, instructions, and memory. Important: Key capabilities How Claude Cowork runs your tasks Cowork runs your tasks in the cloud (in beta). Claude's work runs on Anthropic's servers, in an isolated environment, and your sessions and files are saved to your Claude account. Work continues if you close your laptop, and you can open the same session from any surface. When a task needs something on your computer, like a local file or your browser, Claude reaches it through the Claude Desktop app on that computer. When you start a task in Cowork, Claude: You maintain visibility into what Claude is planning and doing throughout the process so you can steer when it matters, or let Claude run independently. Get started Requirements Start a Cowork session Chat and Cowork share one home. To start a session on any surface: What to expect during a task When Claude is working on a task in Cowork: Tasks can run for extended periods depending on complexity. You can monitor progress or step away and return when Claude finishes. Choose how Claude checks with you Cowork has three modes that control when Claude asks your permission before taking an action, like using your connectors. You can change the mode at any time from the mode selector in the chat box.
Connector tool permission: "Always allow"
Connector tool permission: "Needs approval"
Connector tool permission: "Blocked"
"Manual" mode Approved Asks for permission Denied "Auto" mode* Read-only tools are approved For write/delete tools, Claude decides Claude decides Denied "Skip" mode Approved Approved Denied *Currently available for Pro and Max plans only. As a reminder, you control which connectors Claude can use via the + menu in the chat box or the Customize > Connectors page. Manually approve (Manual), formerly "Ask before acting." Claude pauses and asks for approval for actions. You review each request and choose Allow or Deny. Automatically approve (Auto). Claude keeps working without stopping to ask about every step. Instead, Claude reviews each action for safety (such as checking for data exfiltration or prompt injection) and automatically blocks anything it determines to be unsafe. When an action is blocked, Claude looks for a safer way to finish the task or pauses and asks you directly. If Claude keeps running into blocks, it switches back to asking your permission for each step. We tested Claude's safety check extensively before releasing it, including working with outside security experts who tried to sneak dangerous actions past it. It gives you the speed of letting Claude work without interruptions, with a layer of protection that "Skip all approvals" doesn't have: every action still gets reviewed before it happens. Of course, no defense is perfect and no mode replaces your judgment. For work with real consequences—money, messages sent as you, important files—stay close and review what Claude does or consider switching back to "Manually approve." Auto mode applies to all of your existing connectors, plugins, Claude in Chrome, and some Cowork actions like fetching websites. Because Claude does this extra checking for you, auto mode consumes more of your usage limit than the other modes. Skip all approvals (Skip), formerly "Act without asking." Claude doesn't pause to ask and nothing checks its actions automatically. Only use this when you completely trust every action, connector, file, app, etc. involved in the task. Add global and folder instructions Global instructions You can give Claude standing instructions that apply to every Cowork session. Use this to specify your preferred tone, output format, or background on your role. To set global instructions: Folder instructions Folder instructions add project-specific context to Cowork when you select a local folder on desktop. Claude can also update these on its own during a session. Claude Cowork plugins Plugins customize how Claude works for your role, team, and company in Cowork. Each one bundles skills, connectors, and sub-agents into a single package. For details on finding, installing, and customizing plugins, see Use plugins in Cowork. Schedule recurring tasks You can set up tasks that Claude runs automatically or on demand. To schedule a task, type /schedule in any Cowork task. You can also click "Scheduled" in the left sidebar to view, create, and manage your scheduled tasks. Scheduled tasks run in the cloud, so they don't need your computer to be awake or the desktop app open. Usage limits Working on tasks with Cowork consumes more of your usage allocation than chatting with Claude. This is because complex, multi-step tasks are compute-intensive and require more tokens to execute. If you find yourself hitting usage limits frequently when using Cowork, consider: Permissions and security Cowork runs with layered protections: Permissions work the same as for chat. You control: Please carefully assess how much you trust an MCP or website before extending access beyond Claude's default settings. Example use cases Cowork is designed for complex, multi-step work that benefits from file access and extended execution time. Here are some examples: File and document management Research and analysis Document creation Data and analysis For more detailed examples, see our use cases and filter by the "Cowork" category. Current limitations Some Cowork capabilities are not yet available: We're iterating on Cowork based on feedback. If you encounter issues or have suggestions, use the feedback button in the app to share feedback with our team. Troubleshooting I'm seeing "Setting up Claude's workspace" when I start Cowork; what does this mean? This message is expected and indicates that Cowork is updating to the most recent version to apply any fixes and improvements. I don't see Cowork on web or mobile Cowork on web and mobile is rolling out gradually across paid plans. Make sure you're on an eligible plan and, on mobile, that you've updated to the latest version of the app. Claude stopped working on my task For local sessions, ensure the Claude Desktop app was open throughout the entire task. If the app was closed or your computer went to sleep, the session may have ended. Sessions in the cloud keep running in the background; open the session from any surface to check its progress. I'm hitting usage limits quickly Cowork consumes more usage than standard chat. Try using standard chat for simpler tasks and reserve Cowork for complex, multi-step work that benefits from file access. Files aren't appearing where expected Check that you've granted Claude the appropriate file access permissions. Review the output location Claude specified when completing the task.

For work with real consequences—money, messages sent as you, important files—stay close and review what Claude does or consider switching back to "Manually approve."

Auto mode applies to all of your existing connectors, plugins, Claude in Chrome, and some Cowork actions like fetching websites. Because Claude does this extra checking for you, auto mode consumes more of your usage limit than the other modes.

Skip all approvals (Skip), formerly "Act without asking." Claude doesn't pause to ask and nothing checks its actions automatically. Only use this when you completely trust every action, connector, file, app, etc. involved in the task.

Add global and folder instructions

Global instructions

You can give Claude standing instructions that apply to every Cowork session. Use this to specify your preferred tone, output format, or background on your role.

To set global instructions:

Folder instructions

Folder instructions add project-specific context to Cowork when you select a local folder on desktop. Claude can also update these on its own during a session.

Claude Cowork plugins

Plugins customize how Claude works for your role, team, and company in Cowork. Each one bundles skills, connectors, and sub-agents into a single package. For details on finding, installing, and customizing plugins, see Use plugins in Cowork.

Schedule recurring tasks

You can set up tasks that Claude runs automatically or on demand. To schedule a task, type /schedule in any Cowork task. You can also click "Scheduled" in the left sidebar to view, create, and manage your scheduled tasks.

Scheduled tasks run in the cloud, so they don't need your computer to be awake or the desktop app open.

Usage limits

Working on tasks with Cowork consumes more of your usage allocation than chatting with Claude. This is because complex, multi-step tasks are compute-intensive and require more tokens to execute.

If you find yourself hitting usage limits frequently when using Cowork, consider:

Permissions and security

Cowork runs with layered protections:

Permissions work the same as for chat. You control:

Please carefully assess how much you trust an MCP or website before extending access beyond Claude's default settings.

Example use cases

Cowork is designed for complex, multi-step work that benefits from file access and extended execution time. Here are some examples:

File and document management

Research and analysis

Document creation

Data and analysis

For more detailed examples, see our use cases and filter by the "Cowork" category.

Current limitations

Some Cowork capabilities are not yet available:

We're iterating on Cowork based on feedback. If you encounter issues or have suggestions, use the feedback button in the app to share feedback with our team.

Troubleshooting

I'm seeing "Setting up Claude's workspace" when I start Cowork; what does this mean?

This message is expected and indicates that Cowork is updating to the most recent version to apply any fixes and improvements.

I don't see Cowork on web or mobile

Cowork on web and mobile is rolling out gradually across paid plans. Make sure you're on an eligible plan and, on mobile, that you've updated to the latest version of the app.

Claude stopped working on my task

For local sessions, ensure the Claude Desktop app was open throughout the entire task. If the app was closed or your computer went to sleep, the session may have ended. Sessions in the cloud keep running in the background; open the session from any surface to check its progress.

I'm hitting usage limits quickly

Cowork consumes more usage than standard chat. Try using standard chat for simpler tasks and reserve Cowork for complex, multi-step work that benefits from file access.

Files aren't appearing where expected

Check that you've granted Claude the appropriate file access permissions. Review the output location Claude specified when completing the task.
