# Get started with Claude Cowork This article explains how to use **[Claude Cowork](https://claude.com/product/cowork)**, which brings Claude Code's agentic capabilities to knowledge work beyond coding. ## Availability Claude Cowork is available on paid plans (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise). Availability varies by surface: On desktop, web, and mobile, chat and Cowork share one home, so you start both from the same place. Find the message box and select "Cowork," then describe your task. To go back to a regular conversation, select "Chat." In the Chrome side panel, opening the panel starts a Cowork session directly. ## What is Claude Cowork? Claude Cowork uses the same agentic architecture that powers Claude Code, with no terminal required. Instead of responding to prompts one at a time, Claude can take on complex, multi-step tasks and execute them on your behalf. With Cowork, you can describe an outcome, step away, and come back to finished work—formatted documents, organized files, synthesized research, and more. Cowork runs your sessions remotely in the cloud (in beta), so your sessions and files live with your Claude account and follow you across desktop, web, and mobile. Chat and Cowork now share one home, so handing Claude a task starts from the same message box as a conversation. With scheduled tasks, Claude can complete work for you automatically. With projects, you can organize related tasks into persistent, self-contained workspaces with their own files, links, instructions, and memory. **Important:** ### Key capabilities ## How Claude Cowork runs your tasks Cowork runs your tasks in the cloud (in beta). Claude's work runs on Anthropic's servers, in an isolated environment, and your sessions and files are saved to your Claude account. Work continues if you close your laptop, and you can open the same session from any surface. When a task needs something on your computer, like a local file or your browser, Claude reaches it through the Claude Desktop app on that computer. When you start a task in Cowork, Claude: You maintain visibility into what Claude is planning and doing throughout the process so you can steer when it matters, or let Claude run independently. ## Get started ### Requirements ## Start a Cowork session Chat and Cowork share one home. To start a session on any surface: ## What to expect during a task When Claude is working on a task in Cowork: Tasks can run for extended periods depending on complexity. You can monitor progress or step away and return when Claude finishes. ## Choose how Claude checks with you Cowork has three modes that control when Claude asks your permission before taking an action, like using your connectors. You can change the mode at any time from the mode selector in the chat box. | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | **Connector tool permission: "Always allow"** | **Connector tool permission: "Needs approval"** | **Connector tool permission: "Blocked"** | | **"Manual" mode** | Approved | Asks for permission | Denied | | **"Auto" mode\*** | Read-only tools are approved

For write/delete tools, Claude decides | Claude decides | Denied | | **"Skip" mode** | Approved | Approved | Denied | _\*Currently available for Pro and Max plans only._ As a reminder, you control which connectors Claude can use via the + menu in the chat box or the **[Customize > Connectors](https://claude.ai/customize/connectors)** page. **Manually approve (Manual)**, formerly "Ask before acting." Claude pauses and asks for approval for actions. You review each request and choose Allow or Deny. **Automatically approve (Auto).** Claude keeps working without stopping to ask about every step. Instead, Claude reviews each action for safety (such as checking for data exfiltration or **[prompt injection](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely)**) and automatically blocks anything it determines to be unsafe. When an action is blocked, Claude looks for a safer way to finish the task or pauses and asks you directly. If Claude keeps running into blocks, it switches back to asking your permission for each step. We tested Claude's safety check extensively before releasing it, including working with outside security experts who tried to sneak dangerous actions past it. It gives you the speed of letting Claude work without interruptions, with a layer of protection that "Skip all approvals" doesn't have: every action still gets reviewed before it happens. _Of course, no defense is perfect and no mode replaces your judgment. For work with real consequences—money, messages sent as you, important files—stay close and review what Claude does or consider switching back to "Manually approve."_ Auto mode applies to all of your existing connectors, plugins, Claude in Chrome, and some Cowork actions like fetching websites. Because Claude does this extra checking for you, **auto mode consumes more of your usage limit than the other modes**. **Skip all approvals (Skip)**, formerly "Act without asking." Claude doesn't pause to ask and nothing checks its actions automatically. Only use this when you completely trust every action, connector, file, app, etc. involved in the task. ## Add global and folder instructions ### Global instructions You can give Claude standing instructions that apply to every Cowork session. Use this to specify your preferred tone, output format, or background on your role. To set global instructions: [![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/lupk8zyo/2525926874/15324ac4155d7802272e8bdef04b/ec66cd09-a4db-4f1d-8f30-226c9d126333?expires=1786665600&signature=16ed455a0e590449c2d2817dfb1e83f298f830a6441eafa1c092afc250ce4b50&req=diUlE8B8m4lYXfMW3nq%2BgcqgxG%2BD2rDableMqW%2FkK1eYnr%2Blc0pR3rVSoyHb%0AN%2FXPz54RAuJd3HuhB95zDcHO55A%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/lupk8zyo/2525926874/15324ac4155d7802272e8bdef04b/ec66cd09-a4db-4f1d-8f30-226c9d126333?expires=1786665600&signature=16ed455a0e590449c2d2817dfb1e83f298f830a6441eafa1c092afc250ce4b50&req=diUlE8B8m4lYXfMW3nq%2BgcqgxG%2BD2rDableMqW%2FkK1eYnr%2Blc0pR3rVSoyHb%0AN%2FXPz54RAuJd3HuhB95zDcHO55A%3D%0A) ### Folder instructions Folder instructions add project-specific context to Cowork when you select a local folder on desktop. Claude can also update these on its own during a session. ## Claude Cowork plugins Plugins customize how Claude works for your role, team, and company in Cowork. Each one bundles skills, connectors, and sub-agents into a single package. For details on finding, installing, and customizing plugins, see **[Use plugins in Cowork](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13837440-use-plugins-in-cowork)**. ## Schedule recurring tasks You can set up tasks that Claude runs automatically or on demand. To schedule a task, type `/schedule` in any Cowork task. You can also click "Scheduled" in the left sidebar to view, create, and manage your scheduled tasks. Scheduled tasks run in the cloud, so they don't need your computer to be awake or the desktop app open. ## Usage limits Working on tasks with Cowork consumes more of your usage allocation than chatting with Claude. This is because complex, multi-step tasks are compute-intensive and require more tokens to execute. If you find yourself hitting usage limits frequently when using Cowork, consider: ## Permissions and security Cowork runs with layered protections: Permissions work the same as for chat. You control: Please carefully assess how much you trust an MCP or website before extending access beyond Claude's default settings. ## Example use cases Cowork is designed for complex, multi-step work that benefits from file access and extended execution time. Here are some examples: ### File and document management ### Research and analysis ### Document creation ### Data and analysis For more detailed examples, see our **[use cases](https://claude.com/resources/use-cases)** and filter by the "Cowork" category. ## Current limitations Some Cowork capabilities are not yet available: We're iterating on Cowork based on feedback. If you encounter issues or have suggestions, use the feedback button in the app to share feedback with our team. ## Troubleshooting ### I'm seeing "Setting up Claude's workspace" when I start Cowork; what does this mean? item.text: NotebookLM is Now Gemini Notebook: What Changed? NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook. Google officially renamed the research tool on July 16, 2026. It is still the same standalone product, so you do not need to recreate your notebooks, move your sources, or open a new account. The new name is only part of the story. Google is also connecting notebooks with the Gemini app, adding deeper analysis through native code execution, and expanding where notebook context can appear across its ecosystem. At the same time, the dedicated Gemini Notebook experience still has important features that the Gemini-app version does not. Is NotebookLM now Gemini Notebook? Yes. Gemini Notebook is the new name for NotebookLM. Google says it remains a standalone research product focused on helping you work with sources. For supported users with a personal Google Account, notebooks can sync with Gemini, but Gemini Notebook and the notebook experience inside the Gemini app do not produce exactly the same answers or outputs. Work and school accounts are not currently supported in the Gemini Apps notebook integration. What you need to do: nothing to migrate. Keep using your existing notebooks. Use the standalone Gemini Notebook product when you want responses grounded only in your notebook sources or when you want Studio outputs such as Audio Overviews, Video Overviews, Infographics, and Slide Decks. NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook: What Changed at a Glance? Area What changed What it means for you Product name NotebookLM became Gemini Notebook on July 16, 2026. Expect new branding in Google, help pages, menus, and search results. Standalone product It remains a separate research product. You can continue using the dedicated Notebook experience for source-grounded chat and Studio outputs. Gemini integration For supported personal Google Accounts, notebooks appear in Gemini and changes sync between the two experiences. You can view, edit, and chat with a notebook from more than one Google surface. Work and school accounts are not currently supported in this integration. Gemini chat context You can add Gemini conversations to a notebook as context. An ongoing Gemini discussion can become part of the notebook’s knowledge base. Deeper analysis Google began adding a secure cloud computer that can write and run code. Eligible accounts can perform more complex analysis and create additional file types from notebook sources. Google Search Google announced plans to bring notebooks into AI Mode in Search. Treat this as an announced expansion, not a feature every account can assume is available. The most important distinction: some changes arrived alongside the rename, but Gemini Notebook is not simply NotebookLM with a different logo. Google is turning the standalone research product into a more connected part of the Gemini ecosystem while preserving its source-grounded role. 1. NotebookLM Has Officially Been Renamed Gemini Notebook Google announced the name change on July 16, 2026. Its official Gemini Notebook announcement says the product remains standalone but will work across more of Google’s ecosystem, including Gemini and Google Search. The name change brings NotebookLM under the Gemini brand, but it does not turn the product into an ordinary Gemini chat. Its defining job remains helping you organize, understand, question, and transform a focused collection of sources. Why keep “NotebookLM” in titles for now? People will continue using the familiar NotebookLM name while Google’s new branding spreads. Clear pages should connect both entities—“NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook”—instead of assuming every reader already knows the rename. 2. Is Gemini Notebook the Same as NotebookLM? Yes. Gemini Notebook is the renamed NotebookLM product. This is not a replacement service that requires a separate signup or a manual transfer. Google explicitly describes it as the same standalone product. The familiar core remains: Notebooks: each notebook remains a focused collection of sources for a project or topic. Source-grounded chat: you can ask questions and receive answers based on the sources selected in that notebook. Citations: answers can point back to supporting source passages so you can check important claims. Source discovery: you can upload your own material or find relevant sources and decide what to add. Studio outputs: the dedicated product can still turn sources into structured learning, research, and presentation formats. The interface, features, limits, and plan availability can continue to change after the rename. “Same product” means continuity of the product and your notebooks—not that every screen will look exactly as it did under the NotebookLM name. 3. Your Notebooks Now Sync With Gemini For supported users signed in with a personal Google Account, Gemini Notebook notebooks can now appear inside the Gemini app. Google’s cross-app Notebook documentation says these notebooks can be viewed, edited, and chatted with from either Gemini Notebook or Gemini. Google’s current Gemini Apps requirements say work and school accounts are not supported in this integration. What syncs between Gemini and Gemini Notebook? Creating or deleting a notebook Renaming a notebook or changing its emoji Adding, deleting, or editing notebook sources Adding instructions for how the notebook should respond Adding a Gemini conversation to a notebook Google’s Gemini Apps notebook guide describes notebooks as a persistent workspace that remembers sources, instructions, and ongoing discussions. That makes the integration useful when research begins as a Gemini conversation but needs a durable notebook around it. Important syncing and sharing exceptions Shared notebooks do not appear in Gemini: notebooks shared through Gemini Notebook remain available in the standalone product, even when you own them. Notebooks containing Gemini chats are private: Google says they cannot be shared. Gemini chat threads are read-only inside Gemini Notebook: manage or remove the original conversation in Gemini Apps. Custom instructions are shared: changing them in one experience changes how the notebook behaves in the other. Review privacy before adding Gemini chats Gemini Notebook content and Gemini Apps conversations can follow different activity and data-handling settings. Google’s documentation says Gemini Notebook files and chats are not used directly to train its foundational models unless you provide feedback, while Gemini-app chats follow Gemini Apps settings. Review both before adding sensitive context. 4. Gemini Notebook Can Run Code for Deeper Analysis A major product upgrade announced around the rename gives each eligible notebook a secure cloud computer. This lets Gemini Notebook write and execute code for more complex research and analysis. Google’s research upgrade announcement connects code execution with tasks such as analyzing inconsistent datasets, creating charts, building spreadsheets, and producing downloadable reports. Google also announced expanded output formats including documents, images, structured data, Excel files, and PowerPoint files. Its current Gemini Notebook chat documentation says these experimental agentic features are available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers on desktop. Code-execution question Current answer What does it do? Lets Gemini Notebook write and run code inside a secure cloud environment for analysis and output creation. What can it help create? Examples include calculations, charts, data visualizations, spreadsheets, documents, and presentation files. Who can use it now? Google’s current help documentation lists Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers on desktop. Is it still experimental? Yes. Google describes these functions as experimental and in early development, so review results and supervise consequential work. This does not mean you need to know how to code. The product can use code behind the scenes when a task benefits from calculation, transformation, or structured file creation. You still need to check the assumptions, formulas, source data, and final output before relying on the result. 5. Gemini and Gemini Notebook Do Not Work Exactly the Same Way The integration makes notebooks easier to access, but the place where you chat still matters. Gemini Notebook is the controlled, source-grounded research experience. Gemini Apps can use the notebook as context while also bringing in broader tools and information. Difference Gemini Notebook Notebook inside Gemini Apps Response grounding Responses are grounded exclusively in the notebook’s selected sources. Responses use notebook sources but may also use web search and other Gemini tools. Studio artifacts Can generate supported Studio outputs such as Audio Overviews, Video Overviews, Infographics, and Slide Decks. Does not generate Gemini Notebook Studio artifacts directly from the Gemini-app notebook interface. Best use Evidence-controlled research, source comparison, study material, briefings, and source-based outputs. Broader planning and ongoing conversations that may benefit from notebook context plus Gemini tools. Gemini conversations Can use opted-in Gemini chats as read-only notebook context. Creates and manages the original Gemini conversations added to the notebook. Choose Gemini Notebook when your answer must stay inside a defined source set or when you want a Studio output. Choose Gemini when you want the notebook to support a broader task that may also use the web or another Gemini tool. 6. What Happens to Existing NotebookLM Notebooks? Your existing NotebookLM notebooks remain your notebooks under the Gemini Notebook name. There is no separate migration process in Google’s rename announcement. For supported users with a personal Google Account, names, sources, instructions, and other changes can sync across the standalone product and Gemini Apps. Work and school accounts are not currently supported in the Gemini Apps notebook integration. You do not need to rebuild Keep your existing notebook structure, sources, notes, and workflows. The product name changed; your research does not restart. You do not need a new account Continue with the Google Account that already has access to your notebooks. Shared notebooks stay separate Continue opening shared notebooks in Gemini Notebook because Google says they do not appear in Gemini Apps. Review new sharing limits A notebook that includes Gemini chats becomes private and cannot be shared, so decide before adding conversation context. The official product link still uses notebooklm.google.com. That makes the old brand visible in the web address even though Google now calls the product Gemini Notebook. 7. Is Gemini Notebook Available in Google Search and AI Mode? Google’s July 16 announcement said it would bring notebooks into AI Mode in Search. The announcement described that expansion as upcoming, so it should not be treated as universally available to every account, region, or device. The safe distinction is: Gemini integration is documented as available for supported Gemini and Gemini Notebook users. AI Mode in Search was announced as a next step. Check your own Google interface and current help documentation before describing it as live for everyone. This distinction matters because Google product announcements often describe a rollout direction before every user receives the feature. For business documentation or client training, record the date you checked and avoid promising access based only on the announcement. Do You Need to Change Anything? You do not need to migrate your notebooks. The useful changes are mostly about language, workflow choice, and permissions. What to update Use both names during the transition: write “Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM)” when readers may know only the old name. Choose the right interface: use Gemini Notebook for strict source grounding and Studio outputs; use Gemini when you want notebook context plus broader tools. Check sharing before adding chats: notebooks containing Gemini chats cannot be shared. Check code-execution access: plan eligibility and rollout can vary by account. Update internal guides: revise screenshots, training documents, bookmarks, and team language without changing the underlying notebook workflow. What not to change Do not recreate notebooks simply because the product name changed. Do not move or re-upload sources unless a source itself needs updating. Do not assume Gemini and Gemini Notebook will return identical answers. Do not assume every announced feature is already enabled for your account. How to Get Started With Gemini Notebook If you already used NotebookLM, open one existing notebook and check how it appears in Gemini Notebook and Gemini. Confirm the sources, instructions, sharing settings, and available Studio outputs before changing your normal workflow. If you are new, use the free NotebookLM setup guide, now updated for Gemini Notebook. It owns the complete beginner walkthrough: creating a notebook, adding sources, asking source-grounded questions, generating a first output, and testing an Audio Overview. For a structured learning path beyond the first notebook, explore the Gemini Notebook Academy. If you prefer a short reference, download the free Notebook guide. NotebookLM and Gemini Notebook FAQs Is NotebookLM now called Gemini Notebook? Yes. Google officially renamed NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook on July 16, 2026. It remains the same standalone research product. Is Gemini Notebook the same as NotebookLM? Yes. Gemini Notebook is the new name for NotebookLM. Your existing notebooks and core source-grounded workflow continue under the new branding. What happened to my existing NotebookLM notebooks? They remain available as Gemini Notebook notebooks. You do not need to recreate them. Supported notebooks can also sync with the Gemini app, although shared notebooks remain available only in the standalone Gemini Notebook experience. Do I need a new account for Gemini Notebook? No. Continue using the Google Account that already has access to NotebookLM. Account type, administrator settings, region, age, plan, and feature rollout can still affect availability. Does the NotebookLM website still work? Yes. Google’s official product link still uses notebooklm.google.com even though the product is now called Gemini Notebook. What is the difference between Gemini and Gemini Notebook? Gemini Notebook answers exclusively from notebook sources. A notebook inside Gemini Apps can use those sources plus web search and other Gemini tools. Studio outputs such as Audio Overviews and Slide Decks are generated in the standalone Gemini Notebook product. Does Gemini Notebook still have Audio Overviews? Yes. Audio Overviews remain part of the Gemini Notebook Studio experience. Google says the Gemini-app notebook interface does not directly generate Studio artifacts. Can Gemini Notebook run code? Yes. Google’s current help documentation says Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can use Gemini Notebook’s experimental agentic capabilities on desktop, including running code, searching the web, and creating downloadable files. Check your account because availability and limits can still change. Can I use my Gemini Notebook inside Gemini? Yes, if you are a supported user signed in with a personal Google Account. You can view, edit, and chat with notebooks in Gemini Apps, and changes can sync with Gemini Notebook. Work and school accounts are not currently supported in this integration, and shared notebooks created in Gemini Notebook do not appear in Gemini. Do I need to change my NotebookLM workflow? No major rebuild is required. Keep your existing notebooks and sources. Choose Gemini Notebook for strict source grounding and Studio outputs, and use Gemini when you want notebook context combined with broader Gemini tools. Official Gemini Notebook Sources Google: NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook Google Help: Notebooks in Gemini Apps Google Help: Use chat and agentic capabilities in Gemini Notebook Google Help: Create and use notebooks in Gemini Apps Google: Gemini Notebook research and code-execution upgrades Google Help: Privacy and Terms of Use in Gemini Notebook Last checked August 12, 2026. Gemini Notebook features, plan access, syncing, sharing behavior, and integrations can change. The new name is only part of the story. Google is also connecting notebooks with the Gemini app, adding deeper analysis through native code execution, and expanding where notebook context can appear across its ecosystem. At the same time, the dedicated Gemini Notebook experience still has important features that the Gemini-app version does not.

Quick answer

Is NotebookLM now Gemini Notebook?

Yes. Gemini Notebook is the new name for NotebookLM. Google says it remains a standalone research product focused on helping you work with sources. For supported users with a personal Google Account, notebooks can sync with Gemini, but Gemini Notebook and the notebook experience inside the Gemini app do not produce exactly the same answers or outputs. Work and school accounts are not currently supported in the Gemini Apps notebook integration.

What you need to do: nothing to migrate. Keep using your existing notebooks. Use the standalone Gemini Notebook product when you want responses grounded only in your notebook sources or when you want Studio outputs such as Audio Overviews, Video Overviews, Infographics, and Slide Decks.

NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook: What Changed at a Glance?

Area What changed What it means for you
Product name NotebookLM became Gemini Notebook on July 16, 2026. Expect new branding in Google, help pages, menus, and search results.
Standalone product It remains a separate research product. You can continue using the dedicated Notebook experience for source-grounded chat and Studio outputs.
Gemini integration For supported personal Google Accounts, notebooks appear in Gemini and changes sync between the two experiences. You can view, edit, and chat with a notebook from more than one Google surface. Work and school accounts are not currently supported in this integration.
Gemini chat context You can add Gemini conversations to a notebook as context. An ongoing Gemini discussion can become part of the notebook’s knowledge base.
Deeper analysis Google began adding a secure cloud computer that can write and run code. Eligible accounts can perform more complex analysis and create additional file types from notebook sources.
Google Search Google announced plans to bring notebooks into AI Mode in Search. Treat this as an announced expansion, not a feature every account can assume is available.

The most important distinction: some changes arrived alongside the rename, but Gemini Notebook is not simply NotebookLM with a different logo. Google is turning the standalone research product into a more connected part of the Gemini ecosystem while preserving its source-grounded role.

1. NotebookLM Has Officially Been Renamed Gemini Notebook

Google announced the name change on July 16, 2026. Its official Gemini Notebook announcement says the product remains standalone but will work across more of Google’s ecosystem, including Gemini and Google Search.

The name change brings NotebookLM under the Gemini brand, but it does not turn the product into an ordinary Gemini chat. Its defining job remains helping you organize, understand, question, and transform a focused collection of sources.

Why keep “NotebookLM” in titles for now?

People will continue using the familiar NotebookLM name while Google’s new branding spreads. Clear pages should connect both entities—“NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook”—instead of assuming every reader already knows the rename.

2. Is Gemini Notebook the Same as NotebookLM?

Yes. Gemini Notebook is the renamed NotebookLM product. This is not a replacement service that requires a separate signup or a manual transfer. Google explicitly describes it as the same standalone product.

The familiar core remains:

  • Notebooks: each notebook remains a focused collection of sources for a project or topic.
  • Source-grounded chat: you can ask questions and receive answers based on the sources selected in that notebook.
  • Citations: answers can point back to supporting source passages so you can check important claims.
  • Source discovery: you can upload your own material or find relevant sources and decide what to add.
  • Studio outputs: the dedicated product can still turn sources into structured learning, research, and presentation formats.

The interface, features, limits, and plan availability can continue to change after the rename. “Same product” means continuity of the product and your notebooks—not that every screen will look exactly as it did under the NotebookLM name.

3. Your Notebooks Now Sync With Gemini

For supported users signed in with a personal Google Account, Gemini Notebook notebooks can now appear inside the Gemini app. Google’s cross-app Notebook documentation says these notebooks can be viewed, edited, and chatted with from either Gemini Notebook or Gemini. Google’s current Gemini Apps requirements say work and school accounts are not supported in this integration.

What syncs between Gemini and Gemini Notebook?

  • Creating or deleting a notebook
  • Renaming a notebook or changing its emoji

  • Custom instructions are shared: changing them in one experience changes how the notebook behaves in the other.

Review privacy before adding Gemini chats

Gemini Notebook content and Gemini Apps conversations can follow different activity and data-handling settings. Google’s documentation says Gemini Notebook files and chats are not used directly to train its foundational models unless you provide feedback, while Gemini-app chats follow Gemini Apps settings. Review both before adding sensitive context.

4. Gemini Notebook Can Run Code for Deeper Analysis

A major product upgrade announced around the rename gives each eligible notebook a secure cloud computer. This lets Gemini Notebook write and execute code for more complex research and analysis.

Google’s research upgrade announcement connects code execution with tasks such as analyzing inconsistent datasets, creating charts, building spreadsheets, and producing downloadable reports. Google also announced expanded output formats including documents, images, structured data, Excel files, and PowerPoint files. Its current Gemini Notebook chat documentation says these experimental agentic features are available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers on desktop.

Code-execution question Current answer
What does it do? Lets Gemini Notebook write and run code inside a secure cloud environment for analysis and output creation.
What can it help create? Examples include calculations, charts, data visualizations, spreadsheets, documents, and presentation files.

Is it still experimental? Yes. Google describes these functions as experimental and in early development, so review results and supervise consequential work.

This does not mean you need to know how to code. The product can use code behind the scenes when a task benefits from calculation, transformation, or structured file creation. You still need to check the assumptions, formulas, source data, and final output before relying on the result.

5. Gemini and Gemini Notebook Do Not Work Exactly the Same Way

The integration makes notebooks easier to access, but the place where you chat still matters. Gemini Notebook is the controlled, source-grounded research experience. Gemini Apps can use the notebook as context while also bringing in broader tools and information.

Difference Gemini Notebook Notebook inside Gemini Apps

You do not need to rebuild

You do not need a new account

Review new sharing limits

The official product link still uses notebooklm.google.com. That makes the old brand visible in the web address even though Google now calls the product Gemini Notebook.

7. Is Gemini Notebook Available in Google Search and AI Mode?

Google’s July 16 announcement said it would bring notebooks into AI Mode in Search. The announcement described that expansion as upcoming, so it should not be treated as universally available to every account, region, or device.

The safe distinction is:

  • Gemini integration is documented as available for supported Gemini and Gemini Notebook users.
  • AI Mode in Search was announced as a next step. Check your own Google interface and current help documentation before describing it as live for everyone.

This distinction matters because Google product announcements often describe a rollout direction before every user receives the feature. For business documentation or client training, record the date you checked and avoid promising access based only on the announcement.

Do You Need to Change Anything?

You do not need to migrate your notebooks. The useful changes are mostly about language, workflow choice, and permissions.

  • Check code-execution access: plan eligibility and rollout can vary by account.
  • Update internal guides: revise screenshots, training documents, bookmarks, and team language without changing the underlying notebook workflow.

  • Do not move or re-upload sources unless a source itself needs updating.
  • Do not assume Gemini and Gemini Notebook will return identical answers.
  • Do not assume every announced feature is already enabled for your account.

How to Get Started With Gemini Notebook

If you already used NotebookLM, open one existing notebook and check how it appears in Gemini Notebook and Gemini. Confirm the sources, instructions, sharing settings, and available Studio outputs before changing your normal workflow.

If you are new, use the free NotebookLM setup guide, now updated for Gemini Notebook. It owns the complete beginner walkthrough: creating a notebook, adding sources, asking source-grounded questions, generating a first output, and testing an Audio Overview.

For a structured learning path beyond the first notebook, explore the Gemini Notebook Academy. If you prefer a short reference, download the free Notebook guide.

NotebookLM and Gemini Notebook FAQs

Does the NotebookLM website still work?

Yes. Google’s official product link still uses notebooklm.google.com even though the product is now called Gemini Notebook.

What is the difference between Gemini and Gemini Notebook?

Gemini Notebook answers exclusively from notebook sources. A notebook inside Gemini Apps can use those sources plus web search and other Gemini tools. Studio outputs such as Audio Overviews and Slide Decks are generated in the standalone Gemini Notebook product.

Does Gemini Notebook still have Audio Overviews?

Yes. Audio Overviews remain part of the Gemini Notebook Studio experience. Google says the Gemini-app notebook interface does not directly generate Studio artifacts.

Can Gemini Notebook run code?

Yes. Google’s current help documentation says Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can use Gemini Notebook’s experimental agentic capabilities on desktop, including running code, searching the web, and creating downloadable files. Check your account because availability and limits can still change.

Can I use my Gemini Notebook inside Gemini?

Yes, if you are a supported user signed in with a personal Google Account. You can view, edit, and chat with notebooks in Gemini Apps, and changes can sync with Gemini Notebook. Work and school accounts are not currently supported in this integration, and shared notebooks created in Gemini Notebook do not appear in Gemini.

Do I need to change my NotebookLM workflow?

No major rebuild is required. Keep your existing notebooks and sources. Choose Gemini Notebook for strict source grounding and Studio outputs, and use Gemini when you want notebook context combined with broader Gemini tools.

item.markdown:
# NotebookLM is Now Gemini Notebook: What Changed?
**NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook.** Google officially renamed the research tool on **July 16, 2026**. It is still the same standalone product, so you do not need to recreate your notebooks, move your sources, or open a new account.
The new name is only part of the story. Google is also connecting notebooks with the Gemini app, adding deeper analysis through native code execution, and expanding where notebook context can appear across its ecosystem. At the same time, the dedicated Gemini Notebook experience still has important features that the Gemini-app version does not.
Quick answer
## Is NotebookLM now Gemini Notebook?
**Yes.** Gemini Notebook is the new name for NotebookLM. Google says it remains a standalone research product focused on helping you work with sources. For supported users with a personal Google Account, notebooks can sync with Gemini, but Gemini Notebook and the notebook experience inside the Gemini app do not produce exactly the same answers or outputs. Work and school accounts are not currently supported in the Gemini Apps notebook integration.
**What you need to do:** nothing to migrate. Keep using your existing notebooks. Use the standalone Gemini Notebook product when you want responses grounded only in your notebook sources or when you want Studio outputs such as Audio Overviews, Video Overviews, Infographics, and Slide Decks.
## NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook: What Changed at a Glance?
| Area | What changed | What it means for you | | --- | --- | --- | | Product name | NotebookLM became Gemini Notebook on July 16, 2026. | Expect new branding in Google, help pages, menus, and search results. | | Standalone product | It remains a separate research product. | You can continue using the dedicated Notebook experience for source-grounded chat and Studio outputs. | | Gemini integration | For supported personal Google Accounts, notebooks appear in Gemini and changes sync between the two experiences. | You can view, edit, and chat with a notebook from more than one Google surface. Work and school accounts are not currently supported in this integration. | | Gemini chat context | You can add Gemini conversations to a notebook as context. | An ongoing Gemini discussion can become part of the notebook’s knowledge base. | | Deeper analysis | Google began adding a secure cloud computer that can write and run code. | Eligible accounts can perform more complex analysis and create additional file types from notebook sources. | | Google Search | Google announced plans to bring notebooks into AI Mode in Search. | Treat this as an announced expansion, not a feature every account can assume is available. |
**The most important distinction:** some changes arrived alongside the rename, but Gemini Notebook is not simply NotebookLM with a different logo. Google is turning the standalone research product into a more connected part of the Gemini ecosystem while preserving its source-grounded role.
## 1\. NotebookLM Has Officially Been Renamed Gemini Notebook
Google announced the name change on July 16, 2026. Its [official Gemini Notebook announcement](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/gemini-notebook/notebooklm-gemini-notebook/) says the product remains standalone but will work across more of Google’s ecosystem, including Gemini and Google Search.
The name change brings NotebookLM under the Gemini brand, but it does not turn the product into an ordinary Gemini chat. Its defining job remains helping you organize, understand, question, and transform a focused collection of sources.
**Why keep “NotebookLM” in titles for now?**
People will continue using the familiar NotebookLM name while Google’s new branding spreads. Clear pages should connect both entities—“NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook”—instead of assuming every reader already knows the rename.
## 2\. Is Gemini Notebook the Same as NotebookLM?
**Yes. Gemini Notebook is the renamed NotebookLM product.** This is not a replacement service that requires a separate signup or a manual transfer. Google explicitly describes it as the same standalone product.
The familiar core remains:
* **Notebooks:** each notebook remains a focused collection of sources for a project or topic. * **Source-grounded chat:** you can ask questions and receive answers based on the sources selected in that notebook. * **Citations:** answers can point back to supporting source passages so you can check important claims. * **Source discovery:** you can upload your own material or find relevant sources and decide what to add. * **Studio outputs:** the dedicated product can still turn sources into structured learning, research, and presentation formats.
The interface, features, limits, and plan availability can continue to change after the rename. “Same product” means continuity of the product and your notebooks—not that every screen will look exactly as it did under the NotebookLM name.
## 3\. Your Notebooks Now Sync With Gemini
For supported users signed in with a personal Google Account, Gemini Notebook notebooks can now appear inside the Gemini app. Google’s [cross-app Notebook documentation](https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/17003757) says these notebooks can be viewed, edited, and chatted with from either Gemini Notebook or Gemini. Google’s current Gemini Apps requirements say work and school accounts are not supported in this integration.
### What syncs between Gemini and Gemini Notebook?
* Creating or deleting a notebook * Renaming a notebook or changing its emoji * Adding, deleting, or editing notebook sources * Adding instructions for how the notebook should respond * Adding a Gemini conversation to a notebook
Google’s [Gemini Apps notebook guide](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16972047) describes notebooks as a persistent workspace that remembers sources, instructions, and ongoing discussions. That makes the integration useful when research begins as a Gemini conversation but needs a durable notebook around it.
### Important syncing and sharing exceptions
* **Shared notebooks do not appear in Gemini:** notebooks shared through Gemini Notebook remain available in the standalone product, even when you own them. * **Notebooks containing Gemini chats are private:** Google says they cannot be shared. * **Gemini chat threads are read-only inside Gemini Notebook:** manage or remove the original conversation in Gemini Apps. * **Custom instructions are shared:** changing them in one experience changes how the notebook behaves in the other.
**Review privacy before adding Gemini chats**
Gemini Notebook content and Gemini Apps conversations can follow different activity and data-handling settings. Google’s documentation says Gemini Notebook files and chats are not used directly to train its foundational models unless you provide feedback, while Gemini-app chats follow Gemini Apps settings. Review both before adding sensitive context.
## 4\. Gemini Notebook Can Run Code for Deeper Analysis
A major product upgrade announced around the rename gives each eligible notebook a secure cloud computer. This lets Gemini Notebook write and execute code for more complex research and analysis.
Google’s [research upgrade announcement](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/notebooklm/better-research-notebooklm/) connects code execution with tasks such as analyzing inconsistent datasets, creating charts, building spreadsheets, and producing downloadable reports. Google also announced expanded output formats including documents, images, structured data, Excel files, and PowerPoint files. Its [current Gemini Notebook chat documentation](https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16179559) says these experimental agentic features are available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers on desktop.
| Code-execution question | Current answer | | --- | --- | | What does it do? | Lets Gemini Notebook write and run code inside a secure cloud environment for analysis and output creation. | | What can it help create? | Examples include calculations, charts, data visualizations, spreadsheets, documents, and presentation files. | | Who can use it now? | Google’s current help documentation lists Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers on desktop. | | Is it still experimental? | Yes. Google describes these functions as experimental and in early development, so review results and supervise consequential work. |
**This does not mean you need to know how to code.** The product can use code behind the scenes when a task benefits from calculation, transformation, or structured file creation. You still need to check the assumptions, formulas, source data, and final output before relying on the result.
## 5\. Gemini and Gemini Notebook Do Not Work Exactly the Same Way
The integration makes notebooks easier to access, but the place where you chat still matters. **Gemini Notebook is the controlled, source-grounded research experience. Gemini Apps can use the notebook as context while also bringing in broader tools and information.**
| Difference | Gemini Notebook | Notebook inside Gemini Apps | | --- | --- | --- | | Response grounding | Responses are grounded exclusively in the notebook’s selected sources. | Responses use notebook sources but may also use web search and other Gemini tools. | | Studio artifacts | Can generate supported Studio outputs such as Audio Overviews, Video Overviews, Infographics, and Slide Decks. | Does not generate Gemini Notebook Studio artifacts directly from the Gemini-app notebook interface. | | Best use | Evidence-controlled research, source comparison, study material, briefings, and source-based outputs. | Broader planning and ongoing conversations that may benefit from notebook context plus Gemini tools. | | Gemini conversations | Can use opted-in Gemini chats as read-only notebook context. | Creates and manages the original Gemini conversations added to the notebook. |
**Choose Gemini Notebook** when your answer must stay inside a defined source set or when you want a Studio output. **Choose Gemini** when you want the notebook to support a broader task that may also use the web or another Gemini tool.
## 6\. What Happens to Existing NotebookLM Notebooks?
**Your existing NotebookLM notebooks remain your notebooks under the Gemini Notebook name.** There is no separate migration process in Google’s rename announcement. For supported users with a personal Google Account, names, sources, instructions, and other changes can sync across the standalone product and Gemini Apps. Work and school accounts are not currently supported in the Gemini Apps notebook integration.
**You do not need to rebuild**
Keep your existing notebook structure, sources, notes, and workflows. The product name changed; your research does not restart.
**You do not need a new account**
Continue with the Google Account that already has access to your notebooks.
**Shared notebooks stay separate**
Continue opening shared notebooks in Gemini Notebook because Google says they do not appear in Gemini Apps.
**Review new sharing limits**
A notebook that includes Gemini chats becomes private and cannot be shared, so decide before adding conversation context.
The official product link still uses [notebooklm.google.com](https://notebooklm.google.com/). That makes the old brand visible in the web address even though Google now calls the product Gemini Notebook.
## 7\. Is Gemini Notebook Available in Google Search and AI Mode?
Google’s July 16 announcement said it would bring notebooks into AI Mode in Search. The announcement described that expansion as upcoming, so it should not be treated as universally available to every account, region, or device.
The safe distinction is:
* **Gemini integration is documented as available** for supported Gemini and Gemini Notebook users. * **AI Mode in Search was announced as a next step.** Check your own Google interface and current help documentation before describing it as live for everyone.
This distinction matters because Google product announcements often describe a rollout direction before every user receives the feature. For business documentation or client training, record the date you checked and avoid promising access based only on the announcement.
## Do You Need to Change Anything?
**You do not need to migrate your notebooks.** The useful changes are mostly about language, workflow choice, and permissions.
### What to update
* **Use both names during the transition:** write “Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM)” when readers may know only the old name. * **Choose the right interface:** use Gemini Notebook for strict source grounding and Studio outputs; use Gemini when you want notebook context plus broader tools. * **Check sharing before adding chats:** notebooks containing Gemini chats cannot be shared. * **Check code-execution access:** plan eligibility and rollout can vary by account. * **Update internal guides:** revise screenshots, training documents, bookmarks, and team language without changing the underlying notebook workflow.
### What not to change
* Do not recreate notebooks simply because the product name changed. * Do not move or re-upload sources unless a source itself needs updating. * Do not assume Gemini and Gemini Notebook will return identical answers. * Do not assume every announced feature is already enabled for your account.
## How to Get Started With Gemini Notebook
If you already used NotebookLM, open one existing notebook and check how it appears in Gemini Notebook and Gemini. Confirm the sources, instructions, sharing settings, and available Studio outputs before changing your normal workflow.
If you are new, use the [free NotebookLM setup guide, now updated for Gemini Notebook](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/setup-guides/notebooklm/). It owns the complete beginner walkthrough: creating a notebook, adding sources, asking source-grounded questions, generating a first output, and testing an Audio Overview.
For a structured learning path beyond the first notebook, explore the [Gemini Notebook Academy](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/academy/gemini-notebook/). If you prefer a short reference, download the [free Notebook guide](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/freebies/notebook-starter-guide/).
## NotebookLM and Gemini Notebook FAQs
Is NotebookLM now called Gemini Notebook?
Yes. Google officially renamed NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook on July 16, 2026. It remains the same standalone research product.
Is Gemini Notebook the same as NotebookLM?
Yes. Gemini Notebook is the new name for NotebookLM. Your existing notebooks and core source-grounded workflow continue under the new branding.
What happened to my existing NotebookLM notebooks?
They remain available as Gemini Notebook notebooks. You do not need to recreate them. Supported notebooks can also sync with the Gemini app, although shared notebooks remain available only in the standalone Gemini Notebook experience.
Do I need a new account for Gemini Notebook?
No. Continue using the Google Account that already has access to NotebookLM. Account type, administrator settings, region, age, plan, and feature rollout can still affect availability.
Does the NotebookLM website still work?
Yes. Google’s official product link still uses notebooklm.google.com even though the product is now called Gemini Notebook.
What is the difference between Gemini and Gemini Notebook?
Gemini Notebook answers exclusively from notebook sources. A notebook inside Gemini Apps can use those sources plus web search and other Gemini tools. Studio outputs such as Audio Overviews and Slide Decks are generated in the standalone Gemini Notebook product.
Does Gemini Notebook still have Audio Overviews?
Yes. Audio Overviews remain part of the Gemini Notebook Studio experience. Google says the Gemini-app notebook interface does not directly generate Studio artifacts.
Can Gemini Notebook run code?
Yes. Google’s current help documentation says Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can use Gemini Notebook’s experimental agentic capabilities on desktop, including running code, searching the web, and creating downloadable files. Check your account because availability and limits can still change.
Can I use my Gemini Notebook inside Gemini?
Yes, if you are a supported user signed in with a personal Google Account. You can view, edit, and chat with notebooks in Gemini Apps, and changes can sync with Gemini Notebook. Work and school accounts are not currently supported in this integration, and shared notebooks created in Gemini Notebook do not appear in Gemini.
Do I need to change my NotebookLM workflow?
No major rebuild is required. Keep your existing notebooks and sources. Choose Gemini Notebook for strict source grounding and Studio outputs, and use Gemini when you want notebook context combined with broader Gemini tools.
## Official Gemini Notebook Sources
* [Google: NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/gemini-notebook/notebooklm-gemini-notebook/) * [Google Help: Notebooks in Gemini Apps](https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/17003757) * [Google Help: Use chat and agentic capabilities in Gemini Notebook](https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16179559) * [Google Help: Create and use notebooks in Gemini Apps](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16972047) * [Google: Gemini Notebook research and code-execution upgrades](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/notebooklm/better-research-notebooklm/) * [Google Help: Privacy and Terms of Use in Gemini Notebook](https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/17004255)

What is an AI skill?

An AI skill is a reusable, step-by-step workflow that helps an AI tool complete a specific task consistently. Instead of starting with a blank chat, you receive the instructions, process, and output structure needed to do the job.

Do I need to download a file to use a skill?

Click the download button once, allow downloads or popups if your browser blocks them, and check your browser's Downloads folder. item.text: Free AI Setup Guides — Claude, Spark, NotebookLM (2026) What’s the difference between a setup guide and All Access? Setup guides are free, quick-start walkthroughs to get one tool running. The All Access Pass is the paid membership — deeper step-by-step training, every workflow, the community, and 7 days of hands-on setup help. Are the setup guides really free? Yes — the starter setup guides for Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark and NotebookLM are free to read. Members unlock the full library plus the hands-on setup help. How does the free 7-day setup help work? item.text: What Are AI Agents? How They Work, Types & Examples AI Agents FAQ Quick, straight answers to the questions beginners ask most about AI agents. What is an AI agent? An AI agent is an AI system that can take a goal, make a plan, use tools, and complete multi-step work on its own with limited human input. Unlike a chatbot that only answers the message in front of it, an agent works toward an outcome and keeps going until the task is done. What are AI agents used for? Common uses include research and summarizing, drafting and repurposing content, planning and prioritizing, follow-ups and outreach, and any repeatable workflow you'd rather not do by hand. For beginners, the most useful agents run one clear task well — like a weekly business brief or an AI news research agent. What's the difference between an AI agent and an AI agent skill? A skill is one reusable workflow for a specific task — a building block. An AI agent is the larger system that can plan, use tools, take multiple steps, and combine one or more skills to reach a goal. Most people start with a single skill, then grow toward a fuller agent. See What Is an AI Agent Skill? for the full breakdown, or browse ready-to-use AI skills. What is an AI agent library? An AI agent library is an organized collection of reusable resources for building or using AI agents — developer frameworks, prebuilt agent platforms, or ready-to-use AI skills and workflows. AI Agents Library is a ready-to-use, no-code AI skills and workflow library — the third kind. See What Is an AI Agent Library? for the full breakdown. Are AI agents free? Yes — you can start free. Our AI agent examples and skills are free to open and try, and the Free AI Agent Generator builds a workflow idea for you at no cost. You only need access to an AI tool, most of which offer a free tier. Academy membership (with hands-on setup help) starts with 7 days free. Do I need to know how to code to use AI agents? No. Everything here is designed for no-code beginners, business owners, and creators. You describe the task in plain language and copy a ready-made workflow into your AI tool — no programming, APIs, or setup skills required. What are the main types of AI agents? The practical types are reflex agents (trigger → response), goal-based agents (plan steps toward an outcome), task and workflow agents (run one repeatable job), research and assistant agents (gather and summarize), multi-agent systems (several agents dividing work), and autonomous or scheduled agents (run on their own). Beginners usually start with a task and workflow agent. How are AI agents different from chatbots? A chatbot primarily responds to messages in a conversation. An AI agent works toward a goal by planning, using tools, taking multiple steps, and checking its progress. Some AI agents include a chat interface, but many run through workflows, connected tools, or scheduled actions. A chatbot is not automatically an AI agent. How do I build my own AI agent as a beginner? Start small. Pick your AI tool, copy one reusable skill for a task you actually have, then customize it with your details. Once that works reliably, add more skills to handle bigger, multi-step goals. Browse the skills library to grab your first one, or generate an idea with the Free AI Agent Generator.

mainEntity.name: What is Claude Cowork?

acceptedAnswer.text: Claude Cowork is a task-focused mode in the Claude Desktop app that lets Claude complete multi-step work on your computer. It can work with folders you choose to share, use plugins and connectors, run scheduled tasks, and create or update files on your Mac or Windows computer. Claude Cowork Academy is the beginner-friendly Claude Cowork course that walks you through all of it.

mainEntity.name: Is Claude Cowork free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Claude Cowork itself requires an Anthropic Claude plan to use; pricing and availability are set by Anthropic and can change. Claude Cowork Academy is included with the AI Agents Library All Access Pass — free for 7 days, then $14/month.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to code to use Claude Cowork?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Claude Cowork is designed for non-developers. You describe tasks in plain English, install ready-made skills and plugins from a library, and connect apps with one-click MCP connectors. Every lesson in Claude Cowork Academy assumes zero coding experience.

mainEntity.name: Is Claude Cowork the same as Claude Desktop?

acceptedAnswer.text: Claude Desktop is the application installed on your Mac or Windows computer. Cowork is the task-focused mode inside Claude Desktop that lets Claude work with selected folders, plugins, connectors and scheduled workflows.

mainEntity.name: Can Claude Cowork run scheduled tasks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can create recurring Claude Cowork tasks that run daily, weekly or on another schedule. Scheduled tasks only run while your computer is awake and the Claude Desktop app is open, so the Academy also shows you how to configure and test them reliably.

mainEntity.name: What will I learn and build in my first 7 days?

acceptedAnswer.text: During your first seven days, you'll install Claude Desktop, connect a safe working folder, understand skills, plugins and connectors, customize a reusable skill, build and test a cross-app workflow, and turn the finished workflow into a scheduled task. See the complete seven-day curriculum above.

mainEntity.name: Does membership include the other Academy training paths?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. One All Access Pass includes all five AI Agents Academy training paths — Claude Cowork, ChatGPT, Gemini Spark, Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM) and AI Skills Fundamentals — plus the shared AI skills library and resources.

mainEntity.name: How does the free seven-day trial work?

acceptedAnswer.text: You get full Claude Cowork Academy access for seven days and can cancel anytime before the trial ends without being charged.

mainEntity.name: How is Claude Cowork Academy different from Anthropic’s official documentation and learning resources?

acceptedAnswer.text: Anthropic provides the official Claude documentation, support articles and introductory learning resources. Claude Cowork Academy is independent, implementation-focused training that adds structured beginner lessons, the complete downloadable AI skill files, workflow templates, setup assistance, community support and practical examples you can customize for your own work.

mainEntity.name: Do I get a certificate when I finish the Claude Cowork path?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You receive an official AI Agents Library certificate of completion when you finish the Claude Cowork path. Every training path issues its own — ChatGPT, Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark, Gemini Notebook and AI Skills Fundamentals each award their own — so completing more than one leaves you with a certificate for each. Certificates are included with All Access at no extra cost. It certifies the training you completed with AI Agents Library and is not a vendor certification from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google.

mainEntity.name: How does Claude Cowork Academy compare to other Claude Cowork courses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Claude Cowork Academy is applied, beginner-first training that ends in a working scheduled workflow rather than a set of videos. We compare it openly against every alternative — including Anthropic's own free course, Academind, Age of Product, Udemy and live instructor-led training — in our independent guide to the best Claude Cowork courses, judged on the same criteria as every other option.

Three beginner recommendations Reach out, reply well, or keep the record clean These three cover the first message, the inbound message, and what the business must remember afterward. item.text: Gemini Notebook Training for Beginners (2026) Common Questions About the Gemini Notebook Path Why is it called Gemini Notebook now instead of NotebookLM? Google rebranded NotebookLM as Gemini Notebook to align it with the broader Gemini product ecosystem. It's the same tool with the same features — new name, same document-grounded research and content workflows. All existing NotebookLM notebooks and Audio Overviews continue to work. If you see "Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM)" in our copy during the transition, it's just there to help returning readers recognize the product. Is this Gemini Notebook training for beginners? Yes — the Gemini Notebook training path in AI Agents Academy is built for beginners with no coding background. Every module starts from the assumption you've only ever added a PDF to a notebook once, if at all. If you can drag a file into a browser, you can finish it. The first module walks you through source setup before you build anything. Do I need Gemini Notebook Plus to take this training? You can take the training on the free Gemini Notebook plan and still finish every module. Gemini Notebook Plus (included with Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra plans) raises limits on notebooks, sources, audio overviews and chat queries per day, and unlocks sharing controls Google's Gemini Notebook documentation describes as premium. The modules note where a premium feature comes in so you can decide whether to upgrade after you've built something with the free tier. How long does it take to finish the Gemini Notebook path? About 2 hours of watch/work across 6 modules. Most members finish in an afternoon or across a couple of coffee breaks. Every module is designed so you leave with something built — a working notebook, a generated briefing or a published audio overview — instead of a list of notes to come back to. What's the difference between the Gemini Notebook training and the free Gemini Notebook skills library? The free Gemini Notebook skills library (/skills/notebooklm/) is a browsable catalog of copy-paste workflows and prompt patterns — free for anyone, no account needed. The Gemini Notebook training path is a structured 6-module course that teaches you to run those workflows as reusable systems, build them into recurring content and briefing pipelines, and get hands-on help when a notebook won't ground its answers. The library is the ingredients; the training is the recipes and the cooking. Can I use Gemini Notebook Enterprise features in these workflows? The training is written to the consumer Gemini Notebook product (free and Gemini Notebook Plus). Google's Gemini Notebook documentation lists Gemini Notebook Enterprise as a separate offering in Google Cloud with organization-level admin controls and different data handling. Every workflow in the path will still run inside Enterprise, but plan-specific admin settings — retention, sharing, source limits — should be checked with your Google Workspace admin before you roll a notebook out to your team. Will this training stay current when Google updates Gemini Notebook? Yes — modules are updated when Gemini Notebook changes. Google ships Gemini Notebook feature updates on a rolling basis, and the Academy tracks the ones that change how a workflow behaves (source types, output formats, Audio Overview, sharing) and updates the affected modules and skill files. If a change breaks a workflow you've built, the community post that flags it is usually up the same week. Can my team share the training if we're on All Access? Access to the training itself is per member — each teammate needs their own All Access seat to log in to the Academy community. The skill files and prompt patterns are yours to share inside your team's notebooks once you've built them, so a team can standardize on the same Gemini Notebook workflows even if not everyone has watched every module. If you're setting this up for a team, get in touch and we'll walk you through the seat-level rules before you buy. What happens after I finish the Gemini Notebook path? You keep everything: your notebooks, your skill files, your briefings and your audio overviews. Inside the same membership you can move on to the ChatGPT, Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark or Fundamentals paths — most members pick up a second platform once one is running smoothly. You also keep access to every new module and skill added to the Gemini Notebook path as Gemini Notebook itself evolves. Official references: Google Gemini Notebook Help and notebooklm.google.

Gemini Notebook Training for Beginners (2026)

Created by Diana’s AI Agents Tips

Learn no-code AI agent workflows from a trusted AI workflow specialist

AI Agents Library helps business owners, beginners, and creators turn tedious business tasks into reusable AI agent skills and workflows for research, content creation, email follow-ups, weekly planning, and document organization with Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark, Google Workspace, ChatGPT, Chrome, and NotebookLM — without coding or technical overwhelm.

Questions

Common Questions About the Gemini Notebook Path

Why is it called Gemini Notebook now instead of NotebookLM?

Google rebranded NotebookLM as Gemini Notebook to align it with the broader Gemini product ecosystem. It's the same tool with the same features — new name, same document-grounded research and content workflows. All existing NotebookLM notebooks and Audio Overviews continue to work. If you see "Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM)" in our copy during the transition, it's just there to help returning readers recognize the product.

Is this Gemini Notebook training for beginners?

Yes — the Gemini Notebook training path in AI Agents Academy is built for beginners with no coding background. Every module starts from the assumption you've only ever added a PDF to a notebook once, if at all. If you can drag a file into a browser, you can finish it. The first module walks you through source setup before you build anything.

Do I need Gemini Notebook Plus to take this training?

You can take the training on the free Gemini Notebook plan and still finish every module. Gemini Notebook Plus (included with Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra plans) raises limits on notebooks, sources, audio overviews and chat queries per day, and unlocks sharing controls Google's Gemini Notebook documentation describes as premium. The modules note where a premium feature comes in so you can decide whether to upgrade after you've built something with the free tier.

How long does it take to finish the Gemini Notebook path?

About 2 hours of watch/work across 6 modules. Most members finish in an afternoon or across a couple of coffee breaks. Every module is designed so you leave with something built — a working notebook, a generated briefing or a published audio overview — instead of a list of notes to come back to.

What's the difference between the Gemini Notebook training and the free Gemini Notebook skills library?

The free Gemini Notebook skills library (/skills/notebooklm/) is a browsable catalog of copy-paste workflows and prompt patterns — free for anyone, no account needed. The Gemini Notebook training path is a structured 6-module course that teaches you to run those workflows as reusable systems, build them into recurring content and briefing pipelines, and get hands-on help when a notebook won't ground its answers. The library is the ingredients; the training is the recipes and the cooking.

Can I use Gemini Notebook Enterprise features in these workflows?

The training is written to the consumer Gemini Notebook product (free and Gemini Notebook Plus). Google's Gemini Notebook documentation lists Gemini Notebook Enterprise as a separate offering in Google Cloud with organization-level admin controls and different data handling. Every workflow in the path will still run inside Enterprise, but plan-specific admin settings — retention, sharing, source limits — should be checked with your Google Workspace admin before you roll a notebook out to your team.

Will this training stay current when Google updates Gemini Notebook?

Yes — modules are updated when Gemini Notebook changes. Google ships Gemini Notebook feature updates on a rolling basis, and the Academy tracks the ones that change how a workflow behaves (source types, output formats, Audio Overview, sharing) and updates the affected modules and skill files. If a change breaks a workflow you've built, the community post that flags it is usually up the same week.

Can my team share the training if we're on All Access?

Access to the training itself is per member — each teammate needs their own All Access seat to log in to the Academy community. The skill files and prompt patterns are yours to share inside your team's notebooks once you've built them, so a team can standardize on the same Gemini Notebook workflows even if not everyone has watched every module. If you're setting this up for a team, get in touch and we'll walk you through the seat-level rules before you buy.

What happens after I finish the Gemini Notebook path?

You keep everything: your notebooks, your skill files, your briefings and your audio overviews. Inside the same membership you can move on to the ChatGPT, Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark or Fundamentals paths — most members pick up a second platform once one is running smoothly. You also keep access to every new module and skill added to the Gemini Notebook path as Gemini Notebook itself evolves.

Official references: Google Gemini Notebook Help and notebooklm.google.

item.text: Gemini Spark Courses & Training (2026) What is Gemini Spark Academy? It’s a beginner-friendly training path for using Gemini Spark, with step-by-step lessons, ready-to-use AI skills and practical Google-connected workflow examples. It’s one of the paths inside AI Agents Academy, not a separate purchase. Is this an official Google course? Do I need Gemini Spark access before joining? Availability can change by account and region. Check the current Gemini Spark availability and requirements first. You can still join, follow the lessons and prepare your workflows while you confirm access. What will I learn and build in my first 7 days? Follow a practical path from initial setup to a tested Gemini Spark workflow you can save, reuse and improve. No coding required — you’ll describe tasks in plain language and customize ready-to-use skills. Day 1: Set up Gemini Spark Confirm access, review permissions and connect the supported Google apps you plan to use. Day 2: Understand tasks, skills and schedules Learn how Spark uses tasks to define the work, skills to guide how it is completed and schedules to control when it runs. Day 3: Choose one repeatable task Select a useful recurring job such as preparing a weekly brief, organizing research or drafting meeting follow-ups. Day 4: Customize a ready-to-use AI skill Start with a structured Academy skill and adapt its instructions, inputs, voice and output format to your work. Day 5: Build your first workflow Combine the task, skill and relevant Google-connected context into one practical workflow. Day 6: Test and review the results Run the workflow, check its sources and actions, and identify where the instructions need to be clearer. Day 7: Save, reuse and improve it Save a reliable version, schedule it when appropriate and use what you learned to build your next workflow. Does membership include the other Academy training paths? Yes. One All Access Pass includes all five AI Agents Academy training paths — Gemini Spark, Claude Cowork, ChatGPT, Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM) and AI Skills Fundamentals — plus the shared AI skills library and resources. Which Gemini Spark course should I take? Choose based on the result you want. Gemini Spark Academy is designed for beginners who want a guided, self-paced path to real Spark workflows, ready-to-use Skills and setup help. For live classroom training, official foundations and other alternatives, compare the best Gemini Spark Skills courses. How does the free seven-day trial work? You get full access for seven days and can cancel anytime before the trial ends without being charged. During the week you can work through lessons and ask for hands-on help getting your first workflow running. Do I get a certificate when I finish the Gemini Spark path? Yes. You receive an official AI Agents Library certificate of completion when you finish the Gemini Spark path. Every training path issues its own — ChatGPT, Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark, Gemini Notebook and AI Skills Fundamentals each award their own — so completing more than one leaves you with a certificate for each. Certificates are included with All Access at no extra cost. It certifies the training you completed with AI Agents Library and is not a vendor certification from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google.

## Frequently asked questions
Everything you need to know about picking a training path and getting started.
Which training path should I start with? How long does each training path take? Do I need coding experience?
No. Every training path is written for beginners — no coding, no terminal work and no prior AI experience required. The lessons are step-by-step and built for small business owners, creators, consultants and anyone who has never installed an AI skill file before.
Do I need paid ChatGPT, Claude or Google plans?
The free copy-paste versions can be adapted for many free AI chat plans. Native Skill installation, Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark, connected tools and advanced automation features may require an eligible paid plan. Every lesson identifies its requirements — see the plan-tier tables inside each training path: [ChatGPT](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/academy/chatgpt/), [Claude Cowork](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/academy/claude-cowork/), [Gemini Spark](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/academy/spark/), [Gemini Notebook](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/academy/gemini-notebook/).
Can I switch between training paths?
Yes. One [AI Agents Library All Access Pass](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/all-access/) membership unlocks every training path in the Academy, so you can start with ChatGPT, jump into Claude Cowork the next day and pick up Gemini Notebook the week after — no extra purchase, no upgrade, no per-platform pricing.
How often are courses and lessons updated?
Courses are updated as the underlying AI tools ship new features — for example, ChatGPT Skills in Excel and Sheets shipped as a mid-course update to the ChatGPT path. Every new skill and training update added while your pass is active is included at no extra cost.
Do AI Agents Academy courses come with a certificate?
Yes. Every training path in AI Agents Academy issues its own official certificate of completion — ChatGPT, Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark, Gemini Notebook and AI Skills Fundamentals each award their own when you finish it. All certificates are included with the AI Agents Library All Access Pass at no extra cost. It certifies the training you completed with AI Agents Library and is not a vendor certification from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google.
