item.text: Local File Access & Setup (2026) Gemini Spark is now available on Mac with local file access. Google has brought its personal AI agent to a native Gemini app for macOS, and this is the first version that can act on the local files sitting on your own computer, not just the ones in the cloud. On Mac, Spark can sort your Downloads folder, rename messy files, and turn locally saved invoices into a Google Sheet, all while you work on something else. This guide explains exactly what the Gemini Spark Mac app does, how to download and install it, how to connect folders safely, and the best Mac-specific tasks to try first. If you only want to know where Spark is available and how much it costs, read the Gemini Spark availability guide instead. This article is about the desktop app itself. Yes, Gemini Spark is available on Mac with local file access Google launched Gemini Spark in beta inside the Gemini app for macOS on June 30, 2026, starting in the United States. Google’s current Mac documentation now says Spark on Mac is available where Gemini Spark is available. Download the app at gemini.google/mac, sign in with an eligible Spark account (Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US), open the Spark tab in the sidebar, connect a folder, and give Spark a task. Last verified: July 26, 2026 against Google’s official Gemini help pages, release notes, and the Gemini for macOS product page. Spark on Mac is an early beta and its features may change. The Gemini app for macOS adds a dedicated Spark tab in the sidebar, mirroring the web layout. From here Spark can act on files in the folders you connect. New to Spark? Start with the free setup guide. In this Gemini Spark for Mac guide: What is Gemini Spark on Mac? What the macOS app adds Requirements and system compatibility How to download and install Gemini Spark on Mac Connect a folder and run your first Mac task Best Gemini Spark use cases on Mac Mac settings and keyboard shortcuts to know How local file access works — and how to use it safely Start a Mac task from another device Mac vs. web vs. mobile Spark not showing on Mac? What is Gemini Spark on Mac? Gemini Spark is Google’s personal AI agent. Instead of answering one question at a time like a normal chat, Spark takes a defined goal, plans the steps, uses the sources you approve, and completes multi-step work under your direction. If you are new to the concept, read what Gemini Spark is and the complete guide to using Spark first. What makes the macOS app different is where Spark can work. On the web and mobile, Spark operates in the cloud, through connected apps, its remote browser, and Google Workspace. The Mac app extends that reach to your local desktop: the actual files and folders on your computer. That is the headline change. Spark can now open, read, organize, rename, and pull information from files you have saved on your Mac, then feed the results into Google Docs and Sheets. In plain terms: the Mac app turns Spark from a cloud assistant into a desktop assistant that can quietly tidy, sort, and process the files you already have on your computer, without you dragging anything into a browser. What the macOS app adds Alongside local file access, the June 2026 Mac launch shipped with several capabilities that also reached the wider Spark experience. Here is what is new: Local file automation Spark can act on files stored on your Mac, sorting, renaming, and organizing them by type or context instead of just chatting about them. Connected folders You choose exactly which directories Spark may touch. It only has access to the folders you explicitly connect. Desktop-to-Workspace bridge Spark can gather scattered details from local files and use them to build or update content in Google Docs and Sheets. Remote Mac tasks Start a Spark task on your Mac from another device signed into the same Google Account, as long as the devices are on the same Wi-Fi network or linked by Bluetooth. Connected apps Spark supports Google Workspace actions plus connected services such as Canva, Dropbox, Instacart, OpenTable, and Zillow. Availability can vary by account and rollout. Real-time tracking Spark can monitor news, finance, shopping, weather, and sports, then alert you, for example when a stock crosses a price you set. The connected-app and tracking upgrades apply across Spark, but combined with local file access on Mac they make the desktop app the most capable place to run Spark today. For a reusable monitoring workflow, pair Spark’s tracking tools with the free AI News Research Skill. Requirements and system compatibility The Gemini Mac app runs on most recent Macs, but Spark inside it has stricter account rules. You need to satisfy both the hardware requirements and the Spark eligibility requirements. RequirementWhat you need for Gemini Spark on Mac macOS version macOS Sequoia (15.0) or later Hardware Apple silicon Mac (Intel Macs are not supported) Memory 8 GB RAM or more Storage At least 200 MB of available disk space Internet A stable internet connection App The latest version of the Gemini app for macOS Subscription Google AI Ultra on a personal Google Account, or Google AI Pro if you are in the US — not the free plan Age 18 or older Country Any country where Gemini Spark is available; it launched first in the United States Language All Gemini Apps languages on AI Ultra; English only on AI Pro in the US Permissions Accessibility access in macOS System Settings, plus the specific folders you connect Have Ultra but no Spark tab? A Google AI Ultra subscription alone is not enough. Your country, account type, age, language, and activity settings all matter. The full checklist and country list live on the Gemini Spark availability page. How to download and install Gemini Spark on Mac Spark is not a separate download. It lives inside the Gemini app for macOS, so you install one app and then open the Spark tab. Here is the full process. 1 Download the Gemini app for macOS Go to gemini.google/mac and select Download for macOS. Open the downloaded .dmg file, then drag Gemini into your Applications folder. If you already have the Gemini Mac app, install any available updates and relaunch the app. 2 Launch and sign in Open Gemini from your Applications folder. Sign in with the personal Google Account that holds your Spark plan — Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US. Using the same account lets you access your Spark task threads across supported devices. 3 Open the Spark tab Look for the Spark tab in the app’s sidebar. It mirrors the layout you may have seen on the web. If you do not see it, confirm you are on an eligible account and in a supported country, then check for an app update. 4 Grant the permissions Spark needs To act on your desktop, Spark needs Accessibility access in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility, and it needs you to connect specific folders. macOS will prompt you; you stay in control of what you approve. Tip: Press Option + Space to summon the Gemini mini window from anywhere on your Mac, or Option + Shift + Space for the full app. You can change these shortcuts in Settings. Connect a folder and run your first Mac task The safest way to learn the Mac app is a small, easy-to-verify task on one folder. A cluttered Downloads folder is the perfect first job. Connect one folder In the Spark tab, open the connected-folders settings and add a single folder, such as Downloads. Spark will only be able to see and act on the folders you add here. Give Spark a clear, specific instruction. Name the folder, the rule, and the result you expect. Copy the prompt below and paste it into the Spark tab. Look at every PDF in my connected Downloads folder. Sort them into subfolders by type: Invoices, Receipts, Contracts, and Other. Use the text inside each PDF to decide which subfolder it belongs in. Do not delete anything. Only move files into the new subfolders. Before you finish, show me a short summary that lists what you moved and where, so I can confirm it looks right. Watch it work and review the result Spark shows its progress in real time. Because you asked for a summary and told it not to delete anything, you can verify the result before trusting it with bigger jobs. Once you are confident, you can turn a repeated version of this into a skill or schedule. Start read-only or reversible. For your first few tasks, ask Spark to move rather than delete, and to summarize before finishing. Spark is an experimental agent and can make mistakes, so keep early tasks low-risk and easy to undo. Best Gemini Spark use cases on Mac The Mac app shines at the desktop chores that eat your time but never feel worth doing manually. These are strong starting points that use local files: Tame a messy Downloads folder Have Spark sort files into labelled subfolders by type or project, and rename them to a consistent pattern so you can actually find things. Turn invoices into a live budget Point Spark at a folder of saved invoices and ask it to build a Google Sheet of totals, then schedule it to update the sheet as new invoices arrive. Summarize a folder of documents Ask Spark to read every file in a project folder and produce a Google Doc summary, so you can brief yourself before a meeting in minutes. Standardize file names Rename photos, exports, or receipts to a clear convention like 2026-07_client_invoice.pdf across a whole folder at once. Pull data out of local files Extract figures, dates, or contact details scattered across saved documents and collect them into one clean spreadsheet. Keep a folder tidy on autopilot Set a schedule so Spark files new downloads into the right place regularly, keeping your desktop organized without you touching it. Here is a ready-to-run prompt for the invoice-to-budget workflow. Replace the folder path with your own, then paste it into the Spark tab. Read every invoice PDF in my connected folder "Finance/Invoices" on this Mac. For each invoice, pull out the vendor name, invoice date, invoice number, and total amount. Create a new Google Sheet called "Invoice Tracker" with one row per invoice and columns for Vendor, Date, Invoice Number, and Amount. Add a total row at the bottom. Do not change or delete any of the original files. When you are done, tell me how many invoices you found and list any you could not read so I can check them myself. Want more ideas built around business outcomes rather than file chores? See the best Gemini Spark use cases for business. If you regularly turn invoice or CSV data into summaries, the free AI Spreadsheet Insights Skill gives you a reusable analysis workflow. Mac settings and keyboard shortcuts to know The Mac app includes Gemini Spark settings for managing which folders Spark can reach, its data, and how it runs. A few things are worth checking on day one: Connected folders — use the Connected folders area in Spark to add or disconnect the folders Spark can access. Keep this list as small as possible. Gemini Spark settings — turn Spark on or off and manage its remote browser and code-execution data. Usage limits — Spark uses compute-based limits based on task complexity, and Gemini notifies you as you approach your limit. Keyboard shortcuts — Option + Space opens the mini window, Option + Shift + Space opens the full app, and pressing both Command keys shares the active window as context. How local file access works — and how to use it safely Giving an AI agent access to your local files is a real decision, so it is worth knowing exactly what Spark can — and cannot — do on your Mac. Important: Gemini Spark can edit, share, and permanently delete files in connected folders when instructed. Google says Spark creates temporary backup files, but they are deleted when you begin another task or after 24 hours. Do not rely on Spark’s temporary backups as your only recovery method. Keep important files backed up separately, and supervise any task that moves, overwrites, shares, or deletes files. Folder-level control. Spark only has access to the specific directories you explicitly connect. It cannot roam your whole drive. Explicit permissions. Local folder access and full-page browser reading require Accessibility permission that you grant in macOS System Settings, and you can revoke it anytime. You approve the scope. Connect one folder to start, review what Spark did, and expand only when you trust the workflow. Never paste secrets. Google warns you not to type passwords, payment details, or other sensitive information directly into a Spark task thread. Good habit: treat connected folders like keys. Give Spark the smallest folder that gets the job done, and disconnect folders you are no longer automating. Start a Mac task from another device Remote control is now live. From another device signed into the same Google Account, open Gemini, switch to Spark, select Add > Computer, and choose your Mac. You can type or speak the task, read past Spark chats, and use quick or media controls without sitting in front of the computer. Your Mac must have the Gemini app set up and running, and you must accept the Spark Mac terms. The Mac and the device you are using must be on the same Wi-Fi network or have Bluetooth turned on and be linked. Cloud-based schedules can continue when your device is off; tasks that act on local Mac files need the Mac available with Gemini running. Gemini Spark on Mac vs. web vs. mobile Spark is the same agent everywhere, but the surface changes what it can reach. Here is how the Mac app compares. CapabilityMac appWebMobile Directly act on local files and folders Yes No No Connected apps and Google Workspace Yes; availability can vary by account and rollout Yes Yes Remote browser and cloud tasks Yes Yes Yes Global keyboard shortcut to summon Gemini Yes No No Start a Mac task remotely Target of the task Look for Add > Computer on the device Yes If your work involves files that live on your computer, the Mac app is the version to use. If your work is entirely in the cloud, the web and mobile versions do the same job. Spark not showing on Mac? If you installed the Gemini Mac app but do not see a Spark tab, run through these quick checks: Update the app. Install any available updates for the Gemini Mac app, then relaunch it. Confirm the account. Sign in with the exact personal Google Account that owns your Spark plan (Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US), not a work, school, or secondary account. Check the plan. Spark needs Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro if you are in the US — not the free plan. Check your country and settings. Spark on Mac is available where Gemini Spark is available and needs Keep Activity turned on. Google AI Ultra supports all Gemini Apps languages; Google AI Pro access in the US is English only. Check your Mac. You need an Apple silicon Mac on macOS Sequoia (15.0) or later. Still stuck? The full requirement-by-requirement checklist, excluded-country list, and account fixes are on the Gemini Spark availability guide. Frequently asked questions about Gemini Spark on Mac Is Gemini Spark available on Mac? Yes. Google launched Gemini Spark in beta inside the Gemini app for macOS on June 30, 2026, starting in the United States. Google’s current Mac help documentation says Spark on Mac is available where Gemini Spark is available, for eligible subscribers aged 18 and over on Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US. How do I get Gemini Spark on my Mac? Go to gemini.google/mac, select Download for macOS, open the .dmg file, and drag Gemini into your Applications folder. Launch it, install any available updates, sign in with the personal Google Account that has your Spark plan (Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US), and open the Spark tab in the sidebar. Then grant Accessibility permission and connect a folder. Is there a separate Gemini Spark app for Mac? No. Spark is built into the Gemini app for macOS. You install one app and open the Spark tab; there is no standalone Spark download. Which Macs can run Gemini Spark? Spark in the Gemini Mac app requires an Apple silicon Mac running macOS Sequoia (15.0) or later. Intel Macs are not supported. Can Gemini Spark access all the files on my Mac? No. Spark only has access to the specific folders you explicitly connect, and desktop access requires Accessibility permission that you grant in macOS System Settings. You can remove folders or revoke permission at any time. Do I need to keep my Mac on for Spark tasks? Time-based Spark schedules run in the cloud and can keep working when your device is off. Tasks that act on local Mac files need your Mac available with the Gemini app running. Can I start a Mac task from my phone? Yes. Remote control is now available. Keep the Gemini app running on your Mac, sign into the same Google Account on both devices, and connect them over the same Wi-Fi network or by linked Bluetooth. On your phone, open Spark and choose Add > Computer to select the Mac. Does Gemini Spark on Mac cost extra? No separate Mac fee. Spark on Mac is included with an eligible paid plan: Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro if you are in the US. See the availability guide for current pricing and plan details. Is Gemini Spark on Mac available outside the US? Yes, if Gemini Spark is available in your country and your account meets Google’s requirements. The macOS beta launched first in the United States, but Google’s current Mac documentation says Spark on Mac can be used where Gemini Spark is available. What can Gemini Spark do on Mac that it cannot do on the web? The Mac app provides direct access to the local folders you connect and can summon Gemini with a global keyboard shortcut. Another supported device can start a task on that connected Mac remotely, but the local file action still happens through the Mac app and its approved folder access. item.html:
Local File Access & Setup (2026)

Gemini Spark is now available on Mac with local file access. Google has brought its personal AI agent to a native Gemini app for macOS, and this is the first version that can act on the local files sitting on your own computer, not just the ones in the cloud. On Mac, Spark can sort your Downloads folder, rename messy files, and turn locally saved invoices into a Google Sheet, all while you work on something else.

This guide explains exactly what the Gemini Spark Mac app does, how to download and install it, how to connect folders safely, and the best Mac-specific tasks to try first. If you only want to know where Spark is available and how much it costs, read the Gemini Spark availability guide instead. This article is about the desktop app itself.

Quick answer

Yes, Gemini Spark is available on Mac with local file access

Google launched Gemini Spark in beta inside the Gemini app for macOS on June 30, 2026, starting in the United States. Google’s current Mac documentation now says Spark on Mac is available where Gemini Spark is available. Download the app at gemini.google/mac, sign in with an eligible Spark account (Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US), open the Spark tab in the sidebar, connect a folder, and give Spark a task.

Last verified: July 26, 2026 against Google’s official Gemini help pages, release notes, and the Gemini for macOS product page. Spark on Mac is an early beta and its features may change.

In this Gemini Spark for Mac guide:

  1. What is Gemini Spark on Mac?
  2. What the macOS app adds
  3. Requirements and system compatibility
  4. How to download and install Gemini Spark on Mac
  5. Connect a folder and run your first Mac task
  6. Best Gemini Spark use cases on Mac
  7. Mac settings and keyboard shortcuts to know
  8. How local file access works — and how to use it safely
  9. Start a Mac task from another device
  10. Mac vs. web vs. mobile
  11. Spark not showing on Mac?
  12. Frequently asked questions

What is Gemini Spark on Mac?

Gemini Spark is Google’s personal AI agent. Instead of answering one question at a time like a normal chat, Spark takes a defined goal, plans the steps, uses the sources you approve, and completes multi-step work under your direction. If you are new to the concept, read what Gemini Spark is and the complete guide to using Spark first.

What makes the macOS app different is where Spark can work. On the web and mobile, Spark operates in the cloud, through connected apps, its remote browser, and Google Workspace. The Mac app extends that reach to your local desktop: the actual files and folders on your computer. That is the headline change. Spark can now open, read, organize, rename, and pull information from files you have saved on your Mac, then feed the results into Google Docs and Sheets.

In plain terms: the Mac app turns Spark from a cloud assistant into a desktop assistant that can quietly tidy, sort, and process the files you already have on your computer, without you dragging anything into a browser.

What the macOS app adds

Alongside local file access, the June 2026 Mac launch shipped with several capabilities that also reached the wider Spark experience. Here is what is new:

Local file automation

Spark can act on files stored on your Mac, sorting, renaming, and organizing them by type or context instead of just chatting about them.

Connected folders

You choose exactly which directories Spark may touch. It only has access to the folders you explicitly connect.

Desktop-to-Workspace bridge

Spark can gather scattered details from local files and use them to build or update content in Google Docs and Sheets.

Remote Mac tasks

Start a Spark task on your Mac from another device signed into the same Google Account, as long as the devices are on the same Wi-Fi network or linked by Bluetooth.

Connected apps

Spark supports Google Workspace actions plus connected services such as Canva, Dropbox, Instacart, OpenTable, and Zillow. Availability can vary by account and rollout.

Real-time tracking

Spark can monitor news, finance, shopping, weather, and sports, then alert you, for example when a stock crosses a price you set.

The connected-app and tracking upgrades apply across Spark, but combined with local file access on Mac they make the desktop app the most capable place to run Spark today. For a reusable monitoring workflow, pair Spark’s tracking tools with the free AI News Research Skill.

Requirements and system compatibility

The Gemini Mac app runs on most recent Macs, but Spark inside it has stricter account rules. You need to satisfy both the hardware requirements and the Spark eligibility requirements.

RequirementWhat you need for Gemini Spark on Mac
macOS versionmacOS Sequoia (15.0) or later
HardwareApple silicon Mac (Intel Macs are not supported)
Memory8 GB RAM or more
StorageAt least 200 MB of available disk space
InternetA stable internet connection
AppThe latest version of the Gemini app for macOS
SubscriptionGoogle AI Ultra on a personal Google Account, or Google AI Pro if you are in the US — not the free plan
Age18 or older
CountryAny country where Gemini Spark is available; it launched first in the United States
LanguageAll Gemini Apps languages on AI Ultra; English only on AI Pro in the US
PermissionsAccessibility access in macOS System Settings, plus the specific folders you connect

Have Ultra but no Spark tab? A Google AI Ultra subscription alone is not enough. Your country, account type, age, language, and activity settings all matter. The full checklist and country list live on the Gemini Spark availability page.

How to download and install Gemini Spark on Mac

Spark is not a separate download. It lives inside the Gemini app for macOS, so you install one app and then open the Spark tab. Here is the full process.

1

Download the Gemini app for macOS

Go to gemini.google/mac and select Download for macOS. Open the downloaded .dmg file, then drag Gemini into your Applications folder. If you already have the Gemini Mac app, install any available updates and relaunch the app.

2

Launch and sign in

Open Gemini from your Applications folder. Sign in with the personal Google Account that holds your Spark plan — Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US. Using the same account lets you access your Spark task threads across supported devices.

3

Open the Spark tab

Look for the Spark tab in the app’s sidebar. It mirrors the layout you may have seen on the web. If you do not see it, confirm you are on an eligible account and in a supported country, then check for an app update.

4

Grant the permissions Spark needs

To act on your desktop, Spark needs Accessibility access in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility, and it needs you to connect specific folders. macOS will prompt you; you stay in control of what you approve.

Tip: Press Option + Space to summon the Gemini mini window from anywhere on your Mac, or Option + Shift + Space for the full app. You can change these shortcuts in Settings.

Connect a folder and run your first Mac task

The safest way to learn the Mac app is a small, easy-to-verify task on one folder. A cluttered Downloads folder is the perfect first job.

1

Connect one folder

In the Spark tab, open the connected-folders settings and add a single folder, such as Downloads. Spark will only be able to see and act on the folders you add here.

2

Copy this starter prompt

Give Spark a clear, specific instruction. Name the folder, the rule, and the result you expect. Copy the prompt below and paste it into the Spark tab.

Look at every PDF in my connected Downloads folder. Sort them into subfolders by type: Invoices, Receipts, Contracts, and Other. Use the text inside each PDF to decide which subfolder it belongs in.

Do not delete anything. Only move files into the new subfolders.

Before you finish, show me a short summary that lists what you moved and where, so I can confirm it looks right.

3

Watch it work and review the result

Spark shows its progress in real time. Because you asked for a summary and told it not to delete anything, you can verify the result before trusting it with bigger jobs. Once you are confident, you can turn a repeated version of this into a skill or schedule.

Start read-only or reversible. For your first few tasks, ask Spark to move rather than delete, and to summarize before finishing. Spark is an experimental agent and can make mistakes, so keep early tasks low-risk and easy to undo.

Best Gemini Spark use cases on Mac

The Mac app shines at the desktop chores that eat your time but never feel worth doing manually. These are strong starting points that use local files:

Tame a messy Downloads folder

Have Spark sort files into labelled subfolders by type or project, and rename them to a consistent pattern so you can actually find things.

Turn invoices into a live budget

Point Spark at a folder of saved invoices and ask it to build a Google Sheet of totals, then schedule it to update the sheet as new invoices arrive.

Summarize a folder of documents

Ask Spark to read every file in a project folder and produce a Google Doc summary, so you can brief yourself before a meeting in minutes.

Standardize file names

Rename photos, exports, or receipts to a clear convention like 2026-07_client_invoice.pdf across a whole folder at once.

Pull data out of local files

Extract figures, dates, or contact details scattered across saved documents and collect them into one clean spreadsheet.

Keep a folder tidy on autopilot

Set a schedule so Spark files new downloads into the right place regularly, keeping your desktop organized without you touching it.

Here is a ready-to-run prompt for the invoice-to-budget workflow. Replace the folder path with your own, then paste it into the Spark tab.

Read every invoice PDF in my connected folder "Finance/Invoices" on this Mac. For each invoice, pull out the vendor name, invoice date, invoice number, and total amount.

Create a new Google Sheet called "Invoice Tracker" with one row per invoice and columns for Vendor, Date, Invoice Number, and Amount. Add a total row at the bottom.

Do not change or delete any of the original files. When you are done, tell me how many invoices you found and list any you could not read so I can check them myself.

Want more ideas built around business outcomes rather than file chores? See the best Gemini Spark use cases for business. If you regularly turn invoice or CSV data into summaries, the free AI Spreadsheet Insights Skill gives you a reusable analysis workflow.

Mac settings and keyboard shortcuts to know

The Mac app includes Gemini Spark settings for managing which folders Spark can reach, its data, and how it runs. A few things are worth checking on day one:

  • Connected folders — use the Connected folders area in Spark to add or disconnect the folders Spark can access. Keep this list as small as possible.
  • Gemini Spark settings — turn Spark on or off and manage its remote browser and code-execution data.
  • Usage limits — Spark uses compute-based limits based on task complexity, and Gemini notifies you as you approach your limit.
  • Keyboard shortcuts — Option + Space opens the mini window, Option + Shift + Space opens the full app, and pressing both Command keys shares the active window as context.

How local file access works — and how to use it safely

Giving an AI agent access to your local files is a real decision, so it is worth knowing exactly what Spark can — and cannot — do on your Mac.

Important: Gemini Spark can edit, share, and permanently delete files in connected folders when instructed. Google says Spark creates temporary backup files, but they are deleted when you begin another task or after 24 hours. Do not rely on Spark’s temporary backups as your only recovery method. Keep important files backed up separately, and supervise any task that moves, overwrites, shares, or deletes files.

  • Folder-level control. Spark only has access to the specific directories you explicitly connect. It cannot roam your whole drive.
  • Explicit permissions. Local folder access and full-page browser reading require Accessibility permission that you grant in macOS System Settings, and you can revoke it anytime.
  • You approve the scope. Connect one folder to start, review what Spark did, and expand only when you trust the workflow.
  • Never paste secrets. Google warns you not to type passwords, payment details, or other sensitive information directly into a Spark task thread.

Good habit: treat connected folders like keys. Give Spark the smallest folder that gets the job done, and disconnect folders you are no longer automating.

Start a Mac task from another device

Remote control is now live. From another device signed into the same Google Account, open Gemini, switch to Spark, select Add > Computer, and choose your Mac. You can type or speak the task, read past Spark chats, and use quick or media controls without sitting in front of the computer.

Your Mac must have the Gemini app set up and running, and you must accept the Spark Mac terms. The Mac and the device you are using must be on the same Wi-Fi network or have Bluetooth turned on and be linked. Cloud-based schedules can continue when your device is off; tasks that act on local Mac files need the Mac available with Gemini running.

Gemini Spark on Mac vs. web vs. mobile

Spark is the same agent everywhere, but the surface changes what it can reach. Here is how the Mac app compares.

CapabilityMac appWebMobile
Directly act on local files and foldersYesNoNo
Connected apps and Google WorkspaceYes; availability can vary by account and rolloutYesYes
Remote browser and cloud tasksYesYesYes
Global keyboard shortcut to summon GeminiYesNoNo
Start a Mac task remotelyTarget of the taskLook for Add > Computer on the deviceYes

If your work involves files that live on your computer, the Mac app is the version to use. If your work is entirely in the cloud, the web and mobile versions do the same job.

Spark not showing on Mac?

If you installed the Gemini Mac app but do not see a Spark tab, run through these quick checks:

  • Update the app. Install any available updates for the Gemini Mac app, then relaunch it.
  • Confirm the account. Sign in with the exact personal Google Account that owns your Spark plan (Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US), not a work, school, or secondary account.
  • Check the plan. Spark needs Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro if you are in the US — not the free plan.
  • Check your country and settings. Spark on Mac is available where Gemini Spark is available and needs Keep Activity turned on. Google AI Ultra supports all Gemini Apps languages; Google AI Pro access in the US is English only.
  • Check your Mac. You need an Apple silicon Mac on macOS Sequoia (15.0) or later.

Still stuck? The full requirement-by-requirement checklist, excluded-country list, and account fixes are on the Gemini Spark availability guide.

Frequently asked questions about Gemini Spark on Mac

Is Gemini Spark available on Mac?

Yes. Google launched Gemini Spark in beta inside the Gemini app for macOS on June 30, 2026, starting in the United States. Google’s current Mac help documentation says Spark on Mac is available where Gemini Spark is available, for eligible subscribers aged 18 and over on Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US.

How do I get Gemini Spark on my Mac?

Go to gemini.google/mac, select Download for macOS, open the .dmg file, and drag Gemini into your Applications folder. Launch it, install any available updates, sign in with the personal Google Account that has your Spark plan (Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US), and open the Spark tab in the sidebar. Then grant Accessibility permission and connect a folder.

Is there a separate Gemini Spark app for Mac?

No. Spark is built into the Gemini app for macOS. You install one app and open the Spark tab; there is no standalone Spark download.

Which Macs can run Gemini Spark?

Spark in the Gemini Mac app requires an Apple silicon Mac running macOS Sequoia (15.0) or later. Intel Macs are not supported.

Can Gemini Spark access all the files on my Mac?

No. Spark only has access to the specific folders you explicitly connect, and desktop access requires Accessibility permission that you grant in macOS System Settings. You can remove folders or revoke permission at any time.

Do I need to keep my Mac on for Spark tasks?

Time-based Spark schedules run in the cloud and can keep working when your device is off. Tasks that act on local Mac files need your Mac available with the Gemini app running.

Can I start a Mac task from my phone?

Yes. Remote control is now available. Keep the Gemini app running on your Mac, sign into the same Google Account on both devices, and connect them over the same Wi-Fi network or by linked Bluetooth. On your phone, open Spark and choose Add > Computer to select the Mac.

Does Gemini Spark on Mac cost extra?

No separate Mac fee. Spark on Mac is included with an eligible paid plan: Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro if you are in the US. See the availability guide for current pricing and plan details.

Is Gemini Spark on Mac available outside the US?

Yes, if Gemini Spark is available in your country and your account meets Google’s requirements. The macOS beta launched first in the United States, but Google’s current Mac documentation says Spark on Mac can be used where Gemini Spark is available.

What can Gemini Spark do on Mac that it cannot do on the web?

The Mac app provides direct access to the local folders you connect and can summon Gemini with a global keyboard shortcut. Another supported device can start a task on that connected Mac remotely, but the local file action still happens through the Mac app and its approved folder access.

# Local File Access & Setup (2026)
**Gemini Spark is now available on Mac with local file access.** Google has brought its personal AI agent to a native **Gemini app for macOS**, and this is the first version that can act on the local files sitting on your own computer, not just the ones in the cloud. On Mac, Spark can sort your Downloads folder, rename messy files, and turn locally saved invoices into a Google Sheet, all while you work on something else.
This guide explains exactly what the **Gemini Spark Mac app** does, how to download and install it, how to connect folders safely, and the best Mac-specific tasks to try first. If you only want to know _where_ Spark is available and how much it costs, read the [Gemini Spark availability guide](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-availability/) instead. This article is about the desktop app itself.
Quick answer
Yes, Gemini Spark is available on Mac with local file access
Google launched Gemini Spark in beta inside the Gemini app for macOS on June 30, 2026, starting in the United States. Google’s current Mac documentation now says Spark on Mac is available where Gemini Spark is available. Download the app at [gemini.google/mac](https://gemini.google/mac/), sign in with an eligible Spark account (Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US), open the **Spark** tab in the sidebar, connect a folder, and give Spark a task.
**Last verified:** July 26, 2026 against Google’s official Gemini help pages, release notes, and the Gemini for macOS product page. Spark on Mac is an early beta and its features may change.
The Gemini app for macOS adds a dedicated **Spark** tab in the sidebar, mirroring the web layout. From here Spark can act on files in the folders you connect. New to Spark? Start with the [free setup guide](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/setup-guides/gemini-spark/).
In this Gemini Spark for Mac guide:
1. [What is Gemini Spark on Mac?](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-mac/#spark-mac-what) 2. [What the macOS app adds](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-mac/#spark-mac-new) 3. [Requirements and system compatibility](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-mac/#spark-mac-requirements) 4. [How to download and install Gemini Spark on Mac](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-mac/#spark-mac-install) 5. [Connect a folder and run your first Mac task](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-mac/#spark-mac-first-task) 6. [Best Gemini Spark use cases on Mac](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-mac/#spark-mac-use-cases) 7. [Mac settings and keyboard shortcuts to know](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-mac/#spark-mac-settings) 8. [How local file access works — and how to use it safely](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-mac/#spark-mac-privacy) 9. [Start a Mac task from another device](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-mac/#spark-mac-remote) 10. [Mac vs. web vs. mobile](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-mac/#spark-mac-vs) 11. [Spark not showing on Mac?](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-mac/#spark-mac-troubleshoot) 12. [Frequently asked questions](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-mac/#spark-mac-faq)
## What is Gemini Spark on Mac?
Gemini Spark is Google’s personal AI agent. Instead of answering one question at a time like a normal chat, Spark takes a defined goal, plans the steps, uses the sources you approve, and completes multi-step work under your direction. If you are new to the concept, read [what Gemini Spark is](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/what-is-gemini-spark/) and the [complete guide to using Spark](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-use-gemini-spark/) first.
What makes the **macOS app** different is _where_ Spark can work. On the web and mobile, Spark operates in the cloud, through connected apps, its remote browser, and Google Workspace. The Mac app extends that reach to your **local desktop**: the actual files and folders on your computer. That is the headline change. Spark can now open, read, organize, rename, and pull information from files you have saved on your Mac, then feed the results into Google Docs and Sheets.
**In plain terms:** the Mac app turns Spark from a cloud assistant into a desktop assistant that can quietly tidy, sort, and process the files you already have on your computer, without you dragging anything into a browser.
## What the macOS app adds
Alongside local file access, the June 2026 Mac launch shipped with several capabilities that also reached the wider Spark experience. Here is what is new:
Local file automation
Spark can act on files stored on your Mac, sorting, renaming, and organizing them by type or context instead of just chatting about them.
Connected folders
You choose exactly which directories Spark may touch. It only has access to the folders you explicitly connect.
Desktop-to-Workspace bridge
Spark can gather scattered details from local files and use them to build or update content in Google Docs and Sheets.
Remote Mac tasks
Start a Spark task on your Mac from another device signed into the same Google Account, as long as the devices are on the same Wi-Fi network or linked by Bluetooth.
Connected apps
Spark supports Google Workspace actions plus connected services such as Canva, Dropbox, Instacart, OpenTable, and Zillow. Availability can vary by account and rollout.
Real-time tracking
Spark can monitor news, finance, shopping, weather, and sports, then alert you, for example when a stock crosses a price you set.
The connected-app and tracking upgrades apply across Spark, but combined with local file access on Mac they make the desktop app the most capable place to run Spark today. For a reusable monitoring workflow, pair Spark’s tracking tools with the free [AI News Research Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/ai-news-agent/).
## Requirements and system compatibility
The Gemini Mac app runs on most recent Macs, but Spark inside it has stricter account rules. You need to satisfy **both** the hardware requirements and the Spark eligibility requirements.
| Requirement | What you need for Gemini Spark on Mac | | --- | --- | | **macOS version** | macOS Sequoia (15.0) or later | | **Hardware** | Apple silicon Mac (Intel Macs are not supported) | | **Memory** | 8 GB RAM or more | | **Storage** | At least 200 MB of available disk space | | **Internet** | A stable internet connection | | **App** | The latest version of the Gemini app for macOS | | **Subscription** | Google AI Ultra on a personal Google Account, or Google AI Pro if you are in the US — not the free plan | | **Age** | 18 or older | | **Country** | Any country where Gemini Spark is available; it launched first in the United States | | **Language** | All Gemini Apps languages on AI Ultra; English only on AI Pro in the US | | **Permissions** | Accessibility access in macOS System Settings, plus the specific folders you connect |
**Have Ultra but no Spark tab?** A Google AI Ultra subscription alone is not enough. Your country, account type, age, language, and activity settings all matter. The full checklist and country list live on the [Gemini Spark availability page](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-availability/).
## How to download and install Gemini Spark on Mac
Spark is not a separate download. It lives inside the Gemini app for macOS, so you install one app and then open the Spark tab. Here is the full process.
1
### Download the Gemini app for macOS
Go to [gemini.google/mac](https://gemini.google/mac/) and select **Download for macOS**. Open the downloaded `.dmg` file, then drag Gemini into your Applications folder. If you already have the Gemini Mac app, install any available updates and relaunch the app.
2
### Launch and sign in
Open Gemini from your Applications folder. Sign in with the **personal Google Account that holds your Spark plan — Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US**. Using the same account lets you access your Spark task threads across supported devices.
3
### Open the Spark tab
Look for the **Spark** tab in the app’s sidebar. It mirrors the layout you may have seen on the web. If you do not see it, confirm you are on an eligible account and in a supported country, then check for an app update.
4
### Grant the permissions Spark needs
To act on your desktop, Spark needs **Accessibility** access in `System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility`, and it needs you to connect specific folders. macOS will prompt you; you stay in control of what you approve.
**Tip:** Press Option + Space to summon the Gemini mini window from anywhere on your Mac, or Option + Shift + Space for the full app. You can change these shortcuts in Settings.
## Connect a folder and run your first Mac task
The safest way to learn the Mac app is a small, easy-to-verify task on one folder. A cluttered Downloads folder is the perfect first job.
1
### Connect one folder
In the Spark tab, open the connected-folders settings and add a single folder, such as `Downloads`. Spark will only be able to see and act on the folders you add here.
2
### Copy this starter prompt
Give Spark a clear, specific instruction. Name the folder, the rule, and the result you expect. Copy the prompt below and paste it into the Spark tab.
``` Look at every PDF in my connected Downloads folder. Sort them into subfolders by type: Invoices, Receipts, Contracts, and Other. Use the text inside each PDF to decide which subfolder it belongs in.
Do not delete anything. Only move files into the new subfolders.
Before you finish, show me a short summary that lists what you moved and where, so I can confirm it looks right. ```
3
### Watch it work and review the result
Spark shows its progress in real time. Because you asked for a summary and told it not to delete anything, you can verify the result before trusting it with bigger jobs. Once you are confident, you can turn a repeated version of this into a [skill or schedule](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-tasks-skills-schedules/).
**Start read-only or reversible.** For your first few tasks, ask Spark to move rather than delete, and to summarize before finishing. Spark is an experimental agent and can make mistakes, so keep early tasks low-risk and easy to undo.
## Best Gemini Spark use cases on Mac
The Mac app shines at the desktop chores that eat your time but never feel worth doing manually. These are strong starting points that use local files:
Tame a messy Downloads folder
Have Spark sort files into labelled subfolders by type or project, and rename them to a consistent pattern so you can actually find things.
Turn invoices into a live budget
Point Spark at a folder of saved invoices and ask it to build a Google Sheet of totals, then schedule it to update the sheet as new invoices arrive.
Summarize a folder of documents
Ask Spark to read every file in a project folder and produce a Google Doc summary, so you can brief yourself before a meeting in minutes.
Standardize file names
Rename photos, exports, or receipts to a clear convention like `2026-07_client_invoice.pdf` across a whole folder at once.
Pull data out of local files
Extract figures, dates, or contact details scattered across saved documents and collect them into one clean spreadsheet.
Keep a folder tidy on autopilot
Set a schedule so Spark files new downloads into the right place regularly, keeping your desktop organized without you touching it.
Here is a ready-to-run prompt for the invoice-to-budget workflow. Replace the folder path with your own, then paste it into the Spark tab.
``` Read every invoice PDF in my connected folder "Finance/Invoices" on this Mac. For each invoice, pull out the vendor name, invoice date, invoice number, and total amount.
Create a new Google Sheet called "Invoice Tracker" with one row per invoice and columns for Vendor, Date, Invoice Number, and Amount. Add a total row at the bottom.
Do not change or delete any of the original files. When you are done, tell me how many invoices you found and list any you could not read so I can check them myself. ```
Want more ideas built around business outcomes rather than file chores? See [the best Gemini Spark use cases for business](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-use-cases/). If you regularly turn invoice or CSV data into summaries, the free [AI Spreadsheet Insights Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/spreadsheet-insights/) gives you a reusable analysis workflow.
## Mac settings and keyboard shortcuts to know
The Mac app includes **Gemini Spark settings** for managing which folders Spark can reach, its data, and how it runs. A few things are worth checking on day one:
* **Connected folders** — use the Connected folders area in Spark to add or disconnect the folders Spark can access. Keep this list as small as possible. * **Gemini Spark settings** — turn Spark on or off and manage its remote browser and code-execution data. * **Usage limits** — Spark uses compute-based limits based on task complexity, and Gemini notifies you as you approach your limit. * **Keyboard shortcuts** — Option + Space opens the mini window, Option + Shift + Space opens the full app, and pressing both Command keys shares the active window as context.
## How local file access works — and how to use it safely
Giving an AI agent access to your local files is a real decision, so it is worth knowing exactly what Spark can — and cannot — do on your Mac.
**Important:** Gemini Spark can edit, share, and permanently delete files in connected folders when instructed. Google says Spark creates temporary backup files, but they are deleted when you begin another task or after 24 hours. Do not rely on Spark’s temporary backups as your only recovery method. Keep important files backed up separately, and supervise any task that moves, overwrites, shares, or deletes files.
* **Folder-level control.** Spark only has access to the specific directories you explicitly connect. It cannot roam your whole drive. * **Explicit permissions.** Local folder access and full-page browser reading require Accessibility permission that you grant in macOS System Settings, and you can revoke it anytime. * **You approve the scope.** Connect one folder to start, review what Spark did, and expand only when you trust the workflow. * **Never paste secrets.** Google warns you not to type passwords, payment details, or other sensitive information directly into a Spark task thread.
**Good habit:** treat connected folders like keys. Give Spark the smallest folder that gets the job done, and disconnect folders you are no longer automating.
## Start a Mac task from another device
**Remote control is now live.** From another device signed into the same Google Account, open Gemini, switch to **Spark**, select **Add > Computer**, and choose your Mac. You can type or speak the task, read past Spark chats, and use quick or media controls without sitting in front of the computer.
Your Mac must have the Gemini app set up and running, and you must accept the Spark Mac terms. The Mac and the device you are using must be on the same Wi-Fi network or have Bluetooth turned on and be linked. Cloud-based schedules can continue when your device is off; tasks that act on local Mac files need the Mac available with Gemini running.
## Gemini Spark on Mac vs. web vs. mobile
Spark is the same agent everywhere, but the surface changes what it can reach. Here is how the Mac app compares.
| Capability | Mac app | Web | Mobile | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Directly act on local files and folders | Yes | No | No | | Connected apps and Google Workspace | Yes; availability can vary by account and rollout | Yes | Yes | | Remote browser and cloud tasks | Yes | Yes | Yes | | Global keyboard shortcut to summon Gemini | Yes | No | No | | Start a Mac task remotely | Target of the task | Look for **Add > Computer** on the device | Yes |
If your work involves files that live on your computer, the Mac app is the version to use. If your work is entirely in the cloud, the web and mobile versions do the same job.
## Spark not showing on Mac?
If you installed the Gemini Mac app but do not see a Spark tab, run through these quick checks:
* **Update the app.** Install any available updates for the Gemini Mac app, then relaunch it. * **Confirm the account.** Sign in with the exact personal Google Account that owns your Spark plan (Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US), not a work, school, or secondary account. * **Check the plan.** Spark needs Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro if you are in the US — not the free plan. * **Check your country and settings.** Spark on Mac is available where Gemini Spark is available and needs Keep Activity turned on. Google AI Ultra supports all Gemini Apps languages; Google AI Pro access in the US is English only. * **Check your Mac.** You need an Apple silicon Mac on macOS Sequoia (15.0) or later.
Still stuck? The full requirement-by-requirement checklist, excluded-country list, and account fixes are on the [Gemini Spark availability guide](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-availability/).
## Frequently asked questions about Gemini Spark on Mac
Is Gemini Spark available on Mac?
Yes. Google launched Gemini Spark in beta inside the Gemini app for macOS on June 30, 2026, starting in the United States. Google’s current Mac help documentation says Spark on Mac is available where Gemini Spark is available, for eligible subscribers aged 18 and over on Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US.

Go to gemini.google/mac, select Download for macOS, open the .dmg file, and drag Gemini into your Applications folder. Launch it, install any available updates, sign in with the personal Google Account that has your Spark plan (Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US), and open the Spark tab in the sidebar. Then grant Accessibility permission and connect a folder.

No. Spark only has access to the specific folders you explicitly connect, and desktop access requires Accessibility permission that you grant in macOS System Settings. You can remove folders or revoke permission at any time.
Do I need to keep my Mac on for Spark tasks?

Yes. Remote control is now available. Keep the Gemini app running on your Mac, sign into the same Google Account on both devices, and connect them over the same Wi-Fi network or by linked Bluetooth. On your phone, open Spark and choose **Add > Computer** to select the Mac.
Does Gemini Spark on Mac cost extra?
No separate Mac fee. Spark on Mac is included with an eligible paid plan: Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro if you are in the US. See the [availability guide](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/gemini-spark-availability/) for current pricing and plan details.

Yes, if Gemini Spark is available in your country and your account meets Google’s requirements. The macOS beta launched first in the United States, but Google’s current Mac documentation says Spark on Mac can be used where Gemini Spark is available.

The Mac app provides direct access to the local folders you connect and can summon Gemini with a global keyboard shortcut. Another supported device can start a task on that connected Mac remotely, but the local file action still happens through the Mac app and its approved folder access.

item.text: The 10 Best Claude Fable 5 Website Prompts for SEO & Sales Claude Fable 5 is at its most valuable right now for one specific job: building your website. From July 20, 2026, Fable 5 is included in Max and Team Premium plans at 50% of limits, while Pro and Team Standard move to usage credits — so on any plan, Fable 5 time is worth rationing. The smartest way to spend it is not on random one-off answers — it’s on Claude Fable 5 website prompts that produce reusable assets: SEO pages, landing pages, and sales pages you can ship, reuse, and turn into repeatable skills. This guide gives you the best website prompts for each, ready to copy, paste, and adapt. New to the model? Read What Claude Fable 5 Is first. Want the general library instead of website-specific prompts? See The 15 Best Claude Fable 5 Prompts. This page assumes you know what Fable 5 is and want to build website assets with it before the credit window changes. What are the best Claude Fable 5 website prompts? The best Claude Fable 5 website prompts are structured, reusable workflows that produce a full website asset in one pass — an SEO landing page blueprint, a lead-gen landing page, a long-form sales page, or a pricing page — instead of a vague paragraph. Each one gives Fable 5 a clear goal, your real context, and an exact output format, so you build the page once and rerun the same prompt for every future page. Start with the master template below, then jump to the prompt you need. The 10 website prompts in this guide cover SEO pages, landing pages, sales pages, and pricing pages — each one built to produce a reusable page asset, not a one-off answer. Why Website Prompts Are the Smartest Use of Your Fable 5 Window Most people spend a powerful model on throwaway questions. That’s the wrong move for Claude Fable 5, especially with a usage-credit window closing in. Fable 5 is built for complex, long-context, multi-step work — exactly what a good website page requires. A homepage, an SEO landing page, or a sales page isn’t one sentence; it’s positioning, structure, proof, objections, search intent, metadata, and copy, all working together. So instead of asking Fable 5 for “some website copy,” use this window to produce reusable website assets: a page you can publish today and a prompt you can rerun for the next page, and the one after that. That’s the difference between spending credits and investing them. Every prompt below is written so the output is a finished page asset and the prompt itself becomes a template you keep. One-Off Outputs vs Reusable Website Assets Here’s the mindset shift in one table. The left column is how most people burn a Fable 5 session. The right column is how you turn the same session into something you use for months. One-off output (avoid) Reusable website asset (do this) “Write me a hero headline.” A homepage messaging prompt that returns positioning, hero, subhead, CTA, and section order you can reuse for any page. “Give me SEO tips for this page.” An SEO landing page blueprint: H1, section outline, FAQ, internal links, and metadata mapped to one keyword and intent. “Make my sales page better.” A full sales page structure plus a repeatable conversion-audit prompt you rerun after every change. Copy lives in a chat you’ll lose next week. Copy and the prompt both saved as a skill you rerun for the next page in seconds. Credit-smart tip Fable 5 is a heavier model, so batch related website work into one longer session instead of many small prompts, and reserve it for the structural pages here. Use a lighter model like Sonnet 5 for quick edits. For a full strategy, read The 9 Best Ways To Reduce Claude Fable 5 Credit Usage. The Master Claude Fable 5 Website Prompt Template Every website prompt in this guide is built on the same skeleton. Learn it once and you can write a strong Fable 5 prompt for any page type. Paste this template and fill in the brackets, or jump to a ready-made prompt below. You are an expert website strategist and conversion copywriter. Produce a complete, ready-to-build [page type: SEO landing page / homepage / sales page] for my business. - Business: [what you sell and to whom] - Primary audience: [who this page is for and what they want] - Offer: [the product, service, or action this page drives] - Brand voice: [e.g. friendly, beginner-first, no hype] - Primary keyword or goal: [target keyword OR the single action the page should drive] [Paste existing copy, notes, competitor URLs, proof, testimonials, or product details] - One clear primary call to action - Match the brand voice above - No invented claims, stats, or testimonials — mark anything I must supply as [NEEDS INPUT] 1. Clarify the page's single goal and target reader in one sentence. 2. Map the page section by section, in order. 3. Draft the copy for each section. 4. Add the metadata and any FAQ the page needs. 5. Flag anything missing that would make the page stronger. - Page goal (one sentence) - Section-by-section outline with a short label for each - Full draft copy under each section - Suggested SEO title and meta description - List of anything marked [NEEDS INPUT] Before finishing, confirm the primary CTA is obvious, the value is clear in the first screen, and no claims are invented. Tell me the single highest-impact thing to finalize first. Best for: Turning one target keyword and search intent into a complete, ready-to-build SEO page — H1, section outline, on-page copy, FAQ, internal links, and metadata. Use when: You want a page that ranks and reads well, not a keyword-stuffed draft. You are an expert SEO strategist and on-page content designer. Design a complete SEO landing page that can rank for one primary keyword and satisfy its search intent. - Primary keyword: [keyword] - Search intent: [informational / commercial / transactional] - Business and offer: [what you sell and the action this page should drive] - Audience: [who is searching and what they need] [Paste any existing page copy, competitor URLs, or notes. If none, say "none".] - Write for the reader first, then optimize — no keyword stuffing - One primary CTA - Do not invent statistics or testimonials — mark as [NEEDS INPUT] 1. Confirm the dominant search intent in one sentence. 2. Propose the single best H1. 3. Outline the page as ordered H2 and H3 sections that fully answer the intent. 4. Draft concise on-page copy under each section. 5. Write 4 to 6 FAQ questions real searchers ask, with short answers. 6. Suggest 3 to 5 internal links by descriptive anchor text. - Search intent (one sentence) - Recommended H1 - Full H2/H3 outline with draft copy - FAQ block (question + short answer) - Internal link suggestions (anchor + where it should point) - SEO title and meta description Confirm every section maps to the search intent and the primary keyword appears naturally in the H1, first 100 words, one H2, and the meta description. Tell me which section to write in full first for the biggest ranking impact. Paste one or two competitor URLs that already rank so Fable 5 can spot gaps and cover what they miss instead of repeating them. What output to expect: A build-ready page blueprint: intent, H1, full outline with copy, FAQ, internal links, and metadata. Next step: Run the SEO Metadata & Schema Prompt to finish the title tag, meta description, and FAQ schema. Best for: The metadata layer that decides your click-through rate and how AI answer engines quote your page — title tags, meta descriptions, and FAQ content designed to be extractable. Use when: A page is written but its metadata is an afterthought, or you want it quotable by AI search. You are an expert technical SEO and metadata specialist. Write the metadata and answer-ready content that improve this page's click-through rate and make it easy for AI answer engines to quote. - Page topic and primary keyword: [topic / keyword] - Page URL or working title: [url or title] - Audience: [who this page is for] [Paste the page copy or a summary of its main sections] - SEO title under about 60 characters, meta description under about 155 characters - Lead every FAQ answer with a direct, quotable first sentence - No invented facts 1. Summarize the page's core promise in one sentence. 2. Write 3 SEO title options and note which you recommend and why. 3. Write 2 meta description options with the keyword used naturally. 4. Write 5 FAQ questions with concise, self-contained answers. 5. Suggest which single fact or definition on the page is most likely to be quoted by an AI answer engine, and how to phrase it clearly. - Core promise (one sentence) - 3 SEO titles (recommended one marked) - 2 meta descriptions - 5 FAQ items (question + answer) - One "most quotable" sentence, rewritten for clarity Confirm each FAQ answer makes sense on its own, out of context, and the title reflects what the page actually delivers. Tell me which title to test first. Ask Fable 5 to output the FAQ as a plain question-and-answer list so you can paste it into a Rank Math FAQ block or your own schema. Confirm current field limits before publishing. What output to expect: Ready-to-paste titles, meta descriptions, and a quotable FAQ block built for both classic search and AI answers. Next step: Feed the FAQ into the Objection-Handling & FAQ Prompt to make sure it also answers buying objections. Best for: A reusable brief that turns a topic into a blog post or resource page designed to rank and support your money pages. Use when: You publish content regularly and want a consistent, repeatable brief instead of starting each post from scratch. You are an expert SEO content strategist. Create a complete content brief for one article that can rank and support my main offer pages. - Topic or primary keyword: [topic / keyword] - Business and offer this content should support: [offer] - Audience and their knowledge level: [audience] [Paste any related pages you already have so we can internal-link and avoid overlap] - Match the search intent, not just the keyword - Recommend internal links to my existing pages by descriptive anchor - No fabricated data 1. State the search intent and the one question the article must answer. 2. Recommend the working title and H1. 3. Outline the article as ordered H2/H3 headings. 4. For each heading, list the key points to cover. 5. List entities, subtopics, and related questions to include for topical depth. 6. Suggest internal links and one clear CTA to a money page. - Search intent + core question - Title and H1 - Full heading outline with key points - Entities and related questions to cover - Internal links (anchor + target) - Recommended CTA Confirm the brief would let a writer produce the article without guessing, and that it links to at least one relevant offer page. Tell me whether to draft the introduction or the highest-intent section first. List the URLs of pages you want the article to link to so Fable 5 can build the internal-linking plan around your real site. What output to expect: A writer-ready brief with intent, outline, key points, entities, internal links, and a CTA. Next step: Turn the brief into a saved skill so every future post starts here — see turning these prompts into a skill. Best for: Fixing the most-visited page on your site — clear positioning, a hero that states who it’s for and why it matters, and a single obvious CTA. Use when: Visitors land on your homepage and can’t tell what you do in five seconds. You are an expert brand messaging strategist and homepage copywriter. Create clear homepage messaging and a hero section that tells the right visitor what I do, who it's for, and why it matters — fast. - Business: [what you sell] - Ideal visitor: [who you most want to reach] - Main action you want them to take: [book, buy, sign up, download] - Brand voice: [tone] [Paste current homepage copy or describe your offer in a few sentences] - The hero must be understandable in about five seconds - One primary CTA, with an optional secondary CTA - No jargon or hype; no invented claims 1. Write a one-sentence positioning statement: for [who], we [do what] so they [outcome]. 2. Draft 3 hero headline options with matching subheadlines. 3. Recommend the primary CTA wording and one secondary CTA. 4. Propose the homepage section order below the hero. 5. Note the single proof element that would most increase trust. - Positioning statement - 3 hero options (headline + subheadline), recommended one marked - Primary and secondary CTA wording - Homepage section order - One recommended proof element Confirm a first-time visitor would understand the offer and the next step without scrolling. Tell me which hero option to publish first and what to test against it. Give Fable 5 one competitor homepage and ask it to make your positioning clearly different, not just cleaner. What output to expect: A positioning statement, three hero options, CTA wording, and a section order you can build immediately. Next step: Run the Landing Page A/B Variant Prompt to generate versions to test. Best for: A focused landing page for one offer — a lead magnet, webinar, waitlist, free trial, or booking — with copy for every section. Use when: You’re running traffic to a dedicated page and need it to convert on one action. You are an expert direct-response landing page copywriter. Write a complete lead-gen landing page focused on one conversion action. - Offer: [lead magnet, webinar, trial, booking, waitlist] - Who it's for: [audience and the problem it solves] - The one action: [what a visitor should do] - Brand voice: [tone] [Paste details about the offer, benefits, and any proof you have] - Keep the page focused on the single action — no competing links - Lead with the visitor's problem and desired outcome, not your features - Mark any proof, stat, or testimonial you need from me as [NEEDS INPUT] 1. State the one action and the promise in a sentence. 2. Draft the hero: headline, subheadline, and CTA. 3. Draft the "what you get" and "who it's for" sections. 4. Draft a short benefits or outcomes section. 5. Draft an objection-reducing section and a proof section. 6. Draft a closing CTA that restates the promise. - One-line promise - Hero (headline + subheadline + CTA) - What you get / who it's for - Benefits or outcomes - Objection reducer + proof (with [NEEDS INPUT] where needed) - Closing CTA Confirm the page drives only one action and the value is clear before any scroll. Tell me the one section most likely to lose conversions and how to strengthen it. Tell Fable 5 the traffic source (ads, email, social) so it matches the page’s message to what the visitor just clicked. What output to expect: Full landing page copy, section by section, focused on one conversion action. Next step: Pressure-test it with the Sales Page Conversion Audit Prompt before you send traffic. Best for: Generating distinct, testable variants of a hero or CTA — different angles, not reworded copies. Use when: A page gets traffic and you want structured options to A/B test. You are an expert conversion optimization strategist. Create distinct, testable variants of my hero and CTA based on different persuasion angles. - Page and offer: [what the page sells or asks for] - Audience: [who lands here] - Current hero and CTA: [paste them] - Each variant must use a genuinely different angle, not reworded copy - Keep every variant honest — no invented claims - One clear CTA per variant 1. Name 3 persuasion angles that fit this audience (for example: outcome, speed, risk-reversal, status quo cost, social proof). 2. For each angle, write a hero headline, subheadline, and CTA. 3. Explain in one line what each variant is testing. 4. Recommend which variant to run first and why. - 3 angles named - 3 variants (headline + subheadline + CTA) - One-line test hypothesis per variant - Recommended first test Confirm the three variants are meaningfully different and each could plausibly win. Tell me what metric to watch and how long to run the first test. Add your current conversion rate or traffic volume so Fable 5 can suggest a realistic test order and priority. What output to expect: Three angle-based variants with a test hypothesis for each and a recommended starting test. Next step: Once a winner emerges, feed it back into the Homepage Messaging Prompt to align the rest of the site. Best for: A complete long-form sales page structure and draft — the kind of multi-section page Fable 5’s long-context strength is genuinely suited to. Use when: You’re selling a product, course, service, or offer that needs more than a short page to convert. You are an expert long-form sales page copywriter. Write a complete long-form sales page that moves a warm reader from interest to purchase. - Offer and price: [what you sell and the price] - Audience and core desire: [who buys and what they really want] - Main objections: [what makes them hesitate] - Brand voice: [tone] [Paste offer details, features, outcomes, guarantees, and any real testimonials or results] - Lead with the reader's desired outcome, not the feature list - Use only proof I provide — mark gaps as [NEEDS INPUT] - One primary offer and CTA, repeated at natural decision points 1. State the core promise and the transformation the offer delivers. 2. Draft the sales page section by section: hook, problem, promise, offer, what's included, benefits/outcomes, proof, objections, guarantee, pricing, FAQ, and final CTA. 3. Keep each section tight and skimmable with clear subheads. 4. Place the CTA at the hero, after the offer, and at the close. - Core promise (one sentence) - Full section-by-section draft with subheads - CTA wording (used at 3 points) - List of [NEEDS INPUT] items I must supply Confirm every claim is supported or marked for input, the offer is unmistakable, and a skimmer could still follow the argument from subheads alone. Tell me which section most needs real proof before this page goes live. Batch this in one Fable 5 session with your offer details already pasted in — a full sales page is exactly the multi-step work worth spending a Fable 5 session on. What output to expect: A full sales page draft with every section, CTA placement, and a clear list of proof you still need to add. Next step: Run the Sales Page Conversion Audit Prompt on the finished draft. Best for: A prioritized, specific fix list for a page that gets traffic but doesn’t convert — the reusable audit you rerun after every change. Use when: You have a live page and want targeted fixes, not a full rewrite. You are an expert conversion rate optimization consultant. Audit this page and give me specific, prioritized fixes to improve conversions. - Page purpose: [sell, sign up, book, download] - Audience: [who lands here and why] - Known performance: [traffic, conversion rate, drop-off point, if known] [Paste the full page copy, or describe each section in order] - Do not suggest a full rewrite unless the offer itself is unclear - Focus on clarity, proof, objection handling, and CTA - Every fix must be specific enough to implement today 1. Judge whether the offer is clear in the first screen. 2. Find proof gaps and where trust breaks down. 3. List the unanswered objections a skeptical buyer would have. 4. Review CTA wording, placement, and frequency. 5. Rank all fixes by likely impact. - Offer clarity (rated + why) - Proof gaps (list) - Unanswered objections (list) - CTA review (specific fixes) - Top 5 fixes in priority order Confirm no fix is vague — I should be able to act on each one without asking a follow-up. Tell me the single fix to make first if I only have 30 minutes. Paste real traffic or conversion numbers if you have them so Fable 5 can prioritize by likely impact instead of guessing. What output to expect: A ranked, specific fix list covering clarity, proof, objections, and CTA. Note: For a broader page audit including layout and UX, the general Fable 5 prompts library has a dedicated Website Design & UX Review Prompt. Best for: Surfacing the real objections a buyer has and turning them into a proof section and FAQ that also helps you get quoted in AI answers. Use when: A page explains the offer well but still loses people at the decision point. You are an expert conversion copywriter who specializes in objections and trust. Surface the real objections that stop my buyer and turn them into a proof section and an FAQ that reassures readers and reads well to AI answer engines. - Offer and price: [what you sell] - Audience: [who buys] - Known hesitations: [anything you already hear from prospects] [Paste the current page copy or offer details] - Base objections on this audience, not generic ones - Answer honestly; never dismiss a real concern - Keep every FAQ answer self-contained and quotable 1. List the top 6 objections this specific buyer would have. 2. For each, write a short, honest response that reduces the risk. 3. Turn the strongest 5 into FAQ questions with concise, standalone answers. 4. Recommend which objections deserve a visible proof element on the page. - Top 6 objections with responses - 5 FAQ items (question + self-contained answer) - Proof elements to add, mapped to specific objections Confirm each FAQ answer makes sense on its own and no response overpromises. Tell me which objection is costing me the most conversions and where to address it on the page. Paste real questions from sales calls, emails, or comments so the objections reflect what your buyers actually say. What output to expect: A ranked objection list, honest responses, a quotable FAQ, and proof elements mapped to each concern. Next step: Turn your top cost objections into a real page with the Pricing Page Prompt. Best for: Turning your pricing into a clear, decision-ready page — plan comparison, an obvious recommended tier, and the cost objections a buyer is silently asking before they reach checkout. Use when: Your offer is priced but the pricing page still reads like a spreadsheet instead of a sales tool. You are an expert pricing strategist and conversion copywriter. Write a complete pricing page that makes the right plan obvious and removes hesitation at the moment of decision. - Offer and pricing tiers: [list plans/tiers and prices, or a single price] - Audience: [who is deciding and what they compare you against] - Recommended plan: [the tier you want most buyers to pick, if any] - Brand voice: [tone] [Paste your plan details, features per tier, guarantee terms, and any competitor pricing you're aware of] - Make the recommended plan visually and logically obvious without pressure tactics - Answer the top 3 cost objections before the reader has to ask - No invented guarantees, refund terms, or comparisons — mark as [NEEDS INPUT] 1. State the pricing page's single goal and which plan you want most visitors to choose. 2. Draft the pricing header and a one-line value reminder above the plans. 3. Draft each plan's name, price, best-for line, and feature list. 4. Write the "why this plan" nudge for the recommended tier. 5. Draft a short FAQ answering cost, billing, and guarantee questions. 6. Draft the final CTA and any risk-reversal line beneath it. - Pricing page goal (one sentence) - Header + value reminder - Plan-by-plan breakdown (name, price, best-for, features) - Recommended-plan nudge - Pricing FAQ (question + short answer) - Final CTA + risk-reversal line Confirm the recommended plan is obvious within the first screen and every likely cost objection is answered before the FAQ. Tell me which plan is underperforming and the single change most likely to fix it. Tell Fable 5 which plan you actually want most customers to pick — it will design the visual and copy emphasis around that tier instead of presenting every option equally. What output to expect: A complete pricing page: header, plan-by-plan breakdown, a nudge toward your recommended tier, a cost FAQ, and a closing CTA. Next step: Run the Sales Page Conversion Audit Prompt on the finished pricing page before it goes live. Turn These Website Prompts Into a Reusable Skill A prompt is one request.
