What Is an AI Agent Skill? Examples and How It Works

An AI agent library is an organized collection of reusable resources for building or using AI agents. The term is not standardized: in practice, it commonly refers to developer frameworks, prebuilt agent platforms and templates, or ready-to-use AI skills and workflows. The right type depends on whether you want to build with code, configure an agent inside a platform, or run a repeatable skill in Claude, Claude Cowork, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark.

The phrase “AI agent library” means different things to different people. A developer hears a code framework. An automation builder hears a catalog of prebuilt agents. A business owner hears ready-to-use skills they can copy and run today. All three readings are valid — this guide explains the difference in plain language, so you can tell which type actually fits what you’re trying to do.

Quick answer

What is an AI agent library, in one sentence?

An AI agent library is an organized collection of reusable resources for building, configuring, or using AI agents, such as developer frameworks, prebuilt agent templates, AI skills, and repeatable no-code workflows.

What Is an AI Agent Library?

To unpack the term, split it in two. An AI agent is an AI system configured to pursue a goal across one or more steps, often using tools, context, memory, or human approval along the way. If that idea is new, our guide to what AI agents are explains it from the beginning. A library is an organized, reusable collection you draw from instead of building everything yourself.

Put them together and an AI agent library is a collection of reusable resources for building or using AI agents. The reason the phrase feels slippery is that there is no single, standardized meaning — the “resources” sit at very different levels. Some are raw code for engineers. Some are prebuilt automations you configure inside a platform. And some are plain-language skills and workflows a non-technical person can copy and run in the AI tool they already use.

Three Common Types of AI Agent Libraries

In practice, people use the phrase “AI agent library” for three common kinds of resources. They can be distinguished by how much the user needs to build, configure, or simply use.

1. Developer framework libraries

These are code libraries and runtimes used to build and orchestrate custom AI agents. They are made for developers and, in most cases, require programming and infrastructure. Examples include:

  • LangGraph — a low-level orchestration framework and runtime for building long-running, stateful agents and workflows.
  • CrewAI — a framework for creating specialized agents with roles, goals, tools, collaborative crews, and structured flows.
  • Microsoft Agent Framework — Microsoft’s multi-language agent SDK and successor to agent-development work previously associated with AutoGen and Semantic Kernel.
  • OpenAI Agents SDK — a lightweight SDK for building agentic applications using tools, handoffs, guardrails, sessions, human approval, and tracing.

If you are a software team building a custom, self-hosted agent system, this is your world. If you are not writing code, the next two types get you the outcome without the engineering.

2. Prebuilt agent platforms and template libraries

These platforms let you assemble agents and automations from prebuilt pieces, usually on a visual canvas, rather than from code. They reduce the amount of traditional programming, but they are not effortless — depending on what you build, you may still need to connect applications, configure credentials, set permissions, map data, test actions, maintain workflows, and monitor errors. Common examples:

  • n8n — an automation tool with AI agent nodes and a large template library; it can be self-hosted.
  • Make — “Make AI Agents” build reusable agents visually inside its canvas.
  • Zapier — Zapier Agents automate tasks across its connected-app ecosystem.
  • Microsoft Copilot Studio — a low-code builder for custom Microsoft 365 copilots and agents.

This tier suits operations people and automation builders who are comfortable wiring tools together. Your agents live inside that platform, and you own the setup and upkeep.

3. Ready-to-use AI skill and workflow libraries

This is the most accessible category for people who want a repeatable result without building an agent application or configuring an automation platform. A skill packages instructions, steps, examples, formatting rules, and sometimes supporting files for a focused task. For a more detailed definition of the individual unit, see what an AI agent skill is. These libraries include:

  • Platform-native skills for Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark, where supported by the user’s account, plan, device, and region.
  • Skills used inside agentic workspaces such as Claude Cowork.
  • Downloadable instruction packages that can be adapted for more than one supported AI platform.
  • Copy-and-use prompts and repeatable workflows for people who do not have access to a platform-native skills feature.

These resources usually require no custom application development or separate agent hosting. Users still need to install them correctly, check compatibility, review included files and permissions, and update them when an AI platform changes.

AI Agents Library specializes in this third category — ready-to-use AI skills and workflows for business owners, creators, and beginners. To compare the strongest starting points by task and platform, see our ranking of the best AI Skills.

Framework vs Platform vs Skill vs Workflow

Here is the whole landscape on one screen. Read down the “Typical technical setup” column if you only care about one thing.

Comparison of AI agent frameworks, platforms, skills, workflows, and prompt libraries
Resource What it provides Best for Typical technical setup
Agent framework Code and orchestration components to build agents Developers building custom systems Programming and infrastructure
Agent platform / template A partly or fully configured agent inside a platform Faster deployment, automation builders Platform configuration; sometimes code
AI agent skill Reusable instructions for one specific capability Adding a focused capability to your AI Usually no custom development
No-code workflow Saved steps for completing a repeatable task Beginners and business users Visual or natural-language configuration
Prompt library Individual prompts for one-off outputs Simple, single-step results None beyond the AI chat tool

Which Type of AI Agent Library Is Right for You?

Match the library to how you actually work, not to the most impressive-sounding option.

  • Software developers and engineering teams building a custom, self-hosted agent → a framework library (LangGraph, CrewAI, Microsoft Agent Framework).
  • Automation builders and operations teams comfortable wiring apps together → a prebuilt agent platform (n8n, Make, Zapier, Microsoft Copilot Studio).
  • Business owners, beginners, creators, and solo operators who want results without building or hosting a system → a ready-to-use skill and workflow library like this one.

The simple rule

If you don’t want to build, host, or configure an agent system, you want the ready-to-use skills and workflows tier. It gives you the repeatable result with the least technical setup, inside the AI tool you already use.

What a Good AI Agent Library Should Include

Whichever type you choose, a trustworthy library makes it easy to use its resources safely and correctly. Look for:

  • Clear classification — it tells you whether each item is a framework, platform, skill, or prompt.
  • Supported platforms — which tools each resource works in, and any account, plan, or region requirements.
  • Setup instructions — plain steps to install or run it, not just a code dump.
  • Example inputs and outputs — so you know what “good” looks like before you start.
  • Stated limitations — what it does not do, written honestly.
  • Security and privacy notes — what data it touches and what to keep out.
  • Human-review guidance — where a person should check the result before it goes out.

Where AI Agents Library Fits

Disclosure: AI Agents Library is the publisher of this guide. AI Agents Library is a ready-to-use, no-code AI skills and workflow library. It is not a developer framework or a visual automation platform. The library provides downloadable skills, supporting files, examples, prompts, setup guides, and repeatable workflows for practical work.

The skills are designed for supported environments including Claude, Claude Cowork, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark, with platform-specific setup instructions where the installation process or available capabilities differ.

The library is intended for business owners, creators, freelancers, teams, and beginners who want to use a repeatable AI process without developing or hosting an agent system. Current categories include website design, research, email, content, planning, documents, data, and business operations.

How to Use an AI Agent Library Safely

The safety bar rises with how much power you hand the agent. A copy-paste skill that drafts an email is low-risk; a platform agent that can send emails or move money is not. Wherever you land, keep these habits:

  • Review the output before you use it — treat the AI as a fast first draft, not a final authority.
  • Protect private information — don’t paste passwords, card numbers, or sensitive client data into a skill.
  • Check what it can act on — for platforms and agents, confirm exactly which tools and permissions they hold.
  • Verify factual claims — anything a reader will rely on gets a human check.
  • Require human approval for consequential actions — sending, publishing, paying, or deleting.

Frequently asked questions

Is an AI agent library the same as an agent framework?

No. An agent framework is one type of AI agent library — the developer, code-based type such as LangGraph or CrewAI. “AI agent library” is the broader phrase that also covers prebuilt agent platforms and templates, and ready-to-use skill and workflow libraries. A framework is a subset, not a synonym.

Do I need to know how to code to use an AI agent library?

It depends on the type. Framework libraries usually require coding. Prebuilt platforms like n8n or Make need configuration rather than programming. Ready-to-use skill and workflow libraries — the kind we publish — typically need no code: you copy a skill and run it inside ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini Spark. If you don’t code, start there.

Are AI agent libraries free?

Some are free and others require payment. Many developer frameworks are open source, although models, hosting, storage, integrations, and maintenance may still cost money. Agent-building platforms commonly charge by subscription, usage, or connected task. AI Agents Library includes free skills, while advanced collections, premium access, support, or All Access membership may be offered separately. Check each resource page for its current access terms.

What is the difference between an AI skill and an AI agent?

A skill is a single, reusable capability — a saved set of instructions for one specific task. An AI agent is the larger system that can pursue a goal across one or more steps, often using several skills and tools along the way. In short: a skill is a part, an agent is the whole. See what an AI agent skill is for the full breakdown.

Can ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini use the same skills?

The underlying process often can be adapted, but the same package may not install or behave identically everywhere. A well-designed skill’s instructions, steps, examples, and output format can often be reused across Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark. However, each platform has different file support, tools, permissions, availability requirements, and installation procedures. Skills used in Claude Cowork may also rely on capabilities or connected resources that are not available in a standard chat. Check the compatibility information and platform-specific setup instructions provided with each skill.

How do I know whether an agent template is safe?

Check what it is allowed to do before you run it. Read which apps and permissions it connects to, keep sensitive data out of it, and require a human to approve any consequential action — sending, publishing, paying, or deleting. A safe library states these limits plainly; if a template hides what it can access, don’t run it.

Which type of AI agent library is best for beginners?

Ready-to-use skill and workflow libraries. They usually need little setup and no code — you copy a skill and run it in the AI tool you already use. Beginners and business owners get a repeatable result quickly, without learning a framework or configuring a platform. Browse the free AI skills library to start.

Is AI Agents Library a developer framework?

No. AI Agents Library is a ready-to-use, no-code AI skills and workflow library for business owners, creators, and beginners — not a code framework like LangGraph or CrewAI. It provides helpful AI skills, prompts, setup guides, and no-code workflows for supported tools such as Claude, Claude Cowork, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark, so you can get results without building an agent system from scratch.

Do not rewrite what is not broken. - You cannot browse the web or open the user's live page — work only from what the user pastes in. - Return copy only. Do not write HTML or CSS. Do not claim a specific conversion rate or result.
## Output format
### Above the Fold Benefit-led H1, one-sentence subhead, one CTA button label.
### The Problem 2-3 sentences that name the audience's frustration and pivot to the offer.
### The Offer What's included, in plain bullets, with the price or terms stated once.
### Proof The proof layout, with every real proof point marked [YOUR INPUT].
### Objections 3-4 real hesitations, each answered in two honest sentences.
### Final CTA A closing block that repeats the single action and lowers friction.
### One Conversion Improvement The single highest-impact change, and why it matters for this offer.
### Needs Your Input Every [YOUR INPUT] placeholder you used, listed so nothing ships unfilled.
If the user has not given you the offer, audience, and single action, ask for those three before writing anything. ```
**Not sure which to use?**
Start with **Format 1** — you’ll have a page written in ten minutes with nothing to set up. Install **Format 2** once you know you’ll run more than one launch, because that’s where writing the same shape every time actually pays. Copied the SKILL.md already? Here’s exactly where it goes in each platform:
[Where It Goes →](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/landing-page/#install)
Part 3 of 5
## Where the SKILL.md goes in Claude, ChatGPT & Gemini Spark
**In Claude it becomes a custom Skill (or a `SKILL.md` file under `.claude/skills/`); in Gemini Spark it goes on the Skills page; in ChatGPT it goes into a Project’s instructions, or a native Skill if you have access.**
### AI skill or prompt? Which one beginners should use
Both formats above contain the same instructions — the only difference is whether your AI has to be reminded every time. Use the prompt for a one-off page, install the SKILL.md once you’re running launches and want the same structure without pasting anything.
For the full breakdown of how a skill differs from a prompt and from a full AI agent, read [what an AI agent skill is](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/what-is-an-ai-agent-skill/). If you already have a landing page prompt you like, [turning a prompt into an AI skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/turn-a-prompt-into-an-ai-skill/) takes about ten minutes.
The prompt works everywhere with no setup. If you copied the **SKILL.md** file instead, here’s exactly where it goes in each platform. Landing page copy is persuasion-heavy long-form work, so we lead with Claude — but it writes a page the same way in all three.
**Claude**
1. Copy the SKILL.md block above. 2. **Claude app:** create a custom Skill and paste it in — name it `landing-page`. 3. **Claude Code:** save it as `.claude/skills/landing-page/SKILL.md` in your project, or `~/.claude/skills/landing-page/SKILL.md` to use it everywhere. The folder name is what names the skill. 4. Say “help me write a landing page” — the `description` line lets Claude fire it on its own.
Prefer no setup? The prompt above works in the Claude app right now. [Browse all free Claude skills →](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/claude/)
**ChatGPT**
1. **Have ChatGPT Skills?** Create a new Skill and paste the SKILL.md in — the description makes it fire on its own. 2. **No Skills access? Use a Project — it’s the quick way.** New Project → Project menu → **Project settings**. 3. Paste everything _below_ the `---` frontmatter into the Project instructions. Projects ignore frontmatter, so the description is just for you. 4. Keep each launch in its own Project so the offer and voice stay consistent across the page and the follow-ups.
Projects work on free and paid plans; native Skills are in beta on eligible work and education plans. New to this? Read [how to use ChatGPT skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-use-chatgpt-skills/) or [how to create a ChatGPT skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-chatgpt-skill/). [Browse all free ChatGPT skills →](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/chatgpt/)
**Gemini Spark**
1. Open Gemini Spark and go to the **Skills** page. 2. Choose **Create manually**, or upload the SKILL.md file directly. 3. Use `landing-page` as the name and paste the `description` line from the file into the description field — that field is what makes Spark apply it automatically. 4. Select the skill with `/` or `@`, or just describe the offer you’re launching.
Gemini Spark skills currently require Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US, plus an eligible account and region. [Browse all free Gemini Spark skills →](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/gemini-spark/)
**Nail the single action and the whole page tightens**
Of the inputs, the single action does the most work — it decides the hero, the CTA, and what gets cut. “Reserve a seat” produces a different page than “download the free guide.” If you put two actions in that field, you’ll get a page that half-argues for both. Pick one, write it, then build the second page separately if you truly need both.
Part 4 of 5
## How to write a landing page in any AI tool
**Say "write my landing page," give it the offer, the audience and the single action you want, and answer the questions it asks before it writes.**
Once the SKILL.md is installed, just ask in plain language — “help me write a landing page.” Because of the `description` line, Claude and Gemini Spark can offer the skill on their own the moment you describe an offer you’re launching. In ChatGPT, open your launch Project and start a new chat.
* Open Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark and start a new chat. * Ask it to write your landing page in plain language, or select the skill. * Give it one offer, one audience, and — above all — one action. * Answer its two or three clarifying questions before it writes anything. * Read “Needs Your Input,” go get those real quotes and numbers, and re-run.
**New to AI assistants?** Start with our [free AI setup guides](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/setup-guides/) to get Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark ready first — then come back and add this skill in minutes.
Try this starter request — copy it, paste it, then fill in your details:
``` Help me write a landing page.
OFFER: [what you're selling, in one sentence] AUDIENCE: [who it's for and the problem they arrive with] SINGLE ACTION: [one action only — buy, book a call, reserve a seat, start a trial] PRICE OR TERMS: [the price, or "free", or the terms] PROOF I HAVE: [real quotes, numbers, guarantees — or "none yet"]
Ask me clarifying questions first if anything above is vague. Use only what I've told you — write [YOUR INPUT] instead of inventing any quote, number, or result, and list every gap at the end. One page, one action. ```
Part 5 of 5
Free copy/paste skill or guided help
## Free Copy/Paste Skill vs Free 7-Day Trial
**Everything you need to run this one skill is free either way.** The free skill gives you the Landing Page workflow immediately — as a prompt or a SKILL.md file. The free 7-day trial gives you guided access to more AI skills and beginner-friendly support inside the Academy.
| Included | Free Copy/Paste Skill | Free 7-Day Trial | | --- | --- | --- | | Landing Page prompt | Yes | Yes | | Ready-made SKILL.md file with description | Yes | Yes | | Hero, problem, offer, proof, objections, CTA | Yes | Yes | | Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark install steps | Yes | Yes | | No credit card required for the starter skill | Yes | No, cancel anytime | | Hands-on setup help | No | Yes | | Access to more AI skills | No | Yes | | Help adapting it to your offer and voice | No | Yes |
Free copy/paste skill
Point this free skill at the offer you’ve been meaning to launch. It comes in two formats — pick the one that matches how often you run pages:
**Prompt** = nothing to install, works right now. **SKILL.md** = install once, then just say “help me write a landing page”.
or
### Want the complete version? Unlock this skill + our full AI skills library free for 7-days today
[Start My Free 7-Day Trial →](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/checkout/?edd_action=add_to_cart&download_id=5466&checkout_source=skill-article&origin=landing-page&placement=6-closing-offer)
Cancel anytime. No coding skills required.
## What to do next?
Consider joining our [AI Agents Academy community](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/academy/) to **instantly access our full library of premium AI skills, step-by-step setup support, and a growing group of business owners building with AI every day** — free for 7 days. Stay as long as it’s useful, or leave whenever you want, no questions asked.
## Landing Page skill: frequently asked questions
Is this AI landing page skill free?
**Yes.** Both the copy-paste prompt and the SKILL.md file are completely free. Optional reusable features may depend on the AI tool and plan you use. ChatGPT Projects are available on free and paid plans, Claude skills are available when code execution is enabled, and Gemini Spark skills currently require Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US.
How is this different from the Website Builder skill?
Different job, different input. The [Website Builder skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/website-builder/) takes your whole business and plans a 5-to-7 page site — the map, the hero, and lighter copy across every page. This Landing Page skill takes **one offer** and goes deep on **one page**: full problem, offer, proof, and objection handling, all pointed at a single action. Use the Builder to decide what your pages are; use this to make one of them actually sell.
What do I paste in to get a good page?
Three things are essential: the offer, who it’s for, and the **single** action you want. Price or terms, any real proof you have, and three to five words of brand voice make it sharper but aren’t required. The single action is the one that changes everything — a page built for “reserve a seat” reads differently from one built for “download the guide.”
Will it invent testimonials, numbers, or guarantees?
**No.** It uses only what you provide. Where a page genuinely needs a proof point you didn’t give it — a testimonial, a result, a guarantee — it writes `[YOUR INPUT]` and lists every gap at the end under “Needs Your Input.” A fabricated testimonial on a live sales page is a real legal and trust problem, so the skill is specifically instructed to leave an honest hole instead.
Does it write the SEO title and meta description too?
**No — on purpose, so the two skills don’t overlap.** This skill writes the on-page copy: the hero, the sections, the CTA. When the page is done, paste it into the [SEO Metadata skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/seo-metadata/) to get the title tag, meta description, URL slug, and image alt text. Keeping them separate means each one does its job properly instead of half-doing both.
Can it look at my live page or a competitor’s page?
**No.** It works only from what you paste into the chat — it can’t browse the web or open a URL, and it won’t pretend otherwise. If you want it to build on an existing draft, paste the copy itself rather than a link. For competitor angles, run the [Competitor Research skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/competitor-research/) first and bring its notes.
Which AI tools does it work with?
Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark all work. Landing page copy is persuasion-heavy long-form writing, so Claude is a natural home, but the prompt writes a page identically in all three. The SKILL.md file installs as a saved skill in Claude and Gemini Spark; in ChatGPT you can use a Project or native Skills.

item.text: What is an AI Agent Skill? – AI Agents vs Skills An AI agent skill is a reusable package of instructions and optional resources that teaches an AI system how to perform one specific task. Unlike a one-time prompt, a skill preserves the process, inputs, rules, and output format. An agent can load that skill when relevant, then use it as one capability within a larger workflow. AI used to feel simple: you typed a prompt and got an answer. Now people are hearing terms like skills, agents, tasks, schedules, workflows, Gems, Claude Skills, and AI coworkers. This guide breaks down the difference in plain language so you know when to use a prompt, when to save a skill, and when a full AI agent actually makes sense. An AI agent skill is a reusable package of instructions and optional resources that teaches an AI system how to perform one specific task. Unlike a one-time prompt, a skill preserves the process, inputs, rules, and output format. An agent can load that skill when relevant, then use it as one capability within a larger workflow. Simple example: input a meeting transcript; the skill follows a saved review process and outputs a summary, decisions, owners, deadlines, and a follow-up email in the same format every time. Prompts, skills, and AI agents each solve different problems: prompts help you ask better questions, skills create reusable workflows, and AI agents work toward larger goals. What is an AI agent skill? An AI agent skill is a repeatable workflow or instruction set — not a single message, but a small system you build once and reuse. A well-built skill usually captures: Terminology used on this site AI agent skill is the broad concept: a reusable capability or task process. Agent Skill refers to the portable open format built around a SKILL.md file. Platform labels such as ChatGPT Skills, Claude Skills, and Gemini Spark Skills describe each product’s implementation. The goal — what the task is actually for. The inputs — what you’ll hand the AI each time (notes, files, a link, a transcript). The process — the steps the AI should follow, in order. The output format — what the finished result should look like. The examples — what a good result actually looks like. The rules — tone, sources, and things to avoid. The review step — what you check before you trust or use the output. Once that’s written down, you’re not starting from a blank page every time. You’re running a process. Some everyday examples of AI agent skills: A weekly business brief An AI news brief A client follow-up email Content repurposing Competitor research A meeting summary Google Docs organization Each of these could be a single prompt you rewrite from memory every time — or a skill you build once, save, and reuse whenever the task comes up again. AI Skill vs Prompt vs GPT vs AI Agent These four ideas are related, but they solve different problems. A prompt is a one-time request. An AI agent skill is a reusable process. A custom GPT is a named ChatGPT experience with persistent configuration. An AI agent is the broader system that can plan, use tools, and work toward a goal. Concept Simple definition Best for Example Level of automation Prompt A one-time instruction you type into an AI tool A single question, quick draft, or one-off task “Write a follow-up email after this meeting.” None — you repeat it manually every time AI agent skill A reusable process the AI can follow for a specific task Tasks you repeat often and want done the same way “Use my client follow-up workflow to draft this email.” Partial — you trigger it, but the steps stay consistent Custom GPT A named version of ChatGPT configured with persistent instructions, knowledge, and capabilities A reusable assistant experience that people deliberately open or share “Open the Client Communications GPT and draft the follow-up.” Varies — the GPT provides the container; its tools and instructions determine what it can do AI agent A system that can plan, use tools, take steps, and complete work toward a goal Multi-step work across tools, apps, or schedules “Check my inbox, find leads that need follow-up, and draft emails for me to approve.” Higher — it plans and acts across steps, usually with approval checkpoints AI skill vs workflow: what is the difference? An AI skill and an AI workflow are closely related, but they are not always the same thing. A skill is the reusable capability or process the AI can follow. A workflow is the larger sequence of steps where that skill may be used. For example, a client follow-up skill may draft the email. The full workflow may include checking your notes, choosing who needs follow-up, drafting the message, reviewing it, and then sending it after approval. Term Simple meaning Example Prompt One instruction “Summarize this meeting.” Skill A reusable capability or task process A saved meeting summary process with format, rules, and review steps. Workflow A sequence of steps, often using one or more skills Upload transcript → summarize meeting → extract action items → draft follow-up email. Agent The system that can run steps, use tools, remember context, and ask for approvals An AI system that checks the meeting notes, drafts follow-ups, and asks before sending. Prompt vs skill vs agent: a simple business example Here’s the same task — following up with a potential client — handled three different ways. 1 Prompt “Write a follow-up email after this meeting.” One instruction. You supply the context in the moment, and you’ll explain it again next time. 2 AI agent skill “Use my client follow-up workflow: review the last conversation, identify the next step, write three subject lines, draft a warm but clear email, include one CTA, and create a second follow-up if they do not reply.” A repeatable process. The steps, tone, and structure stay the same every time you use it. 3 AI agent “Check my CRM or inbox, find leads that need follow-up, draft the right email for each one, and ask me to approve before sending.” A broader system. It finds the work and takes multiple steps — but still checks with you before anything sends. Notice what changed across the three versions. The prompt needs you to think it through every time. The skill remembers the process so you don’t have to. The agent goes a step further and finds the work itself — but it still asks for your approval before sending anything. That last part isn’t optional in a well-designed workflow: emails, publishing, deleting files, and anything touching sensitive data should stay behind a human review step, no matter how capable the tool is. What can an AI agent skill include? A strong skill is more than a clever prompt. It captures the way you want a task done, repeatedly — including the small judgment calls you’d otherwise make yourself each time. Depending on the task, a skill can include: Skill name Purpose When to use it Required inputs Step-by-step process Output format Tone or style rules Examples Source rules Safety or approval rules Review checklist Platform notes You don’t need every field to start Most beginner skills only need a goal, the inputs, a short process, and an output format. Add rules, examples, and approval steps once you see what the AI tends to get wrong. How Do AI Agent Skills Work? Discover: the AI system sees each available skill’s name and description. Match: your request explicitly names a skill, or the system decides the request matches its description. Load: the system reads the full instructions and only the supporting resources needed for the task. Run: it applies the saved steps, rules, examples, and output format to your current input. Return and review: you receive the defined output and check any facts, approvals, or edge cases the skill flags. This staged loading is often called progressive disclosure: lightweight metadata is visible first, while full instructions and resources load only when relevant. How AI agent skills work in Claude, Gemini Spark, Gemini Gems, and ChatGPT The idea is the same everywhere — save the process once, reuse it every time — but each tool implements it a little differently. Claude Skills Claude Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads when relevant. See Anthropic’s official Claude Skills help page, then compare concrete workflows in the Claude skills library. Gemini Spark Skills In Gemini Spark, Skills define how Spark should handle repeated work, Tasks define what it should do, and Schedules define when or under what conditions it runs. See Google’s official Gemini Spark page, then browse Gemini Spark skill examples. Gemini Gems Gems are saved, custom AI experts inside Gemini — you set the instructions once, and Gemini reuses them every time you open that Gem. They’re useful for repeatable behavior and tone, but a Gem is not the same thing as a full autonomous agent: it doesn’t plan multi-step work or act across tools on its own. ChatGPT Personal Skills are reusable, shareable workflows that can include instructions, examples, code, and supporting resources. Once installed, ChatGPT can select a relevant skill automatically. See how to use ChatGPT Skills, or browse ChatGPT skill examples. When should you use an AI skill instead of a prompt? Use a skill when: You do the task more than once You want consistent output You have a preferred process You need the AI to follow rules You want to save setup time You want a repeatable business workflow You want to train AI on your style, structure, or standards If you only need one quick answer, use a prompt. If you keep repeating the same kind of task, turn it into a skill. Want examples of reusable AI workflows? Browse the AI agent skills library to see ready-made skill structures for follow-ups, briefs, research, content, and other repeatable tasks. When should you use a full AI agent instead? A full AI agent is worth the extra complexity when a task needs more than one saved process. Look for these signs: The work needs planning across several unknown steps, not just one fixed process It needs to use multiple tools or connected apps to finish the job It needs to remember state or context across a longer session It involves external apps, inboxes, or accounts beyond a single chat It needs built-in approval checkpoints before taking real-world actions It should run on a schedule or in response to a condition, not just on request OpenAI’s own framing is a useful reference here: agents are systems that combine models, tools, and instructions to complete multi-step work on their own — see the OpenAI Agents SDK documentation for the technical version of that definition. Start smaller than you think For most beginners, it’s smarter to start with a skill before trying to automate the whole workflow. Prove the process works manually first, then decide whether it’s worth wiring into a full agent. Beginner examples of AI agent skills Use these as starting points. Each one is a task you likely already repeat — the only difference is whether you’re solving it from scratch each time or running a saved process. Skill What it does Best input → output Best platform fit AI News Agent Skill Tracks updates across Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, and Google Workspace and turns them into one clean brief. A date range (e.g. “last 24 hours”) → a formatted brief with sources and action steps. Claude, Gemini Spark, or ChatGPT Weekly Business Brief Skill Reviews the week’s notes, metrics, or updates and produces one leadership-ready summary. Weekly notes or a few bullet updates → a structured brief with priorities and next steps. Claude or Gemini Spark Client Follow-Up Email Skill Reviews the last conversation and drafts a warm, clear follow-up with subject lines and a CTA. Last email or call notes → a ready-to-review email plus a no-response follow-up. Claude, Gemini, or ChatGPT Social Media Post Generator Skill Turns one idea or update into several platform-ready posts. A topic or existing post/blog → multiple post variations with hooks and captions. ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini Spark Competitor Research Skill Reviews a competitor’s site, pricing, or messaging and summarizes what stands out. A competitor URL or notes → a comparison summary with strengths, gaps, and ideas. Claude or Gemini Spark Meeting Notes Skill Turns raw notes or a transcript into a clean summary with decisions and action items. Raw notes or a transcript → a structured summary with owners and next steps. Claude, ChatGPT, or NotebookLM Google Docs Organizer Skill Reviews a messy set of docs or folders and proposes a clearer structure. A folder or file list → a proposed folder structure and renaming plan. Gemini Spark or Claude Email Triage Skill Reviews an inbox and sorts messages by urgency and required action. A batch of emails or inbox summary → a prioritized action list. Gemini Spark or ChatGPT Content Repurposing Skill Turns one piece of content into multiple formats without starting from scratch. A blog post or transcript → social posts, an email, and short-form captions. Claude, ChatGPT, or NotebookLM Weekly Planning Skill Reviews last week’s progress and helps plan the coming week’s priorities. Last week’s notes or task list → a prioritized weekly plan with focus blocks. Claude or Gemini Spark How to create your first AI agent skill This is a short preview, not the full walkthrough. Here’s the basic shape: 1 Pick one repeated task Choose something you already do weekly or more often. 2 Define the final output Decide exactly what “done” looks like. 3 Write the process step by step Tell the AI how you want it done, not just what you want back. 4 Add rules, examples, and review criteria Include tone, formatting, sources, and what needs your approval. 5 Test it, improve it, and save it Run it, fix what’s off, then save it so you can reuse it next time. Using Claude? Follow our complete guide on how to create a Claude skill, including the required SKILL.md structure, installation steps, and testing process. Want a beginner-friendly starting point for your first AI agent skill? Browse ready-made AI agent skills to compare today’s step-by-step preview with reusable skill examples you can adapt. Common mistakes when creating AI agent skills Mistake Better habit Making the skill too broad Scope it to one task with one clear output, not “help with my business.” Writing a vague prompt instead of a process Spell out the steps in order, not just the end result you want. Forgetting examples Include at least one example of what a good output looks like. Not defining the output format State the exact format, sections, and length you expect back. Giving the AI too much access too early Start narrow — one folder, one inbox, or one data source at a time. Skipping human review Always check the output before sending, publishing, or acting on it. Trying to automate sensitive tasks before testing Test on low-risk, reversible tasks before touching anything sensitive. Creating too many skills instead of improving one Perfect one skill you actually use before you build the next one. Final takeaway A prompt helps you ask once. An AI agent skill helps you repeat a process. An AI agent helps you delegate a larger outcome. For most beginners, the best place to start is not with a complex AI agent. It is with one simple AI agent skill for a task they already repeat every week. If you would rather begin with a proven workflow, compare the best AI Skills for business owners and choose the task closest to work you already repeat. What is an AI agent skill? An AI agent skill is a reusable package of instructions and optional resources that teaches an AI system how to perform one specific task. It preserves the process, inputs, rules, and output format so an agent can load that capability when relevant. If you want to build one, start with the complete AI skill guide. Is an AI skill the same as a prompt? No. A prompt is a one-time instruction you type in. A skill is a saved, repeatable process built from one or more prompts, plus rules, examples, and an expected output format. For the practical process, see how to turn a prompt into an AI skill. Is an AI skill the same as an AI agent? No. A skill is a repeatable instruction set for one type of task. An AI agent is the broader system that can plan, use tools, take multiple steps, and sometimes work across apps or schedules — often using one or more skills along the way. What is the difference between an AI skill and an AI workflow? An AI skill is the reusable capability or process the AI can follow. An AI workflow is the larger sequence of steps where that skill may be used, often alongside other skills, tools, approvals, or schedules. Can I use AI agent skills without coding? Yes. An instruction-only skill can be written in plain language. Code is optional and is useful only when the workflow needs a deterministic script or integration. Use the platform guides for ChatGPT Skills, Claude Skills, and Gemini Spark Skills when you are ready to make one. Can I use the same AI skill in Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT? The core instructions can usually transfer because they are mostly plain language. ChatGPT and Claude both document support for the open Agent Skills format, while Gemini Spark has its own product workflow. Always check scripts, tools, permissions, and platform-specific metadata before moving a skill. What is the easiest AI skill to create first? Pick a task you already repeat weekly with a clear, low-risk output — such as a weekly business brief, meeting summary, or follow-up email. Avoid starting with sensitive or irreversible tasks. What is the difference between Claude Skills and Gemini Spark Skills? Both let you save reusable instructions, but they live inside different systems. Claude Skills are a native Claude feature that can include instructions, scripts, and resources. Gemini Spark Skills work alongside Spark’s Tasks and Schedules to run repeated work automatically. Check each platform’s official documentation for current details. What is the difference between Gemini Gems and AI agent skills? A Gem is a saved custom AI expert inside Gemini. An AI agent skill is a reusable task capability with a defined process, inputs, rules, and output. A Gem can hold repeatable instructions, but it is a product-specific assistant container rather than the portable Agent Skills file format. Should I start with prompts, skills, or agents? Start with prompts for one-off tasks. Move to a skill once you notice yourself repeating the same type of task with the same instructions; this prompt-to-skill guide shows the bridge. Consider a full AI agent only after a skill works well and the task genuinely needs planning, tool use, or multiple steps. Are AI agent skills safe to use? A skill can contain instructions, reference files, and executable code, so review its source, requested tools, and permissions before installing it. Keep sensitive actions — such as sending emails, publishing content, deleting files, or accessing private data — behind a human approval step, especially while testing.

  • The goal — what the task is actually for.
  • The inputs — what you’ll hand the AI each time (notes, files, a link, a transcript).
  • The process — the steps the AI should follow, in order.
  • The output format — what the finished result should look like.
  • The examples — what a good result actually looks like.
  • The rules — tone, sources, and things to avoid.
  • The review step — what you check before you trust or use the output.

Once that’s written down, you’re not starting from a blank page every time. You’re running a process. Some everyday examples of AI agent skills:

  • A weekly business brief
  • An AI news brief
  • A client follow-up email
  • Content repurposing
  • Competitor research
  • A meeting summary
  • Google Docs organization

AI Skill vs Prompt vs GPT vs AI Agent

These four ideas are related, but they solve different problems. A prompt is a one-time request. An AI agent skill is a reusable process. A custom GPT is a named ChatGPT experience with persistent configuration. An AI agent is the broader system that can plan, use tools, and work toward a goal.

Prompt A one-time instruction you type into an AI tool A single question, quick draft, or one-off task “Write a follow-up email after this meeting.” None — you repeat it manually every time
AI agent skill A reusable process the AI can follow for a specific task Tasks you repeat often and want done the same way “Use my client follow-up workflow to draft this email.” Partial — you trigger it, but the steps stay consistent
Custom GPT A named version of ChatGPT configured with persistent instructions, knowledge, and capabilities A reusable assistant experience that people deliberately open or share “Open the Client Communications GPT and draft the follow-up.” Varies — the GPT provides the container; its tools and instructions determine what it can do
AI agent A system that can plan, use tools, take steps, and complete work toward a goal Multi-step work across tools, apps, or schedules “Check my inbox, find leads that need follow-up, and draft emails for me to approve.” Higher — it plans and acts across steps, usually with approval checkpoints

AI skill vs workflow: what is the difference?

An AI skill and an AI workflow are closely related, but they are not always the same thing. A skill is the reusable capability or process the AI can follow. A workflow is the larger sequence of steps where that skill may be used.

For example, a client follow-up skill may draft the email. The full workflow may include checking your notes, choosing who needs follow-up, drafting the message, reviewing it, and then sending it after approval.

Prompt One instruction “Summarize this meeting.”
Skill A reusable capability or task process A saved meeting summary process with format, rules, and review steps.
Workflow A sequence of steps, often using one or more skills Upload transcript → summarize meeting → extract action items → draft follow-up email.
Agent The system that can run steps, use tools, remember context, and ask for approvals An AI system that checks the meeting notes, drafts follow-ups, and asks before sending.

1 Prompt

“Write a follow-up email after this meeting.”

2 AI agent skill

“Use my client follow-up workflow: review the last conversation, identify the next step, write three subject lines, draft a warm but clear email, include one CTA, and create a second follow-up if they do not reply.”

A repeatable process. The steps, tone, and structure stay the same every time you use it.

3 AI agent

“Check my CRM or inbox, find leads that need follow-up, draft the right email for each one, and ask me to approve before sending.”

A broader system. It finds the work and takes multiple steps — but still checks with you before anything sends.

  4. Run: it applies the saved steps, rules, examples, and output format to your current input.
  5. Return and review: you receive the defined output and check any facts, approvals, or edge cases the skill flags.

Use a skill when:

  • You do the task more than once
  • You want consistent output
  • You have a preferred process
  • You need the AI to follow rules
  • You want to save setup time
  • You want a repeatable business workflow
  • You want to train AI on your style, structure, or standards

If you only need one quick answer, use a prompt. If you keep repeating the same kind of task, turn it into a skill.

A full AI agent is worth the extra complexity when a task needs more than one saved process. Look for these signs:

  • It needs to remember state or context across a longer session
  • It involves external apps, inboxes, or accounts beyond a single chat
  • It needs built-in approval checkpoints before taking real-world actions
  • It should run on a schedule or in response to a condition, not just on request

Common mistakes when creating AI agent skills

Mistake Better habit
Making the skill too broad Scope it to one task with one clear output, not “help with my business.”
Writing a vague prompt instead of a process Spell out the steps in order, not just the end result you want.
Forgetting examples Include at least one example of what a good output looks like.
Not defining the output format State the exact format, sections, and length you expect back.
Giving the AI too much access too early Start narrow — one folder, one inbox, or one data source at a time.
Skipping human review Always check the output before sending, publishing, or acting on it.
Trying to automate sensitive tasks before testing Test on low-risk, reversible tasks before touching anything sensitive.
Creating too many skills instead of improving one Perfect one skill you actually use before you build the next one.

Final takeaway

A prompt helps you ask once. An AI agent skill helps you repeat a process. An AI agent helps you delegate a larger outcome.

For most beginners, the best place to start is not with a complex AI agent. It is with one simple AI agent skill for a task they already repeat every week.

If you would rather begin with a proven workflow, compare the best AI Skills for business owners and choose the task closest to work you already repeat.

Frequently asked questions

What is an AI agent skill?

An AI agent skill is a reusable package of instructions and optional resources that teaches an AI system how to perform one specific task. It preserves the process, inputs, rules, and output format so an agent can load that capability when relevant. If you want to build one, start with the complete AI skill guide.

Is an AI skill the same as a prompt?

No. A prompt is a one-time instruction you type in. A skill is a saved, repeatable process built from one or more prompts, plus rules, examples, and an expected output format. For the practical process, see how to turn a prompt into an AI skill.

Is an AI skill the same as an AI agent?

No. A skill is a repeatable instruction set for one type of task. An AI agent is the broader system that can plan, use tools, take multiple steps, and sometimes work across apps or schedules — often using one or more skills along the way.

What is the difference between an AI skill and an AI workflow?

An AI skill is the reusable capability or process the AI can follow. An AI workflow is the larger sequence of steps where that skill may be used, often alongside other skills, tools, approvals, or schedules.

Can I use AI agent skills without coding?

Yes. An instruction-only skill can be written in plain language. Code is optional and is useful only when the workflow needs a deterministic script or integration. Use the platform guides for ChatGPT Skills, Claude Skills, and Gemini Spark Skills when you are ready to make one.

Can I use the same AI skill in Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT?

The core instructions can usually transfer because they are mostly plain language. ChatGPT and Claude both document support for the open Agent Skills format, while Gemini Spark has its own product workflow. Always check scripts, tools, permissions, and platform-specific metadata before moving a skill.

What is the easiest AI skill to create first?

Pick a task you already repeat weekly with a clear, low-risk output — such as a weekly business brief, meeting summary, or follow-up email. Avoid starting with sensitive or irreversible tasks.

What is the difference between Claude Skills and Gemini Spark Skills?

Both let you save reusable instructions, but they live inside different systems. Claude Skills are a native Claude feature that can include instructions, scripts, and resources. Gemini Spark Skills work alongside Spark’s Tasks and Schedules to run repeated work automatically. Check each platform’s official documentation for current details.

What is the difference between Gemini Gems and AI agent skills?

A Gem is a saved custom AI expert inside Gemini. An AI agent skill is a reusable task capability with a defined process, inputs, rules, and output. A Gem can hold repeatable instructions, but it is a product-specific assistant container rather than the portable Agent Skills file format.

Should I start with prompts, skills, or agents?

Start with prompts for one-off tasks. Move to a skill once you notice yourself repeating the same type of task with the same instructions; this prompt-to-skill guide shows the bridge. Consider a full AI agent only after a skill works well and the task genuinely needs planning, tool use, or multiple steps.

Are AI agent skills safe to use?

A skill can contain instructions, reference files, and executable code, so review its source, requested tools, and permissions before installing it. Keep sensitive actions — such as sending emails, publishing content, deleting files, or accessing private data — behind a human approval step, especially while testing.

| Mistake | Better habit | | --- | --- | | Making the skill too broad | Scope it to one task with one clear output, not “help with my business.” | | Writing a vague prompt instead of a process | Spell out the steps in order, not just the end result you want. | | Forgetting examples | Include at least one example of what a good output looks like. | | Not defining the output format | State the exact format, sections, and length you expect back. | | Giving the AI too much access too early | Start narrow — one folder, one inbox, or one data source at a time. | | Skipping human review | Always check the output before sending, publishing, or acting on it. | | Trying to automate sensitive tasks before testing | Test on low-risk, reversible tasks before touching anything sensitive. | | Creating too many skills instead of improving one | Perfect one skill you actually use before you build the next one. |
## Final takeaway
A prompt helps you ask once. An AI agent skill helps you repeat a process. An AI agent helps you delegate a larger outcome.
For most beginners, the best place to start is not with a complex AI agent. It is with one simple **AI agent skill** for a task they already repeat every week.
If you would rather begin with a proven workflow, compare the [**best AI Skills for business owners**](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-ai-skills/) and choose the task closest to work you already repeat.
## Frequently asked questions
What is an AI agent skill?
An AI agent skill is a reusable package of instructions and optional resources that teaches an AI system how to perform one specific task. It preserves the process, inputs, rules, and output format so an agent can load that capability when relevant. If you want to build one, start with the [complete AI skill guide](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-an-ai-skill/).
Is an AI skill the same as a prompt?
No. A prompt is a one-time instruction you type in. A skill is a saved, repeatable process built from one or more prompts, plus rules, examples, and an expected output format. For the practical process, see how to [turn a prompt into an AI skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/turn-a-prompt-into-an-ai-skill/).
Is an AI skill the same as an AI agent?
No. A skill is a repeatable instruction set for one type of task. An [AI agent](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/ai-agents/) is the broader system that can plan, use tools, take multiple steps, and sometimes work across apps or schedules — often using one or more skills along the way.
What is the difference between an AI skill and an AI workflow?
An AI skill is the reusable capability or process the AI can follow. An AI workflow is the larger sequence of steps where that skill may be used, often alongside other skills, tools, approvals, or schedules.
Can I use AI agent skills without coding?
Yes. An instruction-only skill can be written in plain language. Code is optional and is useful only when the workflow needs a deterministic script or integration. Use the platform guides for [ChatGPT Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-chatgpt-skill/), [Claude Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-claude-skill/), and [Gemini Spark Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-gemini-spark-skill/) when you are ready to make one.
Can I use the same AI skill in Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT?
The core instructions can usually transfer because they are mostly plain language. ChatGPT and Claude both document support for the open Agent Skills format, while Gemini Spark has its own product workflow. Always check scripts, tools, permissions, and platform-specific metadata before moving a skill.
What is the easiest AI skill to create first?
Pick a task you already repeat weekly with a clear, low-risk output — such as a weekly business brief, meeting summary, or follow-up email. Avoid starting with sensitive or irreversible tasks.
What is the difference between Claude Skills and Gemini Spark Skills?
Both let you save reusable instructions, but they live inside different systems. [Claude Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-claude-skill/) are a native Claude feature that can include instructions, scripts, and resources. [Gemini Spark Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-gemini-spark-skill/) work alongside Spark’s Tasks and Schedules to run repeated work automatically. Check each platform’s official documentation for current details.
What is the difference between Gemini Gems and AI agent skills?
A Gem is a saved custom AI expert inside Gemini. An AI agent skill is a reusable task capability with a defined process, inputs, rules, and output. A Gem can hold repeatable instructions, but it is a product-specific assistant container rather than the portable Agent Skills file format.
Should I start with prompts, skills, or agents?
Start with prompts for one-off tasks. Move to a skill once you notice yourself repeating the same type of task with the same instructions; this [prompt-to-skill guide](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/turn-a-prompt-into-an-ai-skill/) shows the bridge. Consider a full [AI agent](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/ai-agents/) only after a skill works well and the task genuinely needs planning, tool use, or multiple steps.
Are AI agent skills safe to use?
A skill can contain instructions, reference files, and executable code, so review its source, requested tools, and permissions before installing it. Keep sensitive actions — such as sending emails, publishing content, deleting files, or accessing private data — behind a human approval step, especially while testing.

item.text: Free AI Brand Voice Check Skill The free AI Brand Voice Check skill Paste in any draft — an email, a post, a page — along with your brand voice rules, and get it back checked line by line and rewritten to sound like you. A voice-match score, the lines that drifted, and an on-brand version. Same standard for everything you publish. Copy it as a prompt, or install it as a real SKILL.md file. This Brand Voice Check skill is a free AI brand voice checker that takes any draft plus your voice rules and returns it audited and rewritten to sound like you — the lines that drifted off-brand, why they drifted, and an on-brand version you can ship. Paste in an email, a post, a landing section, or a proposal, and it holds every line to the same standard. It applies the same rules to everything, so the intern’s email and your sales page get judged by one voice, not two. That’s the difference between a skill and a one-off prompt: the standard is saved, so consistency stops depending on who wrote the draft or how tired they were. It checks and rewrites for voice — it does not judge whether a page converts (that’s a different skill) and it does not invent facts to make a line sound better. Use it as a copy-paste prompt in any AI chat, or install the ready-made SKILL.md file so it runs on command in Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark. No coding required. The Brand Voice Check skill takes a draft and your brand voice rules and returns four things: a voice-match score, the specific lines that are off-brand with a short reason for each, an on-brand rewrite of the whole draft, and any brand words it should have used but didn’t. It works on any text — an email, a social post, a web page, a proposal — not just website copy. It answers one question: “does this sound like us?” It does not judge whether a page converts or a headline sells — that’s the Website Copy Refresh skill’s job. It applies the rules; it does not create them — if you don’t have voice rules yet, the Brand Style Guide skill writes them first. It uses only your rules and your draft: it never invents a statistic, quote, or claim to make a sentence land better, and it won’t send or publish anything — it hands you a rewrite to approve. Two ways to get the Brand Voice Check skill Any draft checked in about five minutes Landing page copy, SEO metadata, competitor research, email, meeting notes Brand Voice Check skill: what it needs and what it returns What it isA free AI skill — a reusable set of instructions — that checks any draft against your brand voice rules and rewrites what’s off. It comes as a copy-paste prompt and as a ready-made SKILL.md file. Who it’s forAnyone publishing on behalf of a brand — yourself, a VA, or a team — who needs everything to sound like the same person wrote it. What you give itTwo inputs — your brand voice rules (or the guide from the Brand Style Guide skill), and the draft you want checked. What you get backA voice-match score out of ten with the reason, every off-brand line quoted with the rule it breaks and a rewrite, any brand words the draft should have used but skipped, the full draft rewritten on-brand with the facts unchanged, and anything you need to decide. What it will not doIt answers "does this sound like us?" — not "does this page convert?" (that’s the Website Copy Refresh skill). It applies rules; it does not invent them (that’s the Brand Style Guide skill). It never changes a fact to fit the voice. Time to first draftAbout five minutes per draft, on any text — an email, a post, a page, or a proposal. Everything you publish sounds like the same company By the end of this AI skill guide, you’ll have the Brand Voice Check skill ready to use — as a copy-paste prompt in any AI chat, or installed as a SKILL.md file that runs on command. It handles the thing that quietly erodes a brand: the drift, where every email, caption, and page sounds a little different because a different person or a different mood wrote it. Run drafts through this and they all sound like you. VOICE CHECK — a launch email against a “plain, specific, a little dry” brand voice (example) Voice-match score: 6 / 10 — “The bones are right, but three lines slip into hype that your guide specifically avoids.” Off-brand line: “We’re thrilled to unveil a game-changing new experience!” → flagged: uses thrilled, unveil, game-changing — all on your avoid list. Rewritten: “New this week: a roast we’ve been working on for a while.” Same news, your actual voice. Full on-brand version: the whole email rewritten top to bottom, ready to paste — with your voice traits held on every line. Missed brand words: the draft never used batch or origin — two words your guide says are core to how you talk about coffee. Note: it did not touch the facts — the price, the date, and the offer are exactly as you wrote them. Only the voice changed. How to use the Brand Voice Check AI skill in 3 steps Pick a format, paste your voice rules and the draft, and read the off-brand lines before you take the rewrite. That’s the whole method — the detail is below. The Brand Voice Check skill is an AI skill — a reusable set of instructions. It comes in two formats below, and they contain the same thinking. Use the prompt if you want one draft checked in the next five minutes. Use the SKILL.md file if you want it on hand permanently, so every draft you or your team writes can be run through it. Copy the prompt for a one-off check, or copy the SKILL.md file to install it permanently. Both are below — same instructions, different packaging. Paste your draft + your voice rules Give it the draft and your brand voice rules. No rules yet? Build them once with the Brand Style Guide skill, then paste that guide in here every time. Read the flags, take the rewrite It shows you the score, the off-brand lines, and a full rewrite. Take the rewrite as-is, or tell it “keep line two, it’s fine” and re-run. It never changes your facts — only the voice. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark, add your draft and your voice rules at the bottom, and send. Works on free plans. Best for a quick one-off check. You are an expert brand editor. Your job is to check a draft against the brand's voice rules and return it rewritten to sound on-brand, changing the voice without changing the facts. PROCESS 1. Read the brand voice rules first. If the user did not provide any voice rules, ask for them before checking anything — do not invent a voice. Point them to the Brand Style Guide skill if they have none. 2. Read the draft and score how well it matches the voice, out of 10, with one honest line explaining the score. 3. Identify every line or phrase that is off-brand. For each, quote it, name which rule it breaks (a trait it misses, or a word from the avoid list), and give a rewritten version. 4. Note any brand words or phrases from the "use" list that the draft should have used but didn't. 5. Produce a full on-brand rewrite of the entire draft, holding every voice trait and respecting the use/avoid lists. 6. Keep the format and purpose of the draft intact — an email stays an email, a caption stays a caption. RULES - Change the VOICE, never the FACTS. Do not alter a price, date, claim, name, number, or offer. If a fact seems wrong, flag it — do not fix it. - Never invent a statistic, quote, testimonial, or claim to make a line sound better. - Judge voice only. Do not critique whether the page converts, whether the offer is good, or whether the CTA is strong — that is the Website Copy Refresh skill's job. Stay in your lane. - Use only the voice rules the user gives you. If the rules and the draft conflict, the rules win — that is the point of a voice check. - Do not send, post, or publish anything. Produce a rewrite for the user to approve. - If the draft is already on-brand, say so plainly and make only the small changes that genuinely help. Do not rewrite for the sake of rewriting. OUTPUT FORMAT ### Voice-Match Score X / 10, with one line explaining it. ### Off-Brand Lines Each: the quoted line, the rule it breaks, and a rewrite. ### Missed Brand Words Any "use" words or phrases the draft skipped. ### On-Brand Rewrite The full draft rewritten to match the voice, facts unchanged. ### Notes Anything the user should decide (a fact to verify, a rule that seems to conflict). MY VOICE RULES: [paste your brand voice rules, or the guide from the Brand Style Guide skill] MY DRAFT: [paste the email, post, page, or proposal you want checked] This is the same skill packaged as a proper SKILL.md — the format Claude and Gemini Spark use for saved skills. The description line at the top is the important part: it tells your AI when to run this on its own, so you can just say “check this against our brand voice” and it fires. Paste the whole block into a new file called SKILL.md, or straight into your platform’s skill instructions. --- name: brand-voice-check description: Check a draft against the brand's voice rules and return it rewritten to sound on-brand — a voice-match score, the off-brand lines with reasons, missed brand words, and a full on-brand rewrite, changing the voice without changing the facts. Use this when the user asks to check something against their brand voice, make a draft on-brand, or says does this sound like us, fix the tone, or make this match our voice. --- # Brand Voice Check When this skill runs, check a draft against the brand's voice rules and return it rewritten to sound on-brand, changing the voice without changing the facts. ## Process 1. Read the brand voice rules first. If the user did not provide any voice rules, ask for them before checking anything — do not invent a voice. Point them to the Brand Style Guide skill if they have none. 2. Read the draft and score how well it matches the voice, out of 10, with one honest line explaining the score. 3. Identify every line or phrase that is off-brand. For each, quote it, name which rule it breaks (a trait it misses, or a word from the avoid list), and give a rewritten version. 4. Note any brand words or phrases from the "use" list that the draft should have used but didn't. 5. Produce a full on-brand rewrite of the entire draft, holding every voice trait and respecting the use/avoid lists. 6. Keep the format and purpose of the draft intact — an email stays an email, a caption stays a caption. ## Rules - Change the voice, never the facts. Do not alter a price, date, claim, name, number, or offer. If a fact seems wrong, flag it — do not fix it. - Never invent a statistic, quote, testimonial, or claim to make a line sound better. - Judge voice only. Do not critique whether the page converts, whether the offer is good, or whether the CTA is strong — that is the Website Copy Refresh skill's job. Stay in your lane. - Use only the voice rules the user gives you. If the rules and the draft conflict, the rules win — that is the point of a voice check. - Do not send, post, or publish anything. Produce a rewrite for the user to approve. - You cannot browse the web or open a URL — work only from the draft and rules the user pastes in. - If the draft is already on-brand, say so plainly and make only the small changes that genuinely help. ## Output format ### Voice-Match Score X / 10, with one line explaining it. ### Off-Brand Lines Each: the quoted line, the rule it breaks, and a rewrite. ### Missed Brand Words Any "use" words or phrases the draft skipped. ### On-Brand Rewrite The full draft rewritten to match the voice, facts unchanged. ### Notes Anything the user should decide (a fact to verify, a rule that seems to conflict). If the user has not given you voice rules and a draft, ask for those two before checking anything. Start with Format 1 — you’ll have a draft checked in five minutes with nothing to set up. Install Format 2 once you know you’ll check drafts regularly, because that’s where running the same standard on everything actually pays. Copied the SKILL.md already? Here’s exactly where it goes in each platform: Both formats above contain the same instructions — the only difference is whether your AI has to be reminded every time. Use the prompt for a one-off check, install the SKILL.md once you’re checking drafts regularly and want the same standard without pasting anything. For the full breakdown of how a skill differs from a prompt and from a full AI agent, read what an AI agent skill is. If you already have a voice prompt you like, turning a prompt into an AI skill takes about ten minutes. The prompt works everywhere with no setup. If you copied the SKILL.md file instead, here’s exactly where it goes in each platform. Voice work rewards a careful reader, so we lead with Claude — but it checks a draft the same way in all three. Claude app: create a custom Skill and paste it in — name it brand-voice-check. Claude Code: save it as .claude/skills/brand-voice-check/SKILL.md in your project, or ~/.claude/skills/brand-voice-check/SKILL.md to use it everywhere. The folder name is what names the skill. Say “check this against our brand voice” — the description line lets Claude fire it on its own. Paste everything below the --- frontmatter into the Project instructions, and add your brand voice rules right under it. Then every draft you check in that Project already knows your voice — just paste and ask. Use brand-voice-check as the name and paste the description line from the file into the description field — that field is what makes Spark apply it automatically. Select the skill with / or @, paste your rules and a draft, and ask for the check. Save your voice rules once and this gets fast The check is only as good as the voice rules you feed it, so the real unlock is having those rules written down. The free skill gives you the Brand Voice Check workflow immediately — as a prompt or a SKILL.md file. The free 7-day trial gives you guided access to more AI skills and beginner-friendly support inside the Academy. Brand Voice Check prompt Yes Yes Voice score, off-brand flags, full rewrite Yes Yes Help wiring it to your saved brand rules No Yes Copy the Free Brand Voice Check Skill Point this free skill at the next thing you’re about to send or publish. It comes in two formats — pick the one that matches how often you check drafts: Prompt = nothing to install, works right now. SKILL.md = install once, then just say “check this against our brand voice”. Brand Voice Check skill: frequently asked questions Is this AI brand voice check skill free? Yes. Both the copy-paste prompt and the SKILL.md file are completely free. Optional reusable features may depend on the AI tool and plan you use. ChatGPT Projects are available on free and paid plans, Claude skills are available when code execution is enabled, and Gemini Spark skills currently require Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US. Do I need a brand style guide before I can use this? You need some voice rules, but they don’t have to be formal. Even three traits and a short “words we avoid” list will work. If you don’t have anything written down, build it once with the Brand Style Guide skill — it produces exactly the rules this skill reads — then paste that guide in here every time. Without any rules, this skill will ask for them rather than invent a voice for you. How is this different from the Website Copy Refresh skill? Different question entirely. This skill asks “does it sound like us?” — brand and voice consistency, on any text. The Website Copy Refresh skill asks “does this page convert?” — clarity, structure, and persuasion, on website pages. A landing page can be perfectly on-brand and still not sell, or sell well but sound like a different company. Run this for voice, run Refresh for performance; on an important page, run both. Will it change my facts or add things I didn’t say? No — this is a hard rule in the skill. It changes the voice, never the facts. Prices, dates, claims, names, and offers come through exactly as you wrote them, and it will never invent a statistic or testimonial to make a line sound better. If it spots a fact that looks wrong, it flags it for you to check rather than “fixing” it. And it never sends or publishes anything — you always get a rewrite to approve. Does it only work on website copy? No — that’s the point of it. It works on any text: emails, social captions, proposals, product descriptions, support replies, web pages. Anywhere your brand voice should be consistent, this holds the draft to the same rules. That’s also what keeps it distinct from the website-specific skills — voice is a layer that sits on top of everything you write, not just your site. Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark all work. Catching subtle voice drift rewards a careful reader, so Claude is a natural home, but the prompt checks a draft the same way in all three. The SKILL.md file installs as a saved skill in Claude and Gemini Spark; in ChatGPT you can use a Project — which is handy here, because you can store your voice rules right in the Project.

Brand Voice Check skill: frequently asked questions

Is this AI brand voice check skill free?

Yes. Both the copy-paste prompt and the SKILL.md file are completely free. Optional reusable features may depend on the AI tool and plan you use. ChatGPT Projects are available on free and paid plans, Claude skills are available when code execution is enabled, and Gemini Spark skills currently require Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US.

Do I need a brand style guide before I can use this?

You need some voice rules, but they don’t have to be formal. Even three traits and a short “words we avoid” list will work. If you don’t have anything written down, build it once with the Brand Style Guide skill — it produces exactly the rules this skill reads — then paste that guide in here every time. Without any rules, this skill will ask for them rather than invent a voice for you.

How is this different from the Website Copy Refresh skill?

Different question entirely. This skill asks “does it sound like us?” — brand and voice consistency, on any text. The Website Copy Refresh skill asks “does this page convert?” — clarity, structure, and persuasion, on website pages. A landing page can be perfectly on-brand and still not sell, or sell well but sound like a different company. Run this for voice, run Refresh for performance; on an important page, run both.

Will it change my facts or add things I didn’t say?

No — this is a hard rule in the skill. It changes the voice, never the facts. Prices, dates, claims, names, and offers come through exactly as you wrote them, and it will never invent a statistic or testimonial to make a line sound better. If it spots a fact that looks wrong, it flags it for you to check rather than “fixing” it. And it never sends or publishes anything — you always get a rewrite to approve.

Does it only work on website copy?

No — that’s the point of it. It works on any text: emails, social captions, proposals, product descriptions, support replies, web pages. Anywhere your brand voice should be consistent, this holds the draft to the same rules. That’s also what keeps it distinct from the website-specific skills — voice is a layer that sits on top of everything you write, not just your site.

Which AI tools does it work with?

Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark all work. Catching subtle voice drift rewards a careful reader, so Claude is a natural home, but the prompt checks a draft the same way in all three. The SKILL.md file installs as a saved skill in Claude and Gemini Spark; in ChatGPT you can use a Project — which is handy here, because you can store your voice rules right in the Project.

Score it out of 10, quote every off-brand line with the rule it breaks and a fix, then give me a full on-brand rewrite. Change the voice, not the facts — don't touch any price, date, or claim, and don't invent anything. ```
