## Brand Voice Check skill: frequently asked questions
Is this AI brand voice check skill free?
**Yes.** Both the copy-paste prompt and the SKILL.md file are completely free. Optional reusable features may depend on the AI tool and plan you use. ChatGPT Projects are available on free and paid plans, Claude skills are available when code execution is enabled, and Gemini Spark skills currently require Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US.
Do I need a brand style guide before I can use this?
You need some voice rules, but they don’t have to be formal. Even three traits and a short “words we avoid” list will work. If you don’t have anything written down, build it once with the [Brand Style Guide skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/brand-style-guide/) — it produces exactly the rules this skill reads — then paste that guide in here every time. Without any rules, this skill will ask for them rather than invent a voice for you.
How is this different from the Website Copy Refresh skill?
Different question entirely. This skill asks **“does it sound like us?”** — brand and voice consistency, on any text. The [Website Copy Refresh skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/website-copy-refresh/) asks **“does this page convert?”** — clarity, structure, and persuasion, on website pages. A landing page can be perfectly on-brand and still not sell, or sell well but sound like a different company. Run this for voice, run Refresh for performance; on an important page, run both.
Will it change my facts or add things I didn’t say?
**No — this is a hard rule in the skill.** It changes the voice, never the facts. Prices, dates, claims, names, and offers come through exactly as you wrote them, and it will never invent a statistic or testimonial to make a line sound better. If it spots a fact that looks wrong, it flags it for you to check rather than “fixing” it. And it never sends or publishes anything — you always get a rewrite to approve.
Does it only work on website copy?
**No — that’s the point of it.** It works on any text: emails, social captions, proposals, product descriptions, support replies, web pages. Anywhere your brand voice should be consistent, this holds the draft to the same rules. That’s also what keeps it distinct from the website-specific skills — voice is a layer that sits on top of everything you write, not just your site.
Which AI tools does it work with?
Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark all work. Catching subtle voice drift rewards a careful reader, so Claude is a natural home, but the prompt checks a draft the same way in all three. The SKILL.md file installs as a saved skill in Claude and Gemini Spark; in ChatGPT you can use a Project — which is handy here, because you can store your voice rules right in the Project.

COPY REFRESH — a freelance web designer’s tired homepage (example) Fix #1 (biggest impact): The headline is “Welcome to my portfolio.” It describes; it doesn’t sell. → Rewrite: “Websites that turn visitors into booked calls — for service businesses.” Fix #2: The only CTA is a “Contact” link in the footer. → Add a “See my work” button in the hero and a “Book a call” at the end of each section. Website Copy Refresh skill: frequently asked questions

Is this AI website copy refresh skill free?

Yes. Both the copy-paste prompt and the SKILL.md file are completely free. Optional reusable features may depend on the AI tool and plan you use. ChatGPT Projects are available on free and paid plans, Claude skills are available when code execution is enabled, and Gemini Spark skills currently require Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US.

How is this different from the Landing Page and Website Builder skills?

It’s about the input. The Website Builder skill plans a whole new site from your business details; the Landing Page skill writes a new page from an offer. This skill starts from a page you already have and improves it — it audits and rewrites what’s there rather than producing something from scratch. Use it when the page exists but isn’t performing.

Can it see my live website?

No. It works only from the copy you paste into the chat — it can’t browse the web or open your URL, and it won’t pretend to. Copy the text of the page (the words, not a screenshot or a link) and paste it in. That’s actually an advantage: it forces the audit to focus on the words themselves, which is what your visitors read and what you can change today.

Will it invent testimonials or numbers to make the page stronger?

Does it also fix my SEO and brand voice?

Which AI tools does it work with?

Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark all work. Auditing and rewriting a page rewards a careful reader, so Claude is a natural home, but the prompt refreshes a page the same way in all three. # Website Copy Refresh
When this skill runs, audit an existing web page and return a prioritized list of what is weakening it, plus rewritten versions of the weakest sections, sharpening what is there rather than replacing it.
## Process
1. Read the page and identify the single action it is supposed to drive. If the user did not say, ask before auditing — the whole audit hangs on it. 2. Audit the page for the things that lose visitors: a headline that describes instead of sells, no clear or early call to action, benefits written as features, "we/I" language where "you" belongs, missing or vague proof, walls of text, weak or absent next step. 3. List the problems in priority order — biggest likely impact on conversion first. For each, name the problem in one line and why it costs conversions. 4. Rewrite the two or three weakest sections in full, ready to paste. Keep the user's facts and voice; sharpen the wording. 5. Quote back anything that already works and explicitly tell the user to leave it alone. 6. Finish with the single highest-impact change if they only do one thing.
## Rules
- Use only what is on the page. Never invent a testimonial, statistic, client name, result, or guarantee to strengthen a claim. - Where a section clearly needs a real proof point the user did not provide, write [YOUR INPUT] and list it at the end — do not fabricate it. - Keep the user's voice. You are refreshing their page, not rebranding it. If the voice itself is the problem, say so in one line and point them to the Brand Voice Check skill — do not rewrite the whole page into a different tone. - Judge conversion and clarity, not SEO metadata. Do not write title tags, meta descriptions, or slugs — point the user to the SEO Metadata skill for those. - Do not plan a new site or new pages. Work on the page in front of you. If they need a whole site, point them to the Website Builder skill. - Prioritize honestly. Two real fixes beat ten cosmetic ones. If the page is basically fine, say so. - You cannot browse the web or open the live page — work only from the copy the user pastes in. - Do not promise a specific lift or conversion rate. You are improving the copy, not forecasting performance.
## Output format
### What This Page Is For The single action, restated, so the audit is anchored.
### Prioritized Fixes Numbered, biggest impact first. Each: the problem in one line, and why it costs conversions.
### Rewritten Sections The 2-3 weakest sections rewritten in full, ready to paste.
### Leave These Alone What already works, quoted back.
### If You Only Do One Thing The single highest-impact change.
### Needs Your Input Every [YOUR INPUT] placeholder and any real proof the page is missing.
If the user has not given you the page copy and what the page is for, ask for those two before auditing anything. ```

## Website Copy Refresh skill: frequently asked questions
Is this AI website copy refresh skill free?
**Yes.** Both the copy-paste prompt and the SKILL.md file are completely free. Optional reusable features may depend on the AI tool and plan you use. ChatGPT Projects are available on free and paid plans, Claude skills are available when code execution is enabled, and Gemini Spark skills currently require Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US.
How is this different from the Landing Page and Website Builder skills?
It’s about the input. The [Website Builder skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/website-builder/) plans a whole new site from your business details; the [Landing Page skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/landing-page/) writes a new page from an offer. Use it when the page exists but isn’t performing.
Can it see my live website?
**No.** It works only from the copy you paste into the chat — it can’t browse the web or open your URL, and it won’t pretend to. Copy the text of the page (the words, not a screenshot or a link) and paste it in. That’s actually an advantage: it forces the audit to focus on the words themselves, which is what your visitors read and what you can change today.
Will it invent testimonials or numbers to make the page stronger?

Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark all work. Auditing and rewriting a page rewards a careful reader, so Claude is a natural home, but the prompt refreshes a page the same way in all three. The SKILL.md file installs as a saved skill in Claude and Gemini Spark; in ChatGPT you can use a Project or native Skills.

item.text: Free AI UX Review Skill The free AI UX Review skill Upload a screenshot of your page, an exported design, or a PDF — get back a plain-language UX review: what’s confusing, where the eye gets lost, why people hesitate, and the two or three fixes that matter most, ranked. Free prompt + SKILL.md file · Free signup · Setup help · Needs image upload This UX Review skill is a free AI UX audit that looks at a screenshot, design, or PDF you upload and returns a prioritized, plain-language review — what’s unclear, where attention gets lost, why visitors hesitate, and the handful of fixes that will help most. Upload the thing you’re about to publish, and it tells you what to fix before anyone else sees it. It runs the same review on every screen, so your homepage and your checkout page get judged by one standard. That’s the difference between a skill and a one-off prompt: the checklist — clear primary action, visual hierarchy, readability, trust, friction — is saved, so you’re not re-explaining “look at the UX” each time. It reviews what you can show it — it does not redesign the page, write code, or open your live site or Figma link, and it will never pretend to see something that isn’t in the image. Use it as a copy-paste prompt in any AI chat that accepts images, or install the ready-made SKILL.md file so it runs on command in Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark. No design training required. The UX Review skill looks at a visual you upload — a screenshot of your website or app, an exported design frame, an image, or a PDF like a flyer, one-pager, or slide — and returns a prioritized usability review: the first thing a visitor’s eye lands on, whether the main action is obvious, where the layout is cluttered or hard to read, what creates hesitation, and the two or three highest-impact fixes, in order. It looks at the design and layout, which is what makes it different from the Website Copy Refresh skill (that reads your written copy). It cannot open a live website or a Figma link and it does not browse — you upload or paste the image, and it reviews what it can actually see, saying so plainly if something is cut off or unclear. It does not redesign the page, write CSS, or certify formal accessibility compliance, though it will flag obvious contrast and legibility problems. It needs a vision-capable AI (Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark) and the ability to upload an image. A second pair of eyes on the thing before you ship it By the end of this AI skill guide, you’ll have the UX Review skill ready to use — as a copy-paste prompt in any AI chat that takes images, or installed as a SKILL.md file that runs on command. It handles the moment every business owner knows: the page or PDF looks “fine,” but you can’t tell what’s actually wrong with it. Upload it, and get a clear, ranked list of what a first-time visitor would trip over — before they do. UX REVIEW — an uploaded screenshot of a neighborhood gym’s homepage (example) First impression (3-second test): “The eye lands on a big stock photo of dumbbells, not on what you do or what to click. A visitor can’t tell in three seconds that this is a gym taking new members.” Fix #1 (biggest impact): There are three buttons in the header — “Join,” “Book a tour,” “Free pass” — competing at the same size. This UX Review skill is a free AI UX audit that looks at a screenshot, design, or PDF you upload and returns a prioritized, plain-language review — what’s unclear, where attention gets lost, why visitors hesitate, and the handful of fixes that will help most. The UX Review skill looks at a visual you upload — a screenshot of your website or app, an exported design frame, an image, or a PDF like a flyer, one-pager, or slide — and returns a prioritized usability review: the first thing a visitor’s eye lands on, whether the main action is obvious, where the layout is cluttered or hard to read, what creates hesitation, and the two or three highest-impact fixes, in order. A second pair of eyes on the thing before you ship it

By the end of this AI skill guide, you’ll have the UX Review skill ready to use — as a copy-paste prompt in any AI chat that takes images, or installed as a SKILL.md file that runs on command. It handles the moment every business owner knows: the page or PDF looks “fine,” but you can’t tell what’s actually wrong with it. Upload it, and get a clear, ranked list of what a first-time visitor would trip over — before they do.

UX REVIEW — an uploaded screenshot of a neighborhood gym’s homepage (example)

First impression (3-second test): “The eye lands on a big stock photo of dumbbells, not on what you do or what to click. A visitor can’t tell in three seconds that this is a gym taking new members.”

Fix #1 (biggest impact): There are three buttons in the header — “Join,” “Book a tour,” “Free pass” — competing at the same size. Pick one primary action, make it bigger and bolder, and demote the other two.

Fix #2: The white headline sits on a light photo — hard to read, and it fails on a phone. Add a dark overlay or move the text onto a solid band.

Fix #3: Hours, price, and location are nowhere above the fold — the three things a local visitor actually came to check. Surface them.

What’s already working: “The class-schedule table is clean and scannable — leave it. The logo and nav are clear.”

Honest limit: “The screenshot cuts off below the schedule — I can’t review the footer or any content past it. Upload a full-length capture if you want those looked at too.”

Part 2 of 5

How to use the UX Review AI skill in 3 steps

The UX Review skill is an AI skill — a reusable set of instructions. It comes in two formats below, and they contain the same thinking. Use the prompt if you want one screen reviewed in the next ten minutes. Use the SKILL.md file if you’ll review several screens and want each held to the same checklist. Either way, you’ll upload an image — this skill reads pictures, not pasted text.

  1. 1

    Grab a clean screenshot or export

    Screenshot your page (a full-length capture is best), export a Figma or Canva frame as a PNG, or save your flyer or one-pager as a PDF. This skill can’t open a live URL — it reviews the image you give it.

  2. 2

    Upload it and say what it’s for

    Attach the image, then tell it the one thing the screen should get a visitor to do, and who that visitor is. The goal is what turns a vague “looks fine” into a real review.

  3. 3

    Fix the top items, re-shoot, re-run

    It ranks the issues by impact. Do the top two or three, take a fresh screenshot, and run it again to confirm they’re resolved and nothing new broke.

Format 1 — Prompt Version (any AI chat that takes images, nothing to install)

Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark, attach your screenshot or PDF, add the two lines at the bottom, and send. Works on any plan that lets you upload an image. Best for reviewing one screen at a time.

You are an expert UX reviewer who explains things in plain language to non-designers. Your job is to review the screenshot, design, or PDF the user uploads and return a prioritized, honest usability review — sharpening what is there, never redesigning it from scratch.

PROCESS
1. Look at the image first. If it is cut off, blurry, or you cannot make out key parts, say so plainly before reviewing — do not guess at what you cannot see.
2. If the user did not say what the screen is for, ask for the single action it should drive and who the visitor is before reviewing. The review hangs on it.
3. Give the 3-second test: describe what the eye lands on first and whether a new visitor can tell, at a glance, what this is and what to do.
4. Audit for the things that cost usability: is the primary action obvious and singular; is the visual hierarchy clear; is text readable (size and contrast); is the layout cluttered or cramped; does anything important sit below the fold; would this hold up on a phone; are there trust or credibility gaps.
5. List the problems in priority order — biggest likely impact on the visitor first. For each, name what you see, why it hurts, and a specific, concrete fix.
6. Call out what already works and tell the user to leave it alone.
7. Finish with the single highest-impact change if they only do one thing.

RULES
- Review ONLY what is visible in the image. Never claim to see a color, word, or element that is not there, and never invent what is off-screen or cut off.
- You cannot open a live website, an app, or a Figma/Canva link, and you cannot browse. Work only from the uploaded image. If the user pastes a link, ask them to upload a screenshot or export instead.
- Judge the design and usability, not the written copy. If the words themselves are the problem, say so in one line and point the user to the Website Copy Refresh skill — do not rewrite the page's copy here.
- Do not produce a redesign, pixel measurements, hex codes, or CSS. Give plain-language direction a non-designer can act on or hand to a designer.
- You are not certifying formal accessibility compliance, but flag obvious problems: low contrast, tiny text, tap targets too close together.
- Prioritize honestly. Two real fixes beat ten nitpicks. If the screen is basically solid, say so.
- Do not promise a specific conversion lift. You are improving usability, not forecasting performance.

OUTPUT FORMAT
### What I Can See
One line confirming what the image shows, and anything cut off or unclear.
### The 3-Second Test
What the eye lands on first, and whether the purpose and next step are clear.
### Prioritized Fixes
Numbered, biggest impact first. Each: what you see, why it hurts, and a concrete fix.
### Leave These Alone
What already works.
### If You Only Do One Thing
The single highest-impact change.

WHAT THIS SCREEN IS FOR: [the one action it should drive — buy, book, sign up, call]
WHO IT'S FOR: [the visitor and what they came to do]
[Attach your screenshot, exported design, or PDF to this message.]

## A second pair of eyes on the thing before you ship it
By the end of this AI skill guide, you’ll have the UX Review skill ready to use — as a copy-paste prompt in any AI chat that takes images, or installed as a SKILL.md file that runs on command. It handles the moment every business owner knows: the page or PDF looks “fine,” but you can’t tell what’s actually wrong with it. Upload it, and get a clear, ranked list of what a first-time visitor would trip over — before they do.
#### UX REVIEW — an uploaded screenshot of a neighborhood gym’s homepage (example)
**First impression (3-second test):** “The eye lands on a big stock photo of dumbbells, not on what you do or what to click. A visitor can’t tell in three seconds that this is a gym taking new members.”
**Fix #1 (biggest impact):** There are three buttons in the header — “Join,” “Book a tour,” “Free pass” — competing at the same size. Pick one primary action, make it bigger and bolder, and demote the other two.
**Fix #2:** The white headline sits on a light photo — hard to read, and it fails on a phone. Add a dark overlay or move the text onto a solid band.
**Fix #3:** Hours, price, and location are nowhere above the fold — the three things a local visitor actually came to check. Surface them.
**What’s already working:** “The class-schedule table is clean and scannable — leave it. The logo and nav are clear.”
**Honest limit:** “The screenshot cuts off below the schedule — I can’t review the footer or any content past it. Upload a full-length capture if you want those looked at too.”

## How to use the UX Review AI skill in 3 steps
The UX Review skill is an **AI skill** — a reusable set of instructions. It comes in two formats below, and they contain the same thinking. Use the **prompt** if you want one screen reviewed in the next ten minutes. Use the **SKILL.md file** if you’ll review several screens and want each held to the same checklist. Either way, you’ll upload an image — this skill reads pictures, not pasted text.
1. 1
**Grab a clean screenshot or export**
Screenshot your page (a full-length capture is best), export a Figma or Canva frame as a PNG, or save your flyer or one-pager as a PDF. This skill can’t open a live URL — it reviews the image you give it.
2. 2
**Upload it and say what it’s for**
Attach the image, then tell it the one thing the screen should get a visitor to do, and who that visitor is. The goal is what turns a vague “looks fine” into a real review.
3. 3
**Fix the top items, re-shoot, re-run**
It ranks the issues by impact. Do the top two or three, take a fresh screenshot, and run it again to confirm they’re resolved and nothing new broke.
**Format 1 — Prompt Version (any AI chat that takes images, nothing to install)**
Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark, attach your screenshot or PDF, add the two lines at the bottom, and send. Works on any plan that lets you upload an image. Best for reviewing one screen at a time.
``` You are an expert UX reviewer who explains things in plain language to non-designers. Your job is to review the screenshot, design, or PDF the user uploads and return a prioritized, honest usability review — sharpening what is there, never redesigning it from scratch.
PROCESS 1. Look at the image first. If it is cut off, blurry, or you cannot make out key parts, say so plainly before reviewing — do not guess at what you cannot see. 2. If the user did not say what the screen is for, ask for the single action it should drive and who the visitor is before reviewing. The review hangs on it. 3. Give the 3-second test: describe what the eye lands on first and whether a new visitor can tell, at a glance, what this is and what to do. 4. Audit for the things that cost usability: is the primary action obvious and singular; is the visual hierarchy clear; is text readable (size and contrast); is the layout cluttered or cramped; does anything important sit below the fold; would this hold up on a phone; are there trust or credibility gaps. 5. List the problems in priority order — biggest likely impact on the visitor first. For each, name what you see, why it hurts, and a specific, concrete fix. 6. Call out what already works and tell the user to leave it alone. 7. Finish with the single highest-impact change if they only do one thing.
RULES - Review ONLY what is visible in the image. Never claim to see a color, word, or element that is not there, and never invent what is off-screen or cut off. - You cannot open a live website, an app, or a Figma/Canva link, and you cannot browse. Work only from the uploaded image. If the user pastes a link, ask them to upload a screenshot or export instead. - Judge the design and usability, not the written copy. If the words themselves are the problem, say so in one line and point the user to the Website Copy Refresh skill — do not rewrite the page's copy here. - Do not produce a redesign, pixel measurements, hex codes, or CSS. Give plain-language direction a non-designer can act on or hand to a designer. - You are not certifying formal accessibility compliance, but flag obvious problems: low contrast, tiny text, tap targets too close together. - Prioritize honestly. Two real fixes beat ten nitpicks. If the screen is basically solid, say so. - Do not promise a specific conversion lift. You are improving usability, not forecasting performance.
OUTPUT FORMAT ### What I Can See One line confirming what the image shows, and anything cut off or unclear. ### The 3-Second Test What the eye lands on first, and whether the purpose and next step are clear. ### Prioritized Fixes Numbered, biggest impact first. Each: what you see, why it hurts, and a concrete fix. ### Leave These Alone What already works. ### If You Only Do One Thing The single highest-impact change.
WHAT THIS SCREEN IS FOR: [the one action it should drive — buy, book, sign up, call] WHO IT'S FOR: [the visitor and what they came to do] [Attach your screenshot, exported design, or PDF to this message.] ```
**Format 2 — SKILL.md File (install once, runs on command)**
This is the same skill packaged as a proper `SKILL.md` — the format Claude and Gemini Spark use for saved skills. The `description` line at the top is the important part: it tells your AI _when_ to run this on its own, so you can just upload a screenshot and say **“review this for UX”** and it fires. Paste the whole block into a new file called `SKILL.md`, or straight into your platform’s skill instructions.
``` --- name: ux-review description: Review an uploaded screenshot, design, or PDF and return a prioritized, plain-language usability review — the 3-second test, ranked fixes with concrete suggestions, what already works, and the one highest-impact change. Use this when the user uploads a screen, mockup, flyer, or PDF and asks for UX or design feedback, or says review this for UX, is this page confusing, or check my design. ---
# UX Review
When this skill runs, review the screenshot, design, or PDF the user uploads and return a prioritized, honest usability review, sharpening what is there rather than redesigning it.
## Process
1. Look at the image first. If it is cut off, blurry, or you cannot make out key parts, say so plainly before reviewing — do not guess at what you cannot see. 2. If the user did not say what the screen is for, ask for the single action it should drive and who the visitor is before reviewing. 3. Give the 3-second test: describe what the eye lands on first and whether a new visitor can tell, at a glance, what this is and what to do. 4. Audit for the things that cost usability: is the primary action obvious and singular; is the visual hierarchy clear; is text readable (size and contrast); is the layout cluttered; does anything important sit below the fold; would this hold up on a phone; are there trust or credibility gaps. 5. List the problems in priority order — biggest likely impact on the visitor first. For each, name what you see, why it hurts, and a specific, concrete fix. 6. Call out what already works and tell the user to leave it alone. 7. Finish with the single highest-impact change if they only do one thing.
## Rules
- Review only what is visible in the image. Never claim to see a color, word, or element that is not there, and never invent what is off-screen or cut off. - You cannot open a live website, an app, or a Figma/Canva link, and you cannot browse. Work only from the uploaded image. If the user pastes a link, ask them to upload a screenshot or export instead. - Judge the design and usability, not the written copy. If the words themselves are the problem, say so in one line and point the user to the Website Copy Refresh skill — do not rewrite the page's copy here. - Do not produce a redesign, pixel measurements, hex codes, or CSS. Give plain-language direction a non-designer can act on or hand to a designer. - You are not certifying formal accessibility compliance, but flag obvious problems: low contrast, tiny text, tap targets too close together. - Prioritize honestly. Two real fixes beat ten nitpicks. If the screen is basically solid, say so. - Do not promise a specific conversion lift. You are improving usability, not forecasting performance.
## Output format
### What I Can See One line confirming what the image shows, and anything cut off or unclear.
### The 3-Second Test What the eye lands on first, and whether the purpose and next step are clear.
### Prioritized Fixes Numbered, biggest impact first. Each: what you see, why it hurts, and a concrete fix.
### Leave These Alone What already works.
### If You Only Do One Thing The single highest-impact change.
If the user has not uploaded an image, ask for a screenshot, export, or PDF before reviewing. If they have not said what the screen is for, ask for that too. ```

## UX Review skill: frequently asked questions
Is this AI UX review skill free?
**Yes — the prompt is free with no account at all, and the SKILL.md file is free with a free account.** Yes. Both the copy-paste prompt and the SKILL.md file are completely free. It does need a plan that lets you upload an image, since it reviews a picture — image upload is available on the free and paid tiers of Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark, though Gemini Spark skills currently require Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US. Claude skills are available when code execution is enabled, and ChatGPT Projects work on free and paid plans.
Can it review my live website or my Figma file directly?
**No — it cannot open a live URL or a Figma link, and it is honest about that.** No — and it’s honest about that. It can’t open a live URL or a Figma/Canva link, and it can’t browse. You give it a picture: a screenshot of your page (a full-length capture is best), or a frame exported from Figma or Canva as a PNG. That’s a feature, not a limit — it reviews exactly what a visitor would see, and it tells you plainly if part of the image is cut off rather than guessing at what’s off-screen.
What can I upload — just websites?
**Anything visual with a job to do — a screen, a flyer, a one-pager, a slide.** Anything visual with a job to do. A website or landing page screenshot, an app screen, a mobile view, an exported design mockup, or a PDF like a flyer, one-pager, menu, or slide. If it’s something a person has to look at and understand, this skill can review it. Tell it what the thing is for, and it measures the design against that goal.
How is this different from the Website Copy Refresh skill?
**This one reviews the design; Copy Refresh reviews the words.** They look at different things. This skill reviews the **design** — the layout, hierarchy, contrast, clutter, and whether the main action is obvious — from a picture you upload. The [Website Copy Refresh skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/website-copy-refresh/) reads the **words** you paste and improves the copy and conversion. A page can look clean but read poorly, or read well but look cluttered. Run this for the design, run Copy Refresh for the words; on an important page, run both.
Does it replace a real designer or a usability test?
**No, and it will not claim to.** No, and it won’t claim to. It’s a fast, honest second pair of eyes that catches the obvious problems — the ones that are costing you visitors right now and don’t need a research study to spot. For a high-stakes redesign, real users and a designer are worth it. For “is this good enough to publish, and what should I fix first,” this gets you most of the way in a few minutes. It also won’t certify formal accessibility compliance, though it will flag obvious contrast and legibility issues.
Which AI tools does it work with?
**Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark — any of them that lets you attach an image.** Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark all work, as long as you can attach an image. Reading a design closely rewards a strong vision model, so Claude is a natural home, but all three can look at an uploaded screen. The SKILL.md file installs as a saved skill in Claude and Gemini Spark; in ChatGPT you can use a Project or native Skills, then attach your screenshot in the chat.

item.text: What is ChatGPT Work? Features, AI Skills, Tasks ChatGPT Work is OpenAI’s agent mode for delegating longer, multi-step tasks to ChatGPT and getting a finished result you can review. It can combine files, connected apps, plugins, skills, web research, and approved tools to create deliverables such as presentations, spreadsheets, reports, analyses, project plans, and recurring updates. Use regular Chat when you want an answer or a quick draft. Switch to Work when you want ChatGPT to carry a task through several steps, create a usable file, or keep checking something over time. ChatGPT Work launched on July 9, 2026. ChatGPT Work is the task-completion side of ChatGPT. You define the outcome, give it the sources and tools it needs, and let the agent research, reason, create files, and return a review-ready result. You can follow its progress, answer questions, redirect it, and approve important actions. It is not a separate download. Work is available inside ChatGPT on supported surfaces. On the web or desktop app, select ChatGPT and switch the composer from Chat to Work. Its exact tools depend on your plan, device, workspace settings, and connected services. ChatGPT Work at a Glance What it is An agent mode inside ChatGPT for longer, multi-step work and reviewable outcomes Best for Research, analysis, presentations, documents, spreadsheets, workflows, recurring updates, and monitoring Can use Chats, uploaded files, Project sources, plugins, connected apps, skills, web search, and approved tools Finished outputs Documents, slide decks, spreadsheets, PDFs, analyses, plans, briefs, and other files Scheduled work One-time or recurring tasks, including tasks that return to an existing chat and monitors that check for changes Where it runs ChatGPT web and the ChatGPT desktop app; cloud conversations can be continued from supported web and mobile experiences Included plans Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, and Enterprise; tools and limits vary Price and usage Included with eligible ChatGPT plans and shares pricing, credits, and usage limits with Codex; regular Chat usage is separate Launch date July 9, 2026 OpenAI’s official ChatGPT Work guide describes it as a way to delegate real work to ChatGPT. The word delegate is the useful distinction: you are asking for an outcome, not only a response. How ChatGPT Work Completes a Task A good Work task has a clear outcome, source material, constraints, and a definition of done. The agent then decides which permitted tools and steps are needed, completes the work, and returns something you can inspect. 1 Define the outcome Ask for a specific result such as an eight-slide deck, a vendor comparison spreadsheet, or a weekly operations brief. 2 Add the context Attach files, use a Project, or point Work to approved sources such as Google Drive, Slack, SharePoint, email, calendars, or a CRM. 3 Set boundaries Name the audience, format, required sources, exclusions, review criteria, and any action it must stop before taking. 4 Let the agent work ChatGPT can gather information, reason across steps, use tools, create a file, and report progress while the task is running. 5 Review the result Check the sources, figures, claims, file contents, and requested format. Ask for focused revisions before sharing or acting on it. The best Work prompts define “done” Do not stop at “research our competitors.” Ask for a five-company comparison, name the criteria, require source links, specify the output file, and tell ChatGPT what to flag for human review. Clear completion criteria make agent work easier to verify. ChatGPT Work Features ChatGPT Work is not one tool. It is the agent experience that coordinates several capabilities around a task. Which capabilities appear for you depends on the surface, plan, workspace policy, and permissions. Feature What it does Why it matters Multi-step agent work Works through a larger task instead of returning only one conversational answer. Better fit for outcomes that require research, synthesis, creation, checking, and revision. Files and finished deliverables Reads source files and creates documents, presentations, spreadsheets, PDFs, analyses, and other artifacts. You receive something to review and use, not merely advice about how to make it. Plugins and connected apps Connects to approved tools such as Slack, Google Drive, SharePoint, email, calendars, CRM systems, and project trackers. The agent can work from current business context instead of relying only on pasted text. Skills Loads reusable instructions, resources, and optional scripts for a specific workflow. Your preferred method and output format can be applied consistently across repeated tasks. Scheduled tasks Runs a saved task later or on a recurring schedule and keeps a run history. Useful for recurring reports, reminders, refreshes, follow-up loops, and monitoring. Local computer tools On desktop, Work can use local files, supported apps, and the built-in browser when those tools are available and permitted. Lets the task use information or software that is not available to a cloud-only chat. Local or cloud execution Desktop users can keep work local or choose cloud when available. Local is for computer-dependent tasks; cloud can keep running when the app is closed or the computer is off. Progress and steering Shows progress and lets you answer questions, add context, change direction, or request a status recap. You remain involved without having to restart the task whenever something changes. Approvals and permissions Uses the access granted by your account, workspace, connected service, and execution environment. Starting Work does not automatically grant access to private files, systems, or high-impact actions. ChatGPT Work vs Regular ChatGPT Regular Chat is for thinking with ChatGPT; ChatGPT Work is for delegating a defined outcome. They live inside the same product, and you can move between them based on the task. OpenAI’s Chat, Work, and Codex guide frames the choice the same way: use Chat for conversation, Work for a reviewable result, and Codex when you want developer tools and technical detail. Difference Regular Chat ChatGPT Work Best for Questions, explanations, brainstorming, short drafts, and quick comparisons Longer tasks with a clear outcome, multiple steps, tools, sources, or a finished file Typical result An answer or conversational draft A reviewable deliverable, completed workflow, recurring update, or monitored result Agent effort Usually brief and interactive Can run for longer and coordinate more context and tool use Files and tools Can use supported Chat features Designed to combine multiple files, plugins, sources, and steps around the outcome Recurring work Useful for drafting the idea Can create and run scheduled tasks when the capability is available Usage Standard Chat usage Shares pricing, credits, and usage limits with Codex Use Chat: “Give me five ideas for a customer webinar.” Use Work: “Review these customer interviews and product notes. What is ChatGPT Work? Features, AI Skills, Tasks

ChatGPT Work is OpenAI’s agent mode for delegating longer, multi-step tasks to ChatGPT and getting a finished result you can review. It can combine files, connected apps, plugins, skills, web research, and approved tools to create deliverables such as presentations, spreadsheets, reports, analyses, project plans, and recurring updates.

Use regular Chat when you want an answer or a quick draft. Switch to Work when you want ChatGPT to carry a task through several steps, create a usable file, or keep checking something over time. ChatGPT Work launched on July 9, 2026.

Quick answer

ChatGPT Work is the task-completion side of ChatGPT. You define the outcome, give it the sources and tools it needs, and let the agent research, reason, create files, and return a review-ready result. You can follow its progress, answer questions, redirect it, and approve important actions.

It is not a separate download. Work is available inside ChatGPT on supported surfaces. On the web or desktop app, select ChatGPT and switch the composer from Chat to Work. Its exact tools depend on your plan, device, workspace settings, and connected services.

ChatGPT Work at a Glance

What it is An agent mode inside ChatGPT for longer, multi-step work and reviewable outcomes
Best for Research, analysis, presentations, documents, spreadsheets, workflows, recurring updates, and monitoring
Can use Chats, uploaded files, Project sources, plugins, connected apps, skills, web search, and approved tools
Finished outputs Documents, slide decks, spreadsheets, PDFs, analyses, plans, briefs, and other files
Scheduled work One-time or recurring tasks, including tasks that return to an existing chat and monitors that check for changes
Where it runs ChatGPT web and the ChatGPT desktop app; cloud conversations can be continued from supported web and mobile experiences
Included plans Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, and Enterprise; tools and limits vary
Price and usage Included with eligible ChatGPT plans and shares pricing, credits, and usage limits with Codex; regular Chat usage is separate
Launch date July 9, 2026

OpenAI’s official ChatGPT Work guide describes it as a way to delegate real work to ChatGPT. The word delegate is the useful distinction: you are asking for an outcome, not only a response.

How ChatGPT Work Completes a Task

A good Work task has a clear outcome, source material, constraints, and a definition of done. The agent then decides which permitted tools and steps are needed, completes the work, and returns something you can inspect.

1 Define the outcome

Ask for a specific result such as an eight-slide deck, a vendor comparison spreadsheet, or a weekly operations brief.

2 Add the context

Attach files, use a Project, or point Work to approved sources such as Google Drive, Slack, SharePoint, email, calendars, or a CRM.

3 Set boundaries

Name the audience, format, required sources, exclusions, review criteria, and any action it must stop before taking.

4 Let the agent work

ChatGPT can gather information, reason across steps, use tools, create a file, and report progress while the task is running.

5 Review the result

Check the sources, figures, claims, file contents, and requested format. Ask for focused revisions before sharing or acting on it.

The best Work prompts define “done”

Do not stop at “research our competitors.” Ask for a five-company comparison, name the criteria, require source links, specify the output file, and tell ChatGPT what to flag for human review. Clear completion criteria make agent work easier to verify.

ChatGPT Work Features

ChatGPT Work is not one tool. It is the agent experience that coordinates several capabilities around a task. Which capabilities appear for you depends on the surface, plan, workspace policy, and permissions.

Feature What it does Why it matters
Multi-step agent work Works through a larger task instead of returning only one conversational answer. Better fit for outcomes that require research, synthesis, creation, checking, and revision.
Files and finished deliverables Reads source files and creates documents, presentations, spreadsheets, PDFs, analyses, and other artifacts. You receive something to review and use, not merely advice about how to make it.
Plugins and connected apps Connects to approved tools such as Slack, Google Drive, SharePoint, email, calendars, CRM systems, and project trackers. The agent can work from current business context instead of relying only on pasted text.
Skills Loads reusable instructions, resources, and optional scripts for a specific workflow. Your preferred method and output format can be applied consistently across repeated tasks.
Scheduled tasks Runs a saved task later or on a recurring schedule and keeps a run history. Useful for recurring reports, reminders, refreshes, follow-up loops, and monitoring.
Local computer tools On desktop, Work can use local files, supported apps, and the built-in browser when those tools are available and permitted. Lets the task use information or software that is not available to a cloud-only chat.
Local or cloud execution Desktop users can keep work local or choose cloud when available. Local is for computer-dependent tasks; cloud can keep running when the app is closed or the computer is off.
Progress and steering Shows progress and lets you answer questions, add context, change direction, or request a status recap. You remain involved without having to restart the task whenever something changes.
Approvals and permissions Uses the access granted by your account, workspace, connected service, and execution environment. Starting Work does not automatically grant access to private files, systems, or high-impact actions.

Regular Chat is for thinking with ChatGPT; ChatGPT Work is for delegating a defined outcome. They live inside the same product, and you can move between them based on the task.

OpenAI’s Chat, Work, and Codex guide frames the choice the same way: use Chat for conversation, Work for a reviewable result, and Codex when you want developer tools and technical detail.

Difference Regular Chat ChatGPT Work

Typical result An answer or conversational draft A reviewable deliverable, completed workflow, recurring update, or monitored result
Agent effort Usually brief and interactive Can run for longer and coordinate more context and tool use
Files and tools Can use supported Chat features Designed to combine multiple files, plugins, sources, and steps around the outcome
Recurring work Useful for drafting the idea Can create and run scheduled tasks when the capability is available
Usage Standard Chat usage Shares pricing, credits, and usage limits with Codex

Use Work: “Review these customer interviews and product notes. Create an eight-slide webinar deck for small-business owners, cite the supporting evidence, write speaker notes, and flag any claim that needs my review.”

It is a mode inside ChatGPT, not a separate company or model. Regular Chat is best for questions, explanations, brainstorming, and short drafts. Work is best when you want ChatGPT to complete a larger task, coordinate several steps or sources, create a finished file, or manage work over time.

Is ChatGPT Work the same as Projects?

No. Work is an execution mode for completing a task. A Project is a container that keeps related chats, files, instructions, and connected sources together. You can start both regular Chat and ChatGPT Work conversations inside the same Project.

How do Skills work inside ChatGPT Work?

A Skill supplies reusable instructions, resources, and optional scripts for a focused workflow. You can select a Skill explicitly, or ChatGPT may use one when your task matches its description. The Skill guides the method but does not bypass your plan, permissions, connected-app access, or approval rules.

Can ChatGPT Work run scheduled tasks?

Yes, when scheduled tasks are available for your account or workspace. A standalone task starts each run from a saved prompt, while a task scheduled inside a chat returns to that conversation with its existing context. Tasks can also use Skills and plugins on supported surfaces.

What is a monitor in ChatGPT Work?

A monitor is a recurring scheduled-task pattern, not a separate product. It checks a source or condition at a set cadence and reports when a defined change or finding appears. A good monitor prompt defines what matters, what to ignore, when to stop, and which actions need approval.

Which plans include ChatGPT Work?

OpenAI’s current documentation says ChatGPT Work and Codex are included in Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, and Enterprise plans. Tools, models, usage limits, cloud options, plugins, and workspace permissions can still vary by plan and account.

Does ChatGPT Work cost extra?

Work is included with supported ChatGPT plans. Its usage shares the same pricing, credits, and limits as Codex, while standard Chat usage is separate. Complex tasks, large files, connected tools, and frequent schedules can consume more of the shared allowance.

Where can I download ChatGPT Work?

There is no separate ChatGPT Work download. Install the official ChatGPT desktop app for Windows or macOS from chatgpt.com/download, sign in, select ChatGPT, and switch from Chat to Work above the composer. Work can also be available on ChatGPT web.

Can ChatGPT Work keep running when my computer is off?

Cloud Work can keep running after you close the app or turn off the computer when that option is available. Local Work depends on your computer, files, and apps, so the computer must stay on and the desktop app must keep running for a local scheduled task.

# What is ChatGPT Work? Features, AI Skills, Tasks
**ChatGPT Work is OpenAI’s agent mode for delegating longer, multi-step tasks to ChatGPT and getting a finished result you can review.** It can combine files, connected apps, plugins, skills, web research, and approved tools to create deliverables such as presentations, spreadsheets, reports, analyses, project plans, and recurring updates.
Use regular Chat when you want an answer or a quick draft. Switch to **Work** when you want ChatGPT to carry a task through several steps, create a usable file, or keep checking something over time. ChatGPT Work launched on **July 9, 2026**.
Quick answer
ChatGPT Work is the task-completion side of ChatGPT. You define the outcome, give it the sources and tools it needs, and let the agent research, reason, create files, and return a review-ready result. You can follow its progress, answer questions, redirect it, and approve important actions.
**It is not a separate download.** Work is available inside ChatGPT on supported surfaces. On the web or desktop app, select ChatGPT and switch the composer from **Chat** to **Work**. Its exact tools depend on your plan, device, workspace settings, and connected services.
## ChatGPT Work at a Glance
| | | | --- | --- | | What it is | An agent mode inside ChatGPT for longer, multi-step work and reviewable outcomes | | Best for | Research, analysis, presentations, documents, spreadsheets, workflows, recurring updates, and monitoring | | Can use | Chats, uploaded files, Project sources, plugins, connected apps, skills, web search, and approved tools | | Finished outputs | Documents, slide decks, spreadsheets, PDFs, analyses, plans, briefs, and other files | | Scheduled work | One-time or recurring tasks, including tasks that return to an existing chat and monitors that check for changes | | Where it runs | ChatGPT web and the ChatGPT desktop app; cloud conversations can be continued from supported web and mobile experiences | | Included plans | Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, and Enterprise; tools and limits vary | | Price and usage | Included with eligible ChatGPT plans and shares pricing, credits, and usage limits with Codex; regular Chat usage is separate | | Launch date | July 9, 2026 |
OpenAI’s [official ChatGPT Work guide](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/get-started-with-work) describes it as a way to delegate real work to ChatGPT. The word _delegate_ is the useful distinction: you are asking for an outcome, not only a response.
## How ChatGPT Work Completes a Task
A good Work task has a clear outcome, source material, constraints, and a definition of done. The agent then decides which permitted tools and steps are needed, completes the work, and returns something you can inspect.
1 **Define the outcome**
Ask for a specific result such as an eight-slide deck, a vendor comparison spreadsheet, or a weekly operations brief.
2 **Add the context**
Attach files, use a Project, or point Work to approved sources such as Google Drive, Slack, SharePoint, email, calendars, or a CRM.
3 **Set boundaries**
Name the audience, format, required sources, exclusions, review criteria, and any action it must stop before taking.
4 **Let the agent work**
ChatGPT can gather information, reason across steps, use tools, create a file, and report progress while the task is running.
5 **Review the result**
Check the sources, figures, claims, file contents, and requested format. Ask for focused revisions before sharing or acting on it.
**The best Work prompts define “done”**
Do not stop at “research our competitors.” Ask for a five-company comparison, name the criteria, require source links, specify the output file, and tell ChatGPT what to flag for human review. Clear completion criteria make agent work easier to verify.
## ChatGPT Work Features
ChatGPT Work is not one tool. It is the agent experience that coordinates several capabilities around a task. Which capabilities appear for you depends on the surface, plan, workspace policy, and permissions.
| Feature | What it does | Why it matters | | --- | --- | --- | | Multi-step agent work | Works through a larger task instead of returning only one conversational answer. | Better fit for outcomes that require research, synthesis, creation, checking, and revision. | | Files and finished deliverables | Reads source files and creates documents, presentations, spreadsheets, PDFs, analyses, and other artifacts. | You receive something to review and use, not merely advice about how to make it. | | Plugins and connected apps | Connects to approved tools such as Slack, Google Drive, SharePoint, email, calendars, CRM systems, and project trackers. | The agent can work from current business context instead of relying only on pasted text. | | Skills | Loads reusable instructions, resources, and optional scripts for a specific workflow. | Your preferred method and output format can be applied consistently across repeated tasks. | | Scheduled tasks | Runs a saved task later or on a recurring schedule and keeps a run history. | Useful for recurring reports, reminders, refreshes, follow-up loops, and monitoring. | | Local computer tools | On desktop, Work can use local files, supported apps, and the built-in browser when those tools are available and permitted. | Lets the task use information or software that is not available to a cloud-only chat. | | Local or cloud execution | Desktop users can keep work local or choose cloud when available. | Local is for computer-dependent tasks; cloud can keep running when the app is closed or the computer is off. | | Progress and steering | Shows progress and lets you answer questions, add context, change direction, or request a status recap. | You remain involved without having to restart the task whenever something changes. | | Approvals and permissions | Uses the access granted by your account, workspace, connected service, and execution environment. | Starting Work does not automatically grant access to private files, systems, or high-impact actions. |
## ChatGPT Work vs Regular ChatGPT
**Regular Chat is for thinking with ChatGPT; ChatGPT Work is for delegating a defined outcome.** They live inside the same product, and you can move between them based on the task.
OpenAI’s [Chat, Work, and Codex guide](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/use-chatgpt) frames the choice the same way: use Chat for conversation, Work for a reviewable result, and Codex when you want developer tools and technical detail.
| Difference | Regular Chat | ChatGPT Work | | --- | --- | --- | | Best for | Questions, explanations, brainstorming, short drafts, and quick comparisons | Longer tasks with a clear outcome, multiple steps, tools, sources, or a finished file | | Typical result | An answer or conversational draft | A reviewable deliverable, completed workflow, recurring update, or monitored result | | Agent effort | Usually brief and interactive | Can run for longer and coordinate more context and tool use | | Files and tools | Can use supported Chat features | Designed to combine multiple files, plugins, sources, and steps around the outcome | | Recurring work | Useful for drafting the idea | Can create and run scheduled tasks when the capability is available | | Usage | Standard Chat usage | Shares pricing, credits, and usage limits with Codex |
**Use Chat:** “Give me five ideas for a customer webinar.”
**Use Work:** “Review these customer interviews and product notes. Create an eight-slide webinar deck for small-business owners, cite the supporting evidence, write speaker notes, and flag any claim that needs my review.”
## ChatGPT Work vs Projects
Work and Projects solve different problems. **Work is how ChatGPT executes a substantial task. A Project is where related context and chats stay organized.**
| Question | ChatGPT Work | ChatGPT Project | | --- | --- | --- | | What is it? | An agent mode for completing a task | A container for related chats, files, instructions, and connected sources | | What does it organize? | The steps, tools, and output for one outcome | Shared context across a body of ongoing work | | Can it contain chats? | A Work task runs as a chat | Yes; the same Project can contain both Chat and Work chats | | When should I use it? | When you need a deliverable or multi-step result | When several chats depend on the same files, sources, or instructions | | Simple analogy | The worker completing the assignment | The workspace holding the assignment’s shared materials |
You do not choose one instead of the other. For ongoing client work, create a Project containing the brand guide, research, prior deliverables, and Project instructions. Then start a separate Work chat inside it for each outcome: the strategy brief, the presentation, the spreadsheet, and the weekly update.
If you are deciding among Skills, Projects, and Custom GPTs, use the dedicated [ChatGPT Skills vs Projects vs Custom GPTs comparison](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/chatgpt-skills-vs-projects-vs-gpts/). It owns that broader container decision.
OpenAI’s [Projects and chats documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/projects) confirms that a single Project can contain both regular Chat and ChatGPT Work conversations while sharing Project files, instructions, and connected sources.
**And what about Codex?**
ChatGPT Work and Codex share core agent technology and can overlap. Work presents the experience for everyday knowledge work and finished outputs; Codex exposes developer-focused detail such as Git changes, shell activity, code review, and pull request views. OpenAI says people already using Codex for non-coding work can keep doing so.
## How Do Skills Operate Inside ChatGPT Work?
A skill gives ChatGPT Work a reusable method. OpenAI’s [Build Skills documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills) defines an agent skill as a package of instructions, resources, and optional scripts for a task-specific capability. The Work agent supplies the reasoning and tools; the skill supplies the process it should follow.
For example, a weekly business brief skill can tell Work which sources to check, which sections to create, how to separate facts from recommendations, which risks to flag, and how the final document should look. You can then reuse that method every week without rewriting the workflow.
### Two ways ChatGPT Work can use a skill
1. **Explicitly:** select or mention the skill in your prompt when you want Work to use that exact workflow. 2. **Implicitly:** ChatGPT can choose a skill when your request matches the scope described by the skill.
### Standalone skills vs skills inside plugins
Standalone skills are supported in the ChatGPT desktop app and other Codex surfaces. Skills can also be distributed inside plugins. Plugin-bundled skills are available on supported plugin surfaces, including ChatGPT Work on the web. Plugins may combine a skill with connectors or other tools, which is useful when the workflow needs live data or actions from another service.
**Skills do not give themselves permission**
A skill can describe the workflow and request a tool, but it cannot bypass your plan, workspace policy, connector authorization, file access, sandbox, or approval rules. It makes the method reusable; it does not expand access.
Native Skills access and setup are changing quickly. Use the [ChatGPT Skills availability guide](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/chatgpt-skills-availability/) to check plans and troubleshooting, [learn how to use ChatGPT Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-use-chatgpt-skills/) for day-to-day setup, or follow the [ChatGPT Skill creation guide](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-chatgpt-skill/) to build your own.
Want a practical example? The [AI Weekly Business Brief Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/weekly-business-brief-agent/) is a natural fit for Work because it turns scattered updates into a repeatable, reviewable brief. For more options, see the [best ChatGPT Skills for business owners](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-chatgpt-skills/).
## ChatGPT Work Scheduled Tasks and Monitors
Scheduled tasks let ChatGPT run work later or repeat it in the background. Open **Scheduled** to review active, paused, and completed tasks and see recent runs. A task can use a skill for the repeatable method and a plugin for current data or actions.
### Standalone scheduled tasks
A standalone task starts each run from its saved prompt and reports the result as a separate run in Scheduled. Use it when every run should be independent, such as a Monday competitor update, a monthly analytics summary, or a daily scan for new industry announcements.
### Scheduled tasks inside a chat
A scheduled task inside a chat returns to the same conversation and uses its existing context. Use it when continuity matters: checking whether a long-running operation finished, polling a connected source until something changes, continuing a research loop, or following up on unresolved items.
### What is a ChatGPT Work monitor?
A monitor is not a separate ChatGPT product. It is a scheduled-task pattern: ChatGPT repeatedly checks a source or condition and reports a finding when something relevant changes. The prompt should state what to check, how often to check, what counts as important, what to ignore, when to stop, and which actions require approval.
| Scheduled workflow | Example | Best setup | | --- | --- | --- | | Recurring update | Every Monday, summarize new decisions, blockers, owners, and deadlines from Slack and Google Drive. | Standalone schedule + connected plugins + reporting skill | | Monitor | Check a product page daily and report only meaningful pricing or feature changes. | Cloud schedule + durable change criteria | | Follow-up loop | Return to this chat every 30 minutes until the external process finishes, then summarize the result. | Scheduled task inside the existing chat | | Local file task | Every Friday, update a report using files in a folder on this computer. | Desktop local schedule; computer on and app running |
**Review unattended work carefully**
Test a scheduled prompt manually before automating it. Start with narrow access, review the first runs, and require human approval before sending messages, sharing files, changing records, making purchases, deleting data, or taking another consequential action.
OpenAI’s [scheduled tasks documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/automations) explains the current management, context, permissions, and run behavior in more detail.
## ChatGPT Work Locally vs in the Cloud
On desktop, the **Work locally** control tells you where the task will run. If Cloud is available, choose based on what the task needs—not on which option sounds more powerful.
| Difference | Work locally | Cloud Work | | --- | --- | --- | | Best for | Tasks that need local files, attached folders, desktop apps, or tools on your computer | Hosted tasks, web research, connected sources, and work that should continue without your computer | | Computer requirement | The computer and desktop app must remain available for local scheduled work | Can continue after you close the app or turn off the computer | | Local folder access | Yes, when you grant the relevant access | No direct access to a folder on your computer | | Continue elsewhere | Local conversations stay on that computer | Cloud Work conversations can sync across supported web, mobile, and desktop experiences | | Scheduled monitoring | Useful when the monitored source or files are local | Better when the task checks websites or connected services over time |
On ChatGPT web, Work can use uploaded context and connected tools but cannot work directly in a folder on your computer. Keep durable source material in a Project, upload it, or place it in a connected service that the task can access.
## ChatGPT Work Availability, Plans, Pricing, and Download
**ChatGPT Work and Codex are included in ChatGPT Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, and Enterprise.** OpenAI states that Work uses the same pricing, credits, and usage limits as Codex. Regular Chat usage is separate.
Included does not mean identical. Longer tasks, larger context, more tools, repeated connector calls, scheduled runs, and large outputs can consume more of the shared Work/Codex allowance. Specific tools, models, cloud options, scheduled tasks, plugins, and connected systems can still vary by plan, region, app version, rollout, and workspace settings. Check [OpenAI’s current pricing and usage page](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing) before choosing or changing a plan.
### Is there a separate ChatGPT Work download?
No. ChatGPT Work is built into ChatGPT; there is no separate “ChatGPT Work” installer. To use it on a computer, [download the official ChatGPT desktop app](https://chatgpt.com/download/) for Windows or macOS, sign in, select ChatGPT, and switch the composer from Chat to Work. You can also use Work on ChatGPT web when it is available to your account. OpenAI’s [desktop app guide](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app) shows the same setup path.
### Business, Enterprise, and Edu availability
Workspace access can depend on admin controls, role-based access, plugin policies, connected-source permissions, and usage limits. OpenAI’s [ChatGPT Work admin FAQ](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/work-admin-faq) says Enterprise and Edu web and mobile access launched off by default during a two-week preview beginning July 9, 2026. Because rollout language can lag the live product, the current workspace setting—not the original launch schedule—is the reliable answer for a specific organization.
**If Work is missing**
Update ChatGPT, check the Chat/Work switcher on web or desktop, confirm you are signed into the intended account or workspace, and ask your admin whether ChatGPT Work, plugins, or scheduled tasks are restricted for your role. A missing tool inside Work may be a separate plugin or workspace-permission issue rather than missing Work access.
## What Can You Use ChatGPT Work For?
The strongest use cases have a concrete output and enough complexity to justify delegation. Good starting points include:
* **Create a presentation:** turn notes, research, and meeting materials into a structured deck with speaker notes and cited evidence. * **Build a comparison spreadsheet:** evaluate options against named criteria, flag missing data, and create a summary tab with a recommendation. * **Write a research brief:** combine approved web and internal sources, separate evidence from inference, and produce a decision-ready document. * **Analyze customer feedback:** synthesize interviews, tickets, surveys, or reviews into themes, evidence, risks, and next steps. * **Prepare a weekly work update:** collect decisions, blockers, owners, and deadlines from connected sources on a schedule. * **Monitor a changing source:** check a website, report, dashboard, channel, or tracker and alert you only when a defined condition is met. * **Create a repeatable business workflow:** pair a skill with connected apps so the same review process and output format are used every time.
Use regular Chat for a two-minute answer. Use Work when the finished result would take meaningful manual effort, requires several sources or tools, needs a reusable file, or should be repeated over time.
## How to Start Using ChatGPT Work
1. **Open ChatGPT web or the official desktop app.** On desktop, use the Windows or macOS app rather than searching for a separate Work download. 2. **Select ChatGPT and switch from Chat to Work.** If Work is missing, check your app version, account, plan, rollout, and workspace permissions. 3. **Choose local or cloud.** Use local for computer files and apps; choose cloud when available if the task should continue without your computer. 4. **Describe the outcome.** Include the audience, sources, constraints, output format, definition of done, and anything that needs human approval. 5. **Add files, a Project, plugins, or a skill.** Give Work only the context and access required for that task. 6. **Review the output.** Verify important claims, numbers, sources, file contents, permissions, and actions before using or sharing the result.
**A strong first ChatGPT Work prompt**
“Review the attached customer interview notes and product brief. Create a six-slide presentation for the leadership team. Identify the three strongest customer problems, cite the evidence for each, separate findings from recommendations, and add speaker notes. Flag missing or contradictory information. Return a draft for my review before treating it as final.”
## The Short Version
ChatGPT Work is the mode to choose when you want ChatGPT to complete a substantial task, use multiple sources or tools, create a finished deliverable, or keep work moving on a schedule. Regular Chat gives you an answer. A Project keeps related context together. A Skill supplies a reusable method. Work brings those pieces together around an outcome.
Start with one reviewable task and narrow permissions. Once the output is reliable, turn the method into a skill, place related work in a Project, and schedule only the parts that are safe and useful to repeat.

item.text: Free AI Brand Style Guide Skill: Create Colors, Fonts The free AI Brand Style Guide skill Paste in what your business does and a sample of your own writing — get back a brand style guide: color and font direction, logo do’s and don’ts, an imagery feel, and your voice rules with the words you use and the ones you avoid. One reference every draft can be checked against. Copy it as a prompt, or install it as a real SKILL.md file. This Brand Style Guide skill is a free AI brand guidelines generator that turns your business details and a sample of your writing into one reference document — color and font direction, logo do’s and don’ts, an imagery feel, and your voice and tone rules, including the specific words you use and the ones you avoid. Paste in who you are and how you already sound, and it gives you the guide that keeps everything you publish consistent. It’s built to be re-run, not filed away. Add a product line, launch a sub-brand, bring on a contractor who needs to sound like you — run it again and extend the guide. That’s the difference between a skill and a one-off prompt: the structure of the guide stays the same, so version two slots cleanly onto version one. It defines the rules — it does not design your logo, pick final hex codes for you, or check individual drafts, and it will never invent an award, a tagline you didn’t approve, or a history you don’t have. Use it as a copy-paste prompt in any AI chat, or install the ready-made SKILL.md file so it runs on command in Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark. No coding required. The Brand Style Guide skill takes your business details and a sample of your existing writing and returns a single reference guide with two halves. The visual half: a brand personality, a color palette direction with roles (primary, accent, neutral), a font pairing recommendation, logo do’s and don’ts, and an imagery and photography feel. The verbal half: your voice in three or four traits, tone rules for different situations, a list of words and phrases you use, a list you avoid, and before/after example lines. It defines the rules; it does not audit individual drafts against them — that’s the Brand Voice Check skill, its companion. It works only from what you give it: it suggests directions and describes colors in plain terms, it does not generate a logo image or promise final brand assets, and it will never invent an award, client, or history. The output is text you keep and reuse — a living guide you re-run whenever the brand grows. Two ways to get the Brand Style Guide skill A full guide in about fifteen minutes Landing page copy, SEO metadata, competitor research, email, meeting notes Brand Style Guide skill: what it needs and what it returns What it isA free AI skill — a reusable set of instructions — that turns your business details and a writing sample into one brand reference guide. It comes as a copy-paste prompt and as a ready-made SKILL.md file. Who it’s forBusiness owners who need their brand written down so everything they publish looks and sounds the same. No design background needed. What you give itFive inputs — your business, your audience, a writing sample you’re happy with, any existing colours or fonts, and how you want to come across. What you get backTwo halves in one guide. Visual: brand personality, a colour direction with roles, a font pairing, logo do’s and don’ts, and an imagery feel. Verbal: three or four voice traits, tone rules by situation, words you use, words you avoid, and before/after example lines. What it will not doIt defines the rules; it does not check a draft against them (that’s the Brand Voice Check skill). It does not design a logo, generate images, or produce colour files — it gives direction in plain words. Time to first draftAbout fifteen minutes, most of which is pasting in a writing sample that actually sounds like you. A scattered brand becomes one page everyone can follow By the end of this AI skill guide, you’ll have the Brand Style Guide skill ready to use — as a copy-paste prompt in any AI chat, or installed as a SKILL.md file that runs on command. It handles the thing most small businesses never write down: what the brand looks like, how it sounds, and which words are yours — so every page, post, and email can be held to the same standard instead of reinvented each time. BRAND STYLE GUIDE — a small-batch coffee roaster (example) Brand personality: “Warm, exacting, unpretentious.” Not a lifestyle brand, not a lab — a serious roaster who talks to you like a regular. Color direction: deep espresso brown as primary, a warm cream as neutral, a single burnt-orange accent used only for buttons and highlights — with a note to lock exact hex codes once, then never drift. Type & logo: a sturdy serif for headlines, a clean sans for body; logo do’s and don’ts (“never on a busy photo, never recolored, always with clear space”). Voice rules: “Plain, specific, a little dry.” Words you use: roast, origin, batch, brew. Words you avoid: artisanal, journey, elevate, curated. Before / after: “Embark on a curated coffee journey” → “This week’s roast: an Ethiopian we’re pretty excited about.” Same idea, actually your voice. Needs your input: Your final hex codes · your actual logo file · whether you have a tagline you want protected — flagged, not invented. How to use the Brand Style Guide AI skill in 3 steps Pick a format, paste in a writing sample you’re happy with, and answer its questions before it writes the guide. That’s the whole method — the detail is below. The Brand Style Guide skill is an AI skill — a reusable set of instructions. It comes in two formats below, and they contain the same thinking. Use the prompt if you want a first guide in the next fifteen minutes. Use the SKILL.md file if you’ll grow the brand and want to extend the same guide as you add products, channels, and people. Copy the prompt for a first draft of the guide, or copy the SKILL.md file to install it permanently. Both are below — same instructions, different packaging. Give it your business + a real writing sample The writing sample is what makes the voice yours instead of generic. Paste a page, a few emails, or a couple of posts you’re happy with — the more it’s actually you, the better the guide. Save it, then feed it to the Voice Check skill Keep the guide somewhere you can paste from. From then on, run any draft through the Brand Voice Check skill with this guide attached, and re-run this skill whenever the brand grows. The free AI Brand Style Guide skill

Paste in what your business does and a sample of your own writing — get back a brand style guide: color and font direction, logo do’s and don’ts, an imagery feel, and your voice rules with the words you use and the ones you avoid. One reference every draft can be checked against. Copy it as a prompt, or install it as a real SKILL.md file.

Free prompt + SKILL.md file · Free signup · Setup help

This Brand Style Guide skill is a free AI brand guidelines generator that turns your business details and a sample of your writing into one reference document — color and font direction, logo do’s and don’ts, an imagery feel, and your voice and tone rules, including the specific words you use and the ones you avoid. Paste in who you are and how you already sound, and it gives you the guide that keeps everything you publish consistent.

It’s built to be re-run, not filed away. Add a product line, launch a sub-brand, bring on a contractor who needs to sound like you — run it again and extend the guide. That’s the difference between a skill and a one-off prompt: the structure of the guide stays the same, so version two slots cleanly onto version one.

It defines the rules — it does not design your logo, pick final hex codes for you, or check individual drafts, and it will never invent an award, a tagline you didn’t approve, or a history you don’t have. Use it as a copy-paste prompt in any AI chat, or install the ready-made SKILL.md file so it runs on command in Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark. No coding required.

Quick answer

The Brand Style Guide skill takes your business details and a sample of your existing writing and returns a single reference guide with two halves. The visual half: a brand personality, a color palette direction with roles (primary, accent, neutral), a font pairing recommendation, logo do’s and don’ts, and an imagery and photography feel. The verbal half: your voice in three or four traits, tone rules for different situations, a list of words and phrases you use, a list you avoid, and before/after example lines. It defines the rules; it does not audit individual drafts against them — that’s the Brand Voice Check skill, its companion. It works only from what you give it: it suggests directions and describes colors in plain terms, it does not generate a logo image or promise final brand assets, and it will never invent an award, client, or history. Where the guide needs something real that you didn’t provide — final hex codes, your logo file, an existing tagline you want protected — it lists it under “Needs Your Input” instead of making one up. A brand guide full of invented claims is worse than no guide at all.
Which AI tools does it work with?
Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark all work. Defining a brand means reading your writing sample carefully, so Claude is a natural home, but the prompt builds a guide the same way in all three. The SKILL.md file installs as a saved skill in Claude and Gemini Spark; in ChatGPT you can use a Project or native Skills.
