item.text: Claude vs ChatGPT: Which AI Agent Is Better? Claude vs ChatGPT is no longer just a comparison between two chatbots. Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Work can now research, use connected services, work with local files, run multi-step tasks, create finished deliverables, and repeat work on a schedule. The more useful question is not which one gives the cleverest one-paragraph answer. It is which AI agent fits the way your work actually gets done. Claude is the stronger choice for direct desktop app control, personal Skills on individual plans, and polished Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF creation. ChatGPT is the stronger choice for switching between cloud and local work, operating in an integrated browser, running trigger-based monitoring, installing from a shared plugin directory, and building publishable Sites. Both are capable business agents. The winner depends on whether your workflow is centered on files and desktop applications or on connected, cloud-based work that should continue across devices. Claude vs ChatGPT — which AI agent is better? Choose Claude Cowork if you want an agent to work directly across approved desktop apps, create professional Microsoft Office and PDF files, or use custom Skills on a personal plan. Choose ChatGPT Work if you want a clear choice between local and cloud execution, a built-in signed-in browser, event-triggered scheduled tasks, a universal plugin directory, or a finished website you can publish as a ChatGPT Site. Both can use local files on Mac and Windows, connect to business tools, create deliverables, and continue work across desktop, web, and mobile. Claude has the edge for desktop and document workflows; ChatGPT has the edge for cloud, browser, and ecosystem workflows. The Agent Comparison Most Claude vs ChatGPT Articles Miss Claude and ChatGPT are broad product families, not single features. Each still has a normal chat experience for answers, explanations, brainstorming, and short drafts. That is not the part this article compares. The like-for-like comparison is Claude Cowork vs ChatGPT Work. Cowork is Claude’s agentic work mode. Work is ChatGPT’s agentic work mode. Both accept a defined outcome, break it into steps, use approved files and tools, show progress, ask for decisions, and return work you can review. OpenAI now directs longer, multi-step tasks and finished deliverables to Work; its previous ChatGPT Agent experience is no longer available. This scope matters. A general model benchmark might tell you which model scored higher on a test, but it will not tell you whether the agent can edit a local folder, control an app, reuse your operating procedure, run on Monday morning, or create the file format your client expects. Those practical capabilities are what determine which AI agent is better for business. The simplest mental model Chat is for a response. An agent is for a result. Use ordinary Claude or ChatGPT Chat when the work can be completed in one conversation. Use Cowork or Work when the task needs several sources, tools, actions, a saved deliverable, or an ongoing schedule. Claude vs ChatGPT: Side-by-Side AI Agent Comparison This table compares currently documented Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Work capabilities as of July 26, 2026. Availability can vary by plan, workspace policy, operating system, region, and rollout. Feature Claude Cowork ChatGPT Work Best choice Best overall fit File-heavy, document-heavy, and direct desktop workflows Cloud-connected, browser-heavy, monitored, and cross-device workflows Depends where the work lives Local files Reads and writes within folders connected through Claude Desktop Reads and writes within local folders or projects opened in the desktop app Tie Desktop app control Computer use can click, type, and navigate approved apps on Mac and Windows Can use approved desktop apps and local tools; capabilities depend on the available plugin or tool Claude for general UI control Browser work Uses Claude in Chrome and can navigate websites through Cowork Built-in desktop browser with its own state, tabs, downloads, sign-in, and annotations; cloud browser for public sites ChatGPT Cloud or local execution Remote Cowork sessions plus desktop access to local files, browser, and apps Explicit Work locally or Cloud choice in the desktop composer ChatGPT for clarity Connected services Connectors, desktop extensions, remote MCP, and plugins Apps, connectors, MCP tools, and plugins Tie Plugins Plugins can bundle Skills, connectors, sub-agents, and hooks; organization marketplaces supported Universal ChatGPT and Codex directory can bundle Skills, connectors, MCP, browser capabilities, hooks, and schedule templates ChatGPT for one shared directory Personal Skills Custom Skills available across Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise when enabled Personal Skills generally available for Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu Claude for individuals Scheduled tasks Recurring and on-demand tasks; remote schedules can use account files, connectors, Skills, and plugins One-time, recurring, event-triggered, and monitoring tasks ChatGPT for triggers Office and PDF files Creates DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, and PDF files with built-in document Skills Creates and edits documents, spreadsheets, presentations, PDFs, and native Google files; direct desktop Office support varies Claude for portable Office files Website creation Can create website files and live artifacts; publishing depends on the chosen tool or host Can create, preview, share, and publish ChatGPT Sites ChatGPT Cross-device continuity Remote sessions can be started, steered, and reviewed across desktop, web, and mobile Cloud Work chats sync across desktop, web, and mobile Tie Safety boundary Remote code runs in isolation; local files are permission-scoped; computer use has no sandbox between Claude and an approved app Local command work uses sandbox and approval controls; websites, plugins, and connected services have separate permissions ChatGPT for configurable local sandboxing Our overall verdict Claude is the better desktop-and-document agent. It has the cleaner advantage when the work must cross arbitrary desktop apps, produce portable Office files, or use a custom Skill on an individual account. ChatGPT is the better cloud-and-browser agent. Its built-in browser, explicit local/cloud choice, event-triggered schedules, shared plugin directory, and Sites publishing make it stronger for connected workflows that should keep running and remain accessible across devices. There is no honest universal winner. Local Files and Desktop Apps Both Claude and ChatGPT can answer questions about local files correctly when you give the agent access to the right folder. On desktop, both can inspect source material, edit files, create new outputs, and save the result locally. Neither should receive your entire home directory as a first test. Where Claude is stronger Claude Cowork’s clearest advantage is computer use. When a connector or browser tool cannot complete the task, Claude can interact with an approved desktop application by clicking, typing, opening files, and navigating the interface. Anthropic documents this on both macOS and Windows for Pro and Max users. That makes Claude a strong fit for messy real-world workflows: read source files from a local folder, open a niche business application with no connector, transfer approved information into a spreadsheet, and save a formatted report. The tradeoff is risk and reliability. Computer use is a research preview, Team and Enterprise do not currently have access, screen interaction is slower than a connector, and Anthropic says there is no sandbox between Claude and an application after you approve access. Where ChatGPT is stronger ChatGPT Work offers an unusually clear decision inside the desktop app: keep Work locally selected when a task needs files or apps on your computer, or choose Cloud when the work should continue after the app closes and remain available on web or mobile. Local commands operate inside a configurable sandbox and approval boundary rather than receiving unrestricted machine access by default. ChatGPT can also use desktop apps when an appropriate tool, plugin, add-in, or computer-use capability is available. Its strength is the permission system and the ability to choose a bounded local workspace. Claude’s strength is the documented fallback to direct general-purpose screen control. Local-work verdict: Claude wins for cross-app control; otherwise it is a tie Choose Claude when the task must operate an application that has no good integration. Choose either agent for controlled local-folder analysis and file creation. Start with one dedicated folder containing copies, define exactly what may change, and inspect the diff or output before replacing an original. Browser Work and Web Research Both agents can search the web, gather sources, compare information, and interact with websites. The difference is how browser work is divided between supervised local browsing and unattended cloud work. Claude’s browser route Claude Cowork can use Claude in Chrome to read, click, navigate, and fill forms. Claude normally prefers a direct connector, then the browser, then screen interaction. That order is sensible: direct integrations are usually faster and more reliable than visual navigation. ChatGPT’s two browser routes ChatGPT Work has a built-in browser on macOS and Windows. It has its own browser state, supports sign-in, tabs, downloads, password management, extensions, and page annotations, and lets you watch the work. If a task needs your existing Chrome session, the separate Chrome extension can use the profile and open tabs you already have. ChatGPT also has a cloud browser for supported public websites. It can continue after you leave, but it cannot sign in or complete payments at launch. This separation is useful: use the local built-in browser for signed-in or supervised work, and cloud browser for public research that can run in the background. Browser verdict: ChatGPT wins Claude is capable in Chrome, but ChatGPT provides the more complete browser system: an integrated signed-in desktop browser, an existing-Chrome option, and a separate cloud browser for public background work. Connected Apps, Plugins, and Business Systems Neither agent is limited to information inside the chat. Claude connects to services through remote connectors, desktop extensions, MCP servers, and plugins. ChatGPT uses apps, connectors, MCP tools, and plugins. In both systems, the agent can only use the services and actions allowed by the account, workspace administrator, and underlying service permissions. Claude’s modular tool system Claude supports remote connectors across surfaces and local desktop extensions for tools that run on your computer. Its plugins can bundle Skills, connectors, sub-agents, and hooks into one workflow. Anthropic documents connections for services such as Google Drive, Gmail, Slack, and DocuSign, and Team or Enterprise owners can distribute curated plugins through organization marketplaces. ChatGPT’s universal plugin directory ChatGPT Work and Codex share a universal plugin directory. A plugin can contain reusable Skills, connectors, MCP servers, browser capabilities, hooks, and scheduled-task templates. A business can install a Gmail or Google Drive plugin for everyday Work tasks and use compatible parts of that same plugin in Codex rather than maintaining unrelated tool catalogs. The practical difference is not the number of logos in a directory. It is whether the system you need offers the exact read and write actions required for your workflow. A Slack connector that can search messages but cannot post a reviewed update is not equivalent to one that supports both. Check the requested permissions and action list before choosing either platform. Apps and plugin verdict: slight ChatGPT win Both ecosystems are powerful and use open integration patterns. ChatGPT receives a slight edge because one public directory serves ChatGPT Work and Codex and can package a particularly broad set of capability types. Claude remains highly competitive and may be better when a local desktop extension is the most direct route to the tool. Scheduled Tasks and Background Work Recurring work is where both products start to feel like agents instead of chatbots. Each can produce regular briefings, refresh reports, monitor a topic, and use approved connected sources without rebuilding the prompt every time. Claude Cowork schedules Claude scheduled tasks are available in Cowork on paid plans. Remote schedules can run when your computer is asleep and can use connectors, account files, Skills, and installed plugins. Claude supports hourly, daily, weekly, weekday, manual, and on-demand patterns. A remote scheduled task cannot reach an arbitrary folder on your computer; a schedule that requires local files or apps must run locally with the necessary computer available. ChatGPT Work schedules ChatGPT Work can run once, repeat on a schedule, respond to a supported trigger, or monitor for changes. Cloud scheduled work does not depend on your computer being awake. The trigger and monitoring options give ChatGPT a meaningful advantage for workflows that should react to an external event rather than run only at a fixed time. Scheduled tasks should not be treated as a license to remove review. Both agents may encounter stale data, missing permissions, prompt injection, or a source that changed structure. Start with a draft-only output, review several runs, and allow sending, publishing, deletion, or financial actions only when the workflow has an appropriate approval step. Schedule verdict: ChatGPT wins for event-driven work For a standard daily or weekly report, both are strong. Choose ChatGPT when the job must react to an event or monitor for changes. Choose Claude when the recurring result depends heavily on a Claude Skill, Cowork plugin, or Claude-connected document workflow. Skills and Reusable Workflows Skills are reusable workflow packages. Instead of rewriting your process every week, you save the instructions, examples, rules, and supporting resources so the agent can apply the same method when a matching task appears. This is more valuable than a collection of clever prompts because a Skill can define how the work is checked and what the output must contain. Claude Skills Claude Skills are currently available on Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise when code execution and file creation are enabled. Claude includes built-in Skills for Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and PDF work; individuals can upload custom Skills; and organizations can provision or share approved Skills. Claude can invoke a relevant Skill automatically. This is a major advantage for a solo operator or small business owner. You can use a formal native Skill without first moving into an enterprise workspace. Follow the step-by-step guide to create a Claude Skill, or start from the free Claude Skills library. ChatGPT Skills ChatGPT Skills are reusable, shareable workflows that can include instructions, examples, and code. ChatGPT can create them with chat, edit them, upload them, share them with selected colleagues, or publish them to a workspace. However, Personal Skills are currently generally available for Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu. They must be added separately on desktop and web/mobile and do not automatically sync between those surfaces. If your account does not have native Personal Skills, the underlying method still works: paste a well-structured workflow into ChatGPT, save it in a Project or Custom GPT where appropriate, and reuse it manually. Our ChatGPT Skills availability guide explains the current plan rules, while the free ChatGPT Skills library gives you portable instructions you can use immediately. Skills verdict: Claude wins for individuals; ChatGPT is strong for managed teams Claude makes native custom Skills available to a much broader range of individual accounts. ChatGPT has excellent workspace sharing, access, and compliance controls where Personal Skills are eligible. Both follow an open Agent Skills approach, so the best workflow logic can often be adapted rather than rebuilt. Documents, Spreadsheets, Presentations, and Sites The best AI agent does not merely summarize your sources. It returns the format the next person can actually use. Claude for portable business files Claude can directly create Excel spreadsheets, PowerPoint presentations, Word documents, and PDFs. Its built-in document Skills support working formulas, charts, visualizations, and structured reports. File creation is documented across Claude web, desktop, and mobile, including Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise. Claude is therefore the cleaner first choice when the deliverable must be a downloadable DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, or PDF that opens outside the AI platform. It can also use supported Microsoft 365 add-ins and coordinate information across Excel and PowerPoint in eligible workflows. ChatGPT for connected files and Sites ChatGPT Work creates and edits documents, spreadsheets, presentations, reports, and analyses. It can create native Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides when the appropriate Google Workspace app is enabled. The desktop app previews supported files beside the chat and supports targeted annotations. Direct inspection and editing of an open Excel workbook uses Codex with the ChatGPT for Excel add-in, and OpenAI says PowerPoint is not included in that specific Work desktop flow at launch. ChatGPT’s distinctive output is a ChatGPT Site: a web experience the agent can create, preview, revise, save, and publish. If the finished result is an interactive internal tool, landing page, directory, tracker, or client portal rather than a static document, ChatGPT has the clearer advantage. Output verdict: Claude for Office files; ChatGPT for Sites and Google-native work Choose Claude when portability into Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or PDF is the requirement. Choose ChatGPT when the output should live natively in Google Workspace or become a hosted Site. For either agent, verify formulas, citations, branding, accessibility, permissions, and sharing settings before delivery. Desktop, Web, Mobile, and Cross-Device Continuity The old shorthand that Claude Cowork is desktop-only and ChatGPT is cloud-only is no longer accurate. Both agents now combine remote work with desktop access. Claude Cowork runs on desktop, web, and mobile, with remote sessions in beta. You can start, steer, and review tasks across devices. Remote sessions continue after the laptop closes. Local files, local connectors, Chrome, and computer use still depend on Claude Desktop being open on the computer that grants access. ChatGPT Work also runs on desktop, web, and mobile. Cloud Work chats sync across those surfaces. A cloud task can continue when the computer is off; a local task stays tied to the desktop and its approved folders or apps. ChatGPT Work’s explicit local/cloud selector makes this boundary easier for a beginner to understand before starting. Device verdict: tie, with a usability edge to ChatGPT Both agents now support genuine cross-device work. ChatGPT makes the execution choice more visible. Claude offers a similarly capable remote/local bridge, but its web and mobile Cowork experience is still described as beta and rolling out. Privacy, Permissions, and Safety An agent that can read email, edit a file, operate a browser, or run on a schedule creates more risk than a chatbot that only drafts text. The safest product is not the one with the longest security page. It is the one you configure with the smallest practical access boundary and supervise in proportion to the consequences. Claude’s safety model Claude Cowork remote sessions run in isolated temporary environments on Anthropic’s servers. Local access is limited to folders and tools you connect, and deletion requires explicit permission. Computer use is different: it takes screenshots, interacts directly with approved apps, and has no sandbox between Claude and those applications. Anthropic recommends blocking sensitive apps and staying close to consequential tasks. ChatGPT’s safety model ChatGPT’s local agent commands operate inside a sandbox with separate approval policies. You can choose a read-only or workspace-write boundary, maintain website allowlists and blocklists, and require approval before broader access. Plugins and external services retain their own authentication and permissions, and browser content should still be treated as untrusted. Business data and personal data are not the same For both vendors, consumer and commercial data terms differ. OpenAI states that ChatGPT Business and Enterprise data is not used for model training by default. Anthropic handles Team and Enterprise under its commercial terms and states in the Cowork architecture overview that commercial Cowork data is not used to train Claude. Consumer-account settings and policies can be different. Review the current terms for the exact plan you will use rather than assuming a brand-wide rule. Use this minimum-safe setup in either agent Create a dedicated working folder. Use copies of important files. Connect only the service needed for the current task. Keep approvals on. Ask for a draft before sending or publishing. Review links, formulas, recipients, permissions, and final files yourself. Do not begin with banking, healthcare, legal, credential, payment, or production-deletion workflows. Which AI Agent Is Better for Your Use Case? The right answer becomes much clearer when the decision is attached to a real job. Your main job Better starting point Why Analyze and reorganize a local folder Either Both work inside approved local folders on desktop Operate a niche desktop app with no connector Claude Claude computer use is a documented general screen-interaction fallback Create a client-ready Word report Claude Native DOCX creation and a professional Word Skill Build a complex Excel workbook Claude for a new file; ChatGPT/Codex for an open workbook ChatGPT can work directly inside supported Excel and Google Sheets workbooks, and it now supports reusable Skills within those spreadsheet experiences. Claude remains stronger for generating portable XLSX files from scratch, while ChatGPT is especially useful when the workbook already exists and the workflow should run beside it. Create native Google Docs, Sheets, or Slides ChatGPT Work can create and edit native Google files through enabled apps Research across signed-in websites ChatGPT The built-in browser supports sign-in, tabs, downloads, and annotations Monitor changes and react to an event ChatGPT Scheduled Tasks support triggers and monitoring as well as fixed schedules Run a weekly connected briefing Either Both can use connectors, Skills, and remote scheduled execution Create a custom native Skill on a personal plan Claude Claude custom Skills are available across individual plans when enabled Govern and share Skills across a large workspace Either Both offer admin controls, organization distribution, and access management Build and publish an interactive website ChatGPT Sites provides an integrated creation, preview, access, and hosting workflow Mix local files, browser research, and desktop apps Claude Claude’s connector → browser → screen-control path covers more fallback routes Claude or ChatGPT: The Final Decision Use these questions in order: Does the task need direct control of an ordinary desktop application with no connector? Start with Claude Cowork. Does the task need a signed-in, multi-tab browser that you can watch and annotate? Start with ChatGPT Work. Must the final deliverable be a polished DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, or PDF? Start with Claude. Must the deliverable be a native Google file or a published interactive Site? Start with ChatGPT. Do you need a native personal Skill on an individual account? Choose Claude under the current access rules. Must the workflow react to an event or monitor for changes? Choose ChatGPT. Is it a normal local-folder task or fixed weekly briefing? Either can work; choose the one already connected to your tools. Still unsure? Run the same low-risk, 30-minute task in both with identical files, instructions, and acceptance criteria. The bottom line: Claude Cowork is the better AI agent for work that ends in a professional file or crosses the visible desktop. ChatGPT Work is the better AI agent for work that lives in browsers, plugins, cloud execution, monitored events, or a hosted Site. If your business does both, using both is not redundant: let Claude handle document and desktop depth, and let ChatGPT handle cloud and browser breadth. Comparing all three AI agents? Gemini Spark changes the decision when your workflow lives in a personal Google Account. Start with the best AI agents for business — the full three-way comparison with a side-by-side table, eligibility rules, and a decision tree covering all three at once. Prefer the other head-to-head pairings? Read Claude Desktop vs Gemini Spark for Claude’s desktop-and-document strengths versus Spark’s Google integration, or see ChatGPT vs Gemini Spark for the choice between ChatGPT’s broader business workflows and Spark’s Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Tasks, Keep, and Mac-folder workflows. Official Sources and How We Compared Them This article uses current product documentation, not subjective writing samples or unsourced benchmark roundups. We compared the agents as work systems: where tasks run, what information they can reach, which actions they can take, how recurring work operates, what deliverables they produce, who can use reusable workflows, and which permission boundaries apply. Anthropic: Use Claude Cowork on web, desktop, and mobile Anthropic: Let Claude use your computer in Cowork Anthropic: Schedule recurring tasks in Claude Cowork Anthropic: Use Skills in Claude Anthropic: Create and edit files with Claude OpenAI: ChatGPT Work and Codex OpenAI: Get started with ChatGPT Work OpenAI: Using the built-in browser in the ChatGPT desktop app OpenAI: Skills in ChatGPT OpenAI: Plugins Last fact-checked: July 26, 2026. Both products are changing quickly. Recheck plan access, rollout notes, preview features, and file-format limitations before making a purchase decision based on one must-have capability. Is Claude better than ChatGPT? Claude is better for direct desktop app control, native personal Skills across individual plans, and creating portable Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF files. ChatGPT is better for its integrated browser, explicit cloud and local modes, event-triggered scheduled tasks, universal plugin directory, and publishable Sites. The better choice depends on the workflow rather than one universal ranking. What is the difference between Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Work? Both are agentic work modes that complete multi-step tasks using approved files and tools. Claude Cowork is strongest in desktop control, document creation, and broadly available custom Skills. ChatGPT Work is strongest in cloud and local flexibility, browser workflows, trigger-based schedules, plugins shared with Codex, and Sites. Can Claude and ChatGPT both access local files? Yes. Claude Cowork can read and write within folders connected through Claude Desktop. ChatGPT Work can use local folders or projects opened in the ChatGPT desktop app. Web and mobile sessions do not independently receive unrestricted access to your computer; local access depends on the relevant desktop host and permissions. Which is better for working with desktop apps? Claude is the better current choice for general desktop app control because computer use can click, type, and navigate approved apps when no connector exists. It is a research preview for Pro and Max and has important safety limitations. ChatGPT can use approved apps and add-ins, but support depends more heavily on the available tool or plugin. Which is better for web research and browser tasks? ChatGPT has the stronger browser system. Its desktop app includes a built-in browser with sign-in, tabs, downloads, annotations, and its own browser state. It also offers a cloud browser for supported public websites. Claude can browse and act through Claude in Chrome and remains highly capable for browser-assisted Cowork tasks. Is Claude or ChatGPT better for Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF files? Claude is the cleaner choice for creating portable Office and PDF deliverables because it directly supports DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, and PDF creation with built-in document Skills. ChatGPT Work also creates and edits common business files and supports native Google files, but direct desktop Office integration varies by application and surface. Do Claude and ChatGPT both support Skills? Yes. Both support reusable workflow packages with instructions and supporting resources. Claude custom Skills are available across Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise when code execution is enabled. ChatGPT Personal Skills are currently generally available for Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu, although portable skill instructions can still be used manually on other plans. Can Claude and ChatGPT run scheduled tasks? Yes. Both can run recurring work remotely using approved connected sources. Claude supports standard recurring schedules and on-demand runs. ChatGPT also supports one-time tasks, recurring schedules, event triggers, and monitoring for changes, which gives it the advantage for event-driven workflows. Is Claude or ChatGPT safer for business files? Either can be configured for safer business use, and neither removes the need for review. ChatGPT offers explicit local sandbox and approval controls. Claude scopes files and tools through permissions and isolates remote execution, but Claude computer use has no sandbox between the agent and an approved app. Use a commercial plan with the appropriate data terms, grant minimum access, and keep human review for consequential actions. Can I use Claude and ChatGPT together? Yes. A practical division is Claude for deep file synthesis, portable business documents, and mixed desktop workflows, with ChatGPT for browser research, connected cloud workflows, event-driven schedules, and Sites. Reusing the same workflow instructions and review checklist across both helps keep quality consistent.

Our overall verdict

Claude is the better desktop-and-document agent. It has the cleaner advantage when the work must cross arbitrary desktop apps, produce portable Office files, or use a custom Skill on an individual account. ChatGPT is the better cloud-and-browser agent. Its built-in browser, explicit local/cloud choice, event-triggered schedules, shared plugin directory, and Sites publishing make it stronger for connected workflows that should keep running and remain accessible across devices. There is no honest universal winner.

Local Files and Desktop Apps

Both Claude and ChatGPT can answer questions about local files correctly when you give the agent access to the right folder. On desktop, both can inspect source material, edit files, create new outputs, and save the result locally. Neither should receive your entire home directory as a first test.

Where Claude is stronger

Claude Cowork’s clearest advantage is computer use. When a connector or browser tool cannot complete the task, Claude can interact with an approved desktop application by clicking, typing, opening files, and navigating the interface. Anthropic documents this on both macOS and Windows for Pro and Max users.

That makes Claude a strong fit for messy real-world workflows: read source files from a local folder, open a niche business application with no connector, transfer approved information into a spreadsheet, and save a formatted report. The tradeoff is risk and reliability. Computer use is a research preview, Team and Enterprise do not currently have access, screen interaction is slower than a connector, and Anthropic says there is no sandbox between Claude and an application after you approve access.

Where ChatGPT is stronger

ChatGPT Work offers an unusually clear decision inside the desktop app: keep Work locally selected when a task needs files or apps on your computer, or choose Cloud when the work should continue after the app closes and remain available on web or mobile. Local commands operate inside a configurable sandbox and approval boundary rather than receiving unrestricted machine access by default.

ChatGPT can also use desktop apps when an appropriate tool, plugin, add-in, or computer-use capability is available. Its strength is the permission system and the ability to choose a bounded local workspace. Claude’s strength is the documented fallback to direct general-purpose screen control.

Local-work verdict: Claude wins for cross-app control; otherwise it is a tie

Choose Claude when the task must operate an application that has no good integration. Choose either agent for controlled local-folder analysis and file creation. Start with one dedicated folder containing copies, define exactly what may change, and inspect the diff or output before replacing an original.

Browser Work and Web Research

Both agents can search the web, gather sources, compare information, and interact with websites. The difference is how browser work is divided between supervised local browsing and unattended cloud work.

Claude’s browser route

Claude Cowork can use Claude in Chrome to read, click, navigate, and fill forms. Claude normally prefers a direct connector, then the browser, then screen interaction. That order is sensible: direct integrations are usually faster and more reliable than visual navigation.

ChatGPT’s two browser routes

ChatGPT Work has a built-in browser on macOS and Windows. It has its own browser state, supports sign-in, tabs, downloads, password management, extensions, and page annotations, and lets you watch the work. If a task needs your existing Chrome session, the separate Chrome extension can use the profile and open tabs you already have.

ChatGPT also has a cloud browser for supported public websites. It can continue after you leave, but it cannot sign in or complete payments at launch. This separation is useful: use the local built-in browser for signed-in or supervised work, and cloud browser for public research that can run in the background.

Browser verdict: ChatGPT wins

Claude is capable in Chrome, but ChatGPT provides the more complete browser system: an integrated signed-in desktop browser, an existing-Chrome option, and a separate cloud browser for public background work.

Connected Apps, Plugins, and Business Systems

Neither agent is limited to information inside the chat. Claude connects to services through remote connectors, desktop extensions, MCP servers, and plugins. ChatGPT uses apps, connectors, MCP tools, and plugins. In both systems, the agent can only use the services and actions allowed by the account, workspace administrator, and underlying service permissions.

Claude’s modular tool system

Claude supports remote connectors across surfaces and local desktop extensions for tools that run on your computer. Its plugins can bundle Skills, connectors, sub-agents, and hooks into one workflow. Anthropic documents connections for services such as Google Drive, Gmail, Slack, and DocuSign, and Team or Enterprise owners can distribute curated plugins through organization marketplaces.

ChatGPT’s universal plugin directory

ChatGPT Work and Codex share a universal plugin directory. A plugin can contain reusable Skills, connectors, MCP servers, browser capabilities, hooks, and scheduled-task templates. A business can install a Gmail or Google Drive plugin for everyday Work tasks and use compatible parts of that same plugin in Codex rather than maintaining unrelated tool catalogs.

The practical difference is not the number of logos in a directory. It is whether the system you need offers the exact read and write actions required for your workflow. A Slack connector that can search messages but cannot post a reviewed update is not equivalent to one that supports both. Check the requested permissions and action list before choosing either platform.

Apps and plugin verdict: slight ChatGPT win

Both ecosystems are powerful and use open integration patterns. ChatGPT receives a slight edge because one public directory serves ChatGPT Work and Codex and can package a particularly broad set of capability types. Claude remains highly competitive and may be better when a local desktop extension is the most direct route to the tool.

Scheduled Tasks and Background Work

Recurring work is where both products start to feel like agents instead of chatbots. Each can produce regular briefings, refresh reports, monitor a topic, and use approved connected sources without rebuilding the prompt every time.

Claude Cowork schedules

Claude scheduled tasks are available in Cowork on paid plans. Remote schedules can run when your computer is asleep and can use connectors, account files, Skills, and installed plugins. Claude supports hourly, daily, weekly, weekday, manual, and on-demand patterns. A remote scheduled task cannot reach an arbitrary folder on your computer; a schedule that requires local files or apps must run locally with the necessary computer available.

ChatGPT Work schedules

ChatGPT Work can run once, repeat on a schedule, respond to a supported trigger, or monitor for changes. Cloud scheduled work does not depend on your computer being awake. The trigger and monitoring options give ChatGPT a meaningful advantage for workflows that should react to an external event rather than run only at a fixed time.

Scheduled tasks should not be treated as a license to remove review. Both agents may encounter stale data, missing permissions, prompt injection, or a source that changed structure. Start with a draft-only output, review several runs, and allow sending, publishing, deletion, or financial actions only when the workflow has an appropriate approval step.

Schedule verdict: ChatGPT wins for event-driven work

For a standard daily or weekly report, both are strong. Choose ChatGPT when the job must react to an event or monitor for changes. Choose Claude when the recurring result depends heavily on a Claude Skill, Cowork plugin, or Claude-connected document workflow.

Skills and Reusable Workflows

Skills are reusable workflow packages. Instead of rewriting your process every week, you save the instructions, examples, rules, and supporting resources so the agent can apply the same method when a matching task appears. This is more valuable than a collection of clever prompts because a Skill can define how the work is checked and what the output must contain.

Claude Skills

Claude Skills are currently available on Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise when code execution and file creation are enabled. Claude includes built-in Skills for Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and PDF work; individuals can upload custom Skills; and organizations can provision or share approved Skills. Claude can invoke a relevant Skill automatically.

This is a major advantage for a solo operator or small business owner. You can use a formal native Skill without first moving into an enterprise workspace. Follow the step-by-step guide to create a Claude Skill, or start from the free Claude Skills library.

ChatGPT Skills

ChatGPT Skills are reusable, shareable workflows that can include instructions, examples, and code. ChatGPT can create them with chat, edit them, upload them, share them with selected colleagues, or publish them to a workspace. However, Personal Skills are currently generally available for Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu. They must be added separately on desktop and web/mobile and do not automatically sync between those surfaces.

If your account does not have native Personal Skills, the underlying method still works: paste a well-structured workflow into ChatGPT, save it in a Project or Custom GPT where appropriate, and reuse it manually. Our ChatGPT Skills availability guide explains the current plan rules, while the free ChatGPT Skills library gives you portable instructions you can use immediately.

Skills verdict: Claude wins for individuals; ChatGPT is strong for managed teams

Claude makes native custom Skills available to a much broader range of individual accounts. ChatGPT has excellent workspace sharing, access, and compliance controls where Personal Skills are eligible. Both follow an open Agent Skills approach, so the best workflow logic can often be adapted rather than rebuilt.

Documents, Spreadsheets, Presentations, and Sites

The best AI agent does not merely summarize your sources. It returns the format the next person can actually use.

Claude for portable business files

Claude can directly create Excel spreadsheets, PowerPoint presentations, Word documents, and PDFs. Its built-in document Skills support working formulas, charts, visualizations, and structured reports. File creation is documented across Claude web, desktop, and mobile, including Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise.

Claude is therefore the cleaner first choice when the deliverable must be a downloadable DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, or PDF that opens outside the AI platform. It can also use supported Microsoft 365 add-ins and coordinate information across Excel and PowerPoint in eligible workflows.

ChatGPT for connected files and Sites

ChatGPT Work creates and edits documents, spreadsheets, presentations, reports, and analyses. It can create native Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides when the appropriate Google Workspace app is enabled. The desktop app previews supported files beside the chat and supports targeted annotations. Direct inspection and editing of an open Excel workbook uses Codex with the ChatGPT for Excel add-in, and OpenAI says PowerPoint is not included in that specific Work desktop flow at launch.

ChatGPT’s distinctive output is a ChatGPT Site: a web experience the agent can create, preview, revise, save, and publish. If the finished result is an interactive internal tool, landing page, directory, tracker, or client portal rather than a static document, ChatGPT has the clearer advantage.

Output verdict: Claude for Office files; ChatGPT for Sites and Google-native work

Choose Claude when portability into Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or PDF is the requirement. Choose ChatGPT when the output should live natively in Google Workspace or become a hosted Site. For either agent, verify formulas, citations, branding, accessibility, permissions, and sharing settings before delivery.

Desktop, Web, Mobile, and Cross-Device Continuity

The old shorthand that Claude Cowork is desktop-only and ChatGPT is cloud-only is no longer accurate. Both agents now combine remote work with desktop access.

Claude Cowork runs on desktop, web, and mobile, with remote sessions in beta. You can start, steer, and review tasks across devices. Remote sessions continue after the laptop closes. Local files, local connectors, Chrome, and computer use still depend on Claude Desktop being open on the computer that grants access.

ChatGPT Work also runs on desktop, web, and mobile. Cloud Work chats sync across those surfaces. A cloud task can continue when the computer is off; a local task stays tied to the desktop and its approved folders or apps. ChatGPT Work’s explicit local/cloud selector makes this boundary easier for a beginner to understand before starting.

Device verdict: tie, with a usability edge to ChatGPT

Both agents now support genuine cross-device work. ChatGPT makes the execution choice more visible. Claude offers a similarly capable remote/local bridge, but its web and mobile Cowork experience is still described as beta and rolling out.

Privacy, Permissions, and Safety

An agent that can read email, edit a file, operate a browser, or run on a schedule creates more risk than a chatbot that only drafts text. The safest product is not the one with the longest security page. It is the one you configure with the smallest practical access boundary and supervise in proportion to the consequences.

Claude’s safety model

Claude Cowork remote sessions run in isolated temporary environments on Anthropic’s servers. Local access is limited to folders and tools you connect, and deletion requires explicit permission. Computer use is different: it takes screenshots, interacts directly with approved apps, and has no sandbox between Claude and those applications. Anthropic recommends blocking sensitive apps and staying close to consequential tasks.

ChatGPT’s safety model

ChatGPT’s local agent commands operate inside a sandbox with separate approval policies. You can choose a read-only or workspace-write boundary, maintain website allowlists and blocklists, and require approval before broader access. Plugins and external services retain their own authentication and permissions, and browser content should still be treated as untrusted.

Business data and personal data are not the same

For both vendors, consumer and commercial data terms differ. OpenAI states that ChatGPT Business and Enterprise data is not used for model training by default. Anthropic handles Team and Enterprise under its commercial terms and states in the Cowork architecture overview that commercial Cowork data is not used to train Claude. Consumer-account settings and policies can be different. Review the current terms for the exact plan you will use rather than assuming a brand-wide rule.

Use this minimum-safe setup in either agent

Create a dedicated working folder. Use copies of important files. Connect only the service needed for the current task. Keep approvals on. Ask for a draft before sending or publishing. Review links, formulas, recipients, permissions, and final files yourself. Do not begin with banking, healthcare, legal, credential, payment, or production-deletion workflows.

Which AI Agent Is Better for Your Use Case?

The right answer becomes much clearer when the decision is attached to a real job.

Your main job Better starting point Why
Analyze and reorganize a local folder Either Both work inside approved local folders on desktop
Operate a niche desktop app with no connector Claude Claude computer use is a documented general screen-interaction fallback
Create a client-ready Word report Claude Native DOCX creation and a professional Word Skill
Build a complex Excel workbook Claude for a new file; ChatGPT/Codex for an open workbook ChatGPT can work directly inside supported Excel and Google Sheets workbooks, and it now supports reusable Skills within those spreadsheet experiences. Claude remains stronger for generating portable XLSX files from scratch, while ChatGPT is especially useful when the workbook already exists and the workflow should run beside it.
Create native Google Docs, Sheets, or Slides ChatGPT Work can create and edit native Google files through enabled apps
Research across signed-in websites ChatGPT The built-in browser supports sign-in, tabs, downloads, and annotations
Monitor changes and react to an event ChatGPT Scheduled Tasks support triggers and monitoring as well as fixed schedules
Run a weekly connected briefing Either Both can use connectors, Skills, and remote scheduled execution
Create a custom native Skill on a personal plan Claude Claude custom Skills are available across individual plans when enabled
Govern and share Skills across a large workspace Either Both offer admin controls, organization distribution, and access management
Build and publish an interactive website ChatGPT Sites provides an integrated creation, preview, access, and hosting workflow
Mix local files, browser research, and desktop apps Claude Claude’s connector → browser → screen-control path covers more fallback routes

Claude or ChatGPT: The Final Decision

Use these questions in order:

  1. Does the task need direct control of an ordinary desktop application with no connector? Start with Claude Cowork.
  2. Does the task need a signed-in, multi-tab browser that you can watch and annotate? Start with ChatGPT Work.
  3. Must the final deliverable be a polished DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, or PDF? Start with Claude.
  4. Must the deliverable be a native Google file or a published interactive Site? Start with ChatGPT.
  5. Do you need a native personal Skill on an individual account? Choose Claude under the current access rules.
  6. Must the workflow react to an event or monitor for changes? Choose ChatGPT.
  7. Is it a normal local-folder task or fixed weekly briefing? Either can work; choose the one already connected to your tools.
  8. Still unsure? Run the same low-risk, 30-minute task in both with identical files, instructions, and acceptance criteria.

The bottom line: Claude Cowork is the better AI agent for work that ends in a professional file or crosses the visible desktop. ChatGPT Work is the better AI agent for work that lives in browsers, plugins, cloud execution, monitored events, or a hosted Site. If your business does both, using both is not redundant: let Claude handle document and desktop depth, and let ChatGPT handle cloud and browser breadth.

Comparing all three AI agents?

Gemini Spark changes the decision when your workflow lives in a personal Google Account. Start with the best AI agents for business — the full three-way comparison with a side-by-side table, eligibility rules, and a decision tree covering all three at once.

Prefer the other head-to-head pairings? Read Claude Desktop vs Gemini Spark for Claude’s desktop-and-document strengths versus Spark’s Google integration, or see ChatGPT vs Gemini Spark for the choice between ChatGPT’s broader business workflows and Spark’s Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Tasks, Keep, and Mac-folder workflows.

Official Sources and How We Compared Them

This article uses current product documentation, not subjective writing samples or unsourced benchmark roundups. We compared the agents as work systems: where tasks run, what information they can reach, which actions they can take, how recurring work operates, what deliverables they produce, who can use reusable workflows, and which permission boundaries apply.

  • Anthropic: Use Claude Cowork on web, desktop, and mobile
  • Anthropic: Let Claude use your computer in Cowork
  • Anthropic: Schedule recurring tasks in Claude Cowork
  • Anthropic: Use Skills in Claude
  • Anthropic: Create and edit files with Claude
  • OpenAI: ChatGPT Work and Codex
  • OpenAI: Get started with ChatGPT Work
  • OpenAI: Using the built-in browser in the ChatGPT desktop app
  • OpenAI: Skills in ChatGPT
  • OpenAI: Plugins

Last fact-checked: July 26, 2026. Both products are changing quickly. Recheck plan access, rollout notes, preview features, and file-format limitations before making a purchase decision based on one must-have capability.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Claude better than ChatGPT?

Claude is better for direct desktop app control, native personal Skills across individual plans, and creating portable Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF files. ChatGPT is better for its integrated browser, explicit cloud and local modes, event-triggered scheduled tasks, universal plugin directory, and publishable Sites. The better choice depends on the workflow rather than one universal ranking.

What is the difference between Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Work?

Both are agentic work modes that complete multi-step tasks using approved files and tools. Claude Cowork is strongest in desktop control, document creation, and broadly available custom Skills. ChatGPT Work is strongest in cloud and local flexibility, browser workflows, trigger-based schedules, plugins shared with Codex, and Sites.

Can Claude and ChatGPT both access local files?

Yes. Claude Cowork can read and write within folders connected through Claude Desktop. ChatGPT Work can use local folders or projects opened in the ChatGPT desktop app. Web and mobile sessions do not independently receive unrestricted access to your computer; local access depends on the relevant desktop host and permissions.

Which is better for working with desktop apps?

Claude is the better current choice for general desktop app control because computer use can click, type, and navigate approved apps when no connector exists. It is a research preview for Pro and Max and has important safety limitations. ChatGPT can use approved apps and add-ins, but support depends more heavily on the available tool or plugin.

Which is better for web research and browser tasks?

ChatGPT has the stronger browser system. Its desktop app includes a built-in browser with sign-in, tabs, downloads, annotations, and its own browser state. It also offers a cloud browser for supported public websites. Claude can browse and act through Claude in Chrome and remains highly capable for browser-assisted Cowork tasks.

Is Claude or ChatGPT better for Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF files?

Claude is the cleaner choice for creating portable Office and PDF deliverables because it directly supports DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, and PDF creation with built-in document Skills. ChatGPT Work also creates and edits common business files and supports native Google files, but direct desktop Office integration varies by application and surface.

Do Claude and ChatGPT both support Skills?

Yes. Both support reusable workflow packages with instructions and supporting resources. Claude custom Skills are available across Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise when code execution is enabled. ChatGPT Personal Skills are currently generally available for Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu, although portable skill instructions can still be used manually on other plans.

Can Claude and ChatGPT run scheduled tasks?

Yes. Both can run recurring work remotely using approved connected sources. Claude supports standard recurring schedules and on-demand runs. ChatGPT also supports one-time tasks, recurring schedules, event triggers, and monitoring for changes, which gives it the advantage for event-driven workflows.

Is Claude or ChatGPT safer for business files?

Either can be configured for safer business use, and neither removes the need for review. ChatGPT offers explicit local sandbox and approval controls. Claude scopes files and tools through permissions and isolates remote execution, but Claude computer use has no sandbox between the agent and an approved app. Use a commercial plan with the appropriate data terms, grant minimum access, and keep human review for consequential actions.

Can I use Claude and ChatGPT together?

Yes. A practical division is Claude for deep file synthesis, portable business documents, and mixed desktop workflows, with ChatGPT for browser research, connected cloud workflows, event-driven schedules, and Sites. Reusing the same workflow instructions and review checklist across both helps keep quality consistent.

A plugin can contain reusable Skills, connectors, MCP servers, browser capabilities, hooks, and scheduled-task templates. A business can install a Gmail or Google Drive plugin for everyday Work tasks and use compatible parts of that same plugin in Codex rather than maintaining unrelated tool catalogs.
The practical difference is not the number of logos in a directory. It is whether the system you need offers the exact read and write actions required for your workflow. A Slack connector that can search messages but cannot post a reviewed update is not equivalent to one that supports both. Check the requested permissions and action list before choosing either platform.
**Apps and plugin verdict: slight ChatGPT win**
Both ecosystems are powerful and use open integration patterns. ChatGPT receives a slight edge because one public directory serves ChatGPT Work and Codex and can package a particularly broad set of capability types. Claude remains highly competitive and may be better when a local desktop extension is the most direct route to the tool.
## Scheduled Tasks and Background Work
Recurring work is where both products start to feel like agents instead of chatbots. Each can produce regular briefings, refresh reports, monitor a topic, and use approved connected sources without rebuilding the prompt every time.
### Claude Cowork schedules
[Claude scheduled tasks](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13854387-schedule-recurring-tasks-in-claude-cowork) are available in Cowork on paid plans. Remote schedules can run when your computer is asleep and can use connectors, account files, Skills, and installed plugins. Claude supports hourly, daily, weekly, weekday, manual, and on-demand patterns. A remote scheduled task cannot reach an arbitrary folder on your computer; a schedule that requires local files or apps must run locally with the necessary computer available.
### ChatGPT Work schedules
ChatGPT Work can run once, repeat on a schedule, respond to a supported trigger, or monitor for changes. Cloud scheduled work does not depend on your computer being awake. The trigger and monitoring options give ChatGPT a meaningful advantage for workflows that should react to an external event rather than run only at a fixed time.
Scheduled tasks should not be treated as a license to remove review. Both agents may encounter stale data, missing permissions, prompt injection, or a source that changed structure. Start with a draft-only output, review several runs, and allow sending, publishing, deletion, or financial actions only when the workflow has an appropriate approval step.
**Schedule verdict: ChatGPT wins for event-driven work**
For a standard daily or weekly report, both are strong. Choose ChatGPT when the job must react to an event or monitor for changes. Choose Claude when the recurring result depends heavily on a Claude Skill, Cowork plugin, or Claude-connected document workflow.
## Skills and Reusable Workflows
Skills are reusable workflow packages. Instead of rewriting your process every week, you save the instructions, examples, rules, and supporting resources so the agent can apply the same method when a matching task appears. This is more valuable than a collection of clever prompts because a Skill can define how the work is checked and what the output must contain.
### Claude Skills
[Claude Skills](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-use-skills-in-claude) are currently available on Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise when code execution and file creation are enabled. Claude includes built-in Skills for Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and PDF work; individuals can upload custom Skills; and organizations can provision or share approved Skills. Claude can invoke a relevant Skill automatically.
This is a major advantage for a solo operator or small business owner. You can use a formal native Skill without first moving into an enterprise workspace. Follow the step-by-step guide to [create a Claude Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-claude-skill/), or start from the [free Claude Skills library](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/claude/).
### ChatGPT Skills
[ChatGPT Skills](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001066) are reusable, shareable workflows that can include instructions, examples, and code. ChatGPT can create them with chat, edit them, upload them, share them with selected colleagues, or publish them to a workspace. However, Personal Skills are currently generally available for Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu. They must be added separately on desktop and web/mobile and do not automatically sync between those surfaces.
If your account does not have native Personal Skills, the underlying method still works: paste a well-structured workflow into ChatGPT, save it in a Project or Custom GPT where appropriate, and reuse it manually. Our [ChatGPT Skills availability guide](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/chatgpt-skills-availability/) explains the current plan rules, while the [free ChatGPT Skills library](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/chatgpt/) gives you portable instructions you can use immediately.
**Skills verdict: Claude wins for individuals; ChatGPT is strong for managed teams**
Claude makes native custom Skills available to a much broader range of individual accounts. ChatGPT has excellent workspace sharing, access, and compliance controls where Personal Skills are eligible. Both follow an open Agent Skills approach, so the best workflow logic can often be adapted rather than rebuilt.
## Documents, Spreadsheets, Presentations, and Sites
The best AI agent does not merely summarize your sources. It returns the format the next person can actually use.
### Claude for portable business files
Claude can directly create [Excel spreadsheets, PowerPoint presentations, Word documents, and PDFs](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12111783-create-and-edit-files-with-claude). Its built-in document Skills support working formulas, charts, visualizations, and structured reports. File creation is documented across Claude web, desktop, and mobile, including Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise.
Claude is therefore the cleaner first choice when the deliverable must be a downloadable DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, or PDF that opens outside the AI platform. It can also use supported Microsoft 365 add-ins and coordinate information across Excel and PowerPoint in eligible workflows.
### ChatGPT for connected files and Sites
[ChatGPT Work creates and edits documents, spreadsheets, presentations, reports, and analyses](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001278). It can create native Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides when the appropriate Google Workspace app is enabled. The desktop app previews supported files beside the chat and supports targeted annotations. Direct inspection and editing of an open Excel workbook uses Codex with the ChatGPT for Excel add-in, and OpenAI says PowerPoint is not included in that specific Work desktop flow at launch.
ChatGPT’s distinctive output is a [ChatGPT Site](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001339): a web experience the agent can create, preview, revise, save, and publish. If the finished result is an interactive internal tool, landing page, directory, tracker, or client portal rather than a static document, ChatGPT has the clearer advantage.
**Output verdict: Claude for Office files; ChatGPT for Sites and Google-native work**
Choose Claude when portability into Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or PDF is the requirement. Choose ChatGPT when the output should live natively in Google Workspace or become a hosted Site. For either agent, verify formulas, citations, branding, accessibility, permissions, and sharing settings before delivery.
## Desktop, Web, Mobile, and Cross-Device Continuity
The old shorthand that Claude Cowork is desktop-only and ChatGPT is cloud-only is no longer accurate. Both agents now combine remote work with desktop access.
[Claude Cowork runs on desktop, web, and mobile](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15520349-use-claude-cowork-on-web-desktop-and-mobile), with remote sessions in beta. You can start, steer, and review tasks across devices. Remote sessions continue after the laptop closes. Local files, local connectors, Chrome, and computer use still depend on Claude Desktop being open on the computer that grants access.
[ChatGPT Work also runs on desktop, web, and mobile](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001275-chatgpt-work-and-codex). Cloud Work chats sync across those surfaces. A cloud task can continue when the computer is off; a local task stays tied to the desktop and its approved folders or apps. ChatGPT Work’s explicit local/cloud selector makes this boundary easier for a beginner to understand before starting.
**Device verdict: tie, with a usability edge to ChatGPT**
Both agents now support genuine cross-device work. ChatGPT makes the execution choice more visible. Claude offers a similarly capable remote/local bridge, but its web and mobile Cowork experience is still described as beta and rolling out.
## Privacy, Permissions, and Safety
An agent that can read email, edit a file, operate a browser, or run on a schedule creates more risk than a chatbot that only drafts text. The safest product is not the one with the longest security page. It is the one you configure with the smallest practical access boundary and supervise in proportion to the consequences.
### Claude’s safety model
Claude Cowork remote sessions run in isolated temporary environments on Anthropic’s servers. Local access is limited to folders and tools you connect, and deletion requires explicit permission. Computer use is different: it takes screenshots, interacts directly with approved apps, and has no sandbox between Claude and those applications. Anthropic recommends blocking sensitive apps and staying close to consequential tasks.
### ChatGPT’s safety model
ChatGPT’s local agent commands operate inside a sandbox with separate approval policies. You can choose a read-only or workspace-write boundary, maintain website allowlists and blocklists, and require approval before broader access. Plugins and external services retain their own authentication and permissions, and browser content should still be treated as untrusted.
### Business data and personal data are not the same
For both vendors, consumer and commercial data terms differ. OpenAI states that [ChatGPT Business and Enterprise data is not used for model training by default](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/5722486-how-your-data-is-used-to-improve-model-performance). Anthropic handles Team and Enterprise under its commercial terms and states in the [Cowork architecture overview](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14479288-claude-cowork-architecture-overview) that commercial Cowork data is not used to train Claude. Consumer-account settings and policies can be different. Review the current terms for the exact plan you will use rather than assuming a brand-wide rule.
**Use this minimum-safe setup in either agent**
Create a dedicated working folder. Use copies of important files. Connect only the service needed for the current task. Keep approvals on. Ask for a draft before sending or publishing. Review links, formulas, recipients, permissions, and final files yourself. Do not begin with banking, healthcare, legal, credential, payment, or production-deletion workflows.
## Which AI Agent Is Better for Your Use Case?
The right answer becomes much clearer when the decision is attached to a real job.
| Your main job | Better starting point | Why | | --- | --- | --- | | Analyze and reorganize a local folder | Either | Both work inside approved local folders on desktop | | Operate a niche desktop app with no connector | **Claude** | Claude computer use is a documented general screen-interaction fallback | | Create a client-ready Word report | **Claude** | Native DOCX creation and a professional Word Skill | | Build a complex Excel workbook | Claude for a new file; ChatGPT/Codex for an open workbook | ChatGPT can work directly inside supported Excel and Google Sheets workbooks, and it now supports reusable Skills within those spreadsheet experiences. Claude remains stronger for generating portable XLSX files from scratch, while ChatGPT is especially useful when the workbook already exists and the workflow should run beside it. | | Create native Google Docs, Sheets, or Slides | **ChatGPT** | Work can create and edit native Google files through enabled apps | | Research across signed-in websites | **ChatGPT** | The built-in browser supports sign-in, tabs, downloads, and annotations | | Monitor changes and react to an event | **ChatGPT** | Scheduled Tasks support triggers and monitoring as well as fixed schedules | | Run a weekly connected briefing | Either | Both can use connectors, Skills, and remote scheduled execution | | Create a custom native Skill on a personal plan | **Claude** | Claude custom Skills are available across individual plans when enabled | | Govern and share Skills across a large workspace | Either | Both offer admin controls, organization distribution, and access management | | Build and publish an interactive website | **ChatGPT** | Sites provides an integrated creation, preview, access, and hosting workflow | | Mix local files, browser research, and desktop apps | **Claude** | Claude’s connector → browser → screen-control path covers more fallback routes |
## Claude or ChatGPT: The Final Decision
Use these questions in order:
1. **Does the task need direct control of an ordinary desktop application with no connector?** Start with Claude Cowork. 2. **Does the task need a signed-in, multi-tab browser that you can watch and annotate?** Start with ChatGPT Work. 3. **Must the final deliverable be a polished DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, or PDF?** Start with Claude. 4. **Must the deliverable be a native Google file or a published interactive Site?** Start with ChatGPT. 5. **Do you need a native personal Skill on an individual account?** Choose Claude under the current access rules. 6. **Must the workflow react to an event or monitor for changes?** Choose ChatGPT. 7. **Is it a normal local-folder task or fixed weekly briefing?** Either can work; choose the one already connected to your tools. 8. **Still unsure?** Run the same low-risk, 30-minute task in both with identical files, instructions, and acceptance criteria.
**The bottom line:** Claude Cowork is the better AI agent for work that ends in a professional file or crosses the visible desktop. ChatGPT Work is the better AI agent for work that lives in browsers, plugins, cloud execution, monitored events, or a hosted Site. If your business does both, using both is not redundant: let Claude handle document and desktop depth, and let ChatGPT handle cloud and browser breadth.
**Comparing all three AI agents?**
Gemini Spark changes the decision when your workflow lives in a personal Google Account. Start with [the best AI agents for business](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/chatgpt-vs-claude-vs-gemini-spark/) — the full three-way comparison with a side-by-side table, eligibility rules, and a decision tree covering all three at once.
Prefer the other head-to-head pairings? Read [Claude Desktop vs Gemini Spark](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/claude-desktop-vs-gemini-spark/) for Claude’s desktop-and-document strengths versus Spark’s Google integration, or see [ChatGPT vs Gemini Spark](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/chatgpt-vs-gemini-spark/) for the choice between ChatGPT’s broader business workflows and Spark’s Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Tasks, Keep, and Mac-folder workflows.
## Official Sources and How We Compared Them
This article uses current product documentation, not subjective writing samples or unsourced benchmark roundups. We compared the agents as work systems: where tasks run, what information they can reach, which actions they can take, how recurring work operates, what deliverables they produce, who can use reusable workflows, and which permission boundaries apply.
* [Anthropic: Use Claude Cowork on web, desktop, and mobile](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15520349-use-claude-cowork-on-web-desktop-and-mobile) * [Anthropic: Let Claude use your computer in Cowork](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14128542-let-claude-use-your-computer-in-cowork) * [Anthropic: Schedule recurring tasks in Claude Cowork](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13854387-schedule-recurring-tasks-in-claude-cowork) * [Anthropic: Use Skills in Claude](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-use-skills-in-claude) * [Anthropic: Create and edit files with Claude](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12111783-create-and-edit-files-with-claude) * [OpenAI: ChatGPT Work and Codex](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001275-chatgpt-work-and-codex) * [OpenAI: Get started with ChatGPT Work](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/get-started-with-work) * [OpenAI: Using the built-in browser in the ChatGPT desktop app](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001277-using-the-built-in-browser-in-the-chatgpt-desktop-app) * [OpenAI: Skills in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001066) * [OpenAI: Plugins](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/plugins)
**Last fact-checked:** July 26, 2026. Both products are changing quickly. Recheck plan access, rollout notes, preview features, and file-format limitations before making a purchase decision based on one must-have capability.
## Frequently Asked Questions
Is Claude better than ChatGPT?
Claude is better for direct desktop app control, native personal Skills across individual plans, and creating portable Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF files. ChatGPT is better for its integrated browser, explicit cloud and local modes, event-triggered scheduled tasks, universal plugin directory, and publishable Sites. The better choice depends on the workflow rather than one universal ranking.
What is the difference between Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Work?
Both are agentic work modes that complete multi-step tasks using approved files and tools. Claude Cowork is strongest in desktop control, document creation, and broadly available custom Skills. ChatGPT Work is strongest in cloud and local flexibility, browser workflows, trigger-based schedules, plugins shared with Codex, and Sites.
Can Claude and ChatGPT both access local files?
Yes. Claude Cowork can read and write within folders connected through Claude Desktop. ChatGPT Work can use local folders or projects opened in the ChatGPT desktop app. Web and mobile sessions do not independently receive unrestricted access to your computer; local access depends on the relevant desktop host and permissions.
Which is better for working with desktop apps?
Claude is the better current choice for general desktop app control because computer use can click, type, and navigate approved apps when no connector exists. It is a research preview for Pro and Max and has important safety limitations. ChatGPT can use approved apps and add-ins, but support depends more heavily on the available tool or plugin.
Which is better for web research and browser tasks?
ChatGPT has the stronger browser system. Its desktop app includes a built-in browser with sign-in, tabs, downloads, annotations, and its own browser state. It also offers a cloud browser for supported public websites. Claude can browse and act through Claude in Chrome and remains highly capable for browser-assisted Cowork tasks.
Is Claude or ChatGPT better for Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF files?
Claude is the cleaner choice for creating portable Office and PDF deliverables because it directly supports DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, and PDF creation with built-in document Skills. ChatGPT Work also creates and edits common business files and supports native Google files, but direct desktop Office integration varies by application and surface.
Do Claude and ChatGPT both support Skills?
Yes. Both support reusable workflow packages with instructions and supporting resources. Claude custom Skills are available across Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise when code execution is enabled. ChatGPT Personal Skills are currently generally available for Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu, although portable skill instructions can still be used manually on other plans.
Can Claude and ChatGPT run scheduled tasks?
Yes. Both can run recurring work remotely using approved connected sources. Claude supports standard recurring schedules and on-demand runs. ChatGPT also supports one-time tasks, recurring schedules, event triggers, and monitoring for changes, which gives it the advantage for event-driven workflows.
Is Claude or ChatGPT safer for business files?
Either can be configured for safer business use, and neither removes the need for review. ChatGPT offers explicit local sandbox and approval controls. Claude scopes files and tools through permissions and isolates remote execution, but Claude computer use has no sandbox between the agent and an approved app. Use a commercial plan with the appropriate data terms, grant minimum access, and keep human review for consequential actions.
Can I use Claude and ChatGPT together?
Yes. A practical division is Claude for deep file synthesis, portable business documents, and mixed desktop workflows, with ChatGPT for browser research, connected cloud workflows, event-driven schedules, and Sites. Reusing the same workflow instructions and review checklist across both helps keep quality consistent.
