mainEntity.name: What is the best AI agent for business in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: ChatGPT Work is the best all-purpose choice for most businesses because it has no structural disqualifier — it runs on Mac and Windows, supports personal and organization accounts, works locally or in the cloud, and covers the widest range of task types. Claude Cowork is stronger for desktop app control and polished Office documents. Gemini Spark is stronger for eligible personal Google users, but it does not support work or school accounts.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, and Gemini Spark?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are the agent layers on top of three chat products. ChatGPT Work runs inside the ChatGPT app with an explicit local-versus-cloud toggle and an integrated browser. Claude Cowork runs inside Claude Desktop with connector access and, on Pro and Max, direct computer use. Gemini Spark is Google’s personal agent mode inside Gemini Apps, built around Gmail, Calendar, Drive, and Keep. All three plan multi-step work and return finished results rather than single replies.

mainEntity.name: Can Gemini Spark be used with a business or work Google account?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Gemini Spark requires a personal Google Account — work and school accounts are not eligible. This rules Spark out for most managed-Workspace businesses regardless of fit. ChatGPT Work or Claude Team and Enterprise are the direct paths for organization-managed deployment.

mainEntity.name: Is Gemini Spark available outside the United States?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it got much easier to reach in July 2026. Google AI Pro previously qualified for Spark only in the US, with Ultra required elsewhere; on July 30, 2026, Google expanded Pro access to over 160 additional countries, so Pro and Ultra now have essentially the same footprint. Spark remains unavailable in the EEA, Nigeria, Switzerland, and the UK.

mainEntity.name: Which AI agent is best for creating Word, Excel, or PowerPoint files?

acceptedAnswer.text: Claude Cowork. It offers native creation and editing of DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, and PDF files, dedicated document Skills, and supported Microsoft 365 add-ins on eligible plans. ChatGPT Work handles a broad range of formats too, but Claude’s Office-file creation is the more purpose-built path.

mainEntity.name: Which AI agent is best for Gmail and Google Workspace?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gemini Spark, for eligible personal Google users — Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Tasks, and Keep are its native environment. Both ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork offer Google Workspace connectors, which is the practical route for anyone on a work or school account where Spark is not available.

mainEntity.name: Do all three support reusable skills?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but plan access differs sharply. Claude has the broadest — Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise when code execution is enabled. ChatGPT’s Personal Skills are generally available on Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu; OpenAI does not list Free, Plus, or Pro, though some accounts report seeing the feature anyway. Gemini Spark supports creating, uploading, and combining skills for eligible personal accounts. All three understand the SKILL.md pattern, so a portable text skill works everywhere.

mainEntity.name: Which AI agent can publish a website or page?

acceptedAnswer.text: ChatGPT Work, through ChatGPT Sites — it can create, preview, share, and publish a page directly. Neither Claude Cowork nor Gemini Spark has an equivalent publishing feature, although Claude can create website files you publish through your own host.

mainEntity.name: Is Claude computer use available on every plan?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Computer use — letting Claude click, type, and navigate approved desktop apps directly — is a research preview limited to Pro and Max plans. Team and Enterprise do not have it yet. If computer use is the reason you are choosing Claude, confirm it is included before buying seats.

mainEntity.name: Which AI agent is cheapest?

acceptedAnswer.text: Prices for all three changed repeatedly during 2026, so the more durable answer is structural: Spark requires a consumer Google AI subscription on a personal account with no business tier, while ChatGPT and Claude both offer organization plans that scale by seat. Check the official pricing pages before subscribing, and note that the capability you actually need — computer use on Claude, Personal Skills on ChatGPT — may sit on a specific tier rather than the cheapest one.

mainEntity.name: Can I use more than one of these AI agents together?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it is often the practical answer. A common split is Gemini Spark for Google-native monitoring and scheduling, Claude Cowork for document-heavy deliverables and desktop app control, and ChatGPT Work for everything else including publishing. Portable plain-text skills keep the method consistent across all three so you are not maintaining three different versions of the same workflow.

mainEntity.name: Should I choose based on which model is best right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The models underneath all three change every few weeks, and a decision made on this month’s benchmark leaderboard rarely survives the next release. Choose on architecture and access instead — which operating systems it runs on, which accounts are eligible, what it can reach, and what it is allowed to change. Those are stable, documented, and they decide whether the tool fits your business.

item.text: ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini Spark ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, and Gemini Spark are the three AI agents actually worth comparing for business right now. Not the chatbots — the agent layers built on top of them, which take a goal, plan several steps, use approved tools and files, and hand back finished work instead of a reply you still have to act on. They are not interchangeable. Each was built around a different center of gravity, and one of them rules itself out entirely for most companies before you compare a single feature. This guide compares all three as business systems: what each can reach, where tasks actually run, who is allowed to use them, and which one wins for specific kinds of work. Why these three, and not a list of twenty These are the three general-purpose AI agents built into the assistants most businesses already pay for — the ones that work alongside you across whatever you happen to be doing. Vertical tools like Zapier Agents, Salesforce Agentforce, or Intercom Fin solve a different problem: automating one specific function, usually with its own setup, seat licences, and implementation project. Those are worth evaluating separately. This page is for deciding which general-purpose agent to put to work first. Which AI agent is best — ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, or Gemini Spark? Choose ChatGPT Work for the widest all-purpose coverage: local or cloud execution, an integrated signed-in browser, event-triggered scheduling, publishable Sites, and a plugin directory shared with Codex. Choose Claude Cowork when the job is desktop app control or polished Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF deliverables, or when you want reusable Skills on the widest range of plans. Choose Gemini Spark only if you have an eligible personal Google Account and your work already lives in Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Keep. The fastest disqualifier: Spark does not support work or school Google Accounts. If your business runs on Google Workspace with managed accounts, Spark is out regardless of how well it would otherwise fit — and that single rule decides this comparison for a large share of readers. What Actually Matters When Choosing an AI Agent Most three-way comparisons of these products are really model comparisons — this quarter’s Claude model against this quarter’s GPT against this quarter’s Gemini, scored on benchmarks. That is interesting, and it is close to useless for choosing a tool you will still be using in six months. The models underneath all three change constantly. Anthropic shipped a new flagship in July 2026 alone, and the pricing and plan rules around these products have moved several times this year. If you pick your agent because one model was ahead on a coding benchmark in July, you will be re-litigating that decision in September. What does not change month to month is the shape of the product: whether it can open a folder on your computer, whether it works on Windows, whether your work Google account is even allowed to use it, whether it can publish a page, whether it can be scheduled to run while you sleep. Those are structural, they are documented, and they decide whether a tool fits your business. The practical rule Choose on access and architecture, not benchmark position. Pick the agent that can reach the systems your work already lives in, then let the model underneath improve on its own — because it will, for all three, without you doing anything. The Distinction Most Comparisons Miss ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are not the same thing as ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, and Gemini Spark. The base products are chat assistants: you ask, they answer. The agent layers are different — they accept a goal, plan multiple steps, use approved tools and files across a session, and return a finished, reviewable result. So the honest comparison is ChatGPT Work vs Claude Cowork vs Gemini Spark — the three agentic work modes. Everywhere this article says an agent can edit a file, control an app, or run on a schedule, it is describing Work, Cowork, or Spark specifically, not the chat product you may already be paying for. The simplest mental model ChatGPT and Claude are apps with an agent mode inside them — Work and Cowork. Gemini Spark is the agent itself, running inside Gemini Apps on web, mobile, and the Gemini Mac app. That is why “Gemini vs Spark” is not really a comparison, while these three genuinely are: different products doing the same job. ChatGPT Work vs Claude Cowork vs Gemini Spark: Side by Side This table reflects officially documented capabilities as of the fact-check date at the bottom of this page. Beta features, plan access, and supported regions change quickly for all three — verify any must-have feature before you subscribe or migrate a workflow. Feature ChatGPT Work Claude Cowork Gemini Spark Best choice What it is Agent mode inside the ChatGPT desktop, web, and mobile apps Agent mode inside Claude Desktop, also on web and mobile Personal AI agent mode inside Gemini Apps Different product layers Desktop operating systems macOS and Windows, local or cloud execution macOS and Windows for the full Cowork desktop experience Mac app for local work; Which Is the Best AI Agent for Business? If you want one answer rather than three: ChatGPT Work is the best AI agent for most businesses today. It is the only one of the three with no structural disqualifier — it runs on Mac and Windows, supports personal and organization accounts, works locally or in the cloud, and covers the widest range of task types without needing a second tool to finish the job. That is a statement about fit, not about intelligence. Claude Cowork produces better business documents and controls desktop applications more directly. Gemini Spark understands a Google-centric workday better than either. But “best AI agent for business” is a question about which tool the largest number of businesses can actually deploy and get value from, and on that measure ChatGPT Work wins on breadth. The honest caveat: the best agent for your business is usually the one that reaches the systems your work already lives in. If your company runs on Microsoft 365 and produces client documents, Claude will feel better immediately. If you are a solo operator on a personal Google Account living in Gmail and Calendar, Spark will save you more time on day one than either competitor. Use the business-type table below rather than defaulting to the broadest option. Local Files and Desktop Control All three can work with files you explicitly connect. What differs is what happens around those files once they are in play. ChatGPT Work: the clearest local model ChatGPT Work offers an explicit choice inside its desktop app — keep work local when a task needs files or apps on your computer, or send it to the cloud when it does not. That toggle removes ambiguity the other two leave implicit, and it means one product covers both modes on Mac and Windows without a separate setup. Claude Cowork: the deepest desktop reach Cowork combines local folder access with connectors, browser work, plugins, and — on eligible Pro and Max plans — computer use, which lets Claude click, type, and navigate approved desktop apps when no connector exists. That makes Claude the strongest fit when a workflow genuinely crosses unrelated desktop tools. Anthropic notes computer use is slower and less reliable than a direct connector, and it remains a research preview. Gemini Spark: the tightest boundaries Spark on Mac is unusually explicit about limits: it can only see files and folders you add to its Connected folders toolbar, and it creates temporary backups while working. Its standout move is bridging desktop files into Google Workspace — turning local invoices into a budgeted Sheet that updates on a schedule, for example. If the destination is already a Google product, Spark has the shortest path. Local-file verdict: ChatGPT for the clearest local and cloud model plus Windows coverage. Claude for workflows crossing many unrelated desktop apps. Spark for Mac work that finishes inside Google Workspace. Connected Apps, Plugins, and Business Tools The most useful agent is rarely the one with the longest feature list. It is the one with reliable access to the systems your business actually runs on. ChatGPT shares a universal plugin directory between Work and Codex, so one integration effort covers both surfaces — a real advantage if your team also uses Codex for engineering work. Claude supports remote connectors for cloud services, desktop extensions for local tools, and plugins that bundle Skills and connectors together. Its Microsoft 365 story is the strongest of the three: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook add-ins on supported plans, with documented cross-app workflows such as analyzing a workbook in Excel and using the results in a PowerPoint deck. Gemini Spark draws on Connected Apps, Personal Intelligence, your chats, signed-in websites, location, skills, and schedules. For a personal Google user that produces a more coherent picture of the day than a set of separately installed integrations — but it is a personal-account capability, not a business deployment today. Apps and plugins verdict: ChatGPT for one ecosystem spanning Work and Codex. Claude for the widest mix of desktop, cloud, and Microsoft tools. Spark for a personal Google-centric stack. Browsers and Web Research All three can research the web and produce cited results, but the browsing architecture differs meaningfully. ChatGPT Work has the most complete system: an integrated signed-in desktop browser with its own tabs, state, downloads, and annotations, plus a separate cloud browser for public sites that do not need a signed-in session. Claude Cowork uses Claude in Chrome and can navigate sites through Cowork. Gemini Spark uses a remote browser and can act on sites you are signed into, asking for confirmation before consequential actions. Browser verdict: ChatGPT wins on completeness — an integrated browser plus a dedicated cloud option covers more cases than either rival offers alone. Schedules and Background Tasks All three support recurring work, and all three separate cloud-capable tasks from tasks that need your physical computer. ChatGPT Work can run a task once, repeat it on a schedule, respond to a supported trigger, or monitor for a change — the widest variety of trigger types among the three. Claude Cowork schedules daily briefings, weekly reports, recurring research, and file processing using connectors, Skills, plugins, and account files; cloud schedules run even while the computer is asleep, though a task needing a local file still needs the desktop connection. Gemini Spark supports time-based and event-based instructions — a morning briefing built from email, calendar, and Drive, or a workflow that reacts when a manager’s email contains an action item. Scheduling verdict: ChatGPT for the widest range of trigger types. Spark for Google-native events specifically. Claude for schedules needing a broader mix of tools or polished deliverables. Skills and Customization All three support reusable skills — saved instructions, context, and supporting files that teach the agent a repeatable task and get invoked when a request matches. This is where the differences in plan access get sharp. Claude has the broadest access: built-in, custom, and organization-provisioned Skills across Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans when code execution is enabled. ChatGPT‘s Personal Skills are generally available on Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu plans — OpenAI does not list Free, Plus, or Pro, though some accounts on other plans report seeing the feature, so check your own Plugins → Skills area rather than assuming. Gemini Spark lets you create a skill with Gemini, start from a template, write one manually, or upload a SKILL.md or ZIP file. All three understand the open SKILL.md pattern to some degree, so a well-written plain-text skill moves between them with small platform-specific adjustments. That portability is why every skill in this site’s library is written as plain text first — it works on any plan, in any of the three, with no feature access required. Customization verdict: Claude for the broadest native Skills access by plan. A portable text skill is the most reliable way to get consistent behavior across all three. Gemini Spark is strongest when the output belongs inside the Google ecosystem: a Sheet, a Doc, a Calendar action, or an organized Drive workflow. Output verdict: Claude for DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, PDF, and complex multi-format deliverables. ChatGPT for broad format support plus the option to publish. Spark when the result should live and stay active inside Google Workspace. Who Can Actually Use Each One Eligibility decides this comparison more often than features do — and it is the section most competitor comparisons get wrong or leave stale. ChatGPT Work and Claude Team or Enterprise are the direct paths for organization-managed deployment. What is more stable — and more useful — is the shape of the cost. ChatGPT Work is tied to a ChatGPT plan, with business and enterprise tiers designed for organization deployment. Cost scales with seats and plan tier. Claude Cowork requires an eligible paid Claude plan. The capability that most often decides the purchase — computer use — is restricted to Pro and Max, so check that before buying a Team seat expecting it. Gemini Spark requires a consumer Google AI subscription (Pro or Ultra) on a personal account. There is no business-tier route, which means it is a personal expense, not a company deployment — a structural cost difference more important than the monthly figure. Check the official pricing pages before subscribing: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. The cheapest way to test all three Run the same real task in each one using the same plain-text skill, the same source files, and the same acceptance criteria. A portable skill removes the biggest variable — how well you happened to prompt each tool — so you are comparing the products rather than your own prompt-writing on a given afternoon. If Gemini Spark Is Not Available to You Two large groups are excluded from Spark before they compare a single feature: anyone whose Google account is a work or school account, and anyone in the EEA, Nigeria, Switzerland, or the UK. If that is you, the practical question is not which of three agents to pick — it is which of two. Choose ChatGPT Work if you want the closest thing to Spark’s breadth: cloud scheduling, monitoring triggers, a signed-in browser, and Gmail, Calendar, and Drive connectors that cover much of what Spark does natively, from an account type your business can actually manage. Choose Claude Cowork if the Spark workflow you wanted was mostly about local files and finished documents rather than Google integration. Either way, the Google-shaped part of the workflow does not have to be lost — both alternatives offer Workspace connectors. What you give up is the native depth, not the access. The cost of a mistake rises with the access you grant. Claude Cowork limits local access to connected folders and checks tool calls against granted permissions. Computer use asks before accessing new applications, supports a blocklist, and can be stopped at any point, though Anthropic notes there is no sandbox between Claude and an approved app. ChatGPT Work builds its permission model around the explicit local-versus-cloud choice, so you decide up front whether a task can touch your machine at all. Gemini Spark on Mac limits access to Connected folders, asks permission before permanent deletion or sharing with third parties, and warns that a connected shared drive can expose information to anyone else with access to it. Use the same beginner rule with any of the three Connect one dedicated test folder, use copies rather than originals, keep approvals on, and supervise the first few runs. Do not start with your entire Documents folder, a shared company drive, financial accounts, health information, or any workflow that sends, deletes, purchases, or publishes without review. The Final Decision Work through these in order and stop at the first one that applies: Is this for a work or school Google account, or do you need managed organization deployment? Spark is not eligible — choose ChatGPT Work or Claude Cowork. Are you in the EEA, UK, Switzerland, or Nigeria? Spark is unavailable — choose ChatGPT Work or Claude Cowork. Does your work live in Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Keep, on an eligible personal account? Choose Gemini Spark. Is the finished result a Word document, Excel model, PowerPoint deck, or PDF? Choose Claude Cowork. Do you need to publish the result as a page or micro-site? Choose ChatGPT Work. Does the workflow need direct control over unrelated desktop apps? Choose Claude Cowork, and confirm your plan includes computer use. Is it an event-triggered or monitoring workflow outside Google? Gemini Spark is the stronger specialist for eligible personal Google users. Choose based on where your work already lives and which accounts you actually control — not on which model is ahead this month. Only Deciding Between Two? This page compares all three at once. Claude Cowork is stronger for desktop app control and polished Office documents. Gemini Spark is stronger for eligible personal Google users, but it does not support work or school accounts. What is the difference between ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, and Gemini Spark? They are the agent layers on top of three chat products. Claude Cowork runs inside Claude Desktop with connector access and, on Pro and Max, direct computer use. Gemini Spark is Google’s personal agent mode inside Gemini Apps, built around Gmail, Calendar, Drive, and Keep. All three plan multi-step work and return finished results rather than single replies. Can Gemini Spark be used with a business or work Google account? No. Gemini Spark requires a personal Google Account — work and school accounts are not eligible. Google AI Pro previously qualified for Spark only in the US, with Ultra required elsewhere; on July 30, 2026, Google expanded Pro access to over 160 additional countries, so Pro and Ultra now have essentially the same footprint. Spark remains unavailable in the EEA, Nigeria, Switzerland, and the UK. Which AI agent is best for creating Word, Excel, or PowerPoint files? Claude Cowork. It offers native creation and editing of DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, and PDF files, dedicated document Skills, and supported Microsoft 365 add-ins on eligible plans. ChatGPT Work handles a broad range of formats too, but Claude’s Office-file creation is the more purpose-built path. Which AI agent is best for Gmail and Google Workspace? Gemini Spark, for eligible personal Google users — Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Tasks, and Keep are its native environment. Both ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork offer Google Workspace connectors, which is the practical route for anyone on a work or school account where Spark is not available. Do all three support reusable skills? Yes, but plan access differs sharply. Claude has the broadest — Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise when code execution is enabled. Gemini Spark supports creating, uploading, and combining skills for eligible personal accounts. All three understand the SKILL.md pattern, so a portable text skill works everywhere. Which AI agent can publish a website or page? ChatGPT Work, through ChatGPT Sites — it can create, preview, share, and publish a page directly. Neither Claude Cowork nor Gemini Spark has an equivalent publishing feature, although Claude can create website files you publish through your own host. Is Claude computer use available on every plan? No. Computer use — letting Claude click, type, and navigate approved desktop apps directly — is a research preview limited to Pro and Max plans. Team and Enterprise do not have it yet. If computer use is the reason you are choosing Claude, confirm it is included before buying seats. Which AI agent is cheapest? Prices for all three changed repeatedly during 2026, so the more durable answer is structural: Spark requires a consumer Google AI subscription on a personal account with no business tier, while ChatGPT and Claude both offer organization plans that scale by seat. Check the official pricing pages before subscribing, and note that the capability you actually need — computer use on Claude, Personal Skills on ChatGPT — may sit on a specific tier rather than the cheapest one. Can I use more than one of these AI agents together? Yes, and it is often the practical answer. A common split is Gemini Spark for Google-native monitoring and scheduling, Claude Cowork for document-heavy deliverables and desktop app control, and ChatGPT Work for everything else including publishing. Portable plain-text skills keep the method consistent across all three so you are not maintaining three different versions of the same workflow. Should I choose based on which model is best right now? No. The models underneath all three change every few weeks, and a decision made on this month’s benchmark leaderboard rarely survives the next release. Choose on architecture and access instead — which operating systems it runs on, which accounts are eligible, what it can reach, and what it is allowed to change. Those are stable, documented, and they decide whether the tool fits your business.

ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini Spark

ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, and Gemini Spark are the three AI agents actually worth comparing for business right now. Not the chatbots — the agent layers built on top of them, which take a goal, plan several steps, use approved tools and files, and hand back finished work instead of a reply you still have to act on.

They are not interchangeable. Each was built around a different center of gravity, and one of them rules itself out entirely for most companies before you compare a single feature. This guide compares all three as business systems: what each can reach, where tasks actually run, who is allowed to use them, and which one wins for specific kinds of work.

Why these three, and not a list of twenty

These are the three general-purpose AI agents built into the assistants most businesses already pay for — the ones that work alongside you across whatever you happen to be doing. Vertical tools like Zapier Agents, Salesforce Agentforce, or Intercom Fin solve a different problem: automating one specific function, usually with its own setup, seat licences, and implementation project. Those are worth evaluating separately. This page is for deciding which general-purpose agent to put to work first.

Quick answer

Which AI agent is best — ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, or Gemini Spark?

Choose ChatGPT Work for the widest all-purpose coverage: local or cloud execution, an integrated signed-in browser, event-triggered scheduling, publishable Sites, and a plugin directory shared with Codex. Choose Claude Cowork when the job is desktop app control or polished Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF deliverables, or when you want reusable Skills on the widest range of plans. Choose Gemini Spark only if you have an eligible personal Google Account and your work already lives in Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Keep.

The fastest disqualifier: Spark does not support work or school Google Accounts. If your business runs on Google Workspace with managed accounts, Spark is out regardless of how well it would otherwise fit — and that single rule decides this comparison for a large share of readers.

What Actually Matters When Choosing an AI Agent

Most three-way comparisons of these products are really model comparisons — this quarter’s Claude model against this quarter’s GPT against this quarter’s Gemini, scored on benchmarks. That is interesting, and it is close to useless for choosing a tool you will still be using in six months.

The models underneath all three change constantly. Anthropic shipped a new flagship in July 2026 alone, and the pricing and plan rules around these products have moved several times this year. If you pick your agent because one model was ahead on a coding benchmark in July, you will be re-litigating that decision in September.

What does not change month to month is the shape of the product: whether it can open a folder on your computer, whether it works on Windows, whether your work Google account is even allowed to use it, whether it can publish a page, whether it can be scheduled to run while you sleep. Those are structural, they are documented, and they decide whether a tool fits your business.

The practical rule

Choose on access and architecture, not benchmark position. Pick the agent that can reach the systems your work already lives in, then let the model underneath improve on its own — because it will, for all three, without you doing anything.

The Distinction Most Comparisons Miss

ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are not the same thing as ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, and Gemini Spark. The base products are chat assistants: you ask, they answer. The agent layers are different — they accept a goal, plan multiple steps, use approved tools and files across a session, and return a finished, reviewable result.

So the honest comparison is ChatGPT Work vs Claude Cowork vs Gemini Spark — the three agentic work modes. Everywhere this article says an agent can edit a file, control an app, or run on a schedule, it is describing Work, Cowork, or Spark specifically, not the chat product you may already be paying for.

The simplest mental model

ChatGPT and Claude are apps with an agent mode inside them — Work and Cowork. Gemini Spark is the agent itself, running inside Gemini Apps on web, mobile, and the Gemini Mac app. That is why “Gemini vs Spark” is not really a comparison, while these three genuinely are: different products doing the same job.

Local-file verdict: ChatGPT for the clearest local and cloud model plus Windows coverage. Claude for workflows crossing many unrelated desktop apps. Spark for Mac work that finishes inside Google Workspace.

Connected Apps, Plugins, and Business Tools

The most useful agent is rarely the one with the longest feature list. It is the one with reliable access to the systems your business actually runs on.

ChatGPT shares a universal plugin directory between Work and Codex, so one integration effort covers both surfaces — a real advantage if your team also uses Codex for engineering work.

Claude supports remote connectors for cloud services, desktop extensions for local tools, and plugins that bundle Skills and connectors together. Its Microsoft 365 story is the strongest of the three: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook add-ins on supported plans, with documented cross-app workflows such as analyzing a workbook in Excel and using the results in a PowerPoint deck.

Gemini Spark draws on Connected Apps, Personal Intelligence, your chats, signed-in websites, location, skills, and schedules. For a personal Google user that produces a more coherent picture of the day than a set of separately installed integrations — but it is a personal-account capability, not a business deployment today.

Apps and plugins verdict: ChatGPT for one ecosystem spanning Work and Codex. Claude for the widest mix of desktop, cloud, and Microsoft tools. Spark for a personal Google-centric stack.

Browsers and Web Research

All three can research the web and produce cited results, but the browsing architecture differs meaningfully.

ChatGPT Work has the most complete system: an integrated signed-in desktop browser with its own tabs, state, downloads, and annotations, plus a separate cloud browser for public sites that do not need a signed-in session. Claude Cowork uses Claude in Chrome and can navigate sites through Cowork. Gemini Spark uses a remote browser and can act on sites you are signed into, asking for confirmation before consequential actions.

Browser verdict: ChatGPT wins on completeness — an integrated browser plus a dedicated cloud option covers more cases than either rival offers alone.

Schedules and Background Tasks

All three support recurring work, and all three separate cloud-capable tasks from tasks that need your physical computer.

ChatGPT Work can run a task once, repeat it on a schedule, respond to a supported trigger, or monitor for a change — the widest variety of trigger types among the three. Claude Cowork schedules daily briefings, weekly reports, recurring research, and file processing using connectors, Skills, plugins, and account files; cloud schedules run even while the computer is asleep, though a task needing a local file still needs the desktop connection. Gemini Spark supports time-based and event-based instructions — a morning briefing built from email, calendar, and Drive, or a workflow that reacts when a manager’s email contains an action item.

Scheduling verdict: ChatGPT for the widest range of trigger types. Spark for Google-native events specifically. Claude for schedules needing a broader mix of tools or polished deliverables.

Skills and Customization

All three support reusable skills — saved instructions, context, and supporting files that teach the agent a repeatable task and get invoked when a request matches. This is where the differences in plan access get sharp.

Claude has the broadest access: built-in, custom, and organization-provisioned Skills across Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans when code execution is enabled. ChatGPT‘s Personal Skills are generally available on Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu plans — OpenAI does not list Free, Plus, or Pro, though some accounts on other plans report seeing the feature, so check your own Plugins → Skills area rather than assuming. Gemini Spark lets you create a skill with Gemini, start from a template, write one manually, or upload a SKILL.md or ZIP file.

All three understand the open SKILL.md pattern to some degree, so a well-written plain-text skill moves between them with small platform-specific adjustments. That portability is why every skill in this site’s library is written as plain text first — it works on any plan, in any of the three, with no feature access required.

Customization verdict: Claude for the broadest native Skills access by plan. A portable text skill is the most reliable way to get consistent behavior across all three.

Documents, Spreadsheets, and Finished Outputs

Claude has the clearest advantage when the deliverable is a polished business file: direct creation and editing of Excel spreadsheets, PowerPoint decks, Word documents, PDFs, and charts, with Cowork able to combine multiple source files into one finished output. ChatGPT Work supports a broad range of formats and adds something neither rival has — publishing the result directly as a ChatGPT Site. Gemini Spark is strongest when the output belongs inside the Google ecosystem: a Sheet, a Doc, a Calendar action, or an organized Drive workflow.

Output verdict: Claude for DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, PDF, and complex multi-format deliverables. ChatGPT for broad format support plus the option to publish. Spark when the result should live and stay active inside Google Workspace.

Who Can Actually Use Each One

Eligibility decides this comparison more often than features do — and it is the section most competitor comparisons get wrong or leave stale.

Requirement ChatGPT Work Claude Cowork Gemini Spark
Desktop platform macOS and Windows, local or cloud macOS and Windows for the full Cowork experience Gemini app on Mac for local files; web and mobile elsewhere
Account type Personal and eligible organization plans Personal plus eligible Team and Enterprise organizations Personal Google Account only — work and school accounts not eligible
Plan required Availability varies by plan; check current plan pages An eligible paid Claude plan; computer use is Pro and Max only A qualifying Google AI subscription (Pro or Ultra)
Country Available in supported locations; features vary by rollout Available in Claude-supported locations; features vary by plan Excluded in the EEA, Nigeria, Switzerland, and the UK
Age 18 or older 18 or older 18 or older
Required setting Permissions depend on the connector, plugin, or app in use Permissions depend on the folder, connector, or plugin in use Keep Activity must be turned on

Recent change worth knowing: Spark got much easier to reach

Until mid-2026, Google AI Pro only qualified for Spark in the United States, and everywhere else required the more expensive Ultra plan. On July 30, 2026, Google expanded Pro access to over 160 additional countries. Pro and Ultra now have essentially the same country footprint, so international users no longer need Ultra purely to get Spark. Many comparisons still repeat the old rule — see the Gemini Spark availability guide for the current country and plan picture.

The account rule that ends the comparison for many businesses

Gemini supports work and school accounts in many contexts, but Spark specifically requires a personal Google Account. If your company runs on managed Google Workspace accounts, Spark is unavailable to your team no matter how well it would otherwise fit. ChatGPT Work and Claude Team or Enterprise are the direct paths for organization-managed deployment.

What Each One Costs You in Practice

Subscription prices for all three have changed repeatedly through 2026, so quoting figures here would mislead you within weeks. What is more stable — and more useful — is the shape of the cost.

  • ChatGPT Work is tied to a ChatGPT plan, with business and enterprise tiers designed for organization deployment. Cost scales with seats and plan tier.
  • Claude Cowork requires an eligible paid Claude plan. The capability that most often decides the purchase — computer use — is restricted to Pro and Max, so check that before buying a Team seat expecting it.
  • Gemini Spark requires a consumer Google AI subscription (Pro or Ultra) on a personal account. There is no business-tier route, which means it is a personal expense, not a company deployment — a structural cost difference more important than the monthly figure.

Check the official pricing pages before subscribing: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

The cheapest way to test all three

Run the same real task in each one using the same plain-text skill, the same source files, and the same acceptance criteria. A portable skill removes the biggest variable — how well you happened to prompt each tool — so you are comparing the products rather than your own prompt-writing on a given afternoon.

If Gemini Spark Is Not Available to You

Two large groups are excluded from Spark before they compare a single feature: anyone whose Google account is a work or school account, and anyone in the EEA, Nigeria, Switzerland, or the UK. If that is you, the practical question is not which of three agents to pick — it is which of two.

Choose ChatGPT Work if you want the closest thing to Spark’s breadth: cloud scheduling, monitoring triggers, a signed-in browser, and Gmail, Calendar, and Drive connectors that cover much of what Spark does natively, from an account type your business can actually manage.

Choose Claude Cowork if the Spark workflow you wanted was mostly about local files and finished documents rather than Google integration.

Either way, the Google-shaped part of the workflow does not have to be lost — both alternatives offer Workspace connectors. What you give up is the native depth, not the access. For the direct head-to-head on this, see ChatGPT vs Gemini Spark.

Best AI Agent by Business Type

Feature tables are useful, but the shape of your business narrows it faster.

Your situation Best starting point Why
Solo operator on a personal Google Account Gemini Spark Native Gmail, Calendar, Drive, and Keep context saves the most time on day one
Freelancer producing client documents Claude Cowork Native Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF creation is the deliverable itself
Small team on managed Google Workspace ChatGPT Work Spark is unavailable on work accounts; ChatGPT covers Workspace via connectors
Agency juggling many client tools Claude Cowork Computer use plus the widest connector and plugin mix handles unrelated systems
Microsoft 365 business Claude Cowork Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook add-ins on supported plans
Team that also uses Codex for engineering ChatGPT Work One universal plugin directory serves both surfaces
Content or marketing business that publishes ChatGPT Work ChatGPT Sites can publish a finished page directly
In the EEA, UK, Switzerland, or Nigeria ChatGPT Work or Claude Cowork Spark is unavailable in these locations
Enterprise needing managed rollout and controls ChatGPT Work or Claude Spark has no organization-managed account path today
Not sure yet, want the safest default ChatGPT Work The only one of the three with no structural disqualifier

Privacy, Permissions, and Safety

All three can take actions more consequential than generating text — editing a file, sending information to an app, clicking through a website, running unattended on a schedule. The cost of a mistake rises with the access you grant.

Claude Cowork limits local access to connected folders and checks tool calls against granted permissions. Computer use asks before accessing new applications, supports a blocklist, and can be stopped at any point, though Anthropic notes there is no sandbox between Claude and an approved app. ChatGPT Work builds its permission model around the explicit local-versus-cloud choice, so you decide up front whether a task can touch your machine at all. Gemini Spark on Mac limits access to Connected folders, asks permission before permanent deletion or sharing with third parties, and warns that a connected shared drive can expose information to anyone else with access to it.

Use the same beginner rule with any of the three

Connect one dedicated test folder, use copies rather than originals, keep approvals on, and supervise the first few runs. Do not start with your entire Documents folder, a shared company drive, financial accounts, health information, or any workflow that sends, deletes, purchases, or publishes without review.

The Final Decision

Work through these in order and stop at the first one that applies:

  1. Is this for a work or school Google account, or do you need managed organization deployment? Spark is not eligible — choose ChatGPT Work or Claude Cowork.
  2. Are you in the EEA, UK, Switzerland, or Nigeria? Spark is unavailable — choose ChatGPT Work or Claude Cowork.
  3. Does your work live in Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Keep, on an eligible personal account? Choose Gemini Spark.
  4. Is the finished result a Word document, Excel model, PowerPoint deck, or PDF? Choose Claude Cowork.
  5. Do you need to publish the result as a page or micro-site? Choose ChatGPT Work.
  6. Does the workflow need direct control over unrelated desktop apps? Choose Claude Cowork, and confirm your plan includes computer use.
  7. Is it an event-triggered or monitoring workflow outside Google? Choose ChatGPT Work.
  8. Still unsure? Start with ChatGPT Work as the widest-coverage default, then test the same task with the same skill in whichever alternative your work leans toward.

The bottom line: ChatGPT Work is the strongest all-purpose choice for most businesses. Claude Cowork is the stronger specialist for desktop control and polished documents. Gemini Spark is the stronger specialist for eligible personal Google users. Choose based on where your work already lives and which accounts you actually control — not on which model is ahead this month.

Only Deciding Between Two?

This page compares all three at once. If you have already narrowed it to a specific pair, the dedicated comparison goes deeper on that exact match-up:

How We Compared Them

This comparison was built from current product documentation rather than benchmark charts or unsourced feature lists. We compared the three as business systems and asked the same questions of each: what can it access, where does the task actually run, what is it allowed to change, how is recurring work configured, what files does it produce, who is eligible to use it, and what safety boundaries apply.

We deliberately excluded two things competitors include. Model benchmark scores, because the models underneath all three change every few weeks and a decision made on July’s leaderboard does not survive September. And subscription prices, because all three have repriced during 2026 and a hardcoded figure turns a useful page into a misleading one — we link to the official pricing pages instead.

  • OpenAI: ChatGPT Work and Codex
  • OpenAI: Get started with ChatGPT Work
  • OpenAI: Skills in ChatGPT
  • Anthropic: Use Claude Cowork on web, desktop, and mobile
  • Anthropic: Let Claude use your computer in Cowork
  • Anthropic: Use Skills in Claude
  • Google: Use Gemini Spark to manage tasks and workflows
  • Google: Use Gemini Spark with the Gemini app on Mac

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best AI agent for business in 2026?

ChatGPT Work is the best all-purpose choice for most businesses because it has no structural disqualifier — it runs on Mac and Windows, supports personal and organization accounts, works locally or in the cloud, and covers the widest range of task types. Claude Cowork is stronger for desktop app control and polished Office documents. Gemini Spark is stronger for eligible personal Google users, but it does not support work or school accounts.

What is the difference between ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, and Gemini Spark?

They are the agent layers on top of three chat products. ChatGPT Work runs inside the ChatGPT app with an explicit local-versus-cloud toggle and an integrated browser. Claude Cowork runs inside Claude Desktop with connector access and, on Pro and Max, direct computer use. Gemini Spark is Google’s personal agent mode inside Gemini Apps, built around Gmail, Calendar, Drive, and Keep. All three plan multi-step work and return finished results rather than single replies.

Can Gemini Spark be used with a business or work Google account?

No. Gemini Spark requires a personal Google Account — work and school accounts are not eligible. This rules Spark out for most managed-Workspace businesses regardless of fit. ChatGPT Work or Claude Team and Enterprise are the direct paths for organization-managed deployment.

Is Gemini Spark available outside the United States?

Yes, and it got much easier to reach in July 2026. Google AI Pro previously qualified for Spark only in the US, with Ultra required elsewhere; on July 30, 2026, Google expanded Pro access to over 160 additional countries, so Pro and Ultra now have essentially the same footprint. Spark remains unavailable in the EEA, Nigeria, Switzerland, and the UK.

Which AI agent is best for creating Word, Excel, or PowerPoint files?

Claude Cowork. It offers native creation and editing of DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, and PDF files, dedicated document Skills, and supported Microsoft 365 add-ins on eligible plans. ChatGPT Work handles a broad range of formats too, but Claude’s Office-file creation is the more purpose-built path.

Which AI agent is best for Gmail and Google Workspace?

Gemini Spark, for eligible personal Google users — Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Tasks, and Keep are its native environment. Both ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork offer Google Workspace connectors, which is the practical route for anyone on a work or school account where Spark is not available.

Do all three support reusable skills?

Yes, but plan access differs sharply. Claude has the broadest — Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise when code execution is enabled. ChatGPT’s Personal Skills are generally available on Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu; OpenAI does not list Free, Plus, or Pro, though some accounts report seeing the feature anyway. Gemini Spark supports creating, uploading, and combining skills for eligible personal accounts. All three understand the SKILL.md pattern, so a portable text skill works everywhere.

Which AI agent can publish a website or page?

ChatGPT Work, through ChatGPT Sites — it can create, preview, share, and publish a page directly. Neither Claude Cowork nor Gemini Spark has an equivalent publishing feature, although Claude can create website files you publish through your own host.

Is Claude computer use available on every plan?

No. Computer use — letting Claude click, type, and navigate approved desktop apps directly — is a research preview limited to Pro and Max plans. Team and Enterprise do not have it yet. If computer use is the reason you are choosing Claude, confirm it is included before buying seats.

Which AI agent is cheapest?

Prices for all three changed repeatedly during 2026, so the more durable answer is structural: Spark requires a consumer Google AI subscription on a personal account with no business tier, while ChatGPT and Claude both offer organization plans that scale by seat. Check the official pricing pages before subscribing, and note that the capability you actually need — computer use on Claude, Personal Skills on ChatGPT — may sit on a specific tier rather than the cheapest one.

Can I use more than one of these AI agents together?

Yes, and it is often the practical answer. A common split is Gemini Spark for Google-native monitoring and scheduling, Claude Cowork for document-heavy deliverables and desktop app control, and ChatGPT Work for everything else including publishing. Portable plain-text skills keep the method consistent across all three so you are not maintaining three different versions of the same workflow.

Should I choose based on which model is best right now?

No. The models underneath all three change every few weeks, and a decision made on this month’s benchmark leaderboard rarely survives the next release. Choose on architecture and access instead — which operating systems it runs on, which accounts are eligible, what it can reach, and what it is allowed to change. Those are stable, documented, and they decide whether the tool fits your business.

# ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini Spark
**ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, and Gemini Spark are the three AI agents actually worth comparing for business right now.** Not the chatbots — the agent layers built on top of them, which take a goal, plan several steps, use approved tools and files, and hand back finished work instead of a reply you still have to act on.
They are not interchangeable. Each was built around a different center of gravity, and one of them rules itself out entirely for most companies before you compare a single feature. This guide compares all three as business systems: what each can reach, where tasks actually run, who is allowed to use them, and which one wins for specific kinds of work.
**Why these three, and not a list of twenty**
These are the three general-purpose AI agents built into the assistants most businesses already pay for — the ones that work _alongside_ you across whatever you happen to be doing. Vertical tools like Zapier Agents, Salesforce Agentforce, or Intercom Fin solve a different problem: automating one specific function, usually with its own setup, seat licences, and implementation project. Those are worth evaluating separately. This page is for deciding which general-purpose agent to put to work first.
Quick answer
## Which AI agent is best — ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, or Gemini Spark?
**Choose ChatGPT Work** for the widest all-purpose coverage: local or cloud execution, an integrated signed-in browser, event-triggered scheduling, publishable Sites, and a plugin directory shared with Codex. **Choose Claude Cowork** when the job is desktop app control or polished Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF deliverables, or when you want reusable Skills on the widest range of plans. **Choose Gemini Spark** only if you have an eligible _personal_ Google Account and your work already lives in Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Keep.
**The fastest disqualifier:** Spark does not support work or school Google Accounts. If your business runs on Google Workspace with managed accounts, Spark is out regardless of how well it would otherwise fit — and that single rule decides this comparison for a large share of readers.
## What Actually Matters When Choosing an AI Agent
Most three-way comparisons of these products are really model comparisons — this quarter’s Claude model against this quarter’s GPT against this quarter’s Gemini, scored on benchmarks. That is interesting, and it is close to useless for choosing a tool you will still be using in six months.
The models underneath all three change constantly. Anthropic shipped a new flagship in July 2026 alone, and the pricing and plan rules around these products have moved several times this year. If you pick your agent because one model was ahead on a coding benchmark in July, you will be re-litigating that decision in September.
**What does not change month to month is the shape of the product:** whether it can open a folder on your computer, whether it works on Windows, whether your work Google account is even allowed to use it, whether it can publish a page, whether it can be scheduled to run while you sleep. Those are structural, they are documented, and they decide whether a tool fits your business.
**The practical rule**
Choose on _access and architecture_, not benchmark position. Pick the agent that can reach the systems your work already lives in, then let the model underneath improve on its own — because it will, for all three, without you doing anything.
## The Distinction Most Comparisons Miss
**ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are not the same thing as ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, and Gemini Spark.** The base products are chat assistants: you ask, they answer. The agent layers are different — they accept a goal, plan multiple steps, use approved tools and files across a session, and return a finished, reviewable result.
So the honest comparison is **ChatGPT Work vs Claude Cowork vs Gemini Spark** — the three agentic work modes. Everywhere this article says an agent can edit a file, control an app, or run on a schedule, it is describing Work, Cowork, or Spark specifically, not the chat product you may already be paying for.
**The simplest mental model**
**ChatGPT and Claude are apps with an agent mode inside them** — Work and Cowork. **Gemini Spark is the agent itself**, running inside Gemini Apps on web, mobile, and the Gemini Mac app. That is why “Gemini vs Spark” is not really a comparison, while these three genuinely are: different products doing the same job.
## ChatGPT Work vs Claude Cowork vs Gemini Spark: Side by Side
This table reflects officially documented capabilities as of the fact-check date at the bottom of this page. Beta features, plan access, and supported regions change quickly for all three — verify any must-have feature before you subscribe or migrate a workflow.
