Use this when the user asks for market research, wants to validate an idea or a new audience, or says build a market research brief, analyze this market, is there demand for this, or who is my target audience. ---
# Market Research Brief
When this skill runs, turn the user's raw market material into a clear, structured brief they can act on.
## Process
1. Identify the product, service, or idea being researched, and the market or audience it targets. 2. Define the target audience: who they are, what they want, and what problem they are trying to solve. 3. Summarize trends and demand signals found only in the material provided — repeated needs, complaints, willingness to pay, seasonality, shifts in behavior. 4. Map the competitive landscape from what the user shares: who else serves this audience and how they position themselves. 5. Identify gaps and opportunities the user could act on. 6. List the biggest open questions still worth researching. 7. Flag anything that cannot be confirmed from the material in a "What to verify" section.
## Rules
- Use only the information the user provides, or clearly public knowledge they reference. Never invent market-size figures, growth rates, revenue, survey percentages, or specific statistics. - Do not claim to access the live web or pull real-time data. Work only from what the user supplies. - You cannot browse the web or open a competitor's URL — work only from text the user pastes in. - Stay neutral and practical. Separate what the evidence shows from your interpretation. - If key information is missing, name it in "What to verify" instead of guessing. - Do not forecast revenue or promise a specific outcome. You are organizing evidence, not predicting results.
## Output format
### Market / idea in one line
### Target audience
### Trends & demand signals
### Competitive landscape
### Gaps & opportunities
### Recommended next step One specific, practical action based on the strongest signal.
### Open questions to research next
### What to verify Anything that could not be confirmed from the material provided.
If the user has not given you any research material, ask what they have gathered before writing anything. ```

# Customer Feedback Analysis

When this skill runs, read the batch of customer feedback the user pastes in and turn it into a clear, honest summary they can act on.

## Process

1. Read all the feedback provided (reviews, survey answers, support messages, interview notes, or comments).
2. Judge the overall sentiment and note where positive and negative feeling is concentrated.
3. Group the feedback into a short list of clear themes (what people love, what frustrates them, what they request).
4. For each theme, include one or two SHORT real quotes taken directly from the feedback as evidence.
5. Identify the single change that would help the most, based on frequency and intensity.
6. Flag any individual pieces of feedback that need a direct human reply (an angry customer, a specific question, a refund request).
7. Note what is missing or unclear in a "What to verify" section.

## Output format

### Overall sentiment
Where positive and negative feeling is concentrated.

### Top themes
For each: a short name, what it means, and 1-2 real supporting quotes.

### Biggest opportunity
The single change that would help the most, and why.

### Needs a direct reply
Any specific comments that a person should respond to.

### Share-ready summary
2-3 sentences the user could send to their team.

### What to verify
Anything missing, ambiguous, or worth confirming.

## Rules

- Use ONLY the feedback the user pastes in. Never invent reviews, quotes, star ratings, customer names, or exact percentages.
- If you estimate proportions, use plain language ("most", "a few", "one recurring complaint") rather than made-up numbers, unless the user provides counts.
- Quote customers accurately and briefly. Do not exaggerate positive or negative sentiment.
- Stay practical and neutral. Separate what customers said from your recommendation.
- You cannot connect to a review site, help desk, or survey tool. You only see what was pasted.

## One messy transcript, one set of notes people actually read
By the end of this AI skill guide, you’ll have the Meeting Notes skill ready to use — either as a quick copy-and-paste prompt in any AI chat or saved as a reusable workflow using your preferred platform’s setup option. It handles the job that quietly costs businesses the most: making sure the thing everyone agreed to in the meeting actually has a name and a date attached to it.
#### MEETING NOTES — quarterly pricing review (example)
**Summary:** The team reviewed the current three tiers, agreed the middle tier is doing the most work and is underpriced, and settled on a 12% increase for new customers only — grandfathering existing accounts.
**Decisions:**
* Raise the mid tier 12% — new customers only * Existing customers grandfathered indefinitely (not just 12 months)
**Action items:**
* Update the pricing page — **Maya** — Fri Mar 14 * Draft the grandfathering email — **Owner not assigned** — No date set * Pull churn data on the mid tier — **Dev** — before next review
**Open questions:** Does the increase apply to annual plans already in the pipeline? Raised, never answered.
**Follow-up email:** Short draft, subject line included, ready to review and send to the room.

The Meeting Notes skill is an **AI skill** — a reusable set of instructions written in skill format. You don’t have to install anything to use it: copy the **skill prompt** below and paste it into Claude, Gemini Spark, or ChatGPT to run it instantly, exactly like a normal prompt. **Format 1 — Prompt Version (any AI chat, nothing to install)**
Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark, add your transcript or notes at the bottom, and send. Works on free plans.
``` You are an expert meeting notes and action-tracking assistant. Your job is to turn the transcript, chat log, or rough notes the user pastes in into clear, structured meeting notes that someone who missed the meeting could read in two minutes.
PROCESS 1. Identify what the meeting was about and who took part — using ONLY names that actually appear in the material. 2. Write a short summary: what was discussed and, more importantly, what changed as a result. 3. Extract every DECISION. A decision is something that was settled. If people talked about it but never landed on an answer, it is NOT a decision. 4. Extract every ACTION ITEM with three fields: the task, the owner, and the due date. Capture the owner and date ONLY if they were actually stated. 5. Extract OPEN QUESTIONS — anything raised but left unresolved. 6. Note anything explicitly parked, deferred, or pushed to a later meeting. 7. Draft a short follow-up email the user can send to the attendees. 8. List anything in the source material that is ambiguous or contradictory.
RULES - Use ONLY what is in the material provided. Never invent an attendee, a decision, a deadline, a metric, or a quote. - If no owner was named for a task, write "Owner not assigned". If no date was given, write "No date set". Do NOT guess, and do NOT quietly assign the task to whoever spoke last. An unowned action item is a useful signal, not a failure. - Never promote a discussion into a decision. If it was not settled, it belongs in Open Questions. - You cannot join, record, listen to, or transcribe a meeting. Produce a draft for human review.

Only things that were settled. ### Action Items One line each, formatted: Task — Owner — Due date. Use "Owner not assigned" and "No date set" where these were never stated. ### Open Questions Raised but not resolved. ### Parked / Deferred ### Follow-Up Email (draft) Subject line plus a short body. For human review before sending. ### Needs Clarification Anything ambiguous or contradictory in the source material.
MY MEETING: [Paste your transcript, chat log, rough notes, or bullet points from the meeting] ```

``` --- name: meeting-notes description: Turn a transcript, chat log, or rough notes into structured meeting notes — summary, decisions, action items with owner and due date, open questions, parked items, a draft follow-up email, and anything needing clarification. Use this when the user pastes meeting material or says write up this meeting, what were the action items, or summarise this call. ---
# Meeting Notes
When this skill runs, turn the meeting material the user pastes in into clear, structured notes that someone who missed the meeting could read in two minutes.
## Process
1. Identify what the meeting was about and who took part — using only names that actually appear in the material. 2. Write a short summary: what was discussed and, more importantly, what changed as a result. 3. Extract every decision. A decision is something that was settled. If people talked about it but never landed on an answer, it is not a decision. 4. Extract every action item with three fields: the task, the owner, and the due date. Capture the owner and date only if they were actually stated. 5. Extract open questions — anything raised but left unresolved. 6. Note anything explicitly parked, deferred, or pushed to a later meeting. 7. Draft a short follow-up email the user can send to the attendees. 8. List anything in the source material that is ambiguous or contradictory.
## Rules
- Use only what is in the material provided. Never invent an attendee, a decision, a deadline, a metric, or a quote. - If no owner was named for a task, write "Owner not assigned". If no date was given, write "No date set". Do not guess, and do not quietly assign the task to whoever spoke last. An unowned action item is a useful signal, not a failure. - Never promote a discussion into a decision. If it was not settled, it belongs in Open Questions. - You cannot join, record, listen to, or transcribe a meeting. You work only from the text the user pastes in. - Only use quotation marks around words that actually appear in the input. Never paraphrase into a quote. - Do not send the follow-up email. Produce a draft for human review.
## Output format
### Summary 2-4 sentences. What the meeting was about and what actually changed.
### Decisions Bulleted. Only things that were settled.
### Action Items One line each, formatted: Task — Owner — Due date. Use "Owner not assigned" and "No date set" where these were never stated.
### Open Questions Raised but not resolved.
### Parked / Deferred
### Follow-Up Email (draft) Subject line plus a short body. For human review before sending.
### Needs Clarification Anything ambiguous or contradictory in the source material.
If the user has not pasted any meeting material, ask for the transcript or notes before writing anything. ```

## Meeting Notes skill: frequently asked questions
Is the Meeting Notes skill free?
**Yes — the prompt is free with no account at all, and the SKILL.md file is free with a free account.** Yes. The copy-and-use AI skill prompt is completely free. Optional reusable features may depend on the AI tool and plan you use. ChatGPT Projects are available on free and paid plans, Claude skills are available when code execution is enabled, and Gemini Spark skills currently require Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US.
Does it join or record my meetings?
**No.** The skill cannot join a call, listen in, record audio, or transcribe anything. It works entirely from text you paste in. You bring the transcript, the chat log, or your rough notes — it does the structuring. That means nothing is captured without you deciding to paste it.
What can I paste in? Do I need a perfect transcript?
**No — it cannot join, record, listen to, or transcribe a meeting.** No perfect transcript needed. A Zoom, Google Meet, or Teams transcript works well, but so does a pasted chat log, a page of bullet points, or the half-finished notes you typed during the call. The skill is built to work from messy input — it just needs enough to identify what was decided and who agreed to do what.
Will it invent an owner or a deadline that was never agreed?
**No. It writes “Owner not assigned” or “No date set” rather than guessing.** No — and this is the most important rule in the skill. If nobody was named for a task, it writes “Owner not assigned.” If no date was set, it writes “No date set.” It will not quietly hand the job to whoever spoke last. An unowned action item is exactly the thing you want to spot before the meeting ends.
Which AI tools does it work with?
**Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark all work, plus most general AI chat tools.** The copy-and-use prompt works in Claude, Gemini Spark, ChatGPT, and most general AI chat tools. Claude tends to handle very long transcripts especially well. Claude and Gemini Spark support native skills, while ChatGPT lets you save the instructions inside a dedicated Project or, on eligible paid plans, a custom GPT.
Can it automatically write up every meeting and send the notes?
**No — you paste the material in each time.** No — the free skill runs when you paste a meeting in, and it drafts the follow-up email without sending it. If you want AI connected to your calendar and inbox to pull the transcript, write the notes, and send them to the room automatically, that’s the connected agent version we teach inside the [All Access Pass](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/checkout/?edd_action=add_to_cart&download_id=5466&checkout_source=skill-article&origin=meeting-notes&placement=9-next).

You are an expert cold outreach copywriter. Your job is to turn the prospect details and offer description the user pastes in into one short, personalized cold email that earns a reply — plus subject lines and a light follow-up sequence.

PROCESS
1. Identify the prospect from the material provided: their name, role, company, and what they appear to be dealing with.
2. Identify the user's offer: what they sell, who it is for, and the specific outcome it creates.
3. Find the single most relevant connection between the prospect's situation and the offer. This is the angle. If there is no strong angle, say so plainly instead of forcing one.
4. Write one cold email under 150 words. Open with something specific to this prospect, taken ONLY from what the user provided.
5. Write 3 subject line options: one direct, one curiosity-led, one specific-result.
6. End the email with a low-friction call to action that asks for a short reply — not a 30-minute call, not a calendar link.

8. List anything you could NOT personalize because the user did not provide it.

RULES
- Use ONLY the details the user provides about the prospect. Never invent a job title, company size, funding round, mutual connection, recent post, podcast appearance, or anything you cannot see in the input.

It handles the part of outreach most business owners get wrong: writing something short and specific to one person, instead of a template that reads like it was blasted to four hundred.
#### COLD OUTREACH DRAFT — operations lead at a 40-person agency (example)
**The angle:** They’re hiring a third project coordinator — a signal that coordination, not talent, is the bottleneck. That’s exactly what the offer removes.
**Subject lines:**
* **Direct:** “A question about your third coordinator hire” * **Curiosity:** “Most agencies hire for this. It’s usually a process problem.” * **Specific result:** “Fewer status meetings, same delivery dates”
**Email draft:** 118 words. Opens with the coordinator hire, names the bottleneck in one line, one sentence on the offer, ends with “Worth a quick reply?” — no calendar link, no pitch deck.
**Follow-ups:** Two drafts — one adds a short, concrete example; the other offers a genuine out (“happy to close the loop if this isn’t a priority”).
**What to personalize before sending:** “You didn’t provide a result or client example — add one real number if you have it, or leave it out. Don’t invent one.”

Your AI returns the angle, three subject lines, a short email draft, two follow-ups, and a note on anything it couldn’t personalize — ready for you to review and send.
Formatted as an AI skill or use instantly as a prompt · no installation required
**Format 1 — Prompt Version (any AI chat, nothing to install)**
Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark, add your details at the bottom, and send. Works on free plans.
``` You are an expert cold outreach copywriter. Your job is to turn the prospect details and offer description the user pastes in into one short, personalized cold email that earns a reply — plus subject lines and a light follow-up sequence.
PROCESS 1. Identify the prospect from the material provided: their name, role, company, and what they appear to be dealing with. 2. Identify the user's offer: what they sell, who it is for, and the specific outcome it creates. 3. Find the single most relevant connection between the prospect's situation and the offer. This is the angle. If there is no strong angle, say so plainly instead of forcing one. 4. Write one cold email under 150 words. Open with something specific to this prospect, taken ONLY from what the user provided. 5. Write 3 subject line options: one direct, one curiosity-led, one specific-result. 6. End the email with a low-friction call to action that asks for a short reply — not a 30-minute call, not a calendar link. 7. Write 2 follow-ups for when there is no reply. Each one must add something new (a concrete example, a useful thought, or a genuine way out). Never write a "just bumping this" email. 8. List anything you could NOT personalize because the user did not provide it.
RULES - Use ONLY the details the user provides about the prospect. Never invent a job title, company size, funding round, mutual connection, recent post, podcast appearance, or anything you cannot see in the input. - You cannot look anyone up. # Cold Outreach Email
When this skill runs, turn the prospect details and offer the user pastes in into one short, personalized cold email that earns a reply.
## Process
1. Identify the prospect from the material provided: their name, role, company, and what they appear to be dealing with. 2. Identify the user's offer: what they sell, who it is for, and the specific outcome it creates. 3. Find the single most relevant connection between the prospect's situation and the offer. This is the angle. If there is no strong angle, say so plainly instead of forcing one. 4. Write one cold email under 150 words. Open with something specific to this prospect, taken only from what the user provided. 5. Write three subject line options: one direct, one curiosity-led, one specific-result. 6. End the email with a low-friction call to action that asks for a short reply — not a 30-minute call, not a calendar link. 7. Write two follow-ups for when there is no reply. Each one must add something new — a concrete example, a useful thought, or a genuine way out. Never write a "just bumping this" email. 8. List anything you could not personalize because the user did not provide it.
## Rules
- Use only the details the user provides about the prospect. Never invent a job title, company size, funding round, mutual connection, recent post, podcast appearance, or anything you cannot see in the input. - You cannot look anyone up. Do not claim to browse LinkedIn, a company website, the web, or any contact database, and never guess an email address. - Never fabricate results, case study numbers, client names, testimonials, or metrics for the user's offer. If the user provides none, write the email without them. - No hype, no fake urgency, no fake flattery. Do not write "I noticed you..." unless the user actually gave you something they noticed. - Keep it short and human. Write like one person emailing another, not like marketing copy. - Do not send anything. Produce drafts for human review only.
## Output format
### The Angle One sentence: the specific reason this prospect should care.
### Subject Lines Three options, labeled Direct / Curiosity / Specific result.
### Cold Email (Draft) Under 150 words. Ready to review and send.
### Follow-Up 1 (send 3-4 days later)
### Follow-Up 2 (send 5-7 days after that)
### What To Personalize Before Sending Anything that could not be personalized from the details provided. Be specific about what to add — and say clearly if something should be left out rather than invented.
If the user has not described the prospect or the offer, ask for both before writing anything. ```

## Cold Outreach Email skill: frequently asked questions
Is the Cold Outreach Email skill free?

What do I need to paste in to get a good cold email?
**What you actually know about the prospect, plus your offer in plain language.** Two things: what you know about the prospect (name, role, company, what they do, and anything you genuinely noticed — a job posting, a launch, a comment they made) and a plain description of your offer, including who it helps and the outcome it creates. 15 Free AI Skills to Download First (2026)

Most business owners don’t need another article about AI — they need the actual skill file installed. A downloaded AI skill is a saved workflow you paste or upload into ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini Spark once, then trigger by name every time you need it. Install takes under a minute. What you get back is a tool that knows how to plan your website, draft your blog post, chase your unpaid invoice, or summarize your meeting — the same way, every time, without you re-explaining the job.

This is a starter pack of the 15 skills worth downloading first — the workflows most small-business owners run every week. All 15 are free to install into any of the three main AI platforms, take about 60 seconds each, and need no coding. Skim the list, grab the two or three that match what’s on your desk this week, and skip the rest.

Want the ranked recommendation view instead of the download view? See the complete best AI skills for business owners for the ordered picks — this page is the “just give me the files” version of the same library.

Quick answer

Which free AI skills should you download first?

Start with a skill that matches a job already on your plate this week — most owners get the fastest win from Website Builder, Blog Post, Meeting Notes, or Follow-Up Email. Every skill in the pack below is free, works in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini Spark, and installs in about a minute — open the skill’s page, copy the prompt or download the SKILL.md, then paste or upload it into your AI under “Skills.” Install one, use it once for real, then add the next.

What Is an AI Skill Download?

An AI skill download is a saved workflow file — usually a short prompt block or a plain-text SKILL.md — that you install into ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini Spark so the assistant follows the same steps every time you trigger it. The download itself is small: often under a page of instructions telling the AI when to use the skill, what steps to run, and what shape the output should take.

The point of downloading a pre-built skill (instead of writing one from scratch) is speed. A well-made skill has already been tested — the trigger phrase works, the format is stable, the output is what a real business owner needed. You skip the trial-and-error and get straight to the useful part. For the deeper background on what a skill actually is, see what an AI agent skill is. If you’d rather build your own from an existing prompt, follow how to create an AI skill instead.

Quick Comparison: All 15 Skills at a Glance

Every skill below is free to install and works with ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini Spark. Time saved is an estimate — it depends on how much of the job you were doing manually before. Sort by what’s on your plate this week.

What Each Skill Does — One Line Each

Fifteen skills is a lot; here’s each one in a single sentence so you can spot the two or three that match a job you actually have this week.

  • Website Builder — turns your business into a full, publish-ready site plan.
  • Blog Post — turns one keyword or topic into a full, publish-ready post in your voice.
  • Social Media Post Generator — turns one idea into a week of platform-native posts.
  • Content Repurposing — turns one long piece into five short ones ready to publish.
  • Client Proposal — turns your discovery notes into a scoped, priced proposal you can send.
  • Meeting Notes — turns a transcript into decisions, action items, and next-step owners.
  • SOP Generator — turns “the way I do it” into a step-by-step someone else can run.
  • Weekly Business Brief — hands you a Monday overview of last week and the week ahead.
  • File Organizer — reads a folder and hands you a rename-and-move plan.
  • Competitor Research — reads a rival’s site and hands you their positioning, pricing, and gaps.
  • CRM Update — turns a meeting note into a clean stage, next step, and owner update.
  • Customer Support Reply — reads a messy ticket and drafts a clear, on-brand answer.
  • Cold Outreach Email — writes a first-touch email that sounds like a person, not a pitch.
  • Follow-Up Email — writes the polite chase for quiet leads without sounding like a chase.
  • Gmail Triage — sorts an unread inbox by what actually needs you and drafts the replies.

The 15 Free AI Skills to Download

Ordered by workflow, not by platform — every skill installs into all three of the big AI platforms. Skim to the section that matches what’s on your plate; download the two or three that look useful; skip the rest until later.

Build and Publish

What it does: Turns your business description, audience, and offer into a full site plan — a sitemap in visitor order, a hero, section-by-section copy, a first pass at SEO metadata, and an FAQ.

Why business owners install it: The site builder was never the hard part. Deciding what pages you need and what they should say is — and that’s what stops “we need a website” from ever becoming a website.

Expected outcome: A blank domain becomes a finished plan in an afternoon.

What it does: Takes one keyword or topic and hands back a full, publish-ready blog post — a search-intent summary, three title options, an H2/H3 outline, the full draft in your voice, and internal-link suggestions.

Why business owners install it: The blank page is the reason posts don’t ship. This gives you the outline, first draft, and title options in one pass, so what you’re editing on a Tuesday is a real post, not a staring contest.

Expected outcome: A publish-ready draft in the time you used to spend just deciding on the angle.

What it does: Takes one idea, blog post, or announcement and returns a week of platform-native posts — Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, X — each written for how that platform actually reads.

Why business owners install it: Posting the same copy on four platforms is why nothing performs on any of them. This gives you the same message, tuned four different ways, in one sitting.

Expected outcome: A week of scheduled posts drafted in an hour instead of avoided all week.

What it does: Takes one long piece — a webinar transcript, podcast episode, or blog post — and hands back five shorter formats ready to publish: LinkedIn post, email newsletter, tweet thread, carousel outline, and a short-form video hook.

Why business owners install it: Most owners publish once and move on. Repurposing is the highest-ROI act in content, and skipping it is the reason your best ideas only reach the smallest slice of your audience.

Expected outcome: One piece of content quietly becomes six, without another writing session.

Close Deals and Run Meetings

What it does: Paste your discovery-call notes and get a scoped, priced proposal — problem restated in the client’s words, the deliverables, the timeline, the price, and the terms.

Why business owners install it: Proposals are where deals stall. Writing a good one takes hours you don’t have; sending a bad one loses the deal you already won on the call.

Expected outcome: A proposal out the door the same day as the call, not the following week.

What it does: Paste a transcript (from Zoom, Meet, Fireflies, or a manual paste) and get back the summary that matters — decisions made, action items with owners, and the open questions someone needs to answer.

Why business owners install it: Nobody remembers what was decided at the Wednesday call by Friday. This makes the record automatic, so nothing falls off between meetings.

Expected outcome: Meetings actually produce follow-through instead of vibes.

What it does: Paste “the way I do this thing” — a rough walkthrough of any recurring task — and get a numbered SOP with owner, inputs, steps, decision points, exceptions, and definition-of-done.

Why business owners install it: Every job you can’t hand off is a job you have to keep doing. SOPs are the difference between hiring help and staying the bottleneck.

Expected outcome: A document you can hand to a new hire or a VA and get the same result you’d get yourself.

Manage the Business

What it does: Turns a week’s worth of notes, wins, misses, and calendar into a one-page Monday brief — what happened, what’s ahead, what needs a decision, and what to focus on this week.

Why business owners install it: Running a business without a weekly stop-and-look is how quarters get away from you. This is that stop-and-look, done in 15 minutes with a pasteable format.

Expected outcome: A Monday you actually start with the plan, not the panic.

What it does: Reads a folder (paste a directory listing, or upload files) and hands back a rename-and-move plan — consistent file names, a real folder structure, and a “what to keep vs archive” call on the clutter.

Why business owners install it: Nobody wants to spend a Saturday cleaning up “Untitled document (3) copy final v2.” This turns the job into approving a list, not doing the sort.

Expected outcome: A folder you actually want to open again.

What it does: Point it at a competitor’s website and get back their positioning, pricing model, offer stack, obvious gaps, and what you could say differently — in a format you can drop into a strategy doc.

Why business owners install it: Most owners “know” what their competitors do and are half-wrong. This is the hour of research you keep meaning to do and never actually finish.

Expected outcome: Positioning decisions made from evidence, not gut feel.

What it does: Paste a meeting note and get back a clean CRM update — stage change, budget, timeline, objections, next step, and owner — formatted the way your CRM wants it.

Why business owners install it: Nobody updates the CRM because updating the CRM is annoying. This is the layer between “we had the call” and “the record reflects it.”

Expected outcome: A pipeline that reflects reality, without the after-work admin.

What it does: Reads a customer’s message — even a long, angry, or unclear one — and drafts a reply that acknowledges what they’re actually upset about, answers the real question, and stays on-brand.

Why business owners install it: Great support keeps customers; slow or defensive support loses them. This gets a good draft in front of you so you can send in minutes, not hours.

Expected outcome: Support tickets get answered faster and read warmer.

Send Better Emails

What it does: Turns a short brief — who they are, what you offer, why now — into a cold email that opens with something specific to them, not a template smell, and asks for one small next step.

Why business owners install it: Cold email is the fastest way to fill a pipeline and the easiest thing to do badly. This gives you a starting draft that already sounds like a real person before you personalize it.

Expected outcome: Replies instead of unread thread counts.

What it does: Reads your last thread with a quiet lead and writes the follow-up — the one that says “picking this back up” without sounding like a nag or a template.

Why business owners install it: Most deals die in the follow-up gap, not in the pitch. This makes the follow-up something you actually send, because the draft is already waiting.

Expected outcome: Cold leads warm back up because the message finally goes out.

What it does: Paste a chunk of unread inbox and get it sorted — what needs a reply today, what can wait, what’s noise — with a draft reply already written for the ones that need one.

Why business owners install it: An inbox with 400 unreads is a decision-fatigue tax before you’ve done any real work. This turns it back into a to-do list you can actually finish.

Expected outcome: The first hour of your day stops being triage.

How to Install a Downloaded AI Skill (60-Second Steps)

Every skill on this page installs the same way inside its platform — open the Skills area, paste the prompt or upload the file, save. The exact clicks and eligibility differ between ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini Spark, so here’s the short version of each. Full walkthroughs live on each platform hub.

**Why business owners install it:** The blank page is the reason posts don’t ship. This gives you the outline, first draft, and title options in one pass, so what you’re editing on a Tuesday is a real post, not a staring contest.
**Expected outcome:** A publish-ready draft in the time you used to spend just deciding on the angle.
**What it does:** Takes one idea, blog post, or announcement and returns a week of platform-native posts — Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, X — each written for how that platform actually reads.
**Why business owners install it:** Posting the same copy on four platforms is why nothing performs on any of them. This gives you the same message, tuned four different ways, in one sitting.
**Expected outcome:** A week of scheduled posts drafted in an hour instead of avoided all week.
**What it does:** Takes one long piece — a webinar transcript, podcast episode, or blog post — and hands back five shorter formats ready to publish: LinkedIn post, email newsletter, tweet thread, carousel outline, and a short-form video hook.
**Why business owners install it:** Most owners publish once and move on. Repurposing is the highest-ROI act in content, and skipping it is the reason your best ideas only reach the smallest slice of your audience.
**Expected outcome:** One piece of content quietly becomes six, without another writing session.
### Close Deals and Run Meetings
**What it does:** Paste your discovery-call notes and get a scoped, priced proposal — problem restated in the client’s words, the deliverables, the timeline, the price, and the terms.
**Why business owners install it:** Proposals are where deals stall. Writing a good one takes hours you don’t have; sending a bad one loses the deal you already won on the call.
**Expected outcome:** A proposal out the door the same day as the call, not the following week.
**What it does:** Paste a transcript (from Zoom, Meet, Fireflies, or a manual paste) and get back the summary that matters — decisions made, action items with owners, and the open questions someone needs to answer.
**Why business owners install it:** Nobody remembers what was decided at the Wednesday call by Friday. This makes the record automatic, so nothing falls off between meetings.
**Expected outcome:** Meetings actually produce follow-through instead of vibes.
**What it does:** Paste “the way I do this thing” — a rough walkthrough of any recurring task — and get a numbered SOP with owner, inputs, steps, decision points, exceptions, and definition-of-done.
**Why business owners install it:** Every job you can’t hand off is a job you have to keep doing. SOPs are the difference between hiring help and staying the bottleneck.
**Expected outcome:** A document you can hand to a new hire or a VA and get the same result you’d get yourself.
### Manage the Business
**What it does:** Turns a week’s worth of notes, wins, misses, and calendar into a one-page Monday brief — what happened, what’s ahead, what needs a decision, and what to focus on this week.
**Why business owners install it:** Running a business without a weekly stop-and-look is how quarters get away from you. This is that stop-and-look, done in 15 minutes with a pasteable format.
**Expected outcome:** A Monday you actually start with the plan, not the panic.
**What it does:** Reads a folder (paste a directory listing, or upload files) and hands back a rename-and-move plan — consistent file names, a real folder structure, and a “what to keep vs archive” call on the clutter.
**Why business owners install it:** Nobody wants to spend a Saturday cleaning up “Untitled document (3) copy final v2.” This turns the job into approving a list, not doing the sort.
**Expected outcome:** A folder you actually want to open again.
**What it does:** Point it at a competitor’s website and get back their positioning, pricing model, offer stack, obvious gaps, and what you could say differently — in a format you can drop into a strategy doc.
**Why business owners install it:** Most owners “know” what their competitors do and are half-wrong. This is the hour of research you keep meaning to do and never actually finish.
**Expected outcome:** Positioning decisions made from evidence, not gut feel.
**What it does:** Paste a meeting note and get back a clean CRM update — stage change, budget, timeline, objections, next step, and owner — formatted the way your CRM wants it.
**Why business owners install it:** Nobody updates the CRM because updating the CRM is annoying. This is the layer between “we had the call” and “the record reflects it.”
**Expected outcome:** A pipeline that reflects reality, without the after-work admin.
**What it does:** Reads a customer’s message — even a long, angry, or unclear one — and drafts a reply that acknowledges what they’re actually upset about, answers the real question, and stays on-brand.
**Why business owners install it:** Great support keeps customers; slow or defensive support loses them. This gets a good draft in front of you so you can send in minutes, not hours.
**Expected outcome:** Support tickets get answered faster and read warmer.
### Send Better Emails
**What it does:** Turns a short brief — who they are, what you offer, why now — into a cold email that opens with something specific to them, not a template smell, and asks for one small next step.
**Why business owners install it:** Cold email is the fastest way to fill a pipeline and the easiest thing to do badly. This gives you a starting draft that already sounds like a real person before you personalize it.
**Expected outcome:** Replies instead of unread thread counts.
**What it does:** Reads your last thread with a quiet lead and writes the follow-up — the one that says “picking this back up” without sounding like a nag or a template.
**Why business owners install it:** Most deals die in the follow-up gap, not in the pitch. This makes the follow-up something you actually send, because the draft is already waiting.
**Expected outcome:** Cold leads warm back up because the message finally goes out.
**What it does:** Paste a chunk of unread inbox and get it sorted — what needs a reply today, what can wait, what’s noise — with a draft reply already written for the ones that need one.
**Why business owners install it:** An inbox with 400 unreads is a decision-fatigue tax before you’ve done any real work. This turns it back into a to-do list you can actually finish.
**Expected outcome:** The first hour of your day stops being triage.
## How to Install a Downloaded AI Skill (60-Second Steps)
**Every skill on this page installs the same way inside its platform — open the Skills area, paste the prompt or upload the file, save.** The exact clicks and eligibility differ between ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini Spark, so here’s the short version of each. Full walkthroughs live on each platform hub.
_Platform install steps and availability verified August 5, 2026. Product surfaces change — check each platform’s own docs if the UI moves._
### Install into ChatGPT
1. Open the skill’s page on this site and copy the prompt block (or click _Download SKILL.md_). 2. In ChatGPT, open the **Skills** area and choose _Create_ → _Create with chat_ (build the skill conversationally) or _Create with editor_ (paste directly into the editor). 3. Paste the prompt or upload the `SKILL.md` in any compatible format, name the skill, and save. 4. Trigger it in any chat by saying the skill’s name — e.g. “run the blog post skill.”
ChatGPT Skills availability depends on your plan and workspace rollout — see [ChatGPT Skills availability](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/chatgpt-skills-availability/) for the current list. To browse everything ChatGPT-ready, open the [ChatGPT skills library](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/chatgpt/).
### Install into Claude
1. Copy the prompt block or download the `SKILL.md`. 2. In Claude, open **Customize → Skills** and make sure _code execution_ is enabled — that’s what unlocks Skills on your account. 3. Add a new skill, upload the file (or paste the prompt), name it, and save. 4. Trigger by name in any conversation.
Claude Skills are available across Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans when code execution is enabled — not paid-only. Every Claude-tested skill lives in the [Claude skills library](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/claude/).
### Install into Gemini Spark
1. Copy the prompt block or download the `SKILL.md` (a zip containing one also works). 2. Switch to **Spark → Skills** and choose _Create with Gemini_, _Create manually_, or _Upload_. 3. Paste or upload the file, name it, and save. 4. Trigger it by typing `/` to pick from your enabled skills — or let Spark apply them automatically when the task matches.
**Spark Skills** is a separate feature from Gems / Custom Sparks. It currently requires an eligible Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription, a personal Google account, and a supported region. New to Spark? Start with [how to set up Gemini Spark](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/setup-guides/gemini-spark/), then browse the [Gemini Spark skills library](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/gemini-spark/).
## Frequently Asked Questions
**Which free AI skill should I download first?**
Pick the one that matches a job on your desk this week. If you don’t have a site yet, start with [Website Builder](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/website-builder/). If you’re behind on content, [Blog Post](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/blog-post/). If your week is call-heavy, [Meeting Notes](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/meeting-notes/). If your inbox is buried, [Gmail Triage](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/gmail-triage/). Install one, use it once on real work, then add the next.
**Are these AI skills really free to download?**
Yes — every skill on this page is free to copy as a prompt and install into ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini Spark. The prompt block on each skill’s page is free to grab with no account. A few skills also offer a downloadable `SKILL.md` file that requires a free account to grab; the prompt itself is still free either way.
**What’s the difference between an AI skill download and a normal ChatGPT prompt?**
A prompt is a single request you retype every time. A skill is the saved workflow behind that prompt — the AI stores when to use it, what steps to follow, and what shape the output should be, so you trigger it by name instead of re-explaining. See [what an AI agent skill is](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/what-is-an-ai-agent-skill/) for the deeper explanation.
**Do I need a paid plan on ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini Spark to install a skill?**
Depends on the platform:
* **ChatGPT:** availability depends on your plan and workspace rollout — see [ChatGPT Skills availability](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/chatgpt-skills-availability/) for the current list. * **Claude:** available across Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans when code execution is enabled. * **Gemini Spark:** requires an eligible Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription, a personal Google account, and a supported region.
The skill files themselves are always free on this site. _Platform availability verified August 5, 2026._
**Can I install the same downloaded skill in ChatGPT and Claude and Gemini Spark?**
Yes — every skill in this starter pack is written to work in all three. You install a separate copy in each platform (they don’t sync between apps), but the same prompt block runs correctly in all three. Handy if you use one platform for drafting and another for review.
**How long does installing a skill actually take?**
About a minute per skill, per platform. Copy the prompt block, open your AI’s Skills or Sparks settings, paste, name it, save. There’s no coding step, no API keys, and nothing to configure — that’s the whole install.
**Where do I go if I want to build my own skill instead of downloading one?**
Start with [how to create an AI skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-an-ai-skill/) for the universal walkthrough, or [turn a prompt into an AI skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/turn-a-prompt-into-an-ai-skill/) if you already have a prompt that works and want to make it reusable.
**What if I want the ranked recommendations, not the download pack?**
Then read the [best AI skills for business owners](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-ai-skills/) — same library, ordered by which are the highest-impact to install first. This page is the “just give me the files” version; that page is the “which ones matter most” version.
**Ready to install?** Pick two skills above, download them today, and use each one once on real work this week. The library isn’t a reading exercise — it’s a stack of tools waiting to save you an hour apiece. item.text: Free AI Content Repurposing Skill (2026) Free AI Agent Skill The free AI Content Repurposing skill Paste one thing you already made — a blog post, a webinar, a podcast, a long email — and get a week of content out of it: a LinkedIn post, a thread, a carousel outline, a newsletter blurb, and short-video hooks, all in your voice and all from your source. Copy it as a prompt, or install it as a real SKILL.md file. Free prompt + SKILL.md file · Free signup · Setup help This Content Repurposing skill is a free AI skill that turns one piece of content you already made — a blog post, a video or webinar, a podcast, a long email — into a week’s worth of posts across the channels you actually use, without inventing a single claim you didn’t make. Paste in the source, tell it where you post, and the skill adapts the ideas to each format — a LinkedIn post, an X thread, a carousel outline, a newsletter blurb, short-video hooks — in your voice, not a chopped-up copy-paste. It pulls only the points, stats, and quotes that are in your source, and shows you what came from where. Use it as a copy-paste prompt in any AI chat, or install the ready-made SKILL.md file so it runs on command in Claude, Gemini Spark, or ChatGPT. No coding required. The Content Repurposing skill takes one finished piece of content you paste in — a blog post, transcript, or long email — and turns it into new formats for the channels you choose: LinkedIn, X, Instagram, a newsletter, short-video hooks. It repurposes what’s already there; it does not come up with net-new topics from a single idea (that’s the Social Media Post Generator) or decide what to post when (that’s a content calendar). It uses only the claims, stats, and quotes in your source — it won’t invent a statistic, a testimonial, or a result — and it never posts or schedules anything: you get drafts to review and publish yourself. Two ways to get the Content Repurposing skill This skill is free either way. Copy the prompt straight off this page with no account at all — or, once you’ve seen what it does, unlock the ready-made file for every skill in the library with a 7-day trial. The free SKILL.md download for this one skill sits with the file itself, a little further down. Free · start here Copy the prompt Paste into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark Works on free plans One post repurposed in about ten minutes $0 — no account, no card Free for 7 days Get this skill free — plus every other one with it Every skill in the library as a ready-made .md file — not just this one Weekly content plan, social posts, customer feedback, market research New skills added every week you’re in Beginner training and hands-on help setting up $0 for 7 days — then only $14/mo., cancel anytime Nothing is charged today. Cancel anytime. At a glance Content Repurposing skill: what it needs and what it returns What it isA free AI skill — a reusable set of instructions — that turns one finished piece of content into native drafts for the channels you pick. It comes as a copy-paste prompt and as a ready-made SKILL.md file. Who it’s forOwners and creators sitting on one good blog post, transcript, or long email who have no time to rewrite it four ways. What you give itOne finished piece — a blog post, transcript, or long email — plus the channels you want it for. What you get backThe Core Message, a native draft per channel (LinkedIn, X thread, Instagram carousel, newsletter blurb), a Repurposing Map, and a “What I Kept Out” list. Works withClaude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark. The prompt runs on free plans; the SKILL.md installs as a saved skill in Claude and Gemini Spark, or as a Project in ChatGPT. What it will not doIt does not post or schedule anything — it produces drafts for human review. It never invents a statistic, study, customer quote, testimonial, result, or claim you did not make. Time to first setAbout ten minutes for one source piece. What it costsThe prompt is free with no account. The SKILL.md file is free with a free account. The downloadable file for every other skill comes with All Access: free for 7 days, then $14/mo., cancel anytime. Part 1 of 5 · Your results One piece of content, a week of posts By the end of this AI skill guide, you’ll have the Content Repurposing skill ready to use — as a copy-paste prompt in any AI chat, or installed as a SKILL.md file that runs on command. It fixes the maths that kills most small-business content: you spend hours making one good thing, then post it once. This turns that one thing into a week of it. REPURPOSED — blog post: “5 email-marketing mistakes small shops make” (example) LinkedIn post: A hook on mistake #1 (sending only when you want to sell), then the fix — written to be read, not skimmed past. X / Twitter thread: 6 posts — one hook + one per mistake, each standing on its own. Instagram carousel: A 7-slide outline — title slide, one slide per mistake, a “save this” close. Newsletter blurb + 3 short-video hooks: A 90-word intro that links back to the post, plus three opening lines for Reels or TikToks. Repurposing map: which post came from which section of the source — so you can see nothing was bolted on. What I kept out: no new statistics, no invented customer quotes — if it isn’t in your post, it isn’t in the posts. Part 2 of 5 How to use the Content Repurposing AI skill in 3 steps The Content Repurposing skill is an AI skill — a reusable set of instructions. It comes in two formats below, and they contain the same thinking. Use the prompt if you just want a week of posts in the next five minutes. Use the SKILL.md file if you publish often and want it saved so it runs on command. 1 Pick your format Copy the prompt for a one-off, or copy the SKILL.md file to install it permanently. Both are below — same instructions, different packaging. 2 Paste your source + pick your channels Drop in the blog post, transcript, or email, and say where you post (LinkedIn, X, Instagram, newsletter) and any formats you want. One asset is enough. 3 Get your week of content You get a draft for each channel in your voice, a map of what came from where, and a note of anything it refused to invent. Edit, then publish. Format 1 — Prompt Version (any AI chat, nothing to install) Paste this into Claude, Gemini Spark, or ChatGPT, add your source at the bottom, and send. Works on free plans. Best if you repurpose content occasionally. You are a content strategist who repurposes one piece of content into many. Your job is to turn the source the user pastes in into ready-to-edit posts for the channels they name — adapting the ideas to each format, not just chopping the text up. PROCESS 1. Read the source and pull out its core message and the 4-7 key points, examples, and any stats or quotes it actually contains. 2. Confirm the channels and formats the user asked for. If they didn't say, default to: one LinkedIn post, one short X/Twitter thread, one Instagram carousel outline, and a short newsletter blurb. 3. For each format, write a real draft that fits how that channel works — a hook and a single idea for a social post, one point per item in a thread, a slide-by-slide outline for a carousel. Do not paste the same paragraph into every box. 4. Keep the user's voice and tone. Match the source; don't switch to generic marketing-speak. 5. Provide a short "repurposing map" — which post came from which part of the source. 6. List what you deliberately left out (anything you would have had to invent). RULES - Use ONLY what's in the source. NEVER invent a statistic, a study, a customer quote, a testimonial, a result, or a claim the user didn't make. - Keep the user's voice. This is the same skill packaged as a proper `SKILL.md` — the format Claude and Gemini Spark use for saved skills. The `description` line at the top is the important part: it tells your AI _when_ to run this on its own, so you can just say **“repurpose this”** and it fires. Paste the whole block into a new file called `SKILL.md`, or straight into your platform’s skill instructions.
``` --- name: content-repurposing description: Turn one piece of source content into ready-to-edit posts for multiple channels — LinkedIn, X, Instagram, a newsletter, short-video hooks — keeping the user's voice and using only what's in the source. Use this when the user pastes a blog post, transcript, video, or long email and says repurpose this, turn this into social posts, or get more out of this content. ---
# Content Repurposing
When this skill runs, turn the user's source content into ready-to-edit posts for the channels they name.
## Process
1. Read the source and pull out its core message and the 4-7 key points, examples, and any stats or quotes it actually contains. 2. Confirm the channels and formats requested. If none are given, default to one LinkedIn post, one short X/Twitter thread, one Instagram carousel outline, and a short newsletter blurb. 3. For each format, write a real draft that fits how that channel works — do not paste the same paragraph into every box. 4. Keep the user's voice and tone. Match the source; don't switch to generic marketing-speak. 5. Provide a short "repurposing map" — which post came from which part of the source. 6. List what you deliberately left out.
## Rules
- Use ONLY what's in the source. Never invent a statistic, a study, a customer quote, a testimonial, a result, or a claim the user didn't make. - Keep the user's voice. If unsure of the tone, mirror the source rather than default to hype. - Adapt to each channel honestly — no fake urgency, no engagement-bait that misrepresents the content. - Suggest a call to action only if the source implies one; don't fabricate an offer. - Do not post or schedule anything. Produce drafts for human review.
## Output format
### Core Message One line: what this content is really about.
### [Channel 1] The draft.
### [Channel 2] The draft.
### [Channel 3] Slide-by-slide outline where relevant.
### [Channel 4] The draft.
### Repurposing Map Which post came from which part of the source.
### What I Kept Out Anything I would have had to invent, and why I left it.
If the user has not pasted any source content, ask for it before repurposing anything. ```
**Not sure which to use?**
Start with **Format 1** — you’ll have a week of posts in five minutes with nothing to set up. Install **Format 2** once you’ve run it a couple of times and know it matches your channels. Copied the SKILL.md already? Here’s exactly where it goes in each platform:

## AI skill or prompt? Which one beginners should use
Both formats above contain the same instructions. The only real difference is whether your AI has to be reminded every time:

Paste it into any AI chat and it works immediately — nothing to install, works on free plans, works in any tool. The trade-off: you paste the whole thing every single time, and it’s on you to remember to. ## Content Repurposing skill: frequently asked questions
Is this AI content repurposing skill free?
**Yes — the prompt is free with no account at all, and the SKILL.md file is free with a free account.** Yes. Both the copy-paste prompt and the SKILL.md file are completely free. Optional reusable features may depend on the AI tool and plan you use. ChatGPT Projects are available on free and paid plans, Claude skills are available when code execution is enabled, and Gemini Spark skills currently require Google AI Ultra, or Google AI Pro in the US.
What can I paste in to repurpose?
**One finished piece — a blog post, a transcript, or a long email.** Anything long enough to have ideas in it: a blog post, a webinar or video transcript, a podcast episode’s notes, a case study, or a long email or LinkedIn post that did well. item.text: The 7 Best AI Email Automation Skills (2026) The average knowledge worker spends 28% of the workweek on email — roughly 13 hours — according to McKinsey Global Institute research. Most of that isn’t new writing. It’s the same follow-up you’ve written a hundred times, an inbox that refills by lunch, and invoices you sent three weeks ago and never chased. AI email automation fixes the repetition without replacing you in the reply. This guide covers the seven best AI email skills that give the biggest hours back to a solopreneur or small-team owner. Every skill works in any AI tool — Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini Spark, or Claude Fable 5 — and every one is free. What’s the fastest way to automate email with AI? The fastest way to automate email with AI is to install 3 free AI email skills in Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark: an AI Gmail triage skill (~90 min/week saved), an AI follow-up email skill (~45 min/week), and an AI overdue invoice follow-up skill (~30 min/week). Together they save most solopreneurs 3–5 hours a week and cost nothing to install. You’re losing 13 hours a week to your inbox Email is the highest-leverage place a business owner can apply AI in 2026 because the work is repetitive, high-volume, and already written down. The numbers say the same thing from four angles: 28% of the workweek — ~13 hours — goes to email, per McKinsey Global Institute research. 40% of workers call email their single biggest productivity drain, ahead of meetings, in Atlassian’s State of Teams research. 29% of workers are still doing email at 10 PM, and 40% check before 6 AM, per Clean.email’s 2026 report. 23 minutes, 15 seconds is what it takes to refocus after a single email interruption, per Gloria Mark’s UC Irvine research — which is why triage beats checking. The upside is measurable too: Microsoft’s Work Trend Index reports Copilot users save roughly 3 hours a week on email once a saved workflow is in place — about a quarter of the email workload gone. An AI email skill is that saved workflow: your context, your voice, your format — captured once and reused every time. (Email is the highest-leverage single job to automate; for the broader picture see the 21 best AI skills across every business function.) AI email skills vs. paid inbox tools ($30/mo) Most readers land here already paying for ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini Spark. The real question is whether an AI email skill inside those tools does the same job as a $30/mo inbox app like Superhuman or SaneBox. Short answer: for the drafting and triage work, yes. AI email skills (this guide) Paid inbox tools (Superhuman, SaneBox, etc.) Cost Free — runs inside the AI tool you already pay for $15–$40/mo per user, on top of your AI plan Lives in Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark (your existing tool) A separate inbox client or Gmail sidebar Drafts in your voice Yes — paste 3–5 real emails once Partial — learns from patterns, not always tunable Portable across tools Yes — the skill is a plain-text file you own No — locked to the vendor’s platform Sends automatically No — you review, you send Yes on some plans (auto-replies, snoozes, follow-ups) Best for Owners who want to keep their inbox and cut the drafting time Heavy inbox users who want a new interface too Many owners run both. The skills replace the writing time; a paid tool replaces the client. If you only want one, start with the free AI email skills and add a paid inbox later if you still need it. Compare all 7 AI email skills in 30 seconds Each skill below solves one specific email task, works in every major AI tool, and is free to install. AI email skill Best AI model for it Best for Time saved AI Follow-Up Email Skill Claude Sonnet 5 Deals and clients going quiet ~45 min/week AI Gmail Triage Skill Gemini Spark (Google AI Pro) Inbox that eats your morning ~90 min/week AI Customer Support Reply Skill Claude Sonnet 5 Repeat support questions ~60 min/week AI Cold Outreach Email Skill Claude Opus 5 (high-stakes) Top-of-pipeline outreach ~75 min/week AI Overdue Invoice Follow-Up Skill ChatGPT Late invoices nobody chases ~30 min/week AI Client Onboarding Email Skill Claude Sonnet 5 Signed clients waiting for kickoff ~40 min/week AI Meeting Follow-Up Email Skill Claude Sonnet 5 Calls with no record of who owns what ~50 min/week Why these 7 skills — and not 40 Every skill on this list clears the same five bars. Works in any AI tool. Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini Spark, or Claude Fable 5 — no vendor lock-in. Handles a specific recurring email task. Not a generic “write better emails” prompt — scoped to one job that repeats every week. Beginner-friendly. No coding, no API keys, no automation platform to configure. Produces a saved output. A finished draft or reply, not just a chat response. Free to install. No paywall in front of the AI email automation itself. The 7 best AI email skills that save the most hours Ordered by how many business owners the underlying problem actually affects. Best for: Drafting the fifth follow-up to a ghosted lead without second-guessing the wording every time. Time saved: ~45 min/week for a solopreneur running 20–30 client conversations at a time. Turns a short context line or messy meeting notes into a clear follow-up — thank-you, what was agreed, action items with owners, specific next step — and keeps every send in the same voice and shape. How it works in one line: Paste the conversation, tell it who you’re writing to, get a ready-to-send follow-up with the next step already proposed. Install the free AI Follow-Up Email skill → Best for: Sorting 40+ overnight messages before your first coffee, without opening every one to decide what it is. Time saved: ~90 min/week — the biggest single win on this list for anyone whose morning disappears into the inbox. Reads a batch of emails and sorts them into reply-now, reply-later, delegate, and archive — each with a one-line reason and a draft reply for the two or three that matter most. How it works in one line: Paste (or connect) your unread threads and get back a prioritized list with the drafts already written. Install the free AI Gmail Triage skill → Best for: Answering the same five customer questions rewritten five ways, without sounding like a bot. Time saved: ~60 min/week for a solo owner handling 20–40 support messages weekly. Takes the inbound message and the facts you provide, then drafts a calm, on-brand reply that answers the question and ends with a clear next step. Never invents an order status, refund, or policy — it flags anything it doesn’t know. How it works in one line: Paste the customer message plus a line of context, get a reply ready to send after a 10-second review. Install the free AI Customer Support Reply skill → Best for: Filling the top of pipeline without sending emails that read like a mail-merge template with the first name dropped in. Time saved: ~75 min/week for anyone doing weekly outbound to 20–40 prospects. Writes a specific, researched cold email built around the prospect’s actual situation. Handles the personalization and research that usually eat the whole hour, so what lands reads like it took ten minutes, not ten seconds. How it works in one line: Paste the prospect’s website or role plus your offer, get an email that references their real context and asks for one small, easy yes. Install the free AI Cold Outreach Email skill → Best for: Chasing an invoice you sent three weeks ago without sounding accusatory the first time or timid the fourth. Time saved: ~30 min/week — the real payoff is cash arriving weeks sooner because the follow-up actually gets sent. Drafts the reminder you keep putting off. Matches tone to how overdue the invoice is (polite nudge at 7 days, firm-but-warm at 14, plain at 30+), pulls in the invoice number and amount you provide, and leaves the payment link where you want it. How it works in one line: Feed it the client, invoice amount, and days late — get a reminder firm enough to work and warm enough to keep the relationship. Install the free AI Overdue Invoice Follow-Up skill → Best for: Sending a signed client the first email of the engagement without leaving them staring at their inbox for a week. Time saved: ~40 min/week for anyone signing 2–5 new clients a month. Turns the client’s signed proposal or intake form into a welcome email plus a kickoff plan — what happens next, what you need from them, when the first session lands. Kills the silence between “invoice paid” and “let’s begin.” How it works in one line: Paste the signed proposal or intake notes, get a welcome email plus a checklist of week-one actions. Install the free AI Client Onboarding Email skill → Best for: Turning a messy call into a follow-up email that lands the same afternoon, not three days later when the conversation has cooled. Time saved: ~50 min/week for anyone in more than three client calls a week. Converts rambling notes or a transcript into a structured recap — decisions, owner-tagged action items with dates, open questions — then produces an email-ready follow-up you can send to everyone on the call. How it works in one line: Drop in notes or a transcript, get a summary Doc plus a follow-up email in the same run. Install the free AI Meeting Follow-Up Email skill → Set up your first AI email skill in 10 minutes Every skill on this page installs the same way: copy, paste, feed inputs. Copy the skill. Each skill page has a “Copy the free skill” button. Expected result: SKILL.md text on your clipboard. Paste it into your AI tool. As a message, a ChatGPT Project, a Claude Project’s custom instructions, or a Gemini Spark Skill. Expected result: the AI has the workflow saved for every future invocation. Feed it your task inputs. Paste the email or notes, add a line of context, ask it to draft. Expected result: a finished draft in the format the skill defines — ready to send after a 10-second review. For the full step-by-step on saving skills as reusable workflows, see how to create a Claude skill from scratch, or the platform-specific best-of lists: the 15 best ChatGPT skills, the best Claude skills, and the 12 best Gemini Spark skills. Which AI model should draft your email? The best AI model for email skills depends on the stakes and the volume. In 2026, four models cover almost every business email workflow. Claude Sonnet 5 Best for: Everyday follow-ups, support replies, meeting recaps, onboarding. Recommendation: The default choice — use it for five of the seven skills here. Most consistent voice-matching model of 2026. For every-job coverage, see the best Claude skills. Claude Opus 5 Best for: High-stakes emails — cold outreach to a dream client, negotiations, delicate customer saves. Recommendation: Released July 24, 2026; Anthropic reports it leads on business analysis at roughly half the price of Claude Fable 5. Reach for it when a single email is worth 20 minutes of thought. ChatGPT Best for: Invoice reminders, quick reformatting, batch drafting. Recommendation: Use ChatGPT when the email is a template that needs the numbers plugged in. Projects override global custom instructions, so a per-workflow project holds your skill cleanly. See also the 15 best ChatGPT skills. Gemini Spark (Google AI Pro) Best for: Gmail-native workflows — triage, scheduled digests, drafts written straight to the Gmail draft folder. Recommendation: Google expanded Google AI Pro to 160+ additional countries on July 30, 2026. Use it for the Gmail Triage skill above every other model — and see the 12 best Gemini Spark skills for wider workflows. The 5 mistakes that make AI email sound like AI Most AI email automation projects fail because the setup skips one of these five steps. Skipping the brand voice reference. Without a sample of your writing, every model defaults to the same LinkedIn-thought-leader tone. Feed it five real emails you’ve sent. Feeding raw threads with no context. The AI can’t infer the relationship or how many times you’ve followed up. One line of context changes the draft entirely. Using Claude Fable 5 for throwaway replies. Fable 5 is premium-priced. Match model to stakes — Sonnet 5 or ChatGPT for volume, Fable 5 or Opus 5 for emails that matter. Skipping human review on cold outreach. Even a tuned cold email skill will occasionally invent a detail. AI drafts, you approve. Forgetting to log the draft in your CRM. A follow-up nobody records is one you’ll re-send in two weeks. Pair with an AI CRM update skill. Once one or two email skills are running, extend the setup to the rest of your business. The rest of the AI Agents Library cluster picks up where this article ends. The wider “best” lists: The 21 best AI skills across every business function — the cross-platform pillar. The best AI skills for building a website — the sibling job-based roundup. The 15 best ChatGPT skills to start with. The best Claude skills for business. The 12 best Gemini Spark skills for business. Skills libraries: Browse the full AI skills library. See every AI email skill in one place. Build your own: How to create a Claude skill from scratch. How to build a website with an AI skill. Frequently asked questions How is an AI email skill different from an inbox tool like Superhuman or SaneBox? Inbox tools like Superhuman AI and SaneBox are full applications that live inside your email client and charge $15–$40 a month. An AI email skill is a reusable set of instructions you paste into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini Spark — free, portable, scoped to one specific email task, and running inside the AI tool you already pay for. Tools give you a polished inbox interface; skills give you the drafting automation without another subscription. Many owners run both — the skills replace the writing time and the paid tool replaces the client. Do I need to install anything to use these email skills? No installation, no extensions. Every skill on this page is a short block of plain-text instructions — copy once, paste into your AI tool, saved for future use. If you want a walkthrough, see how to create a Claude skill from scratch. All Access users have every email skill preloaded. Which AI model is best for email tasks? Claude Sonnet 5 is the best all-round AI model for email in 2026 — it holds tone most consistently across a thread. Use Claude Opus 5 for high-stakes emails, ChatGPT for structured templates like invoice reminders, and Gemini Spark with Google AI Pro when the workflow needs to touch Gmail directly. How many emails can these AI skills handle per week? The limit is your AI plan, not the skills. Free ChatGPT and free Claude handle roughly 20–40 drafts a day. Paid plans handle hundreds. For a solopreneur processing 100–300 emails a week, one paid plan runs every skill here. Can these skills write on-brand for my business? Yes. Every skill has a section where you paste in a paragraph of your actual writing — three or four real emails are enough. Once the skill has that voice reference, drafts come back in your tone rather than a generic AI voice. Are these skills safe for cold outreach or spam-sensitive workflows? The skills don’t send — they draft, you review, you send. To stay on the right side of CAN-SPAM, GDPR, and PECR, keep your list opted-in, include a clear unsubscribe line, and use the skill for personalization — not volume a real person couldn’t send by hand. Do I need ChatGPT Plus or Claude Pro to use these email skills? No. Every skill on this page works on the free tier of ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini Spark. Paid plans get you higher limits and bigger models like Claude Opus 5. Free is enough to prove the workflow works before spending anything. Editorial note: AI Agents Library is an independent educational resource, not affiliated with Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or any AI vendor mentioned above. Every skill is free to copy and adapt; verify each draft before you send, especially for cold outreach, invoicing, and support. Model availability, pricing, and features change — check the vendor’s own documentation for current details.

Do I need to install anything to use these email skills?

Which AI model is best for email tasks?

Claude Sonnet 5 is the best all-round AI model for email in 2026 — it holds tone most consistently across a thread. How many emails can these AI skills handle per week?

The limit is your AI plan, not the skills. Free ChatGPT and free Claude handle roughly 20–40 drafts a day. Paid plans handle hundreds. For a solopreneur processing 100–300 emails a week, one paid plan runs every skill here.

Can these skills write on-brand for my business?

Yes. Every skill has a section where you paste in a paragraph of your actual writing — three or four real emails are enough. Once the skill has that voice reference, drafts come back in your tone rather than a generic AI voice.

Are these skills safe for cold outreach or spam-sensitive workflows?

The skills don’t send — they draft, you review, you send. To stay on the right side of CAN-SPAM, GDPR, and PECR, keep your list opted-in, include a clear unsubscribe line, and use the skill for personalization — not volume a real person couldn’t send by hand.

Do I need ChatGPT Plus or Claude Pro to use these email skills?

No. Every skill on this page works on the free tier of ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini Spark. Paid plans get you higher limits and bigger models like Claude Opus 5. Free is enough to prove the workflow works before spending anything.

Tools give you a polished inbox interface; skills give you the drafting automation without another subscription. Many owners run both — the skills replace the writing time and the paid tool replaces the client.
Do I need to install anything to use these email skills?
No installation, no extensions. Every skill on this page is a short block of plain-text instructions — copy once, paste into your AI tool, saved for future use. If you want a walkthrough, see [how to create a Claude skill from scratch](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-claude-skill/). All Access users have every email skill preloaded.
Which AI model is best for email tasks?
Claude Sonnet 5 is the best all-round AI model for email in 2026 — it holds tone most consistently across a thread. Use Claude Opus 5 for high-stakes emails, [ChatGPT](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-chatgpt-skills/) for structured templates like invoice reminders, and [Gemini Spark with Google AI Pro](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-gemini-spark-skills/) when the workflow needs to touch Gmail directly.
How many emails can these AI skills handle per week?
The limit is your AI plan, not the skills. Free ChatGPT and free Claude handle roughly 20–40 drafts a day. Paid plans handle hundreds. For a solopreneur processing 100–300 emails a week, one paid plan runs every skill here.
Can these skills write on-brand for my business?
Yes. Every skill has a section where you paste in a paragraph of your actual writing — three or four real emails are enough. Once the skill has that voice reference, drafts come back in your tone rather than a generic AI voice.
Are these skills safe for cold outreach or spam-sensitive workflows?
The skills don’t send — they draft, you review, you send. To stay on the right side of CAN-SPAM, GDPR, and PECR, keep your list opted-in, include a clear unsubscribe line, and use the skill for personalization — not volume a real person couldn’t send by hand.
Do I need ChatGPT Plus or Claude Pro to use these email skills?
No. Every skill on this page works on the free tier of ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini Spark. Paid plans get you higher limits and bigger models like Claude Opus 5. Free is enough to prove the workflow works before spending anything.
**Editorial note:** AI Agents Library is an independent educational resource, not affiliated with Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or any AI vendor mentioned above. Every skill is free to copy and adapt; verify each draft before you send, especially for cold outreach, invoicing, and support. Model availability, pricing, and features change — check the vendor’s own documentation for current details.
