## How We Chose the Best AI Skills
We did not rank these Skills by how impressive they sound in a demo. We favored workflows that satisfy five practical tests:
1. **The task repeats.** A Skill should save a method you will use again, not decorate a one-off prompt. 2. **The input is knowable.** The workflow can identify the files, notes, messages, or fields it needs before starting. 3. **The output is inspectable.** You can tell whether the result is complete, accurate, and usable. 4. **The business value is clear.** The Skill helps move revenue, reduce delay, improve a decision, or create a necessary deliverable. 5. **A human stays responsible.** The Skill asks instead of inventing and keeps consequential sending, publishing, payment, and replacement decisions under review.
The comparison table gives the overall ranking. The detailed reviews below now follow that same order from 1 through 21, with closely related workflows placed under clear business-outcome headings.
## The Best AI Skills to Start With
These three Skills solve broad, high-value business problems: seeing what matters each week, making better competitive decisions, and turning an offer into a complete website plan. They are the strongest starting points when you want one reusable workflow with value across the business.
**What it does:** Turns weekly notes, numbers, progress, blockers, and upcoming commitments into one short operating brief.
**Why it ranks first:** It gives an owner a repeatable way to see wins, changes, blockers, risks, decisions, and next priorities in one place—without building a reporting system first.
**Use it when:** The week feels busy but you cannot quickly explain what moved, what is stuck, and what matters next.
**What it does:** Compares competitor positioning, offers, pricing evidence, strengths, gaps, and customer-facing language from the sources you approve.
**Why it earns a place:** It turns browsing into a repeatable decision process. Instead of collecting screenshots and impressions, you get the same fields compared across every competitor.
**Use it when:** You are revising an offer, entering a category, updating pricing, or looking for a meaningful positioning gap.
**What it does:** Turns a business, audience, offer, proof, and conversion goal into a sitemap, page plan, core copy, SEO metadata, FAQ, and implementation brief.
**Why it earns a place:** A website fails when it becomes a collection of disconnected writing tasks. This Skill keeps every page tied to one audience journey and one measurable action.
**Use it when:** You need a new small-business site or a coherent plan before opening a website builder.
## Best AI Skills for Operations, Documents, and Data
These Skills create the operating artifacts that keep work moving: decisions, SOPs, proposals, onboarding plans, analysis, and summaries. Browse the [free AI Documents and Data Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/documents-data/) collection for the complete category.
**What it does:** Turns a transcript or rough notes into a concise summary, explicit decisions, unresolved questions, and action items with owners and due dates.
**Why it earns a place:** A meeting is only useful if the decisions survive it. This Skill separates what was discussed from what was actually decided.
**Use it when:** Important tasks are being lost inside transcripts, recordings, chat logs, or handwritten notes.
**What it does:** Interviews you about a process or reads your rough notes, then converts the method into an SOP with prerequisites, steps, exceptions, common mistakes, and a quality check.
**Why it earns a place:** An undocumented process cannot be delegated or improved. This Skill captures what an experienced person actually does, including the parts that are usually assumed.
**Use it when:** A recurring job still depends on one person remembering the correct sequence.
**What it does:** Turns discovery notes into a proposal covering the client’s problem, your approach, deliverables, boundaries, timeline, investment, and one clear next step.
**Why it earns a place:** The value is not “AI writes sales copy.” The value is getting a complete proposal out while the conversation is still fresh and the facts are available.
**Use it when:** You have enough discovery information to define the engagement but keep delaying the document.
**What it does:** Converts a signed engagement into a welcome email, intake questions, kickoff agenda, access checklist, and practical first-30-day plan.
**Why it earns a place:** Onboarding is predictable enough to standardize but important enough that inconsistency immediately damages confidence.
**Use it when:** A deal has closed and the client needs to know what happens next, what you need, and when progress begins.
**What it does:** Reviews spreadsheet rows and identifies the trend, key totals, outliers, missing fields, and questions worth investigating next.
**Why it earns a place:** Many businesses collect more data than they interpret. This Skill forces a repeatable analysis structure instead of asking for a vague “summary of my spreadsheet.”
**Use it when:** You have a sales, expense, lead, content, or operations export and need to understand what changed.
**What it does:** Turns a long PDF or report into a concise executive summary containing the bottom line, key figures, risks, decisions, and a page reference for every material claim.
**Why it earns a place:** Summaries are only useful when the reader can return to the source. Page grounding makes the output reviewable rather than merely fluent.
**Use it when:** A report, proposal, policy, or research document is too long to absorb before the decision it affects.
## Best AI Skills for Research and Better Decisions
Research Skills are useful when they expose evidence, uncertainty, and missing information. They are dangerous when they merely produce confident prose. The Skills below require traceable inputs and a decision-ready output.
**What it does:** Organizes market notes and approved research into audience signals, trends, risks, assumptions, and questions that still need validation.
**Why it earns a place:** It produces a brief built for a decision rather than a generic “market overview.” The explicit unknowns are as important as the findings.
**Use it when:** You are considering a new audience, offer, location, product, partnership, or campaign.
**What it does:** Groups reviews, survey responses, interviews, or support notes into themes, pain points, requests, evidence, and recommended priorities.
**Why it earns a place:** Your customers have already described the problem. This Skill helps you see the pattern without flattening every comment into one vague summary.
**Use it when:** You have enough feedback to make manual reading inconsistent, but still need examples behind every theme.
**What it does:** Tracks a defined topic, compares reporting dates with event dates, removes duplicates, and turns the meaningful developments into a sourced brief.
**Why it earns a place:** News monitoring becomes valuable when it distinguishes “new article” from “new event” and tells you what changed since the previous brief.
**Use it when:** A market, technology, competitor set, or regulation changes often enough to justify a recurring review.
## Best AI Skills for Email, Sales, and Customer Communication
These Skills are strongest when speed matters but the final message still needs judgment. They draft, organize, and recommend; you review before anything consequential is sent. If email is where most of your week goes, see [the 7 best AI email skills for 2026](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-ai-email-skills/) for the deep-dive roundup, or browse the complete [free AI Email Skills collection](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/email/).
**What it does:** Turns a previous email, meeting, proposal, or short context note into a focused follow-up with useful subject lines and an optional no-reply sequence.
**Why it earns a place:** Follow-through affects sales, client experience, hiring, partnerships, and everyday operations. It is frequent, easy to postpone, and costly when forgotten.
**Use it when:** A conversation needs a clear next step, a decision is waiting, or a good lead has gone quiet.
**What it does:** Sorts email into urgent, reply soon, waiting, and FYI buckets, then identifies the messages that need your attention first.
**Why it earns a place:** A full inbox is not only a volume problem; it is a decision problem. This Skill creates a manageable queue without pretending every unread message matters equally.
**Use it when:** You are scanning the same inbox repeatedly but still cannot tell what must be handled today.
**What it does:** Drafts a firm but professional payment reminder and maps an escalation sequence that becomes more direct without becoming hostile.
**Why it earns a place:** The task is uncomfortable, repetitive, and attached directly to cash flow. A saved method helps you follow up consistently instead of waiting until frustration changes the tone.
**Use it when:** An invoice is past due and you need to preserve both the payment expectation and the client relationship.
**What it does:** Drafts a calm reply to a customer question or complaint using the policies, facts, and tone you provide.
**Why it earns a place:** Support messages often need the same policy explained in different language. The Skill creates consistency while preserving space for empathy and human review.
**Use it when:** A reply must be clear and helpful without promising a refund, exception, timeline, or outcome that has not been approved.
**What it does:** Uses a real prospect, a clear offer, and available evidence to draft a concise outreach email with subject lines and follow-ups that add information rather than nag.
**Why it earns a place:** Generic outreach is easy to automate and easy to ignore. A good Skill forces relevance, brevity, and a defensible reason for contacting that person.
**Use it when:** You can explain who the offer is for and why a specific prospect is a credible fit.
## Best AI Skills for Content, Marketing, and Websites
The useful marketing Skills do more than generate words. They start from an audience, source, offer, or finished page and create a specific asset with a reviewable goal. Explore the full [Content and Marketing Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/content-marketing/) and [Website and Design Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/web-design/) collections.
**What it does:** Turns one offer, one audience, and one desired action into a complete landing-page draft in visitor reading order: hero, problem, offer, proof, objections, and call to action.
**Why it earns a place:** A homepage introduces the business; a landing page gives one audience a focused reason to take one action. This Skill keeps a promotion from turning into disconnected sections and generic sales copy.
**Use it when:** You are launching one offer, promotion, course, service, event, or paid campaign and need a focused conversion page.
**What it does:** Converts one business goal, audience, available sources, and chosen channels into a realistic seven-day content plan.
**Why it earns a place:** It solves the decision before the writing. A small, coherent plan is more likely to be published than a month of disconnected AI-generated ideas.
**Use it when:** You are deciding what to post each morning instead of working from a weekly theme and goal.
**What it does:** Turns one real idea, offer, lesson, or source into ready-to-review posts adapted for Facebook, LinkedIn, and Instagram.
**Why it earns a place:** The Skill begins with something true and worth saying, then adapts it. That is more useful than producing a high volume of interchangeable captions.
**Use it when:** You know the message but lose time rewriting it for each platform.
**What it does:** Reviews a finished page and produces a search-focused title tag, meta description, slug recommendation, and image alt text aligned with what the page actually contains.
**Why it earns a place:** Metadata should package a finished page, not compensate for an unfocused one. This Skill waits for the content, extracts its real promise, and creates a concise search result.
**Use it when:** A page is ready to publish in WordPress and needs a clean Rank Math or Yoast handoff.
## Should You Use These Skills in ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini Spark?
Choose the Skill first and the platform context second. The plain-text workflow is portable; the practical difference is what each agent can access, where the work runs, and what kind of deliverable you need.
* **Use ChatGPT** when you already organize recurring work in ChatGPT or Projects and want a broad set of general workflows. Native Skills availability depends on the account, but the plain-text instructions remain usable as Project instructions or a saved prompt. See [free ChatGPT Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/chatgpt/). * **Use Claude** when the job centers on reading files, building documents, analyzing data, or producing a polished deliverable. See [free Claude Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/claude/). * **Use Gemini Spark** when the task depends on supported Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Tasks, schedules, or other eligible connected apps. Account, plan, language, and country restrictions apply. See [free Gemini Spark Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/gemini-spark/).
If you are still choosing the agent itself, use the full comparison triangle: [Claude vs ChatGPT](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/claude-vs-chatgpt/), [ChatGPT vs Gemini Spark](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/chatgpt-vs-gemini-spark/), and [Claude Desktop vs Gemini Spark](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/claude-desktop-vs-gemini-spark/).
## How to Start Without Overcomplicating It
1. **Choose one recurring task.** Start with the work you postponed twice this month. 2. **Open the matching Skill page.** Review what it uses, what it produces, and where human approval remains. 3. **Test with safe material.** Use copies, sample records, or a controlled folder before exposing originals or connected systems. 4. **Define “done.”** State the required format, facts, fields, and checks before the agent starts. 5. **Review the output.** Correct the Skill when the method is wrong; correct the individual output when the source material is wrong. 6. **Reuse it for a week.** Only add the next Skill after the first one has earned a place in your workflow.
## Frequently Asked Questions
What are the best AI Skills for business owners?
The best starting Skills are AI Weekly Business Brief for seeing what changed and what matters next, AI Competitor Research for pricing and positioning decisions, AI Website Builder for creating a complete conversion-focused site plan, AI Meeting Notes for turning discussions into accountable actions, and AI SOP Generator for making important processes repeatable. Your best first Skill is the one attached to a valuable task you already repeat.
What is the difference between an AI Skill and a prompt?
A prompt is one request. An AI Skill is the reusable method for a type of request. It can define when to run, required inputs, steps, tools, templates, output format, quality checks, and common mistakes. A good Skill reduces the need to reconstruct those instructions in every conversation.
Do AI Skills work in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini Spark?
The instruction-based Skills in this guide are portable across ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini Spark. Each platform’s native installation, plan availability, connectors, file tools, and scheduled actions differ, so the same method may need a small platform-specific setup. The individual Skill pages explain those differences.
Are these AI Skills free?
Each Skill in this guide has a free individual page where you can learn the workflow and access the free version. You can browse all currently published Skills in the [free AI Skills Library](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/). The complete downloadable library is also available for readers who want all Skill files together.
Do I need coding experience to use an AI Skill?
No. Most business workflows in this guide are instruction-based and designed for beginners. Some native Skill systems can also support scripts and additional resources, but you do not need code to use the email, research, document, planning, content, or website methods recommended here.
Which AI Skill should I install first?
Choose the recurring task with the clearest cost of delay. If opportunities go quiet, start with Follow-Up Email. If meetings create confusion, choose Meeting Notes. If you make decisions without enough evidence, choose Competitor Research. If the entire week feels reactive, choose Weekly Business Brief.
How many AI Skills should I use?
Start with one and use it repeatedly for a week. Add another only after the first workflow is reliable and easy to review. A small set of trusted Skills is more valuable than a large library you have never tested.
Can an AI Skill send emails or change files automatically?
A Skill defines the method; the agent and its approved tools determine which actions are possible. Connected platforms may be able to draft, send, create, edit, or schedule work, but permissions and account access differ. Keep consequential actions under review, begin with copies, and confirm exactly what the agent may change.
How do I know whether an AI Skill is safe to download?
Review the Skill before installing it, especially if it contains scripts, code, or supporting files. Confirm the source, inspect its instructions and requested access, and test it with non-sensitive information. OpenAI and other platforms may scan uploaded Skills, but automated scanning does not replace your own review.
Can I create my own AI Skill?
Yes. Start with a task you already perform consistently, document the inputs, steps, output format, missing-information rules, and review checklist, then test it on several real examples. Follow [how to create an AI Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-an-ai-skill/) for the complete beginner process.

item.text: The 15 Best Claude Skills for Business (2026) Most business owners don’t have a Claude problem — they have a finished-work problem. The proposal that sits half-written, the spreadsheet you export but never read, the research you keep meaning to do. Claude is unusually good at the last mile: not just drafting text, but building the actual document, analyzing the actual data, and handing you a finished file you can send. This guide covers the 15 Claude skills worth setting up first — ordered by what Claude does best. Save a skill once and Claude can reuse the same method more consistently, with no coding required for the instructions featured here. To skim what’s available first, browse the full Claude skills library — every skill below is in there. Comparing workflows across every major agent? Start with the complete guide to the best AI Skills for business owners, then use this platform-specific list to decide which document, data, and research workflows fit Claude best. What are the best Claude skills for business owners? The best Claude skills for business owners lean on Claude’s strengths: building finished documents, analyzing data, and running deep research. Start with the AI Client Proposal Skill if proposals take you days, the AI Spreadsheet Insights Skill if you export data you never read, or the AI Market Research Brief Skill before your next launch. Pick one, use it for a week, then add the next. What Are Claude Skills? A Claude skill is a reusable set of instructions — a saved SKILL.md file with the context, rules, and output format for one task. Claude loads it when a request matches, helping it follow the same method more consistently without making you re-explain the workflow. That’s the difference between a prompt and a skill: a prompt is a single request you retype; a skill is the saved method behind it. For the deeper distinction, see what an AI agent skill is. What makes Claude skills different from the same skill in another tool is what Claude hands back. Claude doesn’t just write the text — it builds the finished file: a formatted Word document, a working Excel spreadsheet, a slide deck, a print-ready PDF. In Claude Cowork it can also pull from your local files and connected apps to complete multi-step work end to end. The skills below are chosen because they turn that strength into a repeatable business deliverable. Read this first: which Claude plan you need Every skill below is a plain-text method, so it works as a normal prompt in any Claude chat, on any plan. To get the finished-file and multi-step version — where Claude builds the document, analyzes the spreadsheet, or works across your local files — you’ll want Claude Cowork, which runs on eligible paid plans. Start free with the prompt version, then move the ones you rely on into Cowork. Quick Comparison: All 15 Claude Skills at a Glance Time saved is an estimate — it depends entirely on your volume. Use it to decide what to fix first, not as a promise. Scan for the job you keep putting off, then jump to its setup. Claude skill Best for What Claude delivers Est. time saved AI Client Proposal Skill Proposals that take days to send A formatted proposal document 2–4 hrs/proposal AI PDF Executive Summary Skill Long PDFs no one has time to read A one-page structured summary 1–2 hrs/document AI Spreadsheet Insights Skill Data you export but never read An analysis + a new summary tab 1–3 hrs/month AI Monthly Business Review Skill The month-end review you keep skipping A dated review doc + variance table 2–3 hrs/month AI Market Research Brief Skill Testing a new offer or market A cited, structured research brief 3–4 hrs/brief AI Competitor Research Skill Pricing and positioning calls A comparison report with sources 2–3 hrs/report AI SOP Generator Skill Processes trapped in your head A step-by-step SOP document 2–4 hrs/SOP AI Meeting Notes Skill Messy notes, forgotten action items A decisions + owner-tagged actions doc 2–3 hrs/week AI Weekly Content Plan Skill Posting consistently without a team A week of planned posts and hooks 2–4 hrs/week AI Customer Feedback Skill Reviews and surveys piling up A themed summary of what to fix 2–3 hrs/month AI Follow-Up Email Skill Deals and clients going cold A ready-to-send follow-up 1–2 hrs/week AI Cold Outreach Email Skill Filling the top of the pipeline Personalized opener drafts 2–3 hrs/week AI Customer Support Reply Skill The same questions, five ways On-brand reply drafts 2–4 hrs/week AI Client Onboarding Skill Slow, inconsistent kickoffs A milestone plan + welcome pack 2–3 hrs/client AI Website Copy Refresh Skill A page that isn’t converting Prioritized fixes + rewritten copy 2–3 hrs/page The 15 Best Claude Skills for Business Owners Ordered by where Claude pulls ahead — documents and data first, then research, then the everyday email and content work. Start at the top with whichever finished file you keep needing. What it does: Turns a short brief — scope, price, timeline — into a complete, formatted client proposal: summary, deliverables, pricing table, timeline, and terms. Why business owners use it: Proposals are where deals stall. Not because the work is unclear, but because building the document from a blank page feels like a chore that can wait until tomorrow. Claude removes the blank page. Real-world example: A consultant pastes the notes from a scoping call and gets back a client-ready proposal document she can polish and send the same afternoon instead of next week. Expected outcome: Proposals go out in hours, not days — while the lead is still warm. What it does: Reads a long PDF — a contract, report, whitepaper, or deck — and returns a one-page executive summary: the key points, the numbers that matter, and the decisions or risks you need to act on. Why business owners use it: The important document always arrives when you have ten minutes. Claude reads it properly so you can decide from a summary instead of skimming and hoping. Real-world example: An owner drops in a 40-page vendor contract and gets the obligations, renewal terms, and red flags on a single page before the call. Expected outcome: You act on long documents the day they arrive, not the week after. What it does: Takes a spreadsheet you already keep — sales, expenses, ad spend, bookings — and returns what actually changed, what stands out, and what to do about it, plus a clean summary tab. Why business owners use it: Most owners export data and never read it. Claude is genuinely strong at analysis, so the numbers become decisions instead of a file you keep meaning to open. Real-world example: An ecommerce owner drops in a monthly sales export and gets the three products trending down, the margin that slipped, and a one-line recommendation for each. Expected outcome: You catch slow trends while they’re small, not at quarter-end. What it does: Reads a KPI sheet you maintain, compares this month to last, and produces a dated review document plus a variance table — with the numbers that moved and three things to change. Why business owners use it: The month-end review is the first thing to get skipped when you’re busy. Claude builds the whole thing from data you already have, so it actually happens. Real-world example: On the 1st, an owner hands Claude the KPI sheet and gets a two-page review — revenue, margin, leads, churn — with a short “what to fix” list up top. Expected outcome: A real monthly review that takes minutes to read and never gets skipped. What it does: Researches a market, audience, or offer across the sources you approve and returns a structured brief — audience, needs, current solutions, pricing signals, gaps, and next steps — with every claim tied to its source. Why business owners use it: Guessing before a launch is expensive. Claude’s depth on multi-source synthesis makes it a strong fit for the kind of research that usually gets skipped for lack of time. Real-world example: Before pricing a new service, a founder gets a cited brief on what competitors charge, what buyers complain about, and where the gap is. Expected outcome: You launch with evidence instead of a hunch. What it does: Runs a structured competitor check — positioning, pricing, offers, messaging — and returns a report on what each rival is doing and what it means for you, with confirmed facts kept separate from interpretation. Why business owners use it: A competitor changes pricing on a Tuesday and you find out from a lost deal a month later. This turns “I should check on them” into a finished report you can act on. Real-world example: A services firm gets a side-by-side of three competitors’ pricing and positioning, plus two openings its own offer could own. Expected outcome: Pricing and positioning calls made with evidence, not vibes. What it does: Turns a rough description of how you do something into a clean, step-by-step standard operating procedure — numbered steps, owners, tools, and the “done” check. Why business owners use it: The processes that only live in your head are the ones you can’t delegate. Claude writes the document so you can hand the task off instead of doing it forever. Real-world example: An owner talks through how she onboards a new hire and gets a formatted SOP a team member can follow without asking her. Expected outcome: Work leaves your head and becomes something you can delegate. What it does: Turns raw notes or a transcript into a structured document — a decisions table, owner-tagged action items with dates, open questions, and a short summary. Why business owners use it: Every call produces three action items and no record of who owns which. Claude turns the mess into a document people actually read. Real-world example: After a team call, an agency lead pastes the transcript and gets a clean notes doc with owners and deadlines already assigned. Expected outcome: Nothing agreed in a meeting quietly disappears afterward. What it does: Reads your topic bank and returns a full week of content — post ideas, hook variations, and the angle for each day — as a plan you can hand to a writer or run yourself. Why business owners use it: Showing up consistently is the hard part, and the blank page is why most owners don’t. Claude removes it. Real-world example: A solo founder drops in five rough topics and gets a Monday-to-Friday plan with two hook options per post. **Real-world example:** A consultant pastes the notes from a scoping call and gets back a client-ready proposal document she can polish and send the same afternoon instead of next week.
**Expected outcome:** Proposals go out in hours, not days — while the lead is still warm.
**What it does:** Reads a long PDF — a contract, report, whitepaper, or deck — and returns a one-page executive summary: the key points, the numbers that matter, and the decisions or risks you need to act on.
**Why business owners use it:** The important document always arrives when you have ten minutes. Claude reads it properly so you can decide from a summary instead of skimming and hoping.
**Real-world example:** An owner drops in a 40-page vendor contract and gets the obligations, renewal terms, and red flags on a single page before the call.
**Expected outcome:** You act on long documents the day they arrive, not the week after.
**What it does:** Takes a spreadsheet you already keep — sales, expenses, ad spend, bookings — and returns what actually changed, what stands out, and what to do about it, plus a clean summary tab.
**Why business owners use it:** Most owners export data and never read it. Claude is genuinely strong at analysis, so the numbers become decisions instead of a file you keep meaning to open.
**Real-world example:** An ecommerce owner drops in a monthly sales export and gets the three products trending down, the margin that slipped, and a one-line recommendation for each.
**Expected outcome:** You catch slow trends while they’re small, not at quarter-end.
**What it does:** Reads a KPI sheet you maintain, compares this month to last, and produces a dated review document plus a variance table — with the numbers that moved and three things to change.
**Why business owners use it:** The month-end review is the first thing to get skipped when you’re busy. Claude builds the whole thing from data you already have, so it actually happens.
**Real-world example:** On the 1st, an owner hands Claude the KPI sheet and gets a two-page review — revenue, margin, leads, churn — with a short “what to fix” list up top.
**Expected outcome:** A real monthly review that takes minutes to read and never gets skipped.
**What it does:** Researches a market, audience, or offer across the sources you approve and returns a structured brief — audience, needs, current solutions, pricing signals, gaps, and next steps — with every claim tied to its source.
**Why business owners use it:** Guessing before a launch is expensive. Claude’s depth on multi-source synthesis makes it a strong fit for the kind of research that usually gets skipped for lack of time.
**Real-world example:** Before pricing a new service, a founder gets a cited brief on what competitors charge, what buyers complain about, and where the gap is.
**Expected outcome:** You launch with evidence instead of a hunch.
**What it does:** Runs a structured competitor check — positioning, pricing, offers, messaging — and returns a report on what each rival is doing and what it means for you, with confirmed facts kept separate from interpretation.
**Why business owners use it:** A competitor changes pricing on a Tuesday and you find out from a lost deal a month later. This turns “I should check on them” into a finished report you can act on.
**Real-world example:** A services firm gets a side-by-side of three competitors’ pricing and positioning, plus two openings its own offer could own.
**Expected outcome:** Pricing and positioning calls made with evidence, not vibes.
**What it does:** Turns a rough description of how you do something into a clean, step-by-step standard operating procedure — numbered steps, owners, tools, and the “done” check.
**Why business owners use it:** The processes that only live in your head are the ones you can’t delegate. Claude writes the document so you can hand the task off instead of doing it forever.
**Real-world example:** An owner talks through how she onboards a new hire and gets a formatted SOP a team member can follow without asking her.
**Expected outcome:** Work leaves your head and becomes something you can delegate.
**What it does:** Turns raw notes or a transcript into a structured document — a decisions table, owner-tagged action items with dates, open questions, and a short summary.
**Why business owners use it:** Every call produces three action items and no record of who owns which. Claude turns the mess into a document people actually read.
**Real-world example:** After a team call, an agency lead pastes the transcript and gets a clean notes doc with owners and deadlines already assigned.
**Expected outcome:** Nothing agreed in a meeting quietly disappears afterward.
**What it does:** Reads your topic bank and returns a full week of content — post ideas, hook variations, and the angle for each day — as a plan you can hand to a writer or run yourself.
**Why business owners use it:** Showing up consistently is the hard part, and the blank page is why most owners don’t. Claude removes it.
**Real-world example:** A solo founder drops in five rough topics and gets a Monday-to-Friday plan with two hook options per post.
**Expected outcome:** A week of content decided in one sitting instead of daily.
**What it does:** Reads a pile of reviews, survey answers, or support messages and returns the themes — what customers love, what they complain about, and what to fix first.
**Why business owners use it:** The answers are already in your feedback; nobody has time to read all of it. Claude reads it all and hands you the pattern.
**Real-world example:** A shop owner pastes three months of reviews and gets the top five recurring complaints, ranked by how often they appear.
**Expected outcome:** Product and service decisions driven by what customers actually say.
**What it does:** Turns raw notes or a context line into a clear client follow-up — thank-you, decisions, action items, and a specific next step.
**Why business owners use it:** Deals rarely die from a bad pitch; they die in the silence afterward. The follow-up is the highest-leverage email you send and the easiest to put off.
**Real-world example:** After a discovery call, a freelancer pastes her scribbled notes and gets a follow-up she can send in under a minute — next step already proposed.
**Expected outcome:** Follow-ups are easier to send promptly and in a consistent format.
**What it does:** Takes a lead list and a short offer, researches each prospect for a specific hook, and drafts a personalized opener per lead — never sent automatically, always yours to review.
**Why business owners use it:** Cold email works when it reads like a person wrote it. Claude lets you personalize at a volume a person couldn’t.
**Real-world example:** A B2B consultant hands over 20 leads and gets 20 openers, each referencing something specific about that prospect.
**Expected outcome:** Pipeline that reads personal without a full day of writing.
**What it does:** Reads an incoming support message, picks the right answer from your policies, and drafts a reply in your voice — polite, specific, and matched to how you actually handle it.
**Why business owners use it:** The same handful of questions arrive rewritten five different ways. Claude drafts the answer so you’re editing one line instead of writing from scratch.
**Real-world example:** A small team pastes a refund request and gets a ready reply that follows their policy and tone, needing one quick check before sending.
**Expected outcome:** Faster, more consistent support without a canned-response feel.
**What it does:** Turns a signed engagement into a complete kickoff pack — a milestone plan, a welcome message, and the first-week checklist — from the proposal and thread you already have.
**Why business owners use it:** New clients wait a week for kickoff because building the plan from scratch takes an hour you don’t have. Claude builds it in one run.
**Real-world example:** A coach hands over the signed proposal and gets a milestone plan plus a warm welcome message ready to send within minutes of the deal closing.
**Expected outcome:** Every client starts fast and gets the same strong first impression.
**What it does:** Reviews an existing page’s copy and returns a prioritized list of conversion fixes plus rewritten sections — clearer headline, stronger value, tighter calls to action.
**Why business owners use it:** A page that isn’t converting rarely needs a redesign; it needs sharper words. Claude diagnoses and rewrites in one pass.
**Real-world example:** An owner pastes a stale services page and gets three high-impact fixes at the top, then rewritten copy for each section below.
**Expected outcome:** A page that reads clearly and asks for the sale — without a redesign.
## How to Choose the Right Claude Skill
Don’t install all fifteen. Pick the one attached to the finished file you keep needing and use it for a week before adding the next.
* **If a document keeps stalling your week** — proposals, SOPs, reviews — start with [Client Proposal](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-claude-skills/#skill-1), [SOP Generator](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-claude-skills/#skill-7), or [Monthly Business Review](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-claude-skills/#skill-4). This is where Claude is strongest. * **If you have data you never read** — start with [Spreadsheet Insights](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-claude-skills/#skill-3) or [PDF Executive Summary](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-claude-skills/#skill-2). * **If you’re about to launch or price something** — start with [Market Research Brief](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-claude-skills/#skill-5) or [Competitor Research](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-claude-skills/#skill-6). * **If email and follow-through are the leak** — start with [Follow-Up Email](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-claude-skills/#skill-11) or [Customer Support Reply](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-claude-skills/#skill-13).
Want to build your own for a process that’s specific to you? See [how to create a Claude skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-claude-skill/) — about fifteen minutes, no code.
For a different starting point, compare the [best ChatGPT Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-chatgpt-skills/), [best Gemini Spark Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-gemini-spark-skills/), and [best AI Website Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-ai-website-skills/), or return to the cross-platform [best AI Skills for business owners](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-ai-skills/).
## Frequently Asked Questions
What are the best Claude skills for business owners?
The best Claude skills lean on what Claude does better than most tools: building finished documents and analyzing data. Start with the AI Client Proposal Skill if proposals stall your deals, the AI Spreadsheet Insights Skill if you export data you never read, and the AI Market Research Brief Skill before a launch. Add the rest as the need comes up.
What is a Claude skill vs. a prompt?
A prompt is a single request you retype. A Claude skill is the saved method behind it — a `SKILL.md` file containing instructions, context, and an output format that Claude can load when the task matches. Install it once, then reuse and improve the same workflow over time.
Do I need a paid Claude plan to use these skills?
No, to start. Every skill here includes a plain-text method that works as instructions in a Claude chat. Claude’s native Skills feature is available on supported Claude plans when the required capability is enabled; [Anthropic’s official Skills guide](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512176-what-are-skills) has the current details. For finished-file and multi-step work across local files, use Claude Cowork on an eligible paid plan and follow the [Claude Cowork setup guide](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/setup-guides/claude-cowork/).
Can Claude actually create Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files?
Yes. Claude can create and edit Word documents, Excel spreadsheets, PowerPoint decks, and PDFs, and it has built-in document skills for exactly that. It’s the main reason these skills lead with document and data work — the deliverable comes back as a real file, not just text in a chat.
Which Claude skill should I install first?
The one attached to the finished file you keep putting off. Proposals stalling deals? [Client Proposal](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/client-proposal/). Data you never read? [Spreadsheet Insights](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/spreadsheet-insights/). A launch coming up? [Market Research Brief](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/market-research-brief/). Use one for a full week before adding the next.
Do these skills work in Claude Cowork and Claude Desktop?
Yes. The skills work in Claude Chat, and their full multi-step versions run in Claude Cowork inside the Claude desktop app on Mac and Windows. Cowork is where Claude can combine a skill with your local files, connectors, and finished-file creation in a single task.
Can Claude work with my local files?
In Claude Cowork, yes — it can read and write inside folders you explicitly connect through Claude Desktop. Start with a dedicated test folder containing copies, not your originals, and keep approvals on for the first few runs.
Are these Claude skills free?
Yes. Every skill in this guide is free to copy and use from the [Claude skills library](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/claude/). The only paid element is Claude Cowork itself, if you want the finished-file and local-file features on top of the plain-text prompt version.
How is this different from the best ChatGPT or Gemini Spark skills?
Same catalog, different strength. The [best Gemini Spark skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-gemini-spark-skills/) lead with Google-Workspace-native work (Gmail, Calendar, Drive). The [best ChatGPT skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-chatgpt-skills/) lead with everyday repetition. This list leads with documents, data, and research — the work Claude does best. If you’re choosing between tools, see [Claude Desktop vs Gemini Spark](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/claude-desktop-vs-gemini-spark/).
Can I use the same skill in Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark?
Yes. These skills are portable plain-text methods, so the same one works across Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini Spark with small platform-specific tweaks. That makes it easy to test the same task in more than one tool and keep whichever gives you the better result.
**Editorial note:** Claude’s features, plans, and file capabilities change over time. Every skill above is free to copy; the finished-file and local-file features depend on Claude Cowork and an eligible paid plan. Verify each output before you send, publish, or act on it.

item.text: Gemini Spark Availability: Now Global (Countries & Plans) Is Gemini Spark available worldwide? Google now describes Spark as “available everywhere” and “available globally” in its latest Gemini Drop. The precise answer is that Gemini Spark is available wherever Gemini Apps are supported, with four current exceptions: the European Economic Area (EEA), Nigeria, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. Eligible users need Google AI Pro or Google AI Ultra; Ultra is no longer required solely for Spark access. You must also be 18 or older, use a personal Google Account and have Keep Activity turned on. Google still calls Spark experimental, and access can roll out unevenly to otherwise eligible accounts. Updated August 8, 2026: This guide reflects Google’s new global wording and the more specific country, plan and account rules in the current Gemini Spark Help Center. Gemini Spark availability status Now global on Google AI Pro and Ultra Latest update: checked August 8, 2026. Google’s newest Gemini Drop says Spark is now available globally. Google’s feature-specific Help Center clarifies that this means wherever Gemini Apps are supported except the EEA, Nigeria, Switzerland and the UK. You still need an eligible personal account on Google AI Pro or Ultra, must be 18 or older and must have Keep Activity on. See countries & requirements ↓ Gemini Spark is accessed inside Gemini on eligible accounts; it is not a separate standalone service. Is Gemini Spark Available Worldwide? Yes, with four important exceptions. Google’s latest Gemini Drop calls Spark “available everywhere” and “now available globally.” Google’s current Help Center supplies the operational definition: Spark is available wherever Gemini Apps are supported except the European Economic Area, Nigeria, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. Both Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra qualify in supported locations. The word “global” does not mean that every country, account type or user is eligible: work and school accounts are not included in the current consumer rollout, users must be at least 18, and Keep Activity must be enabled. Review the full Gemini Spark requirements before subscribing or changing plans. Does Google AI Pro Include Gemini Spark? Yes. Google’s current feature requirements list Google AI Pro or Google AI Ultra, without a separate country rule for Pro. Pro access began in the United States on July 16, 2026, reached India on July 29, and expanded to more than 160 additional countries on July 30. Taken together, the global announcement and current requirements make Pro the lower-cost eligible plan wherever Spark itself is supported. Gemini Spark Supported Countries: Availability Chart Google now markets Gemini Spark as globally available. For country-level decisions, use the narrower language in Google’s feature-specific Help Center: Spark is available wherever Gemini Apps are supported except the European Economic Area, Nigeria, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. Both Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra qualify in supported locations. Country or regionGemini Spark statusEligible planWhat to know United States Available Google AI Pro or Ultra Pro access began July 16, 2026 India Available Google AI Pro or Ultra Pro access began July 29, 2026 Other supported Gemini Apps countries (including Australia, Canada, Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea and Malaysia) Available Google AI Pro or Ultra Pro expanded to 160+ additional countries on July 30, 2026 European Economic Area (EEA) Not currently available None Still excluded from the global rollout Nigeria Not currently available None Still excluded from the global rollout Switzerland Not currently available None Still excluded from the global rollout United Kingdom Not currently available None Still excluded from the global rollout Last checked: August 8, 2026, using Google’s live Gemini Drops hub, current Gemini Spark Help Center and July 30 expansion post. Google has not published launch dates for the four locations that remain excluded. What still varies by plan: Spark country eligibility is now the same for Pro and Ultra, but Ultra offers higher usage limits and costs more. Google’s current Spark requirements page no longer lists the earlier plan-specific language distinction. Confirm your own account because feature rollouts and plan benefits can still change. Gemini Spark Pro vs Ultra Availability PlanCurrent Gemini Spark accessMain difference Free Not included A paid eligible plan is required Google AI Pro Available to eligible users in supported locations Lowest-cost eligible Spark plan; lower usage limits than Ultra Google AI Ultra Available to eligible users in supported locations Higher Spark usage limits at a higher price This table reflects Google’s latest global announcement and current feature requirements, checked August 8, 2026. Google can still change plan eligibility, usage limits and country support at any time. Use the requirements and dated update history on this page to confirm the latest position. A qualifying subscription is only one requirement. You must also meet Google’s country, account, age, activity and platform rules below. What Are the Requirements for Gemini Spark? According to the official Gemini Apps Help Center, checked August 8, 2026, you currently need all of the following to use Gemini Spark: You must be at least 18 years old. You must be in a country where Gemini Spark is supported (see the excluded-country list above). You must sign in with a personal Google Account. Your personal account must have a qualifying plan: Google AI Pro or Google AI Ultra. Keep Activity must be turned on. Google’s current requirements page does not list a separate Spark language restriction for Google AI Pro or Ultra. App and feature availability can still vary by account and rollout. You must access it through the Gemini web app, Gemini mobile app, or Gemini app for macOS. 1. Your country must be supported Google’s current Gemini Help Center lists Spark as available wherever Gemini Apps are supported, except for a specific set of excluded locations. A Google AI Ultra membership may be available in your country while Spark itself is not. This distinction is important. The subscription and the individual feature have different availability rules. See the current excluded-country list in the Gemini Spark supported countries section above. 2. You need a personal Google Account The current consumer version of Gemini Spark requires a personal Google Account that you manage yourself. A work, school or supervised account may have different Gemini features, but it does not meet the account requirement Google currently lists for Gemini Spark. 3. You need Google AI Pro or Google AI Ultra Gemini Spark is not included with the free Gemini plan. You need a paid subscription on the same personal Google Account you use to open Gemini — either Google AI Pro or Google AI Ultra. Pro began in the US and India, expanded to more than 160 additional countries on July 30, 2026, and is now part of Google’s global Spark availability framing. 4. You must be 18 or older Google currently limits Gemini Spark to users age 18 and older. A supervised account or an account belonging to someone under 18 is not eligible. 5. Keep Activity must be on Gemini Spark requires the Gemini Apps Keep Activity setting to be enabled. If you otherwise qualify but do not see Spark, check this setting before assuming your account is not eligible. 6. Use a supported Gemini app Google currently lists Spark in the Gemini mobile app, the Gemini app on Mac and the Gemini web app at gemini.google.com. Its current feature requirements no longer list the earlier Pro-versus-Ultra language rule. If Spark is missing in one app, update it and check the web app with the same eligible account. How much does Gemini Spark cost? Gemini Spark does not have a separate standalone price. Access is bundled with an eligible paid plan in supported locations. Google AI Pro is now the lower-cost route into Spark; Google AI Ultra provides higher usage limits. Google AI planCurrent US monthly priceGemini Spark access Google AI Free $0 No Google AI Pro $19.99 Yes, for eligible users in supported locations Google AI Ultra 5x $99.99 Yes, with higher usage limits than Pro Google AI Ultra 20x $199.99 Yes, with the highest listed usage limits These are current US prices, checked August 8, 2026; local pricing and plan availability vary. Pricing and plan benefits can change, so check the official Google AI subscription page before subscribing. Gemini Spark Availability in Key Countries The country availability chart above is the quickest reference for current access. Google now calls Spark globally available, but its feature Help Center still excludes the EEA, Nigeria, Switzerland and the UK. Is Gemini Spark available in India? Yes. India joined the supported locations during the July 2026 expansion, and Google added Google AI Pro access there on July 29, 2026 — one day before the same Pro access rolled out to 160+ other countries at once. Eligible users in India need a personal Google Account with Google AI Pro or Ultra, must be at least 18 and must have Keep Activity turned on. Is Gemini Spark on Google AI Pro available outside the US and India? Yes. Google’s latest Gemini Drop says Spark is now available globally, and the current Help Center lists Google AI Pro or Ultra as eligible plans. Country-level access covers wherever Gemini Apps are supported except the European Economic Area, Nigeria, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. Is Gemini Spark available in Canada or the United Kingdom? Gemini Spark is available in Canada for eligible Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra users. It is not currently available in the United Kingdom, regardless of plan. Is Gemini Spark available in Australia or Japan? Australia and Japan are supported for eligible Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra users. Hong Kong and South Korea are also included in Spark’s current supported-country footprint. When will Gemini Spark be available in excluded countries? Google has not announced launch dates for the European Economic Area, Nigeria, Switzerland or the United Kingdom. The new “available globally” Gemini Drop does not remove those exceptions from Google’s more specific Help Center. This guide will be updated when Google changes country, plan or account eligibility. How to Check Whether You Have Access The fastest way to check Gemini Spark availability for your account is to look for the Spark mode while signed in to the exact personal Google Account that owns your eligible plan. Sign in to the personal Google Account on your Spark-eligible plan — Google AI Pro or Google AI Ultra. Update the Gemini mobile or Mac app, or open the latest version of a supported browser and go to gemini.google.com. Open the Gemini menu or sidebar. Look for the Spark tab or select Change mode. Select Switch to Spark. If Spark opens, go to the Tasks area to create or review a Spark task. The exact navigation can look slightly different on the web, Android, iPhone and Mac. Spark should appear inside Gemini rather than as a separate standalone application. If you do not see it, compare your account against the troubleshooting checklist below. For a full walkthrough after you get access, see the How to Use Gemini Spark: Complete Guide. Why Gemini Spark Is Not Showing If Gemini Spark is not showing, check each requirement individually. Start by confirming that Gemini is signed into the exact personal Google Account that owns your Spark-eligible plan — Google AI Ultra or Google AI Pro. The rollout has not reached your account Google describes Pro access as a rollout. Two people with the same plan and country may not receive a new feature at the same time. If every requirement below is satisfied, check again later rather than changing subscriptions immediately. Check that you are using the correct Google Account Many people have several personal, work and school Google accounts. Confirm that the account currently active in Gemini is the exact personal account that owns the qualifying Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription. Confirm your plan qualifies Spark needs a paid plan. Google’s current requirements list either Google AI Pro or Google AI Ultra in supported locations. Neither plan currently qualifies in the European Economic Area, Nigeria, Switzerland or the United Kingdom. Confirm which plan is active on the personal account you are using. Confirm your country is supported Google’s latest Gemini Drop says Spark is now global, but the current Gemini Help Center still lists the European Economic Area, Nigeria, Switzerland and the United Kingdom as excluded locations. Having Google AI Pro or Ultra does not provide Spark access if your location is on that list. If you last checked before the global update, try again from the same eligible personal account. Turn on Keep Activity Open your Gemini activity settings and confirm that Keep Activity is enabled. Spark depends on this setting for its tasks and workflows. Update the app or browser Install the latest Gemini app update, update your browser, close and reopen Gemini, or sign out and back in. Check the web version at gemini.google.com to determine whether the issue is limited to your mobile or Mac app. Check Workspace or managed-account restrictions Google’s current consumer requirements exclude work and school accounts. A Workspace administrator cannot make that account eligible simply by enabling other Gemini features. Use the eligible personal account associated with your qualifying plan. Confirm your age and account eligibility You must be at least 18 years old. Supervised accounts and accounts that do not meet Google’s age or personal-account requirements will not show Spark. What to Do After Getting Access Once Spark appears, start with one small, reviewable workflow before creating complex schedules. These guides will take you from first access to a reusable setup: Install one of the best Gemini Spark skills for a practical first result. Follow the beginner walkthrough for how to use Gemini Spark. Explore Gemini Spark skill examples and business use cases. Learn how to create a Gemini Spark skill for your own workflow. Browse Gemini Spark skills in the free skills hub. Can you use Gemini Spark with a work or school account? Not through the current consumer eligibility path described in Google’s Gemini Apps Help Center. Google currently requires users to sign in with a personal Google Account on Google AI Ultra or Google AI Pro. A Google Workspace, school or employer-managed account does not meet that stated requirement. Google has not announced consumer Spark access for work or school accounts. Do not assume that a business Gemini subscription includes the same Spark access as an eligible personal Google AI account. What devices support Gemini Spark? Gemini Spark is currently available through: The Gemini web app at gemini.google.com The Gemini mobile app on supported Android devices The Gemini mobile app on supported iPhone and iPad devices The Gemini app for Mac where Gemini Spark is available The macOS version allows Gemini Spark to complete tasks across your desktop files and apps. For example, it can organize files into folders or use invoices saved on your computer to create and regularly update a spreadsheet in Google Workspace. Spark only has access to the files you give it permission to use. Can I use Gemini Spark on Mac? Yes. Eligible users can access Gemini Spark through the Gemini app for Mac where Spark is available. On Mac, Spark can help automate tasks involving permitted desktop files, folders, apps and Google Workspace. If Spark is set up on your Mac, you can also ask Gemini from another device to take action on that Mac. For step-by-step installation, folder permissions and local-file examples, see the Gemini Spark on Mac setup guide. Eligible cloud-based Spark tasks can continue running in the background after you leave Gemini. Local Mac tasks are different: if Spark needs to act on files stored on your computer, keep your Mac on, awake, and connected while that task runs. Does Gemini Spark have usage limits? Yes. Gemini Apps use compute-based limits, and the amount of usage consumed by Spark depends on the number and complexity of your requests. Long, multi-step tasks may use more of your allowance than a simple request. Gemini should notify you when you are approaching a limit. The 5x and 20x Ultra plans offer different usage levels, which is one reason their monthly prices differ. Google also caps how many Spark tasks can run at once: you can have up to 15 tasks running at a given time, and a schedule will not start a new task while 15 are already running. Spark otherwise draws on the same compute-based usage limits as the rest of Gemini. What can you do if Gemini Spark is not available to you? You do not need to wait to start learning the workflow skills behind Gemini Spark. You can already practice how to: Turn a repeated task into a clear workflow Write reusable AI instructions Define the information an agent needs Create consistent output formats Design tasks that include human review Build reusable skills for business and productivity Plan schedules and conditions for ongoing work You can practice these concepts with Gemini, Gemini Gems, Claude, ChatGPT and the free AI agent generator while you wait for Spark access. Gemini Spark availability update history The dated product changes below follow Google’s latest Gemini Drops hub, Google’s official Gemini Spark update history, the Gemini Spark Help Center requirements, and Google’s July 29, 2026 India availability announcement; the latest verification records when this guide was checked against Google’s live requirements. August 8, 2026: Google’s current Gemini Drops hub now describes Gemini Spark as “available everywhere” and “now available globally.” Google’s feature-specific Help Center continues to define that availability as everywhere Gemini Apps are supported except the EEA, Nigeria, Switzerland and the UK. The Help Center lists Google AI Pro or Ultra and no longer shows the earlier plan-specific Spark language rule. August 7, 2026: Availability, plan, country and language requirements rechecked against Google’s Gemini Spark Help Center and official update history. No changes since the July 30 expansion. July 30, 2026: Google expanded Google AI Pro access to Gemini Spark to over 160 additional countries in a single rollout, alongside a new Chrome auto-browse capability (initially US-only). Pro and Ultra now have essentially the same country footprint — both exclude only the EEA, Nigeria, Switzerland and the UK. Google’s Help Center no longer distinguishes Pro from Ultra by country. Verified against Google’s official July 2026 Spark update post and independent press. July 29, 2026: Google announced that Gemini Spark expanded to Google AI Pro subscribers in India. July 25, 2026: Availability, plan, language and country requirements rechecked against Google’s current Gemini Spark Help page and official update history. July 16, 2026: Google began rolling out Gemini Spark in English to Google AI Pro subscribers in the United States, ending the Ultra-only requirement in the US.
