It spans ChatGPT, Claude, prompt engineering, custom GPTs, AI writing, image, voice and video tools, and automation with Zapier and Make. Breadth is the product here, and it is genuinely useful breadth. It also illustrates the honest limitation of the whole marketplace category. Udemy lists over 1,800 ChatGPT courses to more than 5.5 million learners at a 4.4 average rating — an enormous, well-reviewed catalogue that has almost entirely not caught up with Skills. LinkedIn Learning is the subscription alternative with the same trade-off: short, polished, LinkedIn-shareable certificates, and the same gap on SKILL.md. ChatGPT and Claude for content, research and productivity Prompt engineering across a wide range of tools Building custom GPTs and AI assistants AI writing, image, voice and video tools Automation with Zapier, Make and the OpenAI API Exceptional breadth for a frequently discounted price Bestseller status with a very large, satisfied student base Updated regularly — last refreshed July 2026 Lifetime access, certificate, and a 30-day refund window Covers many tools, so no single one in real depth Tool-led rather than business-outcome-led Little to nothing on ChatGPT Skills or SKILL.md Udemy list prices fluctuate wildly — never pay full price Verdict: Buy it on sale for a broad tour of the AI tool landscape. Do not expect it to teach you Skills — for that, pair it with OpenAI’s Using Skills guide or the ChatGPT Academy. View the Udemy course → Best ChatGPT course for each type of learner Best free ChatGPT course OpenAI Academy — AI Foundations. Free, official, updated as the products change, and it issues a free course-completion certificate. Nothing else on this list matches it for accuracy on how ChatGPT itself behaves. Its limit is scope rather than quality: it teaches AI at work, not the reusable Skills you would build with it. For that, read the free Using Skills guide immediately afterwards. Best ChatGPT course for beginners AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy, or AI Foundations if you want free. Beginners rarely fail because a concept was too hard — they fail because nobody was there when setup broke. The Academy covers workspace setup, your first installed Skill and a shipped deliverable in one ~3-hour path, with human support attached. If you would rather self-serve at zero cost, AI Foundations is the best free equivalent. Best ChatGPT Skills course for business AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy. Business owners do not need to understand agents — they need last week’s reporting done without them. This is the only option here organised by business outcome rather than product feature, and the only one that hands you ready-made ChatGPT Skills you can install the same day. OpenAI’s small business program is the best free companion to it. Best ChatGPT workflow course OpenAI Academy — Applied AI Foundations. It is built around exactly the move most people miss: taking a task you already repeat and turning it into a defined workflow with inputs, checkpoints and human review. Agents and Workflows is the natural sequel once the workflow exists and you want it supervised rather than driven. Best ChatGPT prompt engineering course DeepLearning.AI if you are technical; Vanderbilt if you are not. DeepLearning.AI is more rigorous and far shorter, but it assumes basic Python. Vanderbilt is longer and needs no code, and its prompt-pattern framing is the closest thing in traditional prompting to the reusable thinking behind Skills. Best ChatGPT course with a certificate OpenAI Academy for a free one; Vanderbilt for a paid, university-backed one. All three OpenAI Academy courses issue a free completion certificate you can share — but OpenAI is explicit that a course-completion certificate is not a formal OpenAI certification, so do not describe it as one on your CV. The ChatGPT Academy and Udemy both issue a certificate of completion too. Be honest with yourself about which kind you actually need: if it is for a CV or a client, the university name is what carries weight; if it is for your own sense of having finished, any of them will do. Best ChatGPT course for non-coders OpenAI Academy, then the ChatGPT Academy. Neither needs a line of code. Deliberately avoid starting with DeepLearning.AI — it is excellent, but its Python examples will convince a non-technical learner that ChatGPT Skills are harder than they are. They are Markdown files. You can write one in a text editor. Which ChatGPT course should you take first? Nine recommendations is not a plan. Find your starting point below and follow the arrows — each step assumes the one before it, and every path ends in something running rather than something finished. If you have never really used ChatGPT AI Foundations → Applied AI Foundations → ChatGPT Academy → install your first Skill → automate one recurring job. Two free official courses to get fluent, then applied training to turn that fluency into workflows. Do not buy anything until you have finished the free two — you will make a much better decision about paid training afterwards. If you already use ChatGPT most days OpenAI’s Using Skills guide → Applied AI Foundations → build your first Skill → Agents and Workflows. Skip the fundamentals; you already have them. Your gap is not prompting — it is that nothing you do on Monday carries over to the following Monday. Start at the Skills guide. If you run a business and want a result this month Install one free Skill → ChatGPT Academy → OpenAI’s small business sessions for fresh use cases. Start with a working result, not a curriculum. One Skill running on real work will tell you more about whether this is worth your time than any course description will. If you need a credential OpenAI Academy for the free certificate → Vanderbilt for the paid, university-backed one. Take the free one first. It costs nothing, carries OpenAI’s name, and may well be all anyone asks to see. Whichever path you are on, the wider progression it sits inside is the ChatGPT learning path below — that one is about the skills you build, not the courses you take. Build real ChatGPT Skills while you learn Here is the thing almost no course tells you: a finished course is worth nothing; a finished Skill runs forever. So do not watch a course and then wonder what to do. Build one Skill a week while you learn, on work you already do. Each week below pairs a real business job with a free Skill from our library. Install it, run it on your own work, then open the SKILL.md and change one thing to fit how you do the job. That single edit teaches more than an hour of video. WeekBuild thisStart from this free SkillWhat you learn 1 An email Skill AI Follow-Up Email Generator The anatomy of a SKILL.md — inputs, steps, output format — on the lowest-risk job you have. 2 A meeting notes Skill AI Meeting Notes Enforcing a fixed output structure — decisions, owners, actions — so every run looks the same. 3 A research brief Skill Market Research Brief Source handling and citation discipline — where review steps genuinely matter. 4 A content planner Skill Weekly Content Plan Encoding voice and standards, so output sounds like you without you re-explaining it. 5 A recurring business brief Weekly Business Brief Chaining Skills and putting one on a schedule — the point where it starts running without you. Every one of those is free to download from the ChatGPT Skills library. If you would rather have the whole set plus the training that goes with them, that is what the ChatGPT Academy is. What should you learn first? The ChatGPT learning path Courses teach concepts; this is the order that actually gets you to a working system. Most people who give up jumped straight from step 2 to step 6. Learn ChatGPT basics. What it is good at, what it invents, and how to review it. AI Foundations is the best free hour here. Get good at prompting. Clear instructions, real context, examples. Vanderbilt’s prompt patterns or DeepLearning.AI, depending on how technical you are. Learn what a Skill is. The concept, the SKILL.md file, and how it differs from a Project or a custom GPT. Start with what an AI Skill is and Skills vs Projects vs GPTs. Install your first Skill. Do not write one yet — run someone else’s on your own work first. How to use ChatGPT Skills walks through it, and the free library gives you something to install. Build a reusable Skill of your own. Take one job you repeat weekly and write it down properly. How to create a ChatGPT Skill is the walkthrough; Applied AI Foundations is the free course that teaches the thinking. Connect your tools. Point ChatGPT at the systems the work already lives in, so it stops depending on you pasting things in. Automate the recurring work. Put a Skill on a schedule and add a review step you actually trust. Agents and Workflows covers the supervision half. Turn it into business workflows. Stack Skills into the jobs that eat your week — reporting, inbox, proposals, client updates. That is what the ChatGPT Academy and All Access are built around. Learning ChatGPT alongside other tools? AI Skills Fundamentals teaches the cross-platform skill format first, so what you learn carries over to Claude and Gemini instead of stopping at ChatGPT’s edge. Common mistakes beginners make with ChatGPT Skills These five come up again and again — and every one of them is a course-selection problem as much as a skill problem. Taking three beginner courses in a row. The second foundation course mostly repeats the first. If you have finished one, the next step is applied, not another overview. Diminishing returns start faster than people expect. Learning prompting and stopping there. This is the expensive one. A great prompt evaporates when you close the tab; a Skill is still there next Tuesday. If a course never mentions SKILL.md, it is teaching you half the job. Building one enormous Skill. OpenAI’s own guidance is that Skills work best as small building blocks you mix and match, and complex workflows should be split into smaller Skills. A single monster Skill is impossible to debug when it drifts. Buying a course before checking access. Skills are not on every ChatGPT plan. Read ChatGPT Skills availability before you spend money on training that assumes a workspace you do not have. Never reviewing the output. ChatGPT is confident whether or not it is correct. Build the review step into the Skill itself — a final-checks section — especially for anything touching numbers, clients or money. Free vs paid ChatGPT courses: which should you choose? You do not need to spend money to learn ChatGPT Skills. For most people the smartest path is to start free, prove the value on one real task, and only then pay for depth or support. Start free if you are unsure or budget-conscious. OpenAI Academy plus the Using Skills guide will take you from zero to your first working Skill at no cost. Start with the ChatGPT Academy if you want the fastest route from “I just opened ChatGPT” to “this runs in my business every week.” Free for 7 days, and it pairs the lessons with 25+ ready-to-install Skills and real human help when you get stuck. Pay for a certificate if a credential genuinely changes something for you — a job application, a client, a training budget. Vanderbilt is the strongest name here. Pay for breadth if you want a tour of the wider AI tool landscape rather than depth on ChatGPT (Udemy, on sale). Do not pay for another prompting course once you have taken one. The next useful thing you buy should teach Skills, workflows or support — not prompting again. ChatGPT Skills courses — FAQs What’s the best free ChatGPT course for beginners? The best free ChatGPT course for beginners is OpenAI Academy’s AI Foundations — it’s official, self-paced, includes a free completion certificate, and is designed for people starting from zero. Take it first, then move to Applied AI Foundations for repeatable workflows. If you want structured lessons that end in installed Skills rather than notes, pair it with our ChatGPT Training for Beginners path. How long does it take to complete a ChatGPT course? Most focused beginner courses take between 90 minutes and a weekend. The AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy runs about 3 hours across six modules, DeepLearning.AI’s prompt-engineering short course is 1h 40m, and OpenAI Academy’s free foundations are self-paced (typically one to two evenings each). Longer certificate courses like Vanderbilt’s Coursera path are a ~19-hour commitment across six modules. Do ChatGPT courses cover Skills, Projects, and workflows? Only some do. As of August 2026, OpenAI’s free Using Skills guide and the AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy are the two on this list that treat Skills as a first-class topic alongside Projects and workflows. Most legacy prompt-engineering courses predate Skills and don’t mention SKILL.md at all — check the syllabus for the words “Skill” and “workflow” before you enrol. Are there ChatGPT courses that come with downloadable skill files? Yes. The AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy ships with 25+ ready-to-install ChatGPT Skills, and the AI Agents Library All Access Pass unlocks the full library across ChatGPT, Claude Cowork and Gemini Spark. Free copy-paste versions of many workflows are also available in the free ChatGPT Skills library — install one before you finish the course and you already have working leverage. Do I need a paid ChatGPT plan for these courses? The lessons themselves can be studied on any ChatGPT plan, including free. The free copy-paste versions can be adapted for many free AI chat plans. Native Skill installation, Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark, connected tools and advanced automation features may require an eligible paid plan. Confirm plan-eligibility in ChatGPT Skills availability before you buy training that assumes access you may not have. How is a ChatGPT course different from ChatGPT Skills? A ChatGPT course teaches you how to use ChatGPT well; a ChatGPT Skill is a reusable SKILL.md file you install into ChatGPT so it does one specific job the same way every time. Courses build knowledge; Skills build leverage. The best training combines the two — you leave with the principles and with installed workflows already running. Our ChatGPT Training for Beginners path is built around that combination. What is the best ChatGPT Skills course? For most beginners and business owners, the best ChatGPT Skills course is the AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy, because it combines six beginner modules with 25+ ready-to-install Skills and real human support — so you finish with working workflows rather than notes. If you want the official fundamentals for free, OpenAI Academy’s AI Foundations is the best free starting course, and OpenAI’s free Using Skills guide is the best free training on Skills specifically. Explore the ChatGPT Academy → Is there a free ChatGPT course? Yes, several. OpenAI Academy offers three free official courses — AI Foundations, Applied AI Foundations, and Agents and Workflows — each with a free completion certificate. OpenAI’s Using Skills guide is free, DeepLearning.AI’s prompt engineering short course is free, and Vanderbilt’s Coursera course is free to audit. The ChatGPT Academy is also free for your first 7 days. Does OpenAI have an official ChatGPT course? Yes. OpenAI Academy is OpenAI’s own free learning platform and currently publishes three public courses: AI Foundations for people new to AI, Applied AI Foundations for turning prompts into repeatable workflows, and Agents and Workflows for directing agent-assisted work. Each issues a free course-completion certificate. OpenAI also runs live sessions, including short Skill Labs, with replays posted afterwards. What is a ChatGPT Skill, and why does it need its own course? OpenAI defines a skill as a reusable, shareable workflow that tells ChatGPT how to do a specific task — you define the process once, in a plain-text SKILL.md file, and it is applied reliably whenever that task comes up. It needs separate teaching because prompting and Skill design are different disciplines: prompting is about one good result now, Skills are about the same good result every time. Most ChatGPT courses were written before Skills existed and only teach the first. See what an AI Skill is for the full explanation. Do I need to know how to code to learn ChatGPT Skills? No. A SKILL.md file is written in Markdown — plain text with a few symbols like # for headings and - for lists. You can write one in any text editor, and you can ask ChatGPT to draft the first version for you. Every course in this guide except DeepLearning.AI’s, which assumes basic Python, is fully no-code. How long does it take to learn ChatGPT Skills? About 15 minutes to understand what a Skill is, an hour or two to install one and run it on real work, and roughly a weekend to finish a structured beginner path — the ChatGPT Academy runs about three hours across six modules. Becoming genuinely fluent takes two to three weeks of using Skills on real jobs. The gap between “I finished a course” and “this saves me time” is almost always step 5 of the learning path — building one Skill for a job you genuinely repeat. Which ChatGPT course teaches reusable Skills? Very few, which is the main finding of this guide. OpenAI’s free Using Skills guide is the authoritative explainer, and Applied AI Foundations teaches the workflow thinking behind Skills. For building and installing them against your own work, the ChatGPT Academy is the applied option — you finish with working Skills rather than an understanding of Skills. You can also install proven ones straight from the free ChatGPT Skills library. Are paid ChatGPT courses worth it? Sometimes — but start free. OpenAI Academy and the Using Skills guide will teach you the fundamentals at no cost. A paid course earns its money when you want structure, business-specific examples, a recognised certificate, or a human to ask when you get stuck. For most business owners, support and ready-made Skills deliver more than another set of videos. What is rarely worth paying for is a second prompting course. Do ChatGPT courses include a certificate? Many do. All three OpenAI Academy courses issue a free course-completion certificate, and the AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy issues a certificate of completion. Vanderbilt’s Coursera course offers a paid, shareable certificate; Udemy issues a certificate of completion; DeepLearning.AI’s certificate requires a paid membership tier. Note the distinction OpenAI itself draws: a course-completion certificate is not a formal OpenAI certification. Certificate terms change, so confirm on the provider’s enrolment page before you sign up. Can I learn ChatGPT Skills without a Business or Enterprise plan? You can learn the concepts on any plan — OpenAI’s Using Skills guide, the Academy courses and articles like how to create a ChatGPT Skill all cost nothing and assume nothing. Installing Skills into a workspace is a different matter and depends on your plan tier. Check ChatGPT Skills availability before buying training that assumes access you may not have. Is ChatGPT training good for business owners? It is arguably better suited to business owners than to developers. The recurring, low-judgement work that eats an owner’s week — weekly reporting, inbox triage, proposal drafts, client updates, content planning — is exactly what Skills handle well, and none of it needs code. The catch is that it rewards people who commit to one workflow rather than experimenting broadly. OpenAI’s free small business program is a good place to see what that looks like in practice. Which course should I take after OpenAI Academy? OpenAI teaches you the product; the natural next step teaches you what to build with it. For business workflows, reusable Skills and scheduled work, the ChatGPT Academy picks up roughly where the free curriculum stops. If you want prompting depth instead, take Vanderbilt or DeepLearning.AI. Do not take two foundation courses back to back — the second will mostly repeat the first. Is there a ChatGPT certification? Not in the sense most people mean. OpenAI Academy issues free course-completion certificates, and OpenAI has been explicit that those are not a formal OpenAI certification. Third-party certificates from Coursera, Udemy and LinkedIn Learning are certificates of completion from those platforms, not from OpenAI. If a credential matters for a job or a client, Vanderbilt’s Coursera certificate carries the most recognisable name. If capability matters more than the credential, a Skill running in your business proves more than any of them. What about courses for Claude or Gemini? The same logic applies — look for training that ends in something reusable. We compare the equivalent Claude options in the best Claude Cowork courses. If you use more than one tool, AI Skills Fundamentals teaches the cross-platform skill format first, so what you learn is not stranded on one platform. Read the walkthrough → The Best ChatGPT Skills The Skills worth installing first, ranked by the business job they finish. The 9 Best ChatGPT Skill Courses for Beginners (2026)

This guide compares the 9 best ChatGPT Skills courses and training resources in 2026 — free and paid. Every pick lists who it is best for, the format and price, what you will actually learn, honest pros and limitations, and a clear verdict — so you can pick training that matches your goal, your budget, and how much time you have.

Last updated August 2026. All course info verified against current provider offerings.

Why “Skills courses” and not just “ChatGPT courses”? Because the gap for most people is no longer prompting. A ChatGPT Skill is a reusable, shareable workflow — a plain-text SKILL.md file that tells ChatGPT how to do one job the same way every time. A course that only teaches prompting leaves you re-explaining yourself forever. A course that teaches Skills leaves you with something that keeps working after the course ends. That distinction is the yardstick used to rank everything below.

Quick answer

The 9 best ChatGPT Skills courses in 2026

The best ChatGPT Skills course depends on whether you want practical business workflows, prompt engineering, official training, or reusable Skills you can install the same day. Best guided option — AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy (6 beginner modules, 25+ ready-to-install Skills, real human support, free for 7 days); best free official first course — OpenAI Academy’s AI Foundations (free, with a completion certificate); best free course for repeatable workflows — Applied AI Foundations; best free training on Skills specifically — OpenAI’s Using Skills guide and live Skill Labs; best university certificate — Vanderbilt’s Prompt Engineering for ChatGPT on Coursera.

Beginners often benefit most from structured learning that includes real projects rather than only videos. If you take one free course and build one real Skill from it, you are ahead of almost everyone who finished five.

Who this guide is for

Business owners, professionals, marketers and complete beginners who want to learn ChatGPT Skills through structured training rather than piecing it together from scattered videos. If you would rather skip the training and just install something that works today, browse the free ChatGPT Skills library instead. And if you are not yet sure whether your plan can install Skills at all, start with ChatGPT Skills availability before you spend anything.

Best ChatGPT Skills courses by goal

The one-line version. The reasoning behind each pick is in the decision table below.

Your goalBest choice
Business ownerAI Agents Library — ChatGPT Academy
Complete beginnerOpenAI Academy — AI Foundations

Which ChatGPT course should you choose?

If you only read one section, read this one. Match what you want on the left to the training on the right.

If you want…Take…Why
Business workflowsAI Agents Library — ChatGPT AcademyOrganised by business job — email, research, reporting — not by product feature, and you leave with installed Skills.
To learn official ChatGPTOpenAI Academy — AI FoundationsFree, from OpenAI, and updated as the products change. The most reliable account of how ChatGPT is meant to be used.
Reusable Skills specificallyOpenAI — Using Skills + Skill LabsThe only free, official training aimed squarely at SKILL.md and reusable workflows.
A certificationVanderbilt on CourseraA university-backed, shareable certificate. OpenAI Academy’s certificate is free but is a completion certificate, not a formal certification.
Prompt engineeringDeepLearning.AITaught by OpenAI’s Isa Fulford and Andrew Ng. Free, and the most rigorous prompting course on this list.
Live training as a small businessOpenAI — ChatGPT for small businessFree webinars and in-person sessions built around small-business use cases, not enterprise rollouts.
A general introductionUdemy — The Complete AI GuideCheap on sale, very broad, lifetime access. Good for tool literacy, weak on Skills.
To direct agentsOpenAI Academy — Agents and WorkflowsThe only free course here about supervising agent-assisted work rather than prompting it.
The fastest useful startThe Using Skills guideA single free article, readable in about 15 minutes, that ends with you building a Skill.

The short version: start free with OpenAI to learn the product, then take applied training to learn what to actually build with it. Those are two different skills, and almost everyone who stalls has only done the first.

How we chose these ChatGPT Skills courses

We prioritised training that teaches ChatGPT as it works today, suits non-technical learners, and leads to something reusable rather than a certificate alone. Each provider’s published curriculum, format, price, certificate terms and update history was reviewed; where we did not complete a full course, the assessment is based on published materials. Ratings, prices and durations change — confirm current details on the provider’s page before enrolling. Reader note: the ChatGPT Academy is our own membership. It is included because it fits this guide’s intent and is judged on the same criteria as everything else: beginner accessibility, practical application, structure, support, price, and update frequency.

What a ChatGPT Skills course actually needs to cover

Most “ChatGPT courses” were written for a product that no longer exists. They teach prompting into a blank chat box. ChatGPT now runs reusable Skills, holds context in Projects, connects to your real tools, and runs work on a schedule — and those are the parts that actually save time.

A course worth your hours should cover all seven of these:

  • Prompting fundamentals. Clear instructions, useful context, and reviewing what comes back. Everything else sits on top of this.
  • What a Skill is. OpenAI defines a skill as a reusable, shareable workflow that tells ChatGPT how to do a specific task — defined once, applied reliably every time it comes up.
  • The SKILL.md file. The plain-text playbook itself: what the skill does, required inputs, step-by-step instructions, required output format, and the final checks. It is Markdown and portable, which is why a Skill you write today survives tool changes.
  • Projects and standing context. The difference between a Skill, a Project and a custom GPT, and when each one is the right container. If a course blurs those three, it will teach you to build the wrong thing. Our ChatGPT Skills vs Projects vs GPTs guide covers the split.
  • Installing and sharing. Where Skills live, how to install one, and how workspace sharing changes who sees what. Step-by-step in how to use ChatGPT Skills.
  • Scheduled and recurring work. Getting a workflow to run without you present. This is where ChatGPT stops being an assistant and starts being leverage.
  • Review habits. Output checks, source verification, and knowing where human judgement is non-negotiable. ChatGPT is confident whether or not it is right.

The gap worth knowing about

Almost every course on this list — including excellent ones — was built around prompting, because Skills only reached most workspaces in 2026. OpenAI’s own free courses now cover repeatable workflows properly, and OpenAI publishes a dedicated Skills guide, but the large video marketplaces have not caught up: Udemy alone lists more than 1,800 ChatGPT courses, and vanishingly few of them mention SKILL.md at all. That is not a reason to avoid them — it is the reason most people need a second, applied step after their first course. See the learning roadmap.

Before you enrol: Skills are not on every ChatGPT plan. Check ChatGPT Skills availability first so you are not paying for a course teaching a feature your workspace cannot install.

9 Udemy — The Complete AI Guide Broad tool literacy on a budget All levels Long-form video Paid; sale price varies Yes

The 9 best ChatGPT Skills courses and training resources

Best for: Beginners, business owners and non-technical professionals who do not want to watch a course — they want ChatGPT actually running in their business, with real human help when setup breaks.

Most ChatGPT courses hand you videos and leave you alone. The ChatGPT Academy is built the other way round: six beginner modules, about three hours total, each one a practical build rather than a lecture. You choose the right workspace, install a real SKILL.md, connect a Skill to a recurring business job, put it on a schedule, then ship one finished deliverable in the last module. 25+ ready-to-install Skills are included, so you are adapting proven workflows instead of writing from a blank page. As of August 2026, the AI Agents Library All Access Pass includes 5 platform training paths and 150+ AI skills across ChatGPT, Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark and Gemini Notebook.

What you’ll learn

  • Choosing the right ChatGPT workspace — chat, Projects, shared workspaces and the editor — and why that choice changes what you can build later
  • Implementing a Skill in ChatGPT: where the Skills area lives, the upload path for a SKILL.md, and how workspace sharing changes who sees what
  • The task–skill–context pattern that turns a recurring job into a running workflow
  • Scheduling and monitoring recurring work, and spotting a bad run before it reaches your inbox
  • Improving results: context, examples, quality checks and a troubleshooting checklist for when outputs drift
  • A capstone build — website copy, a research brief, a content system or an email sequence — shipped inside the module

Strengths

  • Beginner-first and explicitly no-code
  • 25+ ready-to-install Skills included, not just theory
  • Every module ends in something built, not a to-do list
  • Hands-on setup help and a real community, not just videos
  • Continuously updated as ChatGPT ships new features
  • Certificate of completion when you finish the path
  • Free to start for 7 days

Keep in mind

  • Community-paced rather than a fixed cohort with deadlines
  • Focused on practical business use, not developer or API topics
  • Full Skill install requires a ChatGPT plan tier that supports it

Verdict: The best starting point if your goal is to use ChatGPT Skills in your business rather than understand them in the abstract. Start free, get one workflow running this week, and lean on the community when you hit a wall.

Explore the ChatGPT Academy →

The Academy is one of five learning paths included with All Access, alongside AI Skills Fundamentals and the Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark and Gemini Notebook paths. Start free for 7 days, cancel anytime.

Best for: Anyone starting from zero who wants the authoritative version, straight from the company that builds ChatGPT — and a free certificate to show for it.

OpenAI Academy is OpenAI’s own free learning platform, and AI Foundations is its entry point. As of August 2026, the Academy front page lists exactly three public courses (AI Foundations, Applied AI Foundations, and Agents and Workflows), all free, each with a completion certificate. It introduces the core concepts and practices for using AI effectively in everyday work — prompting, giving context, reviewing outputs, and responsible use — so you leave able to improve routine tasks like drafting, summarising, planning and meeting prep. It is the shortest honest route from “I use ChatGPT sometimes” to “I know what I am doing.”

What you’ll learn

  • The basics of AI, large language models and ChatGPT
  • Giving clear instructions and adding useful context
  • Reviewing outputs rather than accepting them
  • Using AI responsibly in everyday work
  • Applying those habits to drafting, summarising, planning and meeting preparation

Strengths

  • Free, official, and unlikely to teach bad habits
  • Curriculum evolves alongside OpenAI’s models and products
  • Free, shareable course-completion certificate
  • Genuinely aimed at people new to AI — no jargon wall

Keep in mind

  • Foundational by design — it makes you confident, not advanced
  • Broadly about “AI at work”, not a deep dive on Skills
  • Requires a free OpenAI Academy account
  • A completion certificate is not a formal OpenAI certification

Verdict: The best free first course, full stop. Take it, then move straight to Applied AI Foundations rather than taking a second beginner course somewhere else.

Take the free OpenAI Academy course →

Best for: People who already prompt competently and keep hitting the same wall — every good result is a one-off, and nothing carries over to next week.

This is the course that most directly maps to what a Skill is, even though it is framed as workflows rather than files. Applied AI Foundations teaches you to turn effective prompts into structured, repeatable workflows: take a recurring task, break it into steps, identify where ChatGPT helps, and build review points into the process. You end with a workflow plan that defines inputs, models, tools, checkpoints and human review — which is, almost line for line, the anatomy of a good SKILL.md.

What you’ll learn

  • Turning a recurring task into a repeatable workflow
  • Breaking work into steps and identifying where ChatGPT genuinely helps
  • Developing a workflow plan: the right inputs, models, tools and checkpoints
  • Designing human review into a process instead of bolting it on
  • Balancing quality, speed and cost across a workflow

Strengths

  • The free course closest to real Skill design
  • Teaches process thinking, which transfers to any AI tool
  • Free certificate, same as the other Academy courses
  • Practises on your own recurring work, not toy examples

Keep in mind

  • Assumes you are already comfortable prompting
  • Teaches workflow design, not the SKILL.md file format itself
  • No ready-made Skills to install at the end

Verdict: The best free ChatGPT course for anyone who wants their work to compound. Take it second, and bring one real recurring task with you — the course is close to useless without one.

See Applied AI Foundations →

Best for: People who have a workflow running and now want ChatGPT to carry more of it — with clear boundaries and a review step they trust.

The third and most advanced of OpenAI Academy’s public courses. Agents and Workflows is about directing agent-assisted work: providing context, defining outputs and boundaries, reviewing drafts, improving the workflow and reusing what works. That last phrase matters — reuse is the entire point of Skills, and this is the free course that treats it as a discipline rather than a feature.

What you’ll learn

  • Providing the context an agent needs to act without hand-holding
  • Defining outputs and setting explicit boundaries
  • Reviewing drafts and refining a workflow between runs
  • Identifying where human judgement and oversight are non-negotiable
  • Running and reusing a workflow you can apply to future work

Strengths

  • The only free course here focused on supervision, not prompting
  • Directly relevant to Skills, scheduled work and connected tools
  • Completes a coherent free three-course path
  • Treats oversight as a skill rather than a disclaimer

Keep in mind

  • Genuinely third in the sequence — do not start here
  • Conceptual; it will not install anything in your workspace for you
  • Some of it assumes tooling not every plan has access to

Verdict: Take it once you have a workflow you already trust. Taken too early it reads as abstract; taken at the right moment it is the best free explanation of where to stop supervising and where never to.

See Agents and Workflows →

Best for: Anyone who specifically wants ChatGPT Skills — not AI in general — and wants the definitive version rather than a YouTube summary of it.

This is not a course, and it is on the list anyway, because it is the single highest-value free hour on the subject. OpenAI’s Using Skills guide defines what a skill is, explains the SKILL.md file, walks through a five-step build flow, and lays out how Skills, GPTs and Projects fit together — with a table of practical skill examples by department. Alongside it, OpenAI Academy runs short recurring Skill Lab sessions on themes like managing daily work, analysing data and building sites and dashboards, most of which are posted as replays if you miss them live.

What you’ll learn

  • What a skill is: a reusable, shareable workflow that tells ChatGPT how to do a specific task
  • What belongs in a SKILL.md file — job, inputs, steps, output format, final checks
  • The five-step flow: pick a repeatable task, write the instructions, review and install, use it daily, then share or keep it personal
  • The three patterns Skills fall into: reusable processes, tool-based workflows, and conventions or standards
  • How Skills, custom GPTs and Projects differ and when to reach for each

Strengths

  • The authoritative source, free, and readable in one sitting
  • Ends with you building something, not just understanding it
  • Live Skill Labs add a practical, current layer
  • Notes that SKILL.md is an open standard — what you learn is portable

Keep in mind

  • A guide plus live sessions, not a structured course
  • No certificate, quizzes or curriculum
  • Live session topics rotate; check the Academy events board
  • Written for workspaces that already have Skills enabled

Verdict: If you read one thing on this page besides this article, make it the Using Skills guide. Then build your first Skill with our how to create a ChatGPT Skill walkthrough.

Read OpenAI’s Using Skills guide →

Best for: Owners and operators of small businesses who learn better from someone demonstrating a real workflow than from a curriculum — and who want examples from businesses their size.

Launched on 21 July 2026, the ChatGPT for small business program pairs free virtual webinars with in-person training run by OpenAI Academy, plus guides and partner tools from Dropbox, Shopify, Intuit, Slack and Atlassian. The webinars are product-specific and small-business-shaped: demos with real use cases, prompts to try, and automations across accounting, marketing and ecommerce. It is the closest thing to free consulting OpenAI offers.

What you’ll learn

  • How small businesses use ChatGPT Work day to day, demonstrated rather than described
  • Prompts and workflows you can copy straight into your own business
  • Automations across accounting, marketing, ecommerce and operations
  • Which partner integrations replace which manual jobs
  • Where to start when you are the whole team

Strengths

  • Free, official, and aimed squarely at small businesses
  • Live demos on real use cases rather than generic lessons
  • In-person sessions in selected cities
  • Partner integrations give concrete starting points

Keep in mind

  • A program, not a course — no curriculum or certificate
  • Session topics and cities vary; you have to catch the right one
  • Naturally steers toward paid ChatGPT Work plans
  • Coverage of Skills depends entirely on the session

Verdict: Worth an hour of any small business owner’s month, and it costs nothing. Treat it as inspiration and a source of use cases, then get structure elsewhere.

See the small business program →

Best for: Anyone who needs a credential an employer or a professional-development budget will recognise — and who wants prompting taught properly rather than as a list of tricks.

Taught by Dr. Jules White, Prompt Engineering for ChatGPT is comfortably the most enrolled course on this list, with over 709,000 learners and a 4.8-star rating across more than 8,000 reviews. Across six modules and roughly 19 hours it teaches prompt patterns — reusable, named structures like persona, question refinement, cognitive verification, few-shot, template and recipe patterns — and ends in a prompt-based application project. Prompt patterns are the intellectual ancestor of Skills: the same instinct to name a repeatable structure and reuse it.

What you’ll learn

  • Prompt engineering fundamentals and how to write a first strong prompt
  • Reusable prompt patterns, including persona and question refinement
  • Few-shot examples, chain-of-thought and ReAct prompting
  • Template and recipe patterns for structured, repeatable output
  • Building a complete prompt-based application as a capstone

Strengths

  • University-backed and genuinely well taught
  • Huge enrolment and a consistently high rating
  • Free to audit — you can take it all without paying
  • Pattern thinking transfers directly to writing Skills

Keep in mind

  • About prompting, not Skills, Projects or scheduled work
  • ~19 hours is a real commitment for a business owner
  • The certificate costs money even though the course does not
  • Predates Skills, so nothing here covers SKILL.md

Verdict: The best choice when you need a certificate with a university name on it. Audit it free if you only want the knowledge — and pair it with applied Skills training, because it will not get you there alone.

View the Vanderbilt course →

Best for: Technically comfortable learners — analysts, ops people, anyone who has met a spreadsheet formula and lived — who want the rigorous version of prompting in under two hours.

ChatGPT Prompt Engineering for Developers is taught by Isa Fulford of OpenAI and Andrew Ng, which is about as strong a pairing as free education gets. Nine lessons, one hour forty minutes, with runnable code examples covering summarising, inferring, transforming and expanding text, plus building a simple chatbot. The “for Developers” title undersells it: the two principles of prompt writing it teaches are the clearest formulation anywhere, and they apply just as well to a SKILL.md as to an API call.

What you’ll learn

  • Two core principles for writing effective prompts
  • Iterative prompt development as a systematic process, not guesswork
  • Summarising, inferring, transforming and expanding text
  • Building a custom chatbot end to end
  • How LLMs actually behave, which makes their failures predictable

Strengths

  • Free, and taught by OpenAI and DeepLearning.AI directly
  • Under two hours with runnable examples throughout
  • Systematic method rather than a bag of prompt tricks
  • The iteration discipline transfers straight into writing Skills

Keep in mind

  • Assumes basic Python — genuinely not a no-code course
  • API-oriented, not about the ChatGPT app or Skills
  • Certificate requires a paid membership tier
  • Overkill if you only want business workflows

Verdict: The best free prompt-engineering course on the internet, with one condition: skip it if the word Python puts you off. Non-coders should take Vanderbilt instead and lose nothing that matters to them.

Take the free short course →

Best for: Learners who want the widest possible tour of AI tools for the price of a takeaway, and who value lifetime access and a certificate over depth on any one product.

The Complete AI Guide by Julian Melanson, Benza Maman and Leap Year Learning is Udemy’s bestselling course in this space — 4.5 stars from 62,674 ratings, over 381,000 students, last updated in July 2026. It spans ChatGPT, Claude, prompt engineering, custom GPTs, AI writing, image, voice and video tools, and automation with Zapier and Make. Breadth is the product here, and it is genuinely useful breadth.

It also illustrates the honest limitation of the whole marketplace category. Udemy lists over 1,800 ChatGPT courses to more than 5.5 million learners at a 4.4 average rating — an enormous, well-reviewed catalogue that has almost entirely not caught up with Skills. LinkedIn Learning is the subscription alternative with the same trade-off: short, polished, LinkedIn-shareable certificates, and the same gap on SKILL.md.

What you’ll learn

  • ChatGPT and Claude for content, research and productivity
  • Prompt engineering across a wide range of tools
  • Building custom GPTs and AI assistants
  • AI writing, image, voice and video tools
  • Automation with Zapier, Make and the OpenAI API

Strengths

  • Exceptional breadth for a frequently discounted price
  • Bestseller status with a very large, satisfied student base
  • Updated regularly — last refreshed July 2026
  • Lifetime access, certificate, and a 30-day refund window

Keep in mind

  • Covers many tools, so no single one in real depth
  • Tool-led rather than business-outcome-led
  • Little to nothing on ChatGPT Skills or SKILL.md
  • Udemy list prices fluctuate wildly — never pay full price

Verdict: Buy it on sale for a broad tour of the AI tool landscape. Do not expect it to teach you Skills — for that, pair it with OpenAI’s Using Skills guide or the ChatGPT Academy.

View the Udemy course →

Best ChatGPT course for each type of learner

Best free ChatGPT course

OpenAI Academy — AI Foundations. Free, official, updated as the products change, and it issues a free course-completion certificate. Nothing else on this list matches it for accuracy on how ChatGPT itself behaves. Its limit is scope rather than quality: it teaches AI at work, not the reusable Skills you would build with it. For that, read the free Using Skills guide immediately afterwards.

Best ChatGPT course for beginners

AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy, or AI Foundations if you want free. Beginners rarely fail because a concept was too hard — they fail because nobody was there when setup broke. The Academy covers workspace setup, your first installed Skill and a shipped deliverable in one ~3-hour path, with human support attached. If you would rather self-serve at zero cost, AI Foundations is the best free equivalent.

Best ChatGPT Skills course for business

AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy. Business owners do not need to understand agents — they need last week’s reporting done without them. This is the only option here organised by business outcome rather than product feature, and the only one that hands you ready-made ChatGPT Skills you can install the same day. OpenAI’s small business program is the best free companion to it.

Best ChatGPT workflow course

OpenAI Academy — Applied AI Foundations. It is built around exactly the move most people miss: taking a task you already repeat and turning it into a defined workflow with inputs, checkpoints and human review. Agents and Workflows is the natural sequel once the workflow exists and you want it supervised rather than driven.

Best ChatGPT prompt engineering course

DeepLearning.AI if you are technical; Vanderbilt if you are not. DeepLearning.AI is more rigorous and far shorter, but it assumes basic Python. Vanderbilt is longer and needs no code, and its prompt-pattern framing is the closest thing in traditional prompting to the reusable thinking behind Skills.

Best ChatGPT course with a certificate

OpenAI Academy for a free one; Vanderbilt for a paid, university-backed one. All three OpenAI Academy courses issue a free completion certificate you can share — but OpenAI is explicit that a course-completion certificate is not a formal OpenAI certification, so do not describe it as one on your CV. The ChatGPT Academy and Udemy both issue a certificate of completion too. Be honest with yourself about which kind you actually need: if it is for a CV or a client, the university name is what carries weight; if it is for your own sense of having finished, any of them will do.

Best ChatGPT course for non-coders

OpenAI Academy, then the ChatGPT Academy. Neither needs a line of code. Deliberately avoid starting with DeepLearning.AI — it is excellent, but its Python examples will convince a non-technical learner that ChatGPT Skills are harder than they are. They are Markdown files. You can write one in a text editor.

Which ChatGPT course should you take first?

Nine recommendations is not a plan. Find your starting point below and follow the arrows — each step assumes the one before it, and every path ends in something running rather than something finished.

If you have never really used ChatGPT

AI Foundations → Applied AI Foundations → ChatGPT Academy → install your first Skill → automate one recurring job.

Two free official courses to get fluent, then applied training to turn that fluency into workflows. Do not buy anything until you have finished the free two — you will make a much better decision about paid training afterwards.

If you already use ChatGPT most days

OpenAI’s Using Skills guide → Applied AI Foundations → build your first Skill → Agents and Workflows.

Skip the fundamentals; you already have them. Your gap is not prompting — it is that nothing you do on Monday carries over to the following Monday. Start at the Skills guide.

If you run a business and want a result this month

Install one free Skill → ChatGPT Academy → OpenAI’s small business sessions for fresh use cases.

Start with a working result, not a curriculum. One Skill running on real work will tell you more about whether this is worth your time than any course description will.

If you need a credential

OpenAI Academy for the free certificate → Vanderbilt for the paid, university-backed one.

Take the free one first. It costs nothing, carries OpenAI’s name, and may well be all anyone asks to see.

Whichever path you are on, the wider progression it sits inside is the ChatGPT learning path below — that one is about the skills you build, not the courses you take.

Build real ChatGPT Skills while you learn

Here is the thing almost no course tells you: a finished course is worth nothing; a finished Skill runs forever. So do not watch a course and then wonder what to do. Build one Skill a week while you learn, on work you already do.

Each week below pairs a real business job with a free Skill from our library. Install it, run it on your own work, then open the SKILL.md and change one thing to fit how you do the job. That single edit teaches more than an hour of video.

WeekBuild thisStart from this free SkillWhat you learn
1 An email Skill AI Follow-Up Email Generator The anatomy of a SKILL.md — inputs, steps, output format — on the lowest-risk job you have.
2 A meeting notes Skill AI Meeting Notes Enforcing a fixed output structure — decisions, owners, actions — so every run looks the same.
3 A research brief Skill Market Research Brief Source handling and citation discipline — where review steps genuinely matter.
4 A content planner Skill Weekly Content Plan Encoding voice and standards, so output sounds like you without you re-explaining it.
5 A recurring business brief Weekly Business Brief Chaining Skills and putting one on a schedule — the point where it starts running without you.

Every one of those is free to download from the ChatGPT Skills library. If you would rather have the whole set plus the training that goes with them, that is what the ChatGPT Academy is.

What should you learn first? The ChatGPT learning path

Courses teach concepts; this is the order that actually gets you to a working system. Most people who give up jumped straight from step 2 to step 6.

  1. Learn ChatGPT basics. What it is good at, what it invents, and how to review it. AI Foundations is the best free hour here.
  2. Get good at prompting. Clear instructions, real context, examples. Vanderbilt’s prompt patterns or DeepLearning.AI, depending on how technical you are.
  3. Learn what a Skill is. The concept, the SKILL.md file, and how it differs from a Project or a custom GPT. Start with what an AI Skill is and Skills vs Projects vs GPTs.
  4. Install your first Skill. Do not write one yet — run someone else’s on your own work first. How to use ChatGPT Skills walks through it, and the free library gives you something to install.
  5. Build a reusable Skill of your own. Take one job you repeat weekly and write it down properly. How to create a ChatGPT Skill is the walkthrough; Applied AI Foundations is the free course that teaches the thinking.
  6. Connect your tools. Point ChatGPT at the systems the work already lives in, so it stops depending on you pasting things in.
  7. Automate the recurring work. Put a Skill on a schedule and add a review step you actually trust. Agents and Workflows covers the supervision half.
  8. Turn it into business workflows. Stack Skills into the jobs that eat your week — reporting, inbox, proposals, client updates. That is what the ChatGPT Academy and All Access are built around.

Learning ChatGPT alongside other tools? AI Skills Fundamentals teaches the cross-platform skill format first, so what you learn carries over to Claude and Gemini instead of stopping at ChatGPT’s edge.

Common mistakes beginners make with ChatGPT Skills

These five come up again and again — and every one of them is a course-selection problem as much as a skill problem.

  • Taking three beginner courses in a row. The second foundation course mostly repeats the first. If you have finished one, the next step is applied, not another overview. Diminishing returns start faster than people expect.
  • Learning prompting and stopping there. This is the expensive one. A great prompt evaporates when you close the tab; a Skill is still there next Tuesday. If a course never mentions SKILL.md, it is teaching you half the job.
  • Building one enormous Skill. OpenAI’s own guidance is that Skills work best as small building blocks you mix and match, and complex workflows should be split into smaller Skills. A single monster Skill is impossible to debug when it drifts.
  • Buying a course before checking access. Skills are not on every ChatGPT plan. Read ChatGPT Skills availability before you spend money on training that assumes a workspace you do not have.
  • Never reviewing the output. ChatGPT is confident whether or not it is correct. Build the review step into the Skill itself — a final-checks section — especially for anything touching numbers, clients or money.

Free vs paid ChatGPT courses: which should you choose?

You do not need to spend money to learn ChatGPT Skills. For most people the smartest path is to start free, prove the value on one real task, and only then pay for depth or support.

  • Start free if you are unsure or budget-conscious. OpenAI Academy plus the Using Skills guide will take you from zero to your first working Skill at no cost.
  • Start with the ChatGPT Academy if you want the fastest route from “I just opened ChatGPT” to “this runs in my business every week.” Free for 7 days, and it pairs the lessons with 25+ ready-to-install Skills and real human help when you get stuck.
  • Pay for a certificate if a credential genuinely changes something for you — a job application, a client, a training budget. Vanderbilt is the strongest name here.
  • Pay for breadth if you want a tour of the wider AI tool landscape rather than depth on ChatGPT (Udemy, on sale).
  • Do not pay for another prompting course once you have taken one. The next useful thing you buy should teach Skills, workflows or support — not prompting again.

ChatGPT Skills courses — FAQs

What’s the best free ChatGPT course for beginners?

The best free ChatGPT course for beginners is OpenAI Academy’s AI Foundations — it’s official, self-paced, includes a free completion certificate, and is designed for people starting from zero. Take it first, then move to Applied AI Foundations for repeatable workflows. If you want structured lessons that end in installed Skills rather than notes, pair it with our ChatGPT Training for Beginners path.

How long does it take to complete a ChatGPT course?

Most focused beginner courses take between 90 minutes and a weekend. The AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy runs about 3 hours across six modules, DeepLearning.AI’s prompt-engineering short course is 1h 40m, and OpenAI Academy’s free foundations are self-paced (typically one to two evenings each). Longer certificate courses like Vanderbilt’s Coursera path are a ~19-hour commitment across six modules.

Do ChatGPT courses cover Skills, Projects, and workflows?

Only some do. As of August 2026, OpenAI’s free Using Skills guide and the AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy are the two on this list that treat Skills as a first-class topic alongside Projects and workflows. Most legacy prompt-engineering courses predate Skills and don’t mention SKILL.md at all — check the syllabus for the words “Skill” and “workflow” before you enrol.

Are there ChatGPT courses that come with downloadable skill files?

Yes. The AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy ships with 25+ ready-to-install ChatGPT Skills, and the AI Agents Library All Access Pass unlocks the full library across ChatGPT, Claude Cowork and Gemini Spark. Free copy-paste versions of many workflows are also available in the free ChatGPT Skills library — install one before you finish the course and you already have working leverage.

Do I need a paid ChatGPT plan for these courses?

The lessons themselves can be studied on any ChatGPT plan, including free. The free copy-paste versions can be adapted for many free AI chat plans. Native Skill installation, Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark, connected tools and advanced automation features may require an eligible paid plan. Confirm plan-eligibility in ChatGPT Skills availability before you buy training that assumes access you may not have.

How is a ChatGPT course different from ChatGPT Skills?

A ChatGPT course teaches you how to use ChatGPT well; a ChatGPT Skill is a reusable SKILL.md file you install into ChatGPT so it does one specific job the same way every time. Courses build knowledge; Skills build leverage. The best training combines the two — you leave with the principles and with installed workflows already running. Our ChatGPT Training for Beginners path is built around that combination.

What is the best ChatGPT Skills course?

For most beginners and business owners, the best ChatGPT Skills course is the AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy, because it combines six beginner modules with 25+ ready-to-install Skills and real human support — so you finish with working workflows rather than notes. If you want the official fundamentals for free, OpenAI Academy’s AI Foundations is the best free starting course, and OpenAI’s free Using Skills guide is the best free training on Skills specifically. Explore the ChatGPT Academy →

Is there a free ChatGPT course?

Yes, several. OpenAI Academy offers three free official courses — AI Foundations, Applied AI Foundations, and Agents and Workflows — each with a free completion certificate. OpenAI’s Using Skills guide is free, DeepLearning.AI’s prompt engineering short course is free, and Vanderbilt’s Coursera course is free to audit. The ChatGPT Academy is also free for your first 7 days.

Does OpenAI have an official ChatGPT course?

Yes. OpenAI Academy is OpenAI’s own free learning platform and currently publishes three public courses: AI Foundations for people new to AI, Applied AI Foundations for turning prompts into repeatable workflows, and Agents and Workflows for directing agent-assisted work. Each issues a free course-completion certificate. OpenAI also runs live sessions, including short Skill Labs, with replays posted afterwards.

What is a ChatGPT Skill, and why does it need its own course?

OpenAI defines a skill as a reusable, shareable workflow that tells ChatGPT how to do a specific task — you define the process once, in a plain-text SKILL.md file, and it is applied reliably whenever that task comes up. It needs separate teaching because prompting and Skill design are different disciplines: prompting is about one good result now, Skills are about the same good result every time. Most ChatGPT courses were written before Skills existed and only teach the first. See what an AI Skill is for the full explanation.

Do I need to know how to code to learn ChatGPT Skills?

No. A SKILL.md file is written in Markdown — plain text with a few symbols like # for headings and - for lists. You can write one in any text editor, and you can ask ChatGPT to draft the first version for you. Every course in this guide except DeepLearning.AI’s, which assumes basic Python, is fully no-code.

How long does it take to learn ChatGPT Skills?

About 15 minutes to understand what a Skill is, an hour or two to install one and run it on real work, and roughly a weekend to finish a structured beginner path — the ChatGPT Academy runs about three hours across six modules. Becoming genuinely fluent takes two to three weeks of using Skills on real jobs. The gap between “I finished a course” and “this saves me time” is almost always step 5 of the learning path — building one Skill for a job you genuinely repeat.

Which ChatGPT course teaches reusable Skills?

Very few, which is the main finding of this guide. OpenAI’s free Using Skills guide is the authoritative explainer, and Applied AI Foundations teaches the workflow thinking behind Skills. For building and installing them against your own work, the ChatGPT Academy is the applied option — you finish with working Skills rather than an understanding of Skills. You can also install proven ones straight from the free ChatGPT Skills library.

Are paid ChatGPT courses worth it?

Sometimes — but start free. OpenAI Academy and the Using Skills guide will teach you the fundamentals at no cost. A paid course earns its money when you want structure, business-specific examples, a recognised certificate, or a human to ask when you get stuck. For most business owners, support and ready-made Skills deliver more than another set of videos. What is rarely worth paying for is a second prompting course.

Do ChatGPT courses include a certificate?

Many do. All three OpenAI Academy courses issue a free course-completion certificate, and the AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy issues a certificate of completion. Vanderbilt’s Coursera course offers a paid, shareable certificate; Udemy issues a certificate of completion; DeepLearning.AI’s certificate requires a paid membership tier. Note the distinction OpenAI itself draws: a course-completion certificate is not a formal OpenAI certification. Certificate terms change, so confirm on the provider’s enrolment page before you sign up.

Can I learn ChatGPT Skills without a Business or Enterprise plan?

You can learn the concepts on any plan — OpenAI’s Using Skills guide, the Academy courses and articles like how to create a ChatGPT Skill all cost nothing and assume nothing. Installing Skills into a workspace is a different matter and depends on your plan tier. Check ChatGPT Skills availability before buying training that assumes access you may not have.

Is ChatGPT training good for business owners?

It is arguably better suited to business owners than to developers. The recurring, low-judgement work that eats an owner’s week — weekly reporting, inbox triage, proposal drafts, client updates, content planning — is exactly what Skills handle well, and none of it needs code. The catch is that it rewards people who commit to one workflow rather than experimenting broadly. OpenAI’s free small business program is a good place to see what that looks like in practice.

Which course should I take after OpenAI Academy?

OpenAI teaches you the product; the natural next step teaches you what to build with it. For business workflows, reusable Skills and scheduled work, the ChatGPT Academy picks up roughly where the free curriculum stops. If you want prompting depth instead, take Vanderbilt or DeepLearning.AI. Do not take two foundation courses back to back — the second will mostly repeat the first.

Is there a ChatGPT certification?

Not in the sense most people mean. OpenAI Academy issues free course-completion certificates, and OpenAI has been explicit that those are not a formal OpenAI certification. Third-party certificates from Coursera, Udemy and LinkedIn Learning are certificates of completion from those platforms, not from OpenAI. If a credential matters for a job or a client, Vanderbilt’s Coursera certificate carries the most recognisable name. If capability matters more than the credential, a Skill running in your business proves more than any of them.

What about courses for Claude or Gemini?

The same logic applies — look for training that ends in something reusable. We compare the equivalent Claude options in the best Claude Cowork courses. If you use more than one tool, AI Skills Fundamentals teaches the cross-platform skill format first, so what you learn is not stranded on one platform.

Keep learning ChatGPT Skills here

Turn Skills on, install one, let it run automatically, then edit or remove it. No code.

Write your first SKILL.md from a job you already repeat, step by step.

Read the walkthrough →

The Skills worth installing first, ranked by the business job they finish.

# The 9 Best ChatGPT Skill Courses for Beginners (2026)
**This guide compares the 9 best ChatGPT Skills courses and training resources in 2026 — free and paid.** Every pick lists who it is best for, the format and price, what you will actually learn, honest pros and limitations, and a clear verdict — so you can pick training that matches your goal, your budget, and how much time you have.
_Last updated August 2026. All course info verified against current provider offerings._
**Why “Skills courses” and not just “ChatGPT courses”?** Because the gap for most people is no longer prompting. A [ChatGPT Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/what-is-an-ai-agent-skill/) is a reusable, shareable workflow — a plain-text `SKILL.md` file that tells ChatGPT how to do one job the same way every time. A course that only teaches prompting leaves you re-explaining yourself forever. A course that teaches Skills leaves you with something that keeps working after the course ends. That distinction is the yardstick used to rank everything below.
Quick answer
## The 9 best ChatGPT Skills courses in 2026
The best ChatGPT Skills course depends on whether you want practical business workflows, prompt engineering, official training, or reusable Skills you can install the same day. **Best guided option** — [AI Agents Library ChatGPT Academy](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-chatgpt-skills-courses/#course-1) (6 beginner modules, 25+ ready-to-install Skills, real human support, free for 7 days); **best free official first course** — [OpenAI Academy’s AI Foundations](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-chatgpt-skills-courses/#course-2) (free, with a completion certificate); **best free course for repeatable workflows** — [Applied AI Foundations](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-chatgpt-skills-courses/#course-3); **best free training on Skills specifically** — [OpenAI’s Using Skills guide and live Skill Labs](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-chatgpt-skills-courses/#course-5); **best university certificate** — [Vanderbilt’s Prompt Engineering for ChatGPT](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-chatgpt-skills-courses/#course-7) on Coursera.
**Beginners often benefit most from structured learning that includes real projects rather than only videos.** If you take one free course and build one real Skill from it, you are ahead of almost everyone who finished five.
**Who this guide is for**
Business owners, professionals, marketers and complete beginners who want to learn [ChatGPT Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/what-is-an-ai-agent-skill/) through structured training rather than piecing it together from scattered videos. If you would rather skip the training and just install something that works today, browse the [free ChatGPT Skills library](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/chatgpt/) instead. And if you are not yet sure whether your plan can install Skills at all, start with [ChatGPT Skills availability](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/chatgpt-skills-availability/) before you spend anything.

**The short version:** start free with OpenAI to learn the product, then take applied training to learn what to actually _build_ with it. Those are two different skills, and almost everyone who stalls has only done the first.
**How we chose these ChatGPT Skills courses**
We prioritised training that teaches ChatGPT as it works today, suits non-technical learners, and leads to something reusable rather than a certificate alone. Each provider’s published curriculum, format, price, certificate terms and update history was reviewed; where we did not complete a full course, the assessment is based on published materials. Ratings, prices and durations change — confirm current details on the provider’s page before enrolling. **Reader note:** the ChatGPT Academy is our own membership. It is included because it fits this guide’s intent and is judged on the same criteria as everything else: beginner accessibility, practical application, structure, support, price, and update frequency.
## What a ChatGPT Skills course actually needs to cover
Most “ChatGPT courses” were written for a product that no longer exists. They teach prompting into a blank chat box. ChatGPT now runs **reusable Skills**, holds context in **Projects**, connects to your real tools, and runs work on a schedule — and those are the parts that actually save time.
A course worth your hours should cover all seven of these:
* **Prompting fundamentals.** Clear instructions, useful context, and reviewing what comes back. Everything else sits on top of this. * **What a Skill is.** OpenAI defines a skill as a reusable, shareable workflow that tells ChatGPT how to do a specific task — defined once, applied reliably every time it comes up. * **The `SKILL.md` file.** The plain-text playbook itself: what the skill does, required inputs, step-by-step instructions, required output format, and the final checks. It is Markdown and portable, which is why a Skill you write today survives tool changes. * **Projects and standing context.** The difference between a Skill, a Project and a custom GPT, and when each one is the right container. If a course blurs those three, it will teach you to build the wrong thing. Our [ChatGPT Skills vs Projects vs GPTs guide](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/chatgpt-skills-vs-projects-vs-gpts/) covers the split. * **Installing and sharing.** Where Skills live, how to install one, and how workspace sharing changes who sees what. Step-by-step in [how to use ChatGPT Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-use-chatgpt-skills/). * **Scheduled and recurring work.** Getting a workflow to run without you present. This is where ChatGPT stops being an assistant and starts being leverage. * **Review habits.** Output checks, source verification, and knowing where human judgement is non-negotiable. ChatGPT is confident whether or not it is right.
**The gap worth knowing about**
Almost every course on this list — including excellent ones — was built around _prompting_, because Skills only reached most workspaces in 2026. OpenAI’s own free courses now cover repeatable workflows properly, and OpenAI publishes a dedicated Skills guide, but the large video marketplaces have not caught up: Udemy alone lists more than 1,800 ChatGPT courses, and vanishingly few of them mention `SKILL.md` at all. That is not a reason to avoid them — it is the reason most people need a second, applied step after their first course. See the [learning roadmap](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-chatgpt-skills-courses/#roadmap-heading).
**Before you enrol:** Skills are not on every ChatGPT plan. Check [ChatGPT Skills availability](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/chatgpt-skills-availability/) first so you are not paying for a course teaching a feature your workspace cannot install.
