item.html:
How to Use ChatGPT Skills: Complete Beginner's Guide (2026)

Here’s the part that surprises most people: you don’t really “run” a ChatGPT skill — it runs itself. Once a skill is turned on, ChatGPT applies it automatically the moment your request matches what the skill is for. There’s no button to press and no reminder to type. This guide walks you through the whole thing: turning skills on, adding one, letting it work, editing it when it’s close but not quite right, and removing it when you’re done.

Want the bigger picture first? What Is an AI Agent Skill? explains how skills differ from prompts. Ready to make your own? See how to create a ChatGPT skill. This page is about using skills that already exist.

See 15 ChatGPT Skills examples for work and business if you want practical workflows to try first.

ChatGPT Skills availability

OpenAI’s dedicated Skills documentation lists Personal Skills as generally available for ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu users; its Plugins FAQ separately says Personal Skills in Work are available on paid plans except Free and Go. Skills are also supported in Codex and the API. Skills do not automatically sync between desktop/web and mobile — you may need to install a Skill in each place you use ChatGPT.

Interface update: Skills are now inside the Plugin Directory

OpenAI replaced the App Directory with the Plugin Directory on July 9, 2026. Open Plugins in the ChatGPT sidebar, then select the Skills tab in the Plugin Directory. From there, you can browse, install, manage, or open the Skills available to your workspace. Plugins can package Skills alongside apps and reusable app templates, so older screenshots may still show an App Directory or a standalone Skills destination.

Quick answer

To use a ChatGPT Skill, select Plugins in the sidebar, then open the Skills tab in the Plugin Directory. Add a Skill by installing one that’s shared with you, creating one, or uploading a trusted skill package. After that, start the task it’s built for and ChatGPT can apply it automatically. If the result is close but off, edit the Skill or ask ChatGPT in the chat to adjust it. To stop using one, remove or delete it. Access varies by plan, product surface, and workspace permissions; use a Project instead if the Skills tab is not available to you.

What “Using” a ChatGPT Skill Actually Means

This is the one thing worth understanding before anything else: a ChatGPT Skill is a reusable workflow that ChatGPT can apply when relevant. Skills can be distributed as standalone workflows or packaged inside a plugin with connected apps and app templates. When you start a task that matches a Skill’s purpose, ChatGPT can apply it automatically — you don’t have to switch it on or repeat its instructions.

So “using” a skill really means two things: making sure the right skill is available (turned on and added), and then simply doing your work. The rest of this guide is about that first part — getting skills set up so they’re ready when you need them.

Do You Have Skills on Your Plan?

OpenAI’s dedicated Skills page lists Personal Skills as generally available on Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu. Its newer Plugins FAQ separately says Personal Skills in Work are available on paid plans except Free and Go. Because those official pages describe different surfaces, the practical check is your current Plugins → Skills tab; see the ChatGPT Skills availability guide for the full plan-by-plan nuance.

Don’t see Skills yet?

Use a Project instead — it works on every plan, including Free, and gives you the same everyday benefit. Jump to the Project method below.

The 5 Steps to Using a ChatGPT Skill

This covers the native Skills feature. Don’t see Skills on your account yet? Skip to the Project method instead.

Open ChatGPT, select Plugins in the sidebar, and open the Skills tab in the Plugin Directory — that’s where your skills live and where you add new ones.

On a shared workspace (Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, or Edu), a workspace admin may need to enable Skills for your role first — so if you don’t see Skills at all, that’s the thing to ask your admin about. Not on one of those plans? Keep an eye out, since availability has been expanding over time.

You can’t use a skill you don’t have, so this is where you get one. There are two common ways:

  • Install one that’s shared with you. Select Plugins in the sidebar, open the Skills tab, and look under Shared with me or Shared by your workspace. Open the more-options menu (•••) next to the skill and choose Install. It’s now available to run. Sharing one out to your team is a different flow — see how to share and install ChatGPT skills.
  • Add your own. Paste a skill from our free ChatGPT skills library using ChatGPT’s build flow, or write one from scratch. The full walkthrough is in how to create a ChatGPT skill.

Fastest way to start

Grab a ready-made skill from the ChatGPT skills library — it’s free, and using someone else’s well-built skill is the quickest way to see how the whole thing works before you make your own.

If a teammate or your workspace has already built a Skill you want to use, you don’t need to recreate it — you just install it. The whole flow is short:

  1. Open Plugins from the ChatGPT sidebar.
  2. Select the Skills tab in the Plugin Directory.
  3. Select Shared with me or Shared by [workspace name].
  4. Open the three-dot menu beside the Skill.
  5. Select Install.
  6. Start a matching task and confirm the Skill is applied correctly.

Before installing a Skill from another source, review it carefully. Uploaded Skills are scanned automatically, but OpenAI recommends reviewing the Skill yourself because it may contain instructions, supporting files, or code.

How to Use a ChatGPT Skill in Excel or Google Sheets

Open ChatGPT for Excel or Google Sheets and select + → Skills, or type @ followed by the Skill name. Ask ChatGPT to build, update, explain, analyze, or summarize the workbook. Spreadsheet conversations do not sync with your main ChatGPT history or memory, so provide any business rules or context the Skill needs inside the workbook session.

This is the step people overthink. You don’t select the skill, switch it on, or mention it. You just start the task it was built for, and ChatGPT applies the skill on its own.

For example, if you’ve added a follow-up email skill, you simply paste your meeting notes and ask for a follow-up — ChatGPT recognizes the task and uses the skill automatically. To confirm it’s working, check the output against what the skill promises: the right structure, tone, and steps. If the result already looks like the skill’s format, it’s running.

If the output is nearly right but not quite — wrong tone, missing a section, too long — you don’t scrap the skill. You adjust it. Two ways:

  • Edit it on the Skills page directly: open the skill and tighten its instructions or output format.
  • Ask ChatGPT in the chat to modify the skill — for example, “update this skill so the email is always under 150 words.” The same flow that builds skills can update and troubleshoot them.

A skill you refine a couple of times to match your voice will always outperform a generic one. This is normal, and expected.

When you no longer need a skill, clear it out so ChatGPT isn’t applying something outdated. On the Skills page, open the skill and choose Delete skill to remove it permanently.

Before deleting a shared Skill, check its ownership and workspace access. Depending on your permissions, you may only be able to stop using it, or the owner or administrator may need to manage broader access.

Don’t See Skills Yet? Use a Project Instead

If Skills haven’t reached your account yet, you can get the same everyday benefit with a Project, which is available on every plan, including Free.

A Project is a workspace that holds files, chats, and instructions for one area of work, and its instructions apply to every conversation inside it. So you can take any instruction-based skill and put it to work like this:

  1. Create a new Project in ChatGPT.
  2. Open the Project’s settings and find the instructions field.
  3. Paste the skill’s instructions there.
  4. Work inside that Project — ChatGPT follows the skill’s workflow in every chat there.

It’s not identical to a native Skill — native Skills can include examples and code and activate across your whole account — but for the instruction-based skills most business owners use, a Project gives you a practical, reusable setup without an upgrade. We break down the differences in full in our upcoming ChatGPT Skills vs GPTs vs Projects guide.

Start by Adding One Good Skill

Using ChatGPT skills comes down to a simple loop: turn skills on, add a good one, and then just do your work while ChatGPT applies it in the background. Edit it when it drifts, remove it when it’s done. The hardest part isn’t using skills — it’s picking the first one worth adding.

Check the Plugins → Skills tab in the ChatGPT surface you use. On a shared workspace, an admin may need to enable Skills for your role. If you do not have the Skills tab, use a Project, which works on every plan.

How do I install a ChatGPT skill someone shared with me?

Select Plugins in the sidebar, open the Skills tab in the Plugin Directory, and look under “Shared with me” or the section shared by your workspace. Open the more-options menu (•••) next to the Skill and choose Install. For the full workspace flow — including how to share or publish a Skill yourself — see how to share and install ChatGPT skills.

How do I edit a ChatGPT skill?

Two ways: open the skill on the Skills page and edit its instructions directly, or ask ChatGPT in the conversation to modify it (for example, “update this skill so the summary is always under 200 words”). The same flow that creates skills can update and troubleshoot them.

item.text: 15 ChatGPT Skills Examples for Work & Business (2026) A useful ChatGPT Skill does not just make ChatGPT “better at work.” It saves one repeatable method: what to ask for, which steps to follow, what not to invent, and what the finished result should look like. That is why the clearest way to understand Skills is to see real examples from beginning to end. This guide shows 15 ChatGPT Skills examples for meetings, email, content, research, sales, operations, documents, data, and websites. Every example answers four practical questions: What do you give it? What does the Skill do? What comes back? Where does it stop? If you want a ranked shortlist instead, see the separate guide to the best ChatGPT Skills for business. Tested on real business tasks I tested these workflows in real business tasks to see what inputs they need, what they actually do, and what kind of output you get. The examples below focus on the observable workflow and result, not what a Skill merely promises. Quick answer What Are Some Examples of ChatGPT Skills? Examples of ChatGPT Skills include turning a meeting transcript into decisions and action items, sorting pasted emails into a daily reply plan, converting customer comments into evidence-backed themes, analyzing spreadsheet rows for trends, building an SOP from rough notes, and turning one offer into landing-page copy. What makes each one a Skill rather than a one-off prompt is the saved workflow: its trigger, required inputs, ordered process, boundaries, and output format can be reused for the same job. What Is a ChatGPT Skill Example? A ChatGPT Skill example shows a reusable workflow in context: the request that activates it, the source material it needs, the process it follows, and the deliverable it returns. “Help with marketing” is not a useful Skill example because the job and the finish line are vague. “Turn these customer reviews into themes, supporting quotes, and three prioritized improvements” is useful because the input, method, evidence, and output are clear. OpenAI’s current Build Skills documentation describes a Skill as a package of instructions, resources, and optional scripts. ChatGPT can use a Skill when you select it with @, or it can choose one when your request matches the Skill description. OpenAI distinguishes standalone Skills in the ChatGPT desktop app from Skills distributed through plugins across ChatGPT surfaces, so the exact way you install or select one can depend on the product and workspace you use. A Skill can still be useful before you install it Every example in this guide has a free page with a copyable workflow. You can try the process in a normal chat, then save or install the structured SKILL.md version when your ChatGPT surface supports it. What Does a ChatGPT Skill Actually Look Like? At minimum, a Skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file that contains a name, a specific description, and the instructions ChatGPT should follow. Optional resources can add templates, references, assets, or scripts, but the core still needs to explain one job clearly. This shortened Meeting Notes example shows the anatomy without repeating the full downloadable file: Example SKILL.md: --- name: meeting-notes description: Use when the user provides a transcript or rough meeting notes and asks for a recap, decisions, action items, or a follow-up email. --- 1. Summarize what changed as a result of the meeting. 2. Separate settled decisions from unresolved questions. 3. Extract each action item with its owner and due date. 4. If an owner or date was not stated, label it as missing. 5. Draft a short follow-up email for human review. Use the Free Landing Page Skill → The Pattern Behind a Strong ChatGPT Skill The strongest ChatGPT Skills follow a simple pattern: one recognizable trigger, one bounded job, one defined input set, one ordered method, and one inspectable output. Drafting a reply is not sending it; preparing a CRM update is not writing to the CRM; suggesting a calendar is not publishing it. The easiest Skill idea is hiding in work you repeat Look for a task where you regularly provide the same kind of source material, make the same judgments, and want the same deliverable. How to Choose Your First ChatGPT Skill Choose by bottleneck and available input—not by which title sounds most impressive. If this is in front of you Start with Why A transcript or rough call notes Meeting Notes Produces an immediately checkable recap and action list A crowded inbox or support queue Gmail Triage or Support Reply Separates prioritization from drafting Customer or competitor evidence Customer Feedback or Competitor Research Turns source material into a structured decision brief A process only one person understands SOP Generator Exposes missing steps and decision rules before they cause errors A real offer that needs a page Landing Page Creator Creates one bounded deliverable around one conversion action Run the Skill on one real piece of work and compare the result with what you normally produce. Check factual accuracy, missing information, usefulness of the structure, and how much editing remains. Then refine the workflow before adding another Skill. The full beginner guide to using ChatGPT Skills covers the install, run, edit, and removal steps. Keep the human approval step Review facts, calculations, quotes, customer language, commitments, legal or regulated statements, and anything that will be sent, published, logged, or used to make a decision. A reusable workflow improves consistency; it does not transfer accountability to ChatGPT. Start With One Input You Already Have You do not need 15 Skills to begin. Pick one recurring task with a clear source and finish line. A meeting transcript, ten customer messages, a pasted spreadsheet, or the rough steps of a process is enough to learn what a reusable Skill changes. Frequently Asked Questions What are examples of ChatGPT Skills? Examples of ChatGPT Skills include Meeting Notes, Gmail Triage, Customer Feedback Analysis, Competitor Research, Spreadsheet Insights, SOP Generator, Website Builder, and Landing Page Creator. Each one turns a recognizable input into a defined output through a saved workflow. For example, Meeting Notes turns a transcript into decisions and action items, while Customer Feedback turns reviews or survey responses into themes, supporting quotes, and priorities. What is a ChatGPT Skill? A ChatGPT Skill is a reusable workflow package containing instructions and, optionally, resources or scripts for a specific task. OpenAI’s current format uses a Skill folder with a required SKILL.md file containing at least a name and description. The instructions can define required inputs, ordered steps, rules, and the output format. What is the difference between a ChatGPT Skill and a prompt? A prompt is usually one request; a Skill saves the method behind a task. A Skill can tell ChatGPT when the workflow applies, what information it needs, which steps to follow, what it must not invent, and how to format the result. You can copy a Skill’s workflow into a normal chat like a prompt, but installing or saving it makes the process easier to reuse. What are the best ChatGPT Skills for work? For general office work, start with Meeting Notes, Gmail Triage, PDF Executive Summary, Spreadsheet Insights, CRM Update, or SOP Generator. The right first choice depends on the source material you handle repeatedly. Use Meeting Notes for transcripts, PDF Executive Summary for reports, Spreadsheet Insights for rows or CSV data, and SOP Generator for undocumented processes. For a ranked list across business functions, see the best ChatGPT Skills guide. Can a ChatGPT Skill read my inbox or update my CRM automatically? Not unless the ChatGPT surface has the relevant connected tool, permission, and Skill instructions—and you authorize the action. The free Gmail Triage and CRM Update examples in this guide work from messages, notes, or exports you provide. They produce an action plan, reply drafts, or paste-ready CRM text; they do not claim to access an inbox, send email, or write to a CRM on their own. Can I use ChatGPT Skills on every device? The exact availability depends on how the Skill is distributed and which ChatGPT or Codex surface you use. OpenAI’s current documentation says standalone Skills are available in the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI, and the IDE extension. Skills bundled in plugins can also work in Chat and Work across ChatGPT on the web, desktop, and mobile. Check OpenAI’s current Skills documentation and your workspace settings before relying on a specific device or installation path. Are these ChatGPT Skills examples free? Yes. Every example in this guide links to a free Skill page with a workflow you can copy and try. The free ChatGPT Skills Library organizes the wider collection. All Access is the optional paid path for complete downloadable files, the full library, training, and setup support. How do I create my own ChatGPT Skill? Start with one repeated task, define the trigger and required inputs, write the steps in order, specify the output, and add rules for missing facts or risky actions. Then test realistic requests and refine the description until the Skill activates for the right work. The complete tutorial on how to create a ChatGPT Skill covers the current authoring options and SKILL.md structure. Which ChatGPT Skill should I try first? Try the Skill that matches a real input you already have and an output you can judge. Meeting Notes is a strong first example because you can compare its decisions and action items directly with the transcript. SOP Generator is useful when a process is undocumented, Customer Feedback when you have a batch of comments, and Landing Page Creator when one real offer needs a focused page.

15 ChatGPT Skills Examples for Work & Business (2026)

A useful ChatGPT Skill does not just make ChatGPT “better at work.” It saves one repeatable method: what to ask for, which steps to follow, what not to invent, and what the finished result should look like. That is why the clearest way to understand Skills is to see real examples from beginning to end.

This guide shows 15 ChatGPT Skills examples for meetings, email, content, research, sales, operations, documents, data, and websites. Every example answers four practical questions: What do you give it? What does the Skill do? What comes back? Where does it stop? If you want a ranked shortlist instead, see the separate guide to the best ChatGPT Skills for business.

Tested on real business tasks

I tested these workflows in real business tasks to see what inputs they need, what they actually do, and what kind of output you get. The examples below focus on the observable workflow and result, not what a Skill merely promises.

Quick answer

What Are Some Examples of ChatGPT Skills?

Examples of ChatGPT Skills include turning a meeting transcript into decisions and action items, sorting pasted emails into a daily reply plan, converting customer comments into evidence-backed themes, analyzing spreadsheet rows for trends, building an SOP from rough notes, and turning one offer into landing-page copy. What makes each one a Skill rather than a one-off prompt is the saved workflow: its trigger, required inputs, ordered process, boundaries, and output format can be reused for the same job.

What Is a ChatGPT Skill Example?

A ChatGPT Skill example shows a reusable workflow in context: the request that activates it, the source material it needs, the process it follows, and the deliverable it returns. “Help with marketing” is not a useful Skill example because the job and the finish line are vague. “Turn these customer reviews into themes, supporting quotes, and three prioritized improvements” is useful because the input, method, evidence, and output are clear.

OpenAI’s current Build Skills documentation describes a Skill as a package of instructions, resources, and optional scripts. ChatGPT can use a Skill when you select it with @, or it can choose one when your request matches the Skill description. OpenAI distinguishes standalone Skills in the ChatGPT desktop app from Skills distributed through plugins across ChatGPT surfaces, so the exact way you install or select one can depend on the product and workspace you use.

A Skill can still be useful before you install it

Every example in this guide has a free page with a copyable workflow. You can try the process in a normal chat, then save or install the structured SKILL.md version when your ChatGPT surface supports it.

What Does a ChatGPT Skill Actually Look Like?

At minimum, a Skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file that contains a name, a specific description, and the instructions ChatGPT should follow. Optional resources can add templates, references, assets, or scripts, but the core still needs to explain one job clearly.

This shortened Meeting Notes example shows the anatomy without repeating the full downloadable file:

Example SKILL.md:

---
name: meeting-notes
description: Use when the user provides a transcript or rough meeting notes and asks for a recap, decisions, action items, or a follow-up email.
---

1. Summarize what changed as a result of the meeting.
2. Separate settled decisions from unresolved questions.
3. Extract each action item with its owner and due date.
4. If an owner or date was not stated, label it as missing.
5. Draft a short follow-up email for human review.

Return:
- Executive summary
- Decisions
- Action-item table
- Open questions
- Follow-up email

Never invent an attendee, decision, owner, deadline, metric, or quote.

The important parts are not the Markdown symbols. They are the decisions encoded in the workflow: a discussion is not promoted into a decision, an unnamed owner stays unassigned, and the follow-up email remains a draft. Those boundaries are what make repeated output more trustworthy.

If you want the complete build process, use the separate tutorial on how to create a ChatGPT Skill. This guide stays focused on examples and outcomes.

Best for: Turning the details of a new engagement into a consistent welcome and kickoff process.

Example request: “Build the onboarding package for this new consulting client from the signed scope and my notes. Do not add deliverables that are not in the agreement.”

What happens: ChatGPT extracts the client, scope, goals, known stakeholders, timing, and dependencies. It drafts the welcome email, intake questions, kickoff agenda, and milestones while marking missing access, approvals, owners, and dates.

Example result: A warm welcome email, a focused intake checklist, a 45-minute kickoff agenda, and a 30-day plan whose open fields make the unresolved setup work visible.

Use the Free Client Onboarding Skill →

Best for: Capturing the sales information that disappears when call notes stay in a notebook.

Example request: “Turn these discovery-call notes into a HubSpot-ready update. Recommend the next deal stage, but list any missing fields instead of filling them.”

What happens: ChatGPT extracts only the stated contact and company details, summarizes the pain, budget or timeline signals, objections, and competitors, recommends a stage with a reason, and identifies the clearest next step with its owner and date when provided.

Example result: A compact contact block, recommended stage, deal notes, next action, and a “fields still missing” list. The Skill produces text to paste; it does not claim to update the CRM.

Use the Free CRM Update Skill →

Best for: Documenting work that currently lives in one person’s head, voice note, or Slack thread.

Example request: “Turn these rough month-end billing notes into an SOP a new coordinator can follow. Put every vague step in a gaps section.”

What happens: ChatGPT identifies the outcome, trigger, frequency, and owner only when stated, converts the process into ordered actions, makes decision points explicit, lists tools, extracts known failure modes, and builds a completion checklist.

Example result: A nine-step SOP, two if/then decision rules, a six-item quality check, and four targeted questions about missing approvals, file locations, and escalation rules.

Use the Free SOP Generator Skill →

Best for: Planning a small business website before opening a page builder and guessing one section at a time.

Example request: “Create the website plan for this local architecture studio. Here are the services, audiences, proof points, brand voice, and primary enquiry action.”

What happens: ChatGPT turns the business context into a sitemap, visitor journeys, a homepage hero, section plans, calls to action, and first-pass SEO direction. Missing proof stays visible instead of becoming a fictional testimonial or result.

Example result: A five-page sitemap, clear page goals, homepage copy from hero to FAQ, service-page briefs, and a list of proof assets the studio still needs to supply.

Use the Free Website Builder Skill →

Best for: Building one focused campaign page around one audience, one offer, and one action.

Example request: “Write a landing page for this fixed-price strategy session. The audience is first-time agency owners, and the only CTA is to book a call. Here are the terms, objections, and proof.”

What happens: ChatGPT locks the primary action, writes the hero, problem, offer, proof layout, objections, and closing CTA in reading order, and marks any missing testimonial, result, logo, or number as an input gap.

Example result: Complete copy from above the fold to the final CTA, with one consistent conversion goal and visible placeholders wherever real proof must be added by the business.

Use the Free Landing Page Skill →

The Pattern Behind a Strong ChatGPT Skill

The strongest ChatGPT Skills follow a simple pattern: one recognizable trigger, one bounded job, one defined input set, one ordered method, and one inspectable output. Across all 15 examples, five design choices keep repeating:

  1. The input predicts the Skill. A transcript triggers meeting work; reviews trigger feedback analysis; an offer and audience trigger a landing page.
  2. The workflow makes decisions explicit. It explains how to separate a decision from a discussion, a bug from a request, or a source fact from an inference.
  3. The output has a stable shape. The result is a table, brief, draft, plan, checklist, or page—not “some ideas.”
  4. Missing information stays missing. A strong Skill labels an unassigned owner, absent proof point, unknown price, or unavailable metric instead of inventing one.
  5. External action is separate from analysis. Drafting a reply is not sending it; preparing a CRM update is not writing to the CRM; suggesting a calendar is not publishing it.

The easiest Skill idea is hiding in work you repeat

Look for a task where you regularly provide the same kind of source material, make the same judgments, and want the same deliverable. That repeated input → decision → output path is usually a better Skill than a broad “assistant” that tries to do everything.

How to Choose Your First ChatGPT Skill

Choose by bottleneck and available input—not by which title sounds most impressive.

If this is in front of you Start with Why
A transcript or rough call notes Meeting Notes Produces an immediately checkable recap and action list
A crowded inbox or support queue Gmail Triage or Support Reply Separates prioritization from drafting
Customer or competitor evidence Customer Feedback or Competitor Research Turns source material into a structured decision brief
A process only one person understands SOP Generator Exposes missing steps and decision rules before they cause errors
A real offer that needs a page Landing Page Creator Creates one bounded deliverable around one conversion action

Run the Skill on one real piece of work and compare the result with what you normally produce. Check factual accuracy, missing information, usefulness of the structure, and how much editing remains. Then refine the workflow before adding another Skill. The full beginner guide to using ChatGPT Skills covers the install, run, edit, and removal steps.

Keep the human approval step

Review facts, calculations, quotes, customer language, commitments, legal or regulated statements, and anything that will be sent, published, logged, or used to make a decision. A reusable workflow improves consistency; it does not transfer accountability to ChatGPT.

Start With One Input You Already Have

You do not need 15 Skills to begin. Pick one recurring task with a clear source and finish line. A meeting transcript, ten customer messages, a pasted spreadsheet, or the rough steps of a process is enough to learn what a reusable Skill changes.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are examples of ChatGPT Skills?

Examples of ChatGPT Skills include Meeting Notes, Gmail Triage, Customer Feedback Analysis, Competitor Research, Spreadsheet Insights, SOP Generator, Website Builder, and Landing Page Creator. Each one turns a recognizable input into a defined output through a saved workflow. For example, Meeting Notes turns a transcript into decisions and action items, while Customer Feedback turns reviews or survey responses into themes, supporting quotes, and priorities.

What is a ChatGPT Skill?

A ChatGPT Skill is a reusable workflow package containing instructions and, optionally, resources or scripts for a specific task. OpenAI’s current format uses a Skill folder with a required SKILL.md file containing at least a name and description. The instructions can define required inputs, ordered steps, rules, and the output format.

What is the difference between a ChatGPT Skill and a prompt?

A prompt is usually one request; a Skill saves the method behind a task. A Skill can tell ChatGPT when the workflow applies, what information it needs, which steps to follow, what it must not invent, and how to format the result. You can copy a Skill’s workflow into a normal chat like a prompt, but installing or saving it makes the process easier to reuse.

What are the best ChatGPT Skills for work?

For general office work, start with Meeting Notes, Gmail Triage, PDF Executive Summary, Spreadsheet Insights, CRM Update, or SOP Generator. The right first choice depends on the source material you handle repeatedly. Use Meeting Notes for transcripts, PDF Executive Summary for reports, Spreadsheet Insights for rows or CSV data, and SOP Generator for undocumented processes. For a ranked list across business functions, see the best ChatGPT Skills guide.

Can a ChatGPT Skill read my inbox or update my CRM automatically?

Not unless the ChatGPT surface has the relevant connected tool, permission, and Skill instructions—and you authorize the action. The free Gmail Triage and CRM Update examples in this guide work from messages, notes, or exports you provide. They produce an action plan, reply drafts, or paste-ready CRM text; they do not claim to access an inbox, send email, or write to a CRM on their own.

Can I use ChatGPT Skills on every device?

The exact availability depends on how the Skill is distributed and which ChatGPT or Codex surface you use. OpenAI’s current documentation says standalone Skills are available in the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI, and the IDE extension. Skills bundled in plugins can also work in Chat and Work across ChatGPT on the web, desktop, and mobile. Check OpenAI’s current Skills documentation and your workspace settings before relying on a specific device or installation path.

Are these ChatGPT Skills examples free?

Yes. Every example in this guide links to a free Skill page with a workflow you can copy and try. The free ChatGPT Skills Library organizes the wider collection. All Access is the optional paid path for complete downloadable files, the full library, training, and setup support.

How do I create my own ChatGPT Skill?

Start with one repeated task, define the trigger and required inputs, write the steps in order, specify the output, and add rules for missing facts or risky actions. Then test realistic requests and refine the description until the Skill activates for the right work. The complete tutorial on how to create a ChatGPT Skill covers the current authoring options and SKILL.md structure.

Which ChatGPT Skill should I try first?

Try the Skill that matches a real input you already have and an output you can judge. Meeting Notes is a strong first example because you can compare its decisions and action items directly with the transcript. SOP Generator is useful when a process is undocumented, Customer Feedback when you have a batch of comments, and Landing Page Creator when one real offer needs a focused page.

# 15 ChatGPT Skills Examples for Work & Business (2026)
**A useful ChatGPT Skill does not just make ChatGPT “better at work.” It saves one repeatable method: what to ask for, which steps to follow, what not to invent, and what the finished result should look like.** That is why the clearest way to understand Skills is to see real examples from beginning to end.
This guide shows 15 ChatGPT Skills examples for meetings, email, content, research, sales, operations, documents, data, and websites. Every example answers four practical questions: **What do you give it? What does the Skill do? What comes back? Where does it stop?** If you want a ranked shortlist instead, see the separate guide to the [best ChatGPT Skills for business](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-chatgpt-skills/).
**Tested on real business tasks**
I tested these workflows in real business tasks to see what inputs they need, what they actually do, and what kind of output you get. The examples below focus on the observable workflow and result, not what a Skill merely promises.
Quick answer
## What Are Some Examples of ChatGPT Skills?
**Examples of ChatGPT Skills include turning a meeting transcript into decisions and action items, sorting pasted emails into a daily reply plan, converting customer comments into evidence-backed themes, analyzing spreadsheet rows for trends, building an SOP from rough notes, and turning one offer into landing-page copy.** What makes each one a Skill rather than a one-off prompt is the saved workflow: its trigger, required inputs, ordered process, boundaries, and output format can be reused for the same job.
## What Is a ChatGPT Skill Example?
**A ChatGPT Skill example shows a reusable workflow in context: the request that activates it, the source material it needs, the process it follows, and the deliverable it returns.** “Help with marketing” is not a useful Skill example because the job and the finish line are vague. “Turn these customer reviews into themes, supporting quotes, and three prioritized improvements” is useful because the input, method, evidence, and output are clear.
OpenAI’s current [Build Skills documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills) describes a Skill as a package of instructions, resources, and optional scripts. ChatGPT can use a Skill when you select it with `@`, or it can choose one when your request matches the Skill description. OpenAI distinguishes standalone Skills in the ChatGPT desktop app from Skills distributed through plugins across ChatGPT surfaces, so the exact way you install or select one can depend on the product and workspace you use.
**A Skill can still be useful before you install it**
Every example in this guide has a free page with a copyable workflow. You can try the process in a normal chat, then save or install the structured SKILL.md version when your ChatGPT surface supports it.
## What Does a ChatGPT Skill Actually Look Like?
**At minimum, a Skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` file that contains a name, a specific description, and the instructions ChatGPT should follow.** Optional resources can add templates, references, assets, or scripts, but the core still needs to explain one job clearly.
This shortened Meeting Notes example shows the anatomy without repeating the full downloadable file:
**Example SKILL.md:**
``` --- name: meeting-notes description: Use when the user provides a transcript or rough meeting notes and asks for a recap, decisions, action items, or a follow-up email. ---
1. Summarize what changed as a result of the meeting. 2. Separate settled decisions from unresolved questions. 3. Extract each action item with its owner and due date. 4. If an owner or date was not stated, label it as missing. 5. Draft a short follow-up email for human review.
Return: - Executive summary - Decisions - Action-item table - Open questions - Follow-up email
Never invent an attendee, decision, owner, deadline, metric, or quote. ```
The important parts are not the Markdown symbols. They are the decisions encoded in the workflow: a discussion is not promoted into a decision, an unnamed owner stays unassigned, and the follow-up email remains a draft. Those boundaries are what make repeated output more trustworthy.
If you want the complete build process, use the separate tutorial on [how to create a ChatGPT Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-chatgpt-skill/). This guide stays focused on examples and outcomes.

The full [beginner guide to using ChatGPT Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-use-chatgpt-skills/) covers the install, run, edit, and removal steps.
**Keep the human approval step**
Review facts, calculations, quotes, customer language, commitments, legal or regulated statements, and anything that will be sent, published, logged, or used to make a decision. A reusable workflow improves consistency; it does not transfer accountability to ChatGPT.
## Start With One Input You Already Have
You do not need 15 Skills to begin. Pick one recurring task with a clear source and finish line. A meeting transcript, ten customer messages, a pasted spreadsheet, or the rough steps of a process is enough to learn what a reusable Skill changes.
## Frequently Asked Questions
What are examples of ChatGPT Skills?
**Examples of ChatGPT Skills include Meeting Notes, Gmail Triage, Customer Feedback Analysis, Competitor Research, Spreadsheet Insights, SOP Generator, Website Builder, and Landing Page Creator.** Each one turns a recognizable input into a defined output through a saved workflow. For example, Meeting Notes turns a transcript into decisions and action items, while Customer Feedback turns reviews or survey responses into themes, supporting quotes, and priorities.
What is a ChatGPT Skill?
**A ChatGPT Skill is a reusable workflow package containing instructions and, optionally, resources or scripts for a specific task.** OpenAI’s current format uses a Skill folder with a required SKILL.md file containing at least a name and description. The instructions can define required inputs, ordered steps, rules, and the output format.
What is the difference between a ChatGPT Skill and a prompt?
**A prompt is usually one request; a Skill saves the method behind a task.** A Skill can tell ChatGPT when the workflow applies, what information it needs, which steps to follow, what it must not invent, and how to format the result. You can copy a Skill’s workflow into a normal chat like a prompt, but installing or saving it makes the process easier to reuse.
What are the best ChatGPT Skills for work?
**For general office work, start with Meeting Notes, Gmail Triage, PDF Executive Summary, Spreadsheet Insights, CRM Update, or SOP Generator.** The right first choice depends on the source material you handle repeatedly. Use Meeting Notes for transcripts, PDF Executive Summary for reports, Spreadsheet Insights for rows or CSV data, and SOP Generator for undocumented processes. For a ranked list across business functions, see the [best ChatGPT Skills guide](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/best-chatgpt-skills/).
Can a ChatGPT Skill read my inbox or update my CRM automatically?
**Not unless the ChatGPT surface has the relevant connected tool, permission, and Skill instructions—and you authorize the action.** The free Gmail Triage and CRM Update examples in this guide work from messages, notes, or exports you provide. They produce an action plan, reply drafts, or paste-ready CRM text; they do not claim to access an inbox, send email, or write to a CRM on their own.
Can I use ChatGPT Skills on every device?
**The exact availability depends on how the Skill is distributed and which ChatGPT or Codex surface you use.** OpenAI’s current documentation says standalone Skills are available in the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI, and the IDE extension. Skills bundled in plugins can also work in Chat and Work across ChatGPT on the web, desktop, and mobile. Check [OpenAI’s current Skills documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills) and your workspace settings before relying on a specific device or installation path.
Are these ChatGPT Skills examples free?
**Yes. Every example in this guide links to a free Skill page with a workflow you can copy and try.** The [free ChatGPT Skills Library](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/chatgpt/) organizes the wider collection. All Access is the optional paid path for complete downloadable files, the full library, training, and setup support.
How do I create my own ChatGPT Skill?
**Start with one repeated task, define the trigger and required inputs, write the steps in order, specify the output, and add rules for missing facts or risky actions.** Then test realistic requests and refine the description until the Skill activates for the right work. The complete tutorial on [how to create a ChatGPT Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-chatgpt-skill/) covers the current authoring options and SKILL.md structure.
Which ChatGPT Skill should I try first?
**Try the Skill that matches a real input you already have and an output you can judge.** Meeting Notes is a strong first example because you can compare its decisions and action items directly with the transcript. SOP Generator is useful when a process is undocumented, Customer Feedback when you have a batch of comments, and Landing Page Creator when one real offer needs a focused page.

__graph.name: Free AI Skills Library — AI Agents Library

mainEntity.name: What is an AI agent skill?

acceptedAnswer.text: An AI agent skill is a reusable workflow for a specific business task. Instead of starting from a blank prompt, you follow a structured process that tells the AI tool what to do, what information to use, and what output to create. It is usually smaller than a full AI agent; if you want to build one, start with the complete AI skill guide.

mainEntity.name: What is an AI agent library?

acceptedAnswer.text: An AI agent library is an organized collection of reusable resources for building or using AI agents — developer frameworks, prebuilt agent templates, or no-code AI skills and workflows. This site is the third type: a free, no-code library of ready-to-use AI agent skills for ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini Spark — no building required.

mainEntity.name: Which free AI skills are live right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: There are 30 free skills live, organized by outcome and by AI tool. The newest are the eight Website & Design skills — the Free AI SEO Audit Skill, Free AI UX Review Skill, Free AI Website Builder Skill, Free AI Landing Page Creator Skill, Free AI SEO Metadata Skill, Free AI Website Copy Refresh Skill, Free AI Brand Style Guide Skill, and Free AI Brand Voice Check Skill — followed by the Free AI Spreadsheet Insights Skill, the Free AI CRM Update Skill, the Free AI Content Repurposing Skill, and the Free AI Weekly Content Plan Skill. Browse by outcome with Free AI Website & Design Skills, Free AI Research Skills, Free AI Email Skills, Free AI Content & Marketing Skills, or Free AI Documents & Data Skills, or by tool with Free Claude Skills, Free Gemini Spark Skills, and Free ChatGPT Skills. Also live: the Free AI Client Proposal Skill, Free AI PDF Executive Summary Skill, Free AI Client Onboarding Skill, Free AI Overdue Invoice Follow-Up Skill, Free AI SOP Generator Skill, Free AI Meeting Notes Skill, Free AI Monthly Business Review Skill, Free AI Cold Outreach Email Skill, Free Claude Credit Saver Skill, Free AI Social Media Post Generator Skill, Free Weekly Business Brief AI Skill, Free AI Gmail Triage Skill, Free AI Competitor Research Skill, Free AI Market Research Brief Skill, Free AI Customer Feedback Skill, Free AI Follow-Up Email Skill, and Free AI News Research Skill — with new skills added every week. If you want to create your own, use the platform guides for ChatGPT skills, Claude skills, and Gemini Spark skills.

mainEntity.name: Can I browse skills by category or by AI tool?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Browse by outcome — like Research & Analysis or Email & Communication — or by AI tool with Claude, Gemini Spark, and ChatGPT from the Free AI Skills menu. The library page also has a Collections sidebar so you can filter by Business Operations, Research & Analysis, Email & Communication, Content & Marketing, Productivity & Planning, Sales & Customer Support, Documents & Data, or Website & Design. New categories are added as more skills are published in each area, so check back often.

mainEntity.name: Are the AI skills free?

acceptedAnswer.text: The free AI skill pages are free to open and try. The All Access Pass starts with 7 days free, then continues at $14/month if you stay. You can cancel anytime.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to know how to code?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. These are no-code workflows for beginners, business owners, creators, and knowledge workers. You only need the AI tool listed on the skill page and a real task you want help with. If you already have a reusable prompt, read how to turn a prompt into an AI skill.

mainEntity.name: Do I need the ChatGPT Skills feature to use these?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Every skill here is written as plain text, so you can paste it straight into a chat or into a ChatGPT Project and it runs on any plan, including Free. OpenAI's built-in Skills feature makes ChatGPT load those instructions automatically, which is convenient but not required — and it isn't on every plan. To check whether your account has it, see ChatGPT Skills availability: which plans have it and why it may not be showing. The same skills also work in Claude and Gemini Spark.

mainEntity.name: How are skills different from setup guides?

acceptedAnswer.text: Setup guides help you get tools like Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark, and NotebookLM ready to use. Skills help you complete a specific workflow after your tool is ready, such as planning your week or turning AI news into a brief. To understand how skills fit inside larger automated systems, read what AI agents are.

mainEntity.name: Can I use these for client work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Active All Access Pass members may use the workflows while delivering services to their own clients. The pass does not include permission to resell, redistribute, or republish the original templates, files, or training materials.

mainEntity.name: Can I cancel anytime?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Cancel during your free 7 days and you pay nothing. After the trial, the All Access Pass is $14/month and you can cancel anytime.

Questions

Quick answers about the free skills, how they fit with setup guides, and what changes when you join the Academy.

What is an AI agent skill?

An AI agent skill is a reusable workflow for a specific business task. Instead of starting from a blank prompt, you follow a structured process that tells the AI tool what to do, what information to use, and what output to create. It is usually smaller than a full AI agent; if you want to build one, start with the complete AI skill guide.

What is an AI agent library?

An AI agent library is an organized collection of reusable resources for building or using AI agents — developer frameworks, prebuilt agent templates, or no-code AI skills and workflows. This site is the third type: a free, no-code library of ready-to-use AI agent skills for ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini Spark — no building required.

Which free AI skills are live right now?

There are 34 free skills live, organized by outcome and by AI tool. The newest are the Free AI Blog Post Skill, Free AI Presentation Skill, Free AI Daily Brief Skill, and Free AI File Organizer Skill — followed by the eight Website & Design skills — the Free AI SEO Audit Skill, Free AI UX Review Skill, Free AI Website Builder Skill, Free AI Landing Page Creator Skill, Free AI SEO Metadata Skill, Free AI Website Copy Refresh Skill, Free AI Brand Style Guide Skill, and Free AI Brand Voice Check Skill — and the Free AI Spreadsheet Insights Skill, the Free AI CRM Update Skill, the Free AI Content Repurposing Skill, and the Free AI Weekly Content Plan Skill. Browse by outcome with Free AI Website & Design Skills, Free AI Research Skills, Free AI Email Skills, Free AI Content & Marketing Skills, or Free AI Documents & Data Skills, or by tool with Free Claude Skills, Free Gemini Spark Skills, and Free ChatGPT Skills. Also live: the Free AI Client Proposal Skill, Free AI PDF Executive Summary Skill, Free AI Client Onboarding Skill, Free AI Overdue Invoice Follow-Up Skill, Free AI SOP Generator Skill, Free AI Meeting Notes Skill, Free AI Monthly Business Review Skill, Free AI Cold Outreach Email Skill, Free Claude Credit Saver Skill, Free AI Social Media Post Generator Skill, Free Weekly Business Brief AI Skill, Free AI Gmail Triage Skill, Free AI Competitor Research Skill, Free AI Market Research Brief Skill, Free AI Customer Feedback Skill, Free AI Follow-Up Email Skill, and Free AI News Research Skill — with new skills added every week. If you want to create your own, use the platform guides for ChatGPT skills, Claude skills, and Gemini Spark skills.

Can I browse skills by category or by AI tool?

Yes. Browse by outcome — like Research & Analysis or Email & Communication — or by AI tool with Claude, Gemini Spark, and ChatGPT from the Free AI Skills menu. The library page also has a Collections sidebar so you can filter by Business Operations, Research & Analysis, Email & Communication, Content & Marketing, Productivity & Planning, Sales & Customer Support, Documents & Data, or Website & Design. New categories are added as more skills are published in each area, so check back often.

Are the AI skills free?

The free AI skill pages are free to open and try. The All Access Pass starts with 7 days free, then continues at $14/mo. if you stay. You can cancel anytime.

Do I need to know how to code?

No. These are no-code workflows for beginners, business owners, creators, and knowledge workers. You only need the AI tool listed on the skill page and a real task you want help with. If you already have a reusable prompt, read how to turn a prompt into an AI skill.

Do I need the ChatGPT Skills feature to use these?

No. Every skill here is written as plain text, so you can paste it straight into a chat or into a ChatGPT Project and it runs on any plan, including Free. OpenAI's built-in Skills feature makes ChatGPT load those instructions automatically, which is convenient but not required — and it isn't on every plan. To check whether your account has it, see ChatGPT Skills availability: which plans have it and why it may not be showing. The same skills also work in Claude and Gemini Spark.

How are skills different from setup guides?

Setup guides help you get tools like Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark, and Gemini Notebook ready to use. Skills help you complete a specific workflow after your tool is ready, such as planning your week or turning AI news into a brief. To understand how skills fit inside larger automated systems, read what AI agents are.

Can I use these for client work?

Active All Access Pass members may use the workflows while delivering services to their own clients. The pass does not include permission to resell, redistribute, or republish the original templates, files, or training materials.

Can I cancel anytime?

Yes. Cancel during your free 7 days and you pay nothing. After the trial, the All Access Pass is $14/mo. and you can cancel anytime.

**AI Agents Library helps business owners, beginners, and creators** turn tedious business tasks into reusable AI agent skills and workflows for research, content creation, email follow-ups, weekly planning, and document organization with Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark, Google Workspace, ChatGPT, Chrome, and NotebookLM — **without coding or technical overwhelm.**
Questions
Quick answers about the free skills, how they fit with setup guides, and what changes when you join the Academy.
What is an AI agent skill?
An [AI agent skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/what-is-an-ai-agent-skill/) is a reusable workflow for a specific business task. Instead of starting from a blank prompt, you follow a structured process that tells the AI tool what to do, what information to use, and what output to create. It is usually smaller than a full [AI agent](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/ai-agents/); if you want to build one, start with the [complete AI skill guide](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-an-ai-skill/).
What is an AI agent library?
An [AI agent library](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/what-is-an-ai-agent-library/) is an organized collection of reusable resources for building or using AI agents — developer frameworks, prebuilt agent templates, or no-code AI skills and workflows. This site is the third type: a free, no-code library of ready-to-use [AI agent skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/what-is-an-ai-agent-skill/) for ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini Spark — no building required.
Which free AI skills are live right now?
There are 34 free skills live, organized by outcome and by AI tool. The newest are the [Free AI Blog Post Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/blog-post/), [Free AI Presentation Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/presentation/), [Free AI Daily Brief Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/daily-brief/), and [Free AI File Organizer Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/file-organizer/) — followed by the eight [Website & Design skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/web-design/) — the [Free AI SEO Audit Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/seo-audit/), [Free AI UX Review Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/ux-review/), [Free AI Website Builder Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/website-builder/), [Free AI Landing Page Creator Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/landing-page/), [Free AI SEO Metadata Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/seo-metadata/), [Free AI Website Copy Refresh Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/website-copy-refresh/), [Free AI Brand Style Guide Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/brand-style-guide/), and [Free AI Brand Voice Check Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/brand-voice-check/) — and the [Free AI Spreadsheet Insights Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/spreadsheet-insights/), the [Free AI CRM Update Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/crm-update/), the [Free AI Content Repurposing Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/content-repurposing/), and the [Free AI Weekly Content Plan Skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/weekly-content-plan/). Browse by outcome with [Free AI Website & Design Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/web-design/), [Free AI Research Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/research/), [Free AI Email Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/email/), [Free AI Content & Marketing Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/content-marketing/), or [Free AI Documents & Data Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/documents-data/), or by tool with [Free Claude Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/claude/), [Free Gemini Spark Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/gemini-spark/), and [Free ChatGPT Skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/chatgpt/). Also live: the Free AI Client Proposal Skill, Free AI PDF Executive Summary Skill, Free AI Client Onboarding Skill, Free AI Overdue Invoice Follow-Up Skill, Free AI SOP Generator Skill, Free AI Meeting Notes Skill, Free AI Monthly Business Review Skill, Free AI Cold Outreach Email Skill, Free Claude Credit Saver Skill, Free AI Social Media Post Generator Skill, Free Weekly Business Brief AI Skill, Free AI Gmail Triage Skill, Free AI Competitor Research Skill, Free AI Market Research Brief Skill, Free AI Customer Feedback Skill, Free AI Follow-Up Email Skill, and Free AI News Research Skill — with new skills added every week. If you want to create your own, use the platform guides for [ChatGPT skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-chatgpt-skill/), [Claude skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-claude-skill/), and [Gemini Spark skills](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/how-to-create-a-gemini-spark-skill/).
Can I browse skills by category or by AI tool?
Yes. Browse by outcome — like [Research & Analysis](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/research/) or [Email & Communication](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/email/) — or by AI tool with [Claude](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/claude/), [Gemini Spark](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/gemini-spark/), and [ChatGPT](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/chatgpt/) from the Free AI Skills menu. The library page also has a Collections sidebar so you can filter by Business Operations, Research & Analysis, Email & Communication, Content & Marketing, Productivity & Planning, Sales & Customer Support, Documents & Data, or Website & Design. New categories are added as more skills are published in each area, so check back often.
Are the AI skills free?
The [free AI skill pages](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/) are free to open and try. The All Access Pass starts with 7 days free, then continues at $14/mo. if you stay. You can cancel anytime.
Do I need to know how to code?
No. These are no-code workflows for beginners, business owners, creators, and knowledge workers. You only need the AI tool listed on the skill page and a real task you want help with. If you already have a reusable prompt, read [how to turn a prompt into an AI skill](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/turn-a-prompt-into-an-ai-skill/).
Do I need the ChatGPT Skills feature to use these?
No. Every skill here is written as plain text, so you can paste it straight into a chat or into a ChatGPT Project and it runs on any plan, including Free. OpenAI's built-in Skills feature makes ChatGPT load those instructions automatically, which is convenient but not required — and it isn't on every plan. To check whether your account has it, see [ChatGPT Skills availability: which plans have it and why it may not be showing](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/blog/chatgpt-skills-availability/). The same skills also work in [Claude](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/claude/) and [Gemini Spark](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/skills/gemini-spark/).
How are skills different from setup guides?
[Setup guides](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/setup-guides/) help you get tools like Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark, and Gemini Notebook ready to use. Skills help you complete a specific workflow after your tool is ready, such as planning your week or turning AI news into a brief. To understand how skills fit inside larger automated systems, read [what AI agents are](https://www.aiagentslibrary.com/ai-agents/).
Can I use these for client work?
Active All Access Pass members may use the workflows while delivering services to their own clients. The pass does not include permission to resell, redistribute, or republish the original templates, files, or training materials.
Can I cancel anytime?
Yes. Cancel during your free 7 days and you pay nothing. After the trial, the All Access Pass is $14/mo. and you can cancel anytime.
